IDX.en_translation:
A - Gaurāṅgasundara is a treasure trove of endless virtues. Ā - He is always immersed in joy, an ocean of divine love. 

I - The charm of His face surpasses the moon. Ī - The Supreme Lord, whom Brahmā and others meditate upon constantly. 

U - He delivered the people of the world by giving the wealth of love. Ū - He did not consider anyone less, whether sinner or distressed. 

Ṛ - To repay the debt to Śrīmatī Rādhā-rāṇī, Ṝ - He properly incarnated in Nadīyā. 

Ḷ - Śrī Gaurāṅga’s body is anointed with sandalwood paste. Ḹ - Seeing His divine pastimes, everyone becomes enraptured. 

E - There will never be another Lord so merciful. Ai - He preached exclusive devotion to Lord Kṛṣṇa. 

O - Going to the land of Odisha, the Lord performed many pastimes. Au - By His quality of magnanimity, He delivered Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya. 

Whoever chants these fourteen vowels soon attains the lotus feet of Lord Gaurāṅga. 

With hope in the feet of Śrī Jāhnavā and Rāmacandra, Premadāsa sings these fourteen vowels.

Advaita Ācārya is directly the Supreme Lord. His glory is not comprehensible to the ordinary soul. 

Lord Mahā-Viṣṇu performs the activities of creation of the universe. His incarnation is directly Advaita Ācārya. 

Advaita is the auspiciousness of the world and the abode of auspicious qualities. His character is always auspicious, and His Name is also “Auspicious.” 

He is the one with lotus eyes, in whom there is both the “limb” and the “portion” of the Lord. He bears the Name “Kamalākṣa” as an ornament. 

Advaita is a portion of Lord Mahā-Viṣṇu and is the abode of all qualities. He is non-different from the Supreme Lord; therefore His full Name is “Advaita.” 

Without teaching devotion, He has no activity. Therefore, His Name became “Advaita Ācārya.” 

Advaita Ācārya is the best portion of the Supreme Lord. His spiritual identity, Name, and qualities are all wonderful. 

By His offering of Tulasī leaves and by His roar, Lord Caitanya incarnated with His own associates. 

Through Him the Lord propagated congregational chanting and delivered the world. 

The qualities and glory of Advaita Ācārya are boundless. At his feet, I offer millions of obeisances. 

All glories, all glories to Advaita Ācārya, the venerable associate of Lord Caitanya! Please grant me devotion at your feet.

IDX.en_translation:
Abandoning ego, false pride, bad association, and ignorance, worship the lotus feet of your spiritual master. Perform self-surrender with your body, home, and relatives, for the words of the guru are of supreme importance. 

Constantly serve Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, the bestower of the wish-fulfilling tree of divine love. The son of the King of Vraja is Rādhā's treasure of life—all these topics are wonderful. 

Appearing in Navadvīpa and accepting the mood of Rādhā, Her luster became the adornment of His body. Desiring to fulfill three wishes, He manifested in the womb of Mother Śacī, taking along His associates. 

Gaura-hari descended, creating a flood of divine love, and accomplished the three works of His heart. In what mood the beloved of Rādhā constantly cries—only the society of devotees understands this. 

If perfection is attained secretly through the nine processes of devotional service, I will always pray with humility. By performing the congregational chanting of the Holy Name with a mind always absorbed, all obstacles are removed for the desired attainment. 

In the marketplace of the material world, lust binds and kills with its noose. A servant of the Lord loudly proclaims: "Seek the association of devotees and engage in the joyful pastimes of loving discussions; then all dangers will be destroyed." 

Wife, sons, and all relatives—hundreds and hundreds will die. Be careful of yourself! I am ruined by these material affairs; I did not worship the lotus feet of the Lord. For me, there is no more deliverance. 

My purpose lies in the association of Rāmacandra Kavirāja. Without his association, everything is void. If I am reborn, may I attain his association; then Narottama will be blessed. 

I will not speak of the topics of my devotional service indiscriminately here and there; be careful in this regard. Let no one be angry, and do not take my fault. Offer obeisances to the feet of the devotees.

IDX.en_translation:
O Lord of Nīlācala! Like a mighty elephant, please trample upon the lotus grove of my distress. 

The king of elephants, Gajendra, meditated while in the midst of terrible waters. You, the wielder of the disc, destroyed the crocodile and saved him. 

In a dense forest, a fawn was trapped. From what great calamity did You save her? 

Hearing Draupadī’s appeal in the assembly of the Kauravas, O Lord, You averted her shame by bestowing millions of garments. 

Rāvaṇa’s brother, Vibhīṣaṇa, took refuge in You. Protecting his feet, You made him the king of Laṅkā. 

Prahlāda’s father was very wicked and terrible. You emerged from the pillar and instantly tore him apart. 

The poet Kālavega says: “I am a person of humble origin. I am appealing at Your lotus feet.”

Will Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, who is dear to Śrīla Jagannātha dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja and one in heart with Śrīla Gaurakiśora dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja, always remain in my memory, full of the mercy of Śrī Gaura? 

Will Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, who established the ideal standard of conduct by widely preaching the wish-fulfilling jewel of the Holy Name, always remain awake in the temple of my memory? 

Will Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, who mercifully revealed to the living entities the glories of the Holy Name free from offenses, remain seated in my memory? 

Will Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, the associate of Gaura who revealed the Lord’s hidden and manifest abodes, as well as the difference between truth and untruth, and true joy and false theater, always be the object of my remembrance? 

Will Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, who like King Bhagīratha removed all obstacles and delivered the whole world by bringing down the current of the Ganges of devotion, be the object of my eternal meditation? 

Will Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, who preached the message of Lord Caitanya throughout the world, glorified the greatness of the Guru and Vaiṣṇavas, and is the ideal of chanting the Holy Name, always remain in my heart? 

Will Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, whose teachings established the ultimate goal (Prayojana), the process (Abhidheya), and the conclusion of devotion, and who is intimately connected with Śrīla Gaurakiśora dāsa Bābājī, remain within my heart? 

Will Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, who bestowed the mercy of Lord Caitanya by publishing books such as “Śrī Śikṣāmṛta”, “Sajjana-toṣaṇī”, “Harināma-cintāmaṇi”, and “Jaiva-dharma”, be held in my heart? 

On the new moon day of Āṣāḍha, he who was non-different from Śrī Gadādhara Paṇḍita, the energy of Lord Gaura, left his earthly pastimes. Will Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura not again become visible to us?

IDX.en_translation:
Lord, there is now nothing left that may be called mine, Thou alone art my father, friends, brother. 

Friends, wife, sons, daughters are now Thy servants: My efforts for them are on Thy account. 

Wealth, followers, house, way, — in as much as they belong to Thee, — I maintain, myself being a mere servant. 

For Thy service I earn riches, And bear the expenses of Thy household. 

I know neither evil nor good, I only serve, A watchman set to guard the properties of Thy household. 

My senses I exercise according to Thy direction And desire to hear, see, smell and taste. 

Nothing I do for my own pleasure, “Thy pleasure is the essence,” says Bhakti-vinode.

matta ha’ye kṛṣṇa-guṇa gā’ba vṛndāvane 

karmī, jñānī, kṛṣṇadveṣī bahirmukha-jana 
ghṛṇā kari’ akiñcane karibe varjana 

karmajaḍa-smārtagaṇa karibe siddhānta 
ācāra-rahita ei nitānta aśānta 

vātula baliyā more paṇḍitābhimānī 
tyajibe āmāra saṅga māyāvādī jñānī 

kusaṅga-rahita dekhi’ vaiṣṇava-sujana

When will such good fortune be mine? When will the Vaiṣṇavas consider me their own? 

By serving the honey-sweet nectar of śrī-guru’s feet, Becoming absorbed, I will sing the glories of Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana. 

The those engaged in fruitive activities, those engaged in speculative knowledge, those envious of Kṛṣṇa, and those averse to Kṛṣṇa consciousness Will scornfully reject this one who considers himself to possess nothing. 

The smārta-brāhmaṇas rigid in fruitive rituals will declare, “This person is devoid of proper conduct and utterly restless.” 

Considering me a madman, those proud of their scholarship, The impersonalists philosophers will abandon my company. 

Seeing me devoid of bad company, the good devotees Will mercifully embrace me. 

When will this wicked and insignificant wretch, by touching a body of a Vaiṣṇava, Joyfully attain spiritual transformations?

dayāhīna svārthaparapara-sukhe duḥkhī, sadā mithyābhāṣī, 
paraduḥkha sukhakara 

aśeṣa kāmanā, hṛdi mājhe mora, 
krodhī dambhaparāyaṇamadamatta sadā, viṣaye mohita, 
hiṁsā-garva-vibhūṣaṇa 

nidrālasya-hata, sukārye virata,

IDX.en_translation:
My life Is ever given to sin, In it there is not a particle of good; Torment to others Much have I caused; I have pained all jivas. 

For my own pleasure I was never afraid of sinning, Selfish and devoid of pity as I am. Dejected by happiness of others, Always untruthful, The misery of others has been my delight. 

Endless are the selfish desires That fill my breast; To anger and insolence I am so prone, Ever drunk with vanity, Bewitched by worldliness, I wear malice and pride as cherished ornaments. 

Ruined by sleep and idleness, Abstaining from all good works, I am ever most zealous in evil deeds. For the sake of worldly fame An adept in the practice of duplicity, A covetous victim of greed am I. 

Even such a sinner, Shunned by all the good, And a constant offender, I am. Void of all good work, Always evilly disposed And poisoned with various misery. 

Now in old age, Bereft of all help, Humbled and hoping naught, Bhaktivinode At the feet of the Lord Tells his grief.

kuladevī yoga-māyā more kṛpā kari’ 
āvaraṇa sambaribe kabe viśvodarī 

śunechi āgame-vede mahimā tomāra 
śrī kṛṣṇa-vimukhe bāṅdhi’ karāo saṁsāra 

śrī kṛṣṇa-sāmmukhya jā’ra bhāgyakrame haya 
tā’re mukti diyā kara’ aśoka-abhaya 

e dāse janani! kari’ akaitava dayā 
vṛndāvane deha sthāna tumi yoga-māyā 

tomāre laṅghiyā kothā jīve kṛṣṇa pāya 
kṛṣṇa rāsa prakaṭila tomāra kṛpāya 

tumi kṛṣṇa-anucarī jagata-jananī 
tumi dekhāile more kṛṣṇa-cintāmaṇi 

niṣkapaṭa ha’ye mātā cāo mora pāne 
vaiṣṇave viśvāsa vṛddhi ha’ka pratikṣaṇe

There is no one as lowly as I in this world. I have become restless, fallen into the ocean of material existence. 

O Yogamāyā! When will you be merciful to me and remove this covering, O goddess who holds the universe in her womb? 

I have heard Your glories in the scriptures: You bind those who are averse to Śrī Kṛṣṇa and make them wander in material existence. 

But whoever by good fortune becomes favorable to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, You grant them liberation and make them fearless and free from sorrow. 

O mother! Be causelessly merciful to this servant; O Yogamāyā, grant me a place in Vṛndāvana. 

How can a soul attain Kṛṣṇa by bypassing You? Kṛṣṇa’s rāsa dance manifested by Your mercy. 

You are Kṛṣṇa’s companion and the mother of the universe. You showed me the touchstone of Kṛṣṇa. 

O mother, look upon me with a guileless heart; may my faith in the devotees increase moment by moment. 

Without the feet of the devotees, Bhaktivinoda can never cross this ocean of material existence.

I am extremely fallen and wicked. What have I done? As a servant of material nature, I have wasted my invaluable life. 

I spent many days with ease in the womb, and my childhood passed in childish play. This youth I uselessly wasted in mundane activities, and now old age has finally arrived. 

There is no happiness in sense objects; the power to enjoy has turned away, my teeth are gone, and my body is weak. Life is full of torment, and I am always afraid of death; tell me, what should I be attached to now? 

I was attached to objects of enjoyment and the power to enjoy them as long as there was strength in my body. Now all that is gone. Tell me, what do I have left? My mind is always restless. 

While my body still had strength, alas, I did not worship Hari. What can I do now as death approaches? Shame on this life of mine! I did not attain the eternal wealth; leaving my true friend, I worshiped the enemy.

kabe uddhāribe more śrī-caraṇa diyā

I am indeed a very wicked person, always acting badly. In millions of births, I have no deliverance. 

Who in this world is so merciful? Who will deliver such a sinner and take him near? 

I have heard that Śrī Caitanya is the deliverer of the fallen. He has liberated infinite sinners. 

Spreading such an ocean of compassion, when will You deliver me by bestowing Your holy feet? 

This time Your mercy will be understood, if You deliver this sinful person. 

I have no karma, no knowledge, no devotion to Kṛṣṇa. Then tell me, how can I obtain those holy feet? 

My only hope is Your mercy. That causeless mercy is the conclusion of the Vedas. 

You are the abode of purity, and I am evil-minded. How will I find shelter at Your feet? 

Weeping and weeping, this fallen wretch says: Your name “Patita-pāvana” (Deliverer of the Fallen) is famous.

I, indeed, am a denizen of the grove called the pleasaunce of the joy of my own self, A hand-maid tending the feet of Radhika and Madhaba. 

I rejoice at the union of the Divine Pair, And die by grief at separation that parts them. 

I never cast my glance on the place of pastime of the maidens who are their confidential associates; I am reminded of Shaibya whenever I behold the site. 

My heart is smitten with grief as I see those Who are the confidantes of Chandra opposed to Radhika. 

She wants to take away Hari of Radha, Causing the grove of Radhika to be overcast with the darkness of gloom! 

I never see the faces of those Who are opposed to the joy of the union of Sri Radha Govinda. 

Never do I find any pleasure In greeting those who are opposed to Radha. 

(Bhaktivinoda, at the feet of Sri Radha, Hath surrendered his very life-breath with the utmost care.)

All your sins and miseries will go far away, your life will become full of essence, no more fear will remain, and you will drown in an ocean of happiness. 

I am poor and without wealth; I have brought this Name by incurring a debt. Seeing me very lowly, please give the price of faith. 

Taking the price from you, I will give it to the Mahājana, O brother. Whatever profit I get from it, I will keep in my own treasury. 

Staying in Nadīyā-Godrūma, Cānda Bāula is calling out: “Without the Holy Name, everything else is a deception; this material world is just a play of shadows.”

kanaka-ketakī rāi, śyāma marakata tāya,

May I not engage in other talk or other pain, but remain in the remembrance of Your lotus feet. Constantly and without break, may I sing Your qualities in the assembly of devotees. 

I will not perform other vows or other charities, nor will I seek knowledge of other things. I will not engage in other services or worship other deities. Calling out “O Kṛṣṇa!”, I will wander joyfully, and may no second thought arise in my mind. 

In life and death, my only goal is Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, the Lords of my life. I find joy in the sweet mellows of Their love. Those who worship the Divine Couple float in the bliss of divine love. May this truth always remain in my heart. 

Please grant me this wealth: service to the lotus feet of the Divine Couple and love for Them in my mind. May the love for the pastimes of the youthful Divine Couple—whose qualities make Them the kings who captivate even the god of love and his consort—remain in my mind. 

Holding a straw between my teeth, I cry out “O Youthful Couple!” and offer my plea at Their lotus feet. Śyāma, the son of the King of Vraja, and the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu, whose enchanting name is Śrī Rādhikā. 

Rādhā is like a golden flower, and Śyāma is like an emerald beside her. They crush the pride of the god of love. Kṛṣṇa is the crown jewel of dancers, and Rādhā is the peak of female dancers. Both Their minds are captivated by each other’s qualities. 

Their beautiful faces, with golden and dark-blue complexions, are adorned with emotional expressions, adding to Their splendor. Wearing blue and yellow garments, the fair and dark pair are enchanting, both alluring with inner loving sentiments.

sārthaka bhajanapatha, sādhusaṅga avirata, 
smaraṇe bhajana kṛṣṇakathā 
premabhakti haya jadi, tabe haya manaḥ śuddhi, 
tabe jāya hṛdayera vyathā 

viṣaya vipatti jāna, saṁsāra svapana māna, 
naratanu bhajanera mūla 
anurāge bhaja sadā, premabhāve līlākathā, 
āra jata hṛdayera śūla
IDX.en_translation:
I will not listen to or speak of anything else; everything I say will be about the ultimate truth. I will always pray and long for my desired spiritual goals; without this, everything else is meaningless. 

How much can I speak of the Supreme Lord’s truth? Who can know the endless and boundless? The love of Vraja is eternal; this is the ultimate truth. Worship with deep affection in your heart. 

Govinda is the moon of Gokula and the root of supreme bliss, accompanied by His family of gopas and gopīs. Nandīśvara is His dwelling place, and Giridhārī is His name. Worship Him joyfully with the companions. 

This is the truth of loving devotion, O brother! Abandon all other evil desires. By the grace of the spiritual master, we attain this worship, with loving devotion as our constant companion. 

The successful path of worship is constant association with the saintly and the remembrance of topics about Kṛṣṇa. If there is loving devotion, then there is purity of mind, and the heart’s distress vanishes. 

Know that material enjoyment is a calamity; consider the material world a dream. The human body is the root of worship. Always worship with deep affection, chanting the pastimes with loving sentiment, and all the thorns of the heart will be removed.

IDX.en_translation:
Fallen by the results of beginningless karma into the waters of the ocean of material existence, I see no way to cross. By this poison of sense gratification, my heart burns day and night, and my mind never finds happiness. 

Hundreds of ropes of desire give constant distress; the waves of material tendencies play there. The six enemies beginning with lust and anger, like highway robbers, instill fear. My time has come to an end. 

The two cheats, dry knowledge and fruitive action, having deceived me, finally throw me into the ocean. At such a time, O friend, You, Kṛṣṇa, are the ocean of mercy; kindly lift me up by Your strength. 

Holding this fallen servant, make him the dust of Your lotus feet. Give Bhaktivinoda shelter. I am Your eternal servant, but having forgotten the noose of illusion, I remain bound, O merciful Lord.

Lord Nitāi is the root of all joy. With reddish eyes and a merciful demeanor, He constantly sheds tears while chanting the name of Hari. 

In a playful mood and in the company of devotees, He manifests various waves of mellows; with a gentle smile and sweet words, He constantly sways His neck. 

Embracing the fallen and chanting the name of Gaura, He is full of joy day and night. With great care He bestows the jewel of divine love upon the people of the world. 

In the midst of congregational chanting He is the king of relishes, shining like a golden mountain. Expanding the mellows of His pastimes in Vraja, He sings sweet songs. 

Covered in dust upon the earth, He sometimes rolls about, overwhelmed with love. Sometimes He walks, sometimes He plays, and sometimes He laughs loudly. 

Sometimes He perspires, sometimes He laments, sometimes He thrills with ecstasy, and sometimes His voice falters. Sometimes He jumps and leaps, and sometimes He sighs deeply. 

He is an ocean of mercy and a friend to all—the full moon dispelling the darkness of this age. Opening the coverings of the eyes of the world, Nitāi fulfills all desires. 

The blind, the fallen, the poor, and the wicked—all are liberated by His gift of divine love. The whole world received it, but only this Rādhāvallabha dāsa has been deprived.

śyāmaṁ hiraṇya-paridhiṁ vanamālya-varha-

We meditate on Dāmodara, whose body’s dark luster completely dims the blue lotus; who by the splendor of His silken garment puts to shame the brilliance of saffron; who sports in Vṛndāvana; who is delightful with shining ropes around His belly; and whose radiant arm is placed on Rādhā’s shoulder. 

I worship Govinda, whose splendor is like a blooming blue lotus, whose face is like the moon, who loves a peacock feather ornament; who bears the Śrīvatsa mark, wears the large Kaustubha jewel, is dressed in yellow garments, and is beautiful. His body is worshiped by the lotus-like eyes of the gopīs, and He is surrounded by cows and cowherds. He is dedicated to playing the sweet flute and has divine bodily ornaments. 

A musk tilaka on His forehead, a Kaustubha on His chest; a fine pearl on the tip of His nose, a flute in His palm, and a bracelet on His wrist. Hari-candana gracefully applied all over His body, and a pearl necklace around His neck. Surrounded by the gopīs, the crest-jewel of cowherds is victorious. 

He entered Vṛndāvana, which is charming with His own footprints, His glories being sung by the cowherd boys. He wore a peacock feather on His head, His body like that of a fine dancer, with karṇikāra flowers in His ears. He wore garments of golden-tawny color and a Vaijayantī garland, filling the holes of His flute with the nectar of His lips. 

I remember Kṛṣṇa, who is dark-complexioned, wearing golden garments, a forest garland, and peacock feathers. Dressed like a dancer with mineral colors and new leaves, with one hand placed on the shoulder of His friend. With the other, He twirls a lotus. His lotus-like face is smiling, with lotus-like ears, locks of hair, and cheeks. 

I praise You, O adorable One, whose body is like a cloud, dressed in garments like lightning. Whose face shines with an ornament of guñjā and a peacock feather. Adorned with a forest garland, carrying a morsel of food, a stick, a horn, and a flute. Whose beauty is characterized by these emblems, with soft feet, the son of the cowherd. 

Yet, O Lord, only one who is graced by a trace of the mercy of Your two lotus feet truly knows the truth of Your greatness, O Lord, and no one else, even by long deliberation alone. 

Therefore, O Lord, may that great fortune be mine, in this birth, or in any other birth, even as an animal; by which I, becoming even one of Your devotees, may serve Your lotus feet. 

Oh, you are indeed most fortunate among human beings in this world! The sages approach you, purifying the world; in whose homes resides directly the hidden Supreme Brahman in human form. 

O Śyāmasundara! O Peacock-feathered One! O One with a smiling face! O Enchanter with the flute! O Connoisseur of Rādhikā! O Ocean of Mercy! Please make me a maidservant of the feet of Your beloved. 

Oh, the great fortune, the great fortune of the residents of Nanda’s Vraja! Whose friend is the Supreme Bliss, the complete Brahman, the Eternal. 

What pious deeds did Nanda perform, O brāhmaṇa, to attain such exceedingly great prosperity? And the greatly fortunate Yaśodā, from whose breast Hari drank milk.

The unparalleled sweetness of the pair, of our Śyāma and Śyāmā! Their eyes are full of divine nectar and delight. 

Their charming and graceful demeanor is beautiful, and Their words are sweet. The sway of Their necks captivates the mind. With crowns and moon-crests upon Their foreheads, and the redness of betel nuts upon Their lips—oh, how beautiful is this sight of our Śyāma and Śyāmā! 

When They roam together in the groves of Śrī Vṛndāvana, Their beauty cannot be fully described. 

I have no desire for wealth, nor do I wish for liberation. O friend! Just grant us the sight of Śyāmā; may we receive the mercy of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa.

Giving up other desires, abandoning jñāna and karma, I will perform worship with body and mind. Service to Kṛṣṇa in the association of sādhus—I will not worship demigods and goddesses; this bhakti is the supreme cause. 

Whatever path the Mahājanas have followed, I will be devoted to that, judging what is prior and posterior. Sādhana, smaraṇa, līlā—do not neglect this; make it the essence with body and mind. 

Always reject bad association, give up other songs and attachment; keep karmīs and jñānīs far away. Only the association of devotees, the loving mellows of topics of love, the topics of pastimes in the abode of Vraja-rasa. 

Yogīs, renunciants, karmīs, jñānīs, worshipers of other gods, meditators—abandoning them far away in this world. Karma, dharma, sorrow, lamentation—whatever other connection exists, leave it and worship the Holder of Govardhana. 

The labor of pilgrimage is only the confusion of the mind; all perfection is the feet of Govinda. Holding firm faith in the heart, giving up pride and envy, always perform exclusive worship. 

Associating with Kṛṣṇa’s devotees, seeing the bodies of Kṛṣṇa’s devotees, hearing and chanting with faith. Worship, prayer, meditation—the nine-fold bhakti of the Mahājanas; this bhakti is the supreme cause. 

Service to Govinda with the senses—I will not worship demigods and goddesses; this indeed is the topic of exclusive devotion. And all other reproaches, specifically all are arrogance; seeing them, pain arises in the mind. 

Enemies reside in the body; all the senses—no one is obedient to anyone. If it hears, the ear does not hear; if it knows, the life does not know; it cannot be made firm, certainly. 

Lust, anger, greed, illusion, pride, envy, along with arrogance—I will engage them in their respective places. Making the heart joyful, defeating the enemies, I will worship Govinda easily. 

“Lust” in offering work to Kṛṣṇa; “anger” towards those who hate devotees; “greed” for topics of Hari in the association of sādhus. “Illusion” without the attainment of the Ishta; “pride” in singing Kṛṣṇa’s qualities—I will engage them here and there. 

Otherwise, independent lust, which is the abode of anarthas, always causes a break in the path of devotion. What can lust or anger do to the practitioner if there is the association of saintly persons? 

Or what does anger not do? Giving up anger day and night—this indeed is the statement regarding greed and illusion. The enemies are always weak; I will make them subordinate to the mind, remembering Kṛṣṇa-candra. 

Everything will flee of its own accord upon hearing the sound of Govinda, like elephants at the roar of a lion. All calamities will go; one will obtain the happiness of great bliss, whose worship is exclusive. 

Do not make bad endeavors for profit, adoration, or prestige; always think of Govinda’s feet. All lamentation will go; one will obtain the happiness of supreme bliss; loving devotion is the supreme cause. 

Bad association, fault-finding—give up other arrangements; do not have attachment to other gods. In their own respective places, love pulls everyone; a deviation occurs on the path of devotion. 

My own path of worship—I will be devoted to that, singing the pastimes in the place of the Worshipable Deity. This is steadfast worship; I told you, brother. Hanumān is the proof of that. 

As it is said: “Although there is no difference between the Lord of Śrī (Viṣṇu) and the Lord of Jānakī (Rāma) in the Supreme Soul, still, my all-in-all is the lotus-eyed Rāma.” 

The Devaloka, Pitṛloka—they attain great happiness; they say “Sādhu! Sādhu!” at every moment. Those who worship the Couple float in the bliss of love; the three worlds are an offering to them. 

Through the connection of separate endeavor, in the miserable enjoyment of objects—residence in Vraja, service to Govinda. Topics of Kṛṣṇa, Name of Kṛṣṇa—truly, truly the abode of rasa—with the people of Vraja at every moment. 

Always the desire for service, having faith in the mind, always being fearless. Narottama Dāsa says: I have fallen into the error of the wicked; deliver me, O Great Soul!

nāme ruci, jīve dayā, vaiṣṇave ullāsa

O Vaiṣṇava Master! You are a boundless ocean of mercy. Please bestow abundant mercy upon a wretch like me.

Greed for wealth, attraction to the opposite sex, and the desire for fame—please free me from these and purify me; this is my sincere prayer. 

O servant of Lord Kṛṣṇa! Please mercifully bestow upon me a taste for the Holy Name, compassion for all living entities, and joy in the company of the devotees. 

The shade of your lotus feet is my only hope. In life and in death, it is my only reliance.

IDX.en_translation:
Due to the fruits of my offenses, my heart has become hard as a thunderbolt; it feels no transformation from Your Holy Name. Becoming hopeless, O Hari, I loudly utter Your Name and call out again and again in great sorrow. 

O merciful abode of compassion for the fallen, please give me a drop of spiritual emotion and sustain my life. 

When, by uttering Your Name, will incessant tears flow from my eyes? 

When will a choked voice arise in my throat, and half-articulated words come from my mouth? 

When will my body be filled with thrills of ecstasy, and when will perspiration, trembling, and paralysis occur again and again? 

With a discolored body, I will lose consciousness, and by taking complete shelter of the Holy Name, I will sustain my life. 

Will such a day ever come for me? Bewildered, Bhaktivinoda cries.

O brother! In the company of an unholy person, the Holy Name of Kṛṣṇa does not appear. The syllables of the Name may certainly be uttered, but it is never truly the Holy Name. 

Sometimes there is a shadow of the Name, but there is constantly offense to the Name. Brother, know all of this to be an obstacle to devotion to Lord Kṛṣṇa. 

If you wish to chant the Holy Name of Kṛṣṇa, then keep the company of the saintly. Cast far away all desires for material enjoyment, liberation, and mystic perfections. 

Abandon the ten offenses and all concern for honor or dishonor. Enjoy sense objects without attachment and chant the Holy Name of Kṛṣṇa. 

Accept everything that is favorable for devotion to Lord Kṛṣṇa, and reject everything that is unfavorable. 

Give up the endeavor for speculative knowledge and mystic yoga, as well as attachment to fruitive work. Abandon “monkey-like” renunciation, which is merely a bodily show. 

Always know that Lord Kṛṣṇa maintains and protects you. Remove all your troubles through self-surrender and humility. 

Knowing that it is very difficult for the living entity to find a saintly person, Lord Kṛṣṇa came to Nadīyā in the form of a saintly devotee. 

O intelligent one! Take shelter of the lotus feet of Lord Gaura. Who else is a saintly Master besides Him?

IDX.first_line: āsala kathā balte ki tomāra kenthādharā
IDX.search: asala katha balte ki tomara kenthadhara kapni anta saba phanki dharmapatni tyaji ghare paranari sanga kare arthalobhe dvare dvare phire rakhle ki baki
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
āsala kathā balte ki 
tomāra kenthādharā, 
kapni’ āṅṭā-saba phāṅki 

dharmapatnī tyaji’ ghare, 
paranārī-saṅga kare, 
arthalobhe dvāre dvāre 
phire’, rākhle ki bākī 

tumi guru balcho baṭe, 
sādhuguru niṣkapaṭe, 
kṛṣṇa-nāma dena karṇapuṭe, 
se ki emana haya meki 

jebā anya śikṣā deya, 
tā’ke ki ‘guru’ balte haya? 
dudhera phala ta’ ghole naya, 
bheve’ cinte dekha dekhi 

śama-dama-titikṣā-bale, 
uparati, śraddhā ha’le, 
tabe bheka, cāṅda-bāula bale, 
eṁcaḍe peke’ ha’be ki
IDX.en_translation:
To tell the real truth, your wearing of a patched quilt and a loincloth is all a pretense. 

Abandoning your lawful wife at home, associating with other women, and wandering from door to door out of greed—what else of your hypocrisy is left? 

You call yourself a spiritual teacher, but a true saintly teacher without deceit gives the Holy Name in the ear; how can such a one be false? 

Should one who gives other teachings even be called a guru? The result of milk is not buttermilk; just think and see. 

When detachment and faith arise through the power of self-control and tolerance, only then should one adopt the external dress of a renunciant. Bāul Cānd says: will a jackfruit be any good if it is forced to ripen prematurely?

IDX.first_line: āśraya kariyā vando śrī guru caraṇa
IDX.search: asraya kariya vando sri guru carana jaha haite mile bhai krsna premadhana jivera nistara lagi nanda suta hari bhuvane prakasa pana guru rupa dhari
IDX.author: sanātana dāsa
IDX.verses: āśraya kariyā vando śrī-guru-caraṇa jāhā haite mile bhāi kṛṣṇa-premadhana jīvera nistāra lāgi’ nanda-suta hari bhuvane prakāśa pāna guru-rūpa dhari’ mahimāya ‘guru’ ‘kṛṣṇa’ eka kari’ jāna guru-ājñā hṛde saba satya kari’ māna satyajñāne guruvākye jāhāra viśvāsa avaśya tāhāra haya vraja-bhūme vāsa jāra prati gurudeva hana parasanna kona vighne sei nāhi haya avasanna kṛṣṇa ruṣṭa ha’le guru rākhi-bāre pāre guru ruṣṭa ha’le kṛṣṇa rākhi-bāre nāre guru-mātā, guru-pitā, guru ha’na pati guru vinā e saṁsāre nāhi āra gati guruke ‘manuṣya’-jñāna nā kara kakhana guru-nindā kabhu karṇe nā kara śravaṇa guru-nindukera mukha kabhu nā heribe jathā haya guru-nindā, tathā nā jāibe gurura vikriyā jadi dekhaha kakhana tathāpi avajñā nāhi kara kadācana gurupāda-padme rahe jāra niṣṭhā-bhakti jamat tārite sei dhare mahā-śakti hena gurupāda-padma karaha vandanā jāhā haite ghuce bhāi sakala jantraṇā gurupāda-padma nitya je kare vandana śire dhari’ vandi āmi tāṅhāra caraṇa śrī-guru-caraṇapadma hṛde kari’ āśa śrī-guru-vandanā kare sanātana dāsa
IDX.en_translation:
Taking shelter, I worship the feet of the spiritual master, from whom, O brother, one obtains the treasure of divine love for Kṛṣṇa. 

For the deliverance of the souls, Kṛṣṇa—the son of Nanda—appears in the world assuming the form of the spiritual master. 

Know that in greatness, the spiritual master and Kṛṣṇa are one. Accept all of the master’s commands in your heart as truth. 

One who has faith in the spiritual master’s instructions with true understanding will surely reside in the sacred land of Vraja. 

One with whom the spiritual master is pleased is never disheartened by any obstacles. 

If Kṛṣṇa becomes angry, the spiritual master can protect you. If the spiritual master becomes angry, Kṛṣṇa cannot protect you. 

The spiritual master is mother, father, and protector. Without him, there is no other refuge in this material world. 

Never consider the spiritual master as an ordinary man. Never listen to blasphemy against him. 

Never look at the face of one who blasphemes the spiritual master. Do not go where such blasphemy takes place. 

If you ever see any peculiar behavior in the spiritual master, never disrespect him. 

One whose steadfast devotion remains at the lotus feet of the spiritual master possesses great power to deliver the world. 

Therefore, worship those lotus feet from which all sufferings cease. 

I reverently hold on my head the feet of him who constantly worships the lotus feet of his spiritual master. 

Cherishing those lotus feet in his heart, Sanātana dāsa offers his prayers.

IDX.search: atmanivedana tuya pade kari hoinu parama sukhiduhkha dure gela cinta na rahila caudike ananda dekhi asoka abhaya amrta adhara tomara caranadvayatahate ekhana visrama labhiya chadinu bhavera bhaya
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
ātmanivedana, tuyā pade kari’, 
hoinu parama sukhīduḥkha dūre gela, cintā nā rahila, 
caudike ānanda dekhi 

aśoka-abhaya, amṛta-ādhāra, 
tomāra caraṇadvayatāhāte ekhana, viśrāma labhiyā, 
chāḍinu bhavera bhaya 

tomāra saṁsāre, kariba sevana, 
nahiba phalera bhāgītava sukha jāhe, kariba jatana, 
ha’ye pade anurāgī 

tomāra sevāya, duḥkha haya jata, 
seo ta’ parama sukhasevā-sukha-duḥkha, parama-sampad, 
nāśaye avidyā-duḥkha 

pūrva-itihāsa, bhulinu sakala, 
sevā-sukha pe’ye maneāmi ta’ tomāra, tumi ta’ āmāra, 
ki kāja apara dhane 

bhakativinoda, ānande ḍubiyā, 
tomāra sevāra taresaba ceṣṭā kare, tava icchā-mata, 
thākiyā tomāra ghare
IDX.translation_intro: From The Harmonist, April 1928. Edited by Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī.
IDX.en_translation:
Having surrendered Myself at Thy feet I feel supremely happy. Sorrow has departed, There are no cares, I find joy on all sides. 

Free from all sorrows and fears, Ever the seat of un-alloyed bliss, Are those twin feet of Thine. In them even now Resting in repose I give up all worldly fear. 

Thy household I shall serve I shall not enjoy the fruit For what-so-ever pleases Thee I shall endeavour Being enamoured of Thy feet. 

In Thy service The sorrows that befall Verily are the highest bliss. The sorrows and joys of Thy service Are the best of estates, They destroy the misery of ignorance. 

My past history I have completely forgot In my mind experiencing the joy of Thy service. I am, indeed, Thine Thou art truly my own, What other treasure I need? 

Bhaktivinode, Unto Thy service Immersed in joy, Devotes all his efforts, In pursuance of Thy will, Living in Thy house.

IDX.search: avatara sara gora avatara kena na bhajili tanre kari nire vasa gela na piyasa apana karama phere kantakera taru sadai sevili man amrta paibara ase prema kalpataru sri gauranga amar tanhare bhavili vise
IDX.author: locana-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
avatāra sāra, gorā-avatāra, 
kena nā bhajili tāṅre 
kari’ nīre vāsa, gela nā piyāsa, 
āpana karama phere 

kaṇṭakera taru, sadāi sevili (man), 
amṛta pāibāra āśe 
prema-kalpataru, śrī-gaurāṅga āmār, 
tāṅhāre bhāvili viṣe 

saurabhera āśe, palāśa śūkili (man), 
nāśāte paśila kīṭa 
ikṣudaṇḍa bhāvi’, kāṭha cuṣili (man), 
kemane pāibi miṭha 

hāra baliyā, galāya parili (man), 
śamana-kiṅkara sāpa 
śītala baliyā, āguna pohāli (man), 
pāili bajara tāpa 

saṁsāra bhajili, śrī-gaurāṅga bhulili, 
nā śunili sādhur kathā 
iha-parakāla, du’kāla khowāli (man), 
khāili āpana māthā
IDX.en_translation:
The best of all incarnations is the incarnation of Gaura. Why did you not worship Him? Like one who lives in water but still remains thirsty, you are caught in the cycle of your own actions. 

O mind, you always served a thorny tree in the hope of finding nectar. My Śrī Gaurāṅga is the wish-fulfilling tree of divine love, but you considered Him to be poison. 

O mind, in the hope of fragrance you sniffed a palāśa flower, and an insect entered your nose. Thinking it to be a sugarcane stalk, you sucked on wood; how will you find sweetness in that? 

O mind, thinking it to be a necklace, you put the snake of the lord of death around your neck. Thinking it would be cool, you warmed yourself by the fire and received the searing heat of a thunderbolt. 

You worshiped the material world, forgot Śrī Gaurāṅga, and did not listen to the words of the saintly. O mind, you lost both this world and the next and thus ruined yourself.

IDX.first_line: avirata rati bandhu smeratā bandhura śrīḥ
IDX.search: avirata rati bandhu smerata bandhura srih kavalita iva radhapanga bhangi tarangaih mudita vadana candras candrakapida dhari mudiba madhura kantir bhati kunje vihari tata susira ghananam nadam anaddha bhajam janayati taruninam mandale manditanam tata bhuvi nataraja kridaya bhanu putrya vidadhad atula carir bhati kunje vihari
IDX.author: rūpa gosvāmī
IDX.verses:
avirata-rati-bandhu-smeratā-bandhura-śrīḥ 
kavalita iva rādhāpāṅga-bhaṅgī-taraṅgaiḥ 
mudita-vadana-candraś candrakāpīḍa-dhārī 
mudiba-madhura-kāntir bhāti kuñje vihārī 

tata-suṣira-ghanānāṁ nādam ānaddha-bhājāṁ 
janayati taruṇīnāṁ maṇḍale maṇḍitānām 
taṭa-bhuvi naṭarāja-krīḍayā bhānu-putryā 
vidadhad-atula-cārīr bhāti kuñje vihārī 

śikhini kalita-ṣaḍje kokile pañcamāḍhye 
svayam api nava-vaṁśyoddāmayan grāma-mukhyam 
dhṛta-mṛga-mada-gandhaḥ suṣṭhu gāndhāra-saṁjñaṁ 
tribhuvana-dhṛti-hārīr bhāti kuñje vihārī 

anupama-kara-śākhopātta-rādhāṅgulīko 
laghu laghu kusumānāṁ paryaṭan vāṭikāyām 
sarabhasam anugītaś citra-kaṇṭhībhir uccair 
vraja-nava-yuvatībhir bhāti kuñje vihārī 

ahiripu-kṛta-lāsye kīcakārabdha-vādye 
vraja-giri-taṭa-raṅge bhṛṅga-saṅgīta-bhāji 
viracita-paricaryāś citra-tauryatrikeṇa 
stimita-karaṇa-vṛttir bhāti kuñje vihārī 

diśi diśi śuka-śārī-maṇḍalair gūḍha-līlāḥ 
prakaṭam anupaṭhadbhir nirmitāś carya-pūraḥ 
tad atirahasi vṛttaṁ preyasī-karṇa-mūle 
smita-mukham abhijalpan bhāti kuñje vihārī 

tava cikura-kadambaṁ stambhate prekṣya kekī 
nayana-kamala-lakṣmīr vandate kṛṣṇa-sāraḥ 
alir alam alakāntaṁ nauti paśyeti rādhāṁ 
sumadhuram anuśaṁsan bhāti kuñje vihārī 

madana-tarala-bālā-cakravālena viṣvag- 
vividha-vara-kalānāṁ śikṣayā sevyamānaḥ 
skhalita-cikura-veśe skandha-deśe priyāyāḥ 
prathita-pṛthula-bāhur bhāti kuñje vihārī 

idam anupama-līlā-hāri kuñje-vihārī- 
smaraṇa-padam adhīte tuṣṭa-dhīr aṣṭakaṁ jaḥ 
nija-guṇa-vṛtayā śrī-rādhayā rādhitas taṁ 
nayati nija-padābjaṁ kuñja-sadmādhirājaḥ
IDX.en_translation:
He whose beauty is enhanced by a continuous loving smile, as if enveloped by the waves of Rādhā’s sidelong glances; whose moon-like face is joyful while wearing a peacock feather; and whose sweet complexion is like a cloud—that enjoyer shines in the forest grove. 

Performing incomparable dance movements like the king of dancers on the bank of the Yamunā, He creates the sound of stringed, wind, and percussion instruments among the adorned young women in a circle, and thus He shines in the grove. 

With the peacock singing the tonic note and the cuckoo the fifth note, He Himself plays the main rāga on His new flute; bearing the fragrance of musk and stealing the composure of the three worlds, He shines in the grove. 

Whose incomparable hands hold Rādhā’s fingers as He lightly wanders through the flower garden, eagerly followed by the high-pitched, wonderfully voiced young women of Vraja—He shines in the grove. 

Where peacocks perform a delicate dance and flutes begin to play on the stage-like banks of the hills of Vraja, filled with the music of humming bees and receiving service from wonderful musical instruments, His senses are stilled and His activities absorbed as He shines in the grove. 

In every direction, flocks of parrots and mynas openly recount His hidden pastimes, creating a flood of wonder; that very secret event He speaks with a smiling face near His beloved’s ear, and thus He shines in the grove. 

“Seeing your dense hair, the peacock is stunned; the blackbuck bows to the beauty of your lotus-like eyes; and the bee praises your locks, saying “Look, Rādhā!”” Sweetly proclaiming this, He shines in the grove. 

Surrounded by a circle of restless young women intoxicated by love, being served by their skill in various excellent arts—with His broad arms spread on His beloved’s shoulder, He shines in the grove. 

Whoever with a contented mind studies this eight-verse prayer for remembering the incomparable, enchanting pastimes of the Lord who sports in the groves—him, who is worshiped by Śrī Rādhā, the King of the groves leads to His own lotus feet.

IDX.first_line: baḍa kṛpā kaile kṛṣṇa adhamera prati
IDX.search: bada krpa kaile krsna adhamera prati ki lagi anile hetha karo ebe gati ache kichu karya tava ei anumane nahe kena anibena ei ugrasthane
IDX.author: bhaktivedānta swami prabhupāda
IDX.verses:
baḍa-kṛpā kaile kṛṣṇa adhamera prati 
ki lāgi ānile hethā karo ebe gati 

āche kichu kārya tava ei anumāne 
nahe kena ānibena ei ugrasthāne 

rajastamo guṇe erā sabāi ācchanna 
vāsudeva-kathā ruci nahe se prasanna 

tabe jadi tava kṛpā haya ahaitukī 
sakaloi sambhava haya tumi se kautukī 

ki bhāve bujhāle tārā bujhe sei rasa 
eta kṛpā karo prabhu kari’ nija-vaśa 

tomāra icchāya saba haya māyā-vaśa 
tomāra icchāya nāśa māyāra paraśa 

tava icchā haya jadi tādera uddhāra 
bujhibe niścayoi tabe kathā se tomāra 

bhāgavatera kathā se tava avatāra 
dhīra hoiyā śune jadi kāne bāra bāra 

śṛṇvatāṁ svakathāḥ kṛṣṇaḥ 
punyaśravaṇakīrtanaḥ 
hṛdyantaḥstho hyabhadrāṇi 
vidhunoti suhṛtsatām 

naṣṭaprāyeṣvabhadreṣu 
nityaṁ bhāgavatasevayā 
bhagavatyuttamaḥśloke 
bhaktirbhavati naiṣṭhikī 

tadā rajastamobhāvāḥ 
kāma-lobhādayaśca je 
ceta etairanāviddhaṁ 
sthitaṁ sattve prasīdati 

evaṁ prasannamanaso 
bhagavadbhaktiyogataḥ 
bhagavattattvavijñānaṁ 
muktasaṅgasya jāyate 

bhidyate hṛdayagranthiś- 
chidyante sarva-saṁśayāḥ 
kṣīyante cāsya karmāṇi 
dṛṣṭa evātmanīśvare 

rajastamo ha’te tabe pāibe nistāra 
hṛdayera abhadra saba ghucibe tāhāra 

ki ka’re bujhāba kathā vara sei cāhi 
kṣudra āmi dīna hīna kono śakti nāhi 

athaca enecha prabhu kathā balibāre 
je tomāra icchā prabhu karo ei bāre 

akhila jagatguru! vacana se āmāra 
alaṅkṛta karibāra kṣamatā tomāra 

tava kṛpā ha’le mora kathā śuddha habe 
śuniyā sabāra śoka-duḥkha je ghucibe 

āniyācha jadi prabhu āmāre nācāte 
nācāo nācāo prabhu nācāo se-mate 
kāṣṭhera putula jathā nācāo se-mate 

bhakti nāi veda nāi nāme khuba baḍa 
‘bhaktivedānta’ nāma ebe sārthaka kara
IDX.en_translation:
O Lord Kṛṣṇa! You have bestowed great mercy upon this fallen soul. For what purpose have You brought me here? Now, please determine my destination. 

I assume You have some business here; otherwise, why would You bring me to such a terrible place? 

Everyone here is covered by the modes of passion and ignorance. They have no taste for topics concerning Lord Kṛṣṇa, nor are they happy. 

But if Your causeless mercy falls upon them, everything becomes possible, for You are the supreme magician. 

How will I make them understand this mellow of devotion? O Lord, show such mercy and bring them under Your control. 

By Your will, everyone falls under the control of illusion, and by Your will alone, the touch of illusion is destroyed. 

If it is Your will to deliver them, then surely they will understand Your message. 

The message of the Śrīmad Bhāgavatam is Your literal incarnation. 

If they listen to it repeatedly with patience, then Kṛṣṇa, who is the benefactor of the truthful devotee, will dwell within their hearts and cleanse them of all inauspicious things. 

By regular service to the Bhāgavatam and the pure devotee, all that is troublesome to the heart is destroyed, and firm devotion to the Supreme Lord is established. 

Then the effects of passion and ignorance, such as lust and greed, disappear from the heart. The mind is no longer pierced by them and becomes situated in pure goodness. 

Thus established in the satisfaction of the mind through devotional service, one realizes the scientific knowledge of God, being freed from all material association. 

The knot in the heart is pierced, and all doubts are cut to pieces. All fruitive actions are exhausted when one sees the Supreme Lord as the Master. 

Then they will find relief from passion and ignorance, and all inauspicious things in their hearts will be removed. 

How will I make them understand this message? I only desire that benediction. I am small, destitute, and fallen; I have no power of my own. 

Yet You have brought me here to speak Your message. Whatever is Your will, O Lord, please do that now. 

O Master of the universe! These words of mine—You have the power to decorate them. If Your mercy is there, my words will be purified. Hearing them, everyone’s grief and misery will disappear. 

Since You have brought me here to dance, O Lord, then make me dance! 

Make me dance as You like, just like a wooden doll in Your hands. 

I have no devotion and no knowledge, but my name is very grand. Now, please make the name “Bhaktivedānta” successful.

IDX.search: bada sukher khabor gai surabhi kunjete namer hata khuleche khoda nitai bada majar katha tay sraddha mulye suddha nama sei hatete vikay
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses: baḍa sukher khabor gāi surabhi-kuñjete nāmer hāṭa khuleche khoda-nitāi baḍa majār kathā tāy śraddhā-mūlye śuddha-nāma sei hāṭete vikāy jata bhakta-vṛnda basi’ adhikārī dekhe’ nāma becche dara kaṣi jadi nāma kinbe bhāi āmār saṅge cala mahā-janer kāche jāi tumi kinbe kṛṣṇa-nām dasturi loiba āmi, pūrṇa ha’be kāma baḍa dayāl nityānanda śraddhā-mātra la’ye dena parama ānanda ek-bāra dekhle cakṣe jal gaura ba’le nitāi dena sakala sambal dena śuddha kṛṣṇa-śikṣā jāti, dhana, vidyā-bala nā kare apekṣā amani chāḍe māyā-jāl gṛhe thāka, vane thāka, nā thāke jañjāl āra nāiko kalir bhay ācaṇḍāle dena nāma nitāi dayā-may bhakativinoda ḍāki’ kay nitāi-cāṅder caraṇ binā ār nāhi āśray
IDX.en_translation:
I sing very happy news: in the fragrant Surabhi grove, Lord Nitāi Himself has opened a marketplace of the Holy Name. 

There is a very interesting thing there: for the price of faith, the pure Name is sold in that market. 

All the devotees sit there and, seeing who is qualified, they sell the Name after settling the price. 

If you want to buy the Name, dear brother, come with me—let’s go to those great souls. 

You will buy the name of Kṛṣṇa; I will take a small commission, and your desire will be fulfilled. 

The very merciful Nityānanda, taking only faith in return, gives supreme bliss. 

If He once sees tears in your eyes as you call out “Gaura!”, Nitāi gives you all his resources. 

He gives the pure teachings of Kṛṣṇa and does not wait for caste, wealth, or the strength of knowledge. 

Immediately the net of illusion is released. Whether you stay at home or in the forest, you will be free from trouble. 

There is no more fear of the Kali age. To everyone, down to the most fallen outcast, the merciful Nitāi gives the Holy Name. 

Bhaktivinoda calls out and says: “Without the feet of Lord Nitāi, there is no other refuge.”

bahujanma-bhāgyavaśe, cinmaya madhura rase, 
spṛhā janme jīvera hiyāya 
sei spṛhā lobha hañā, vraja-dhāme jīve lañā, 
rūpānuga-bhajane mātāya 

bhajana-prakāra jata, sakalera sāra mata, 
śikhāila śrī-rūpa gosāi 
se bhajana nā jāniyā, kṛṣṇa bhajibāre giyā, 
tuccha kāje jīvana kāṭāi 

bujhibāre se bhajana, bahu jatne akiñcana, 
viracila bhajana-darpaṇa 
vraje rādhā-kṛṣṇa-sevā, karite utsuka jebā, 
sukhe teṁha karuna śravaṇa 

lobhete janama pāi, atiśīghra bāḍi jāi, 
śraddhā, rati, tabe haya prīti 
sahaja bhajana rati, nāhi cāya śikṣā mati, 
tabu śikṣā prāthamika rīti 

putra-sneha jananīra, sahaja hṛdaye sthira, 
dūṣita hṛdaye śikṣā cāi 
kṛṣṇaprema seirūpa, nityasiddha aparūpa, 
baddha-jīve aprakaṭa bhāi 

sei ta’ sahaja rati, pāiyāche apagati, 
śikṣānuśīlana jadi pāya 
se rati jāgiyā uṭhe, jīvera bandhana chuṭe, 
vrajānanda tāhāre nācāya
IDX.en_translation:
Due to the good fortune accumulated over many births, a desire awakens in the heart of the soul for the spiritual, sweet taste of devotion. That desire, turning into intense greed, takes the soul to Vraja-dhāma and intoxicates one in devotional service following Śrī Rūpa Gosāñi. 

All types of devotional service, their essence, were taught by Śrī Rūpa Gosāñi. Not knowing that service, when I go to worship Kṛṣṇa, I spend my life in insignificant activities. 

To understand that worship, with great effort, the humble one composed Bhajana-darpaṇa. Whoever is eager to perform the service of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in Vraja, may they happily listen. 

Born from intense greed, I quickly grow. First comes faith, then attachment, and finally pure love develops. Natural attachment to devotional service does not desire education or intellect; still, education is the primary method. 

A mother’s affection for her son is naturally fixed in her heart. In a polluted heart, education is needed. Love for Kṛṣṇa is like that - eternally perfect, unparalleled. In the conditioned soul, it is unmanifest, brother. 

That natural attachment has attained a degraded state. If it receives education and practice, that attachment awakens, the soul’s bondage breaks, and the bliss of Vraja makes one dance.

balabhid-upala-kānti-drohiṇi śrīmad-aṅge 
ghusṛṇa-rasa-vilāsaiḥ suṣṭhu gāndharvikāyāḥ 
sva-madana-nṛpa-śobhāṁ vardhayan deha-rājye 
praṇayatu mama netrābhīṣṭa-pūrtiṁ mukundaḥ 

udita-vidhu-parārdha-jyotir ullaṅghi-vaktro 
nava-taruṇima-rajyad-bālya-śeṣātiramyaḥ 
pariṣadi lalitālīṁ dolayan kuṇḍalābhyāṁ 
praṇayatu mama netrābhīṣṭa-pūrtiṁ mukundaḥ 

kanaka-nivaha-śobhānandi pītaṁ nitambe 
tad-upari navaraktaṁ vastram itthaṁ dadhānaḥ 
priyam iva kila varṇaṁ rāga-yuktaṁ priyāyāḥ 
praṇayatu mama netrābhīṣṭa-pūrtiṁ mukundaḥ 

surabhi-kusuma-vṛndair vāsitāmbhaḥ-samṛddhe 
priya-sarasi nidāghe sāyam ālī-parītām 
madana-janaka-sekaiḥ khelayann eva rādhāṁ 
praṇayatu mama netrābhīṣṭa-pūrtiṁ mukundaḥ 

parimalam iha labdhvā hanta gāndharvikāyāḥ 
pulakita-tanur uccair unmadas tat-kṣaṇena 
nikhila-vipina-deśān vāsitān eva jighran 
praṇayatu mama netrābhīṣṭa-pūrtiṁ mukundaḥ 

praṇihita-bhuja-daṇḍaḥ skandha-deśe varāṅgyāḥ 
smita-vikasita-gaṇḍe kīrtidā-kanyakāyāḥ 
manasija-jani-saukhyaṁ cumbanenaiva tanvan 
praṇayatu mama netrābhīṣṭa-pūrtiṁ mukundaḥ 

pramada-danuja-goṣṭhyāḥ ko’pi saṁvarta-vahnir 
vraja-bhuvi kila pitror mūrtimān sneha-puñjaḥ 
prathama-rasa-mahendraḥ śyāmalo rādhikāyāḥ 
praṇayatu mama netrābhīṣṭa-pūrtiṁ mukundaḥ 

svakadana-kathayāṅgīkṛtya mṛdvīṁ viśākhāṁ 
kṛta-caṭu lalitāṁ tu prārthayan prauḍha-śīlām 
praṇaya-vidhura-rādhā-māna-vidhvaṁsanāya 
praṇayatu mama netrābhīṣṭa-pūrtiṁ mukundaḥ

IDX.en_translation:
May Kṛṣṇa fulfill the desires of my eyes! His glorious body defeats the luster of sapphire and is beautifully adorned with the saffron decorations of Rādhā, thus increasing the splendor of the god of love within the kingdom of His body. 

May Kṛṣṇa fulfill the desires of my eyes! His face surpasses the brilliance of countless rising moons, and He is extremely charming with the last traces of boyhood beautified by fresh youth. In the assembly, He sways Lalitā and her companions with His earrings. 

May Kṛṣṇa fulfill the desires of my eyes! He wears a yellow garment on His hips, delighting in the splendor of gold, and above that He wears a fresh red cloth as if adopting the color of His beloved’s affection. 

May Kṛṣṇa fulfill the desires of my eyes! In His beloved lake—rich with fragrant flower clusters and scented water—He causes Rādhā to play by sprinkling water during the summer evenings while surrounded by His companions. 

May Kṛṣṇa fulfill the desires of my eyes! Having obtained the fragrance of Rādhā, His body bristles with joy; at that moment, He becomes highly ecstatic and smells all the scented regions of the forest. 

May Kṛṣṇa fulfill the desires of my eyes! With His arm placed on the shoulder of the daughter of Kīrtidā—whose cheeks blossom with a smile—He generates the joy of love with a kiss. 

May Kṛṣṇa fulfill the desires of my eyes! He is a fire of universal destruction for the proud assembly of demons, yet in the land of Vraja He is a personified mass of affection for His parents—the great king of transcendental mellows, dark-complexioned, and Rādhā’s own. 

May Kṛṣṇa fulfill the desires of my eyes! Accepting gentle Viśākhā through His own stories and charmingly entreating dignified Lalitā, He acts to soothe Rādhā’s love-sick pride. 

Whoever recites these eight verses of Mukunda with humble prayers, while restraining all senses from material attachments, will be established among His own dearest associates by the young prince of Vraja, who shows Himself along with Rādhā.

IDX.search: bandhila maya jedina hate avidya moha dore aneka janma labhinu ami phirinu maya ghore deva danava manava pasu patanga kita haye svarge narake bhutale phiri anitya asa laye
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses: “bāṅdhila māyā, jedina ha’te, avidyā-moha-ḍore aneka janma, labhinu āmi, phirinu māyā-ghore deva-dānava, mānava-paśu, pataṅga kīṭa ha’ye svarge-narake, bhūtale phiri, anitya āśā la’ye nā jāni kibā, sukṛti-bale, śrīvāsa-suta hainu nadīyā-dhāme, caraṇa tava, daraśa paraśa kainu sakala bāre, maraṇa-kāle, aneka duḥkha pāi tuyā prasaṅge, parama sukhe, ebāra cale’ jāi icchāya tora, janama jadi, ābāra haya, hari caraṇe tava, prema-bhakati, thāke, minati kari” jakhana śiśu, nīraba bhela, dekhiyā prabhura līlā śrīvāsa-goṣṭhī, tyajiyā śoka, ānanda-magana bhelā gaura-carita, amṛta-dhārā, karite karite pāna bhaktivinoda, śrīvāse māge, jāya jena mora prāṇa
IDX.en_translation:
Since the day illusion bound me with the ropes of ignorance and delusion, I have taken many births, wandering in the whirlpool of material existence. 

As a demigod, demon, human, animal, insect, or worm, I have wandered in heaven, hell, and on earth, clinging to impermanent hopes. 

I do not know by what pious credits I became the son of Śrīvāsa. In Nadiyā, I saw and touched Your lotus feet. 

Every time, at the moment of death, I experienced much suffering. Now, in Your company, with supreme happiness, I depart. 

By Your desire, if I take birth again, O Hari, I pray that loving devotion may remain at Your feet. 

When the child became silent, seeing the pastimes of the Lord, Śrīvāsa’s family, abandoning grief, became absorbed in bliss. 

By continuously drinking the nectarean current of Lord Caitanya’s life and pastimes, Bhaktivinoda begs Śrīvāsa that his life may pass in this way.

IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses: bandhu-gaṇa! śunaha vacana mora bhāvete vibhora, thākiye jakhana, dekhā deya cita-cora vicakṣaṇa kari’, dekhite cāhile, haya āṅkhi agocara punaḥ nāhi dekhi’, kāṅdaye parāṇa, duḥkhera nāhi thāke ora jagatera bandhu sei kabhu more laya sātha jathā tathā rākhu more, āmāra se prāṇa-nātha darśana-ānanda-dāne, sukha deya mora prāṇe, bale more praṇaya-vacana punaḥ adarśana diyā, dagdha kare mora hiyā, prāṇe more māre prāṇadhana jāhe tāra sukha haya, sei sukha mama nija sukhe duḥkhe mora sarvadāi sama bhakativinoda, saṁyoge-viyoge, tāhe jāne prāṇeśvara tāṅ’ra sukhe sukhī, sei prāṇa-nātha, se kabhu nā haya para
IDX.en_translation:
Friends, listen to my words! When I am immersed in spiritual emotion, the thief of my heart appears. 

When I try to see Him carefully, He becomes invisible to my eyes. Not seeing Him again, my heart cries; there is no end to my sorrow. 

He is the friend of the world. Sometimes He takes me along with Him. Wherever He may keep me, He is the Lord of my life. 

By granting the joy of His sight, He gives happiness to my soul and speaks words of love to me. Again, by disappearing, He burns my heart; the treasure of my life thus kills me. 

Whatever gives Him happiness, that happiness is mine. In my own happiness and sorrow, I remain always the same. 

Bhaktivinoda knows Him as the Lord of his life in both union and separation. Happy in His happiness, that Lord is never a stranger.

IDX.search: bandhu he nayane lukaye thoba prema cintamani rasete ganthiya hrdaye tuliya laba sisukala haite ana nahi cite o pada karechi sara dhana jana mana jivana jauvana tumi se galara hara
IDX.author: caṇḍīdāsa
IDX.verses:
bandhu he nayane lukāye thoba 
prema cintāmaṇi, rasete gaṅthiyā, 
hṛdaye tuliyā la’ba 

śiśukāla haite, āna nāhi cite, 
o pada karechi sāra 
dhana jana mana, jīvana jauvana, 
tumi se galāra hāra 

śayane svapane, nidrā jāgaraṇe, 
kabhu nā pāśari tomā 
abalāra truṭi, haya śatakoṭi, 
sakali karibā kṣamā 

nā ṭhelio bale, abalā akhale, 
je haya ucita tora 
bhāviyā dekhilāma, tomā baṁdhū vine, 
āra keha nāhi mora 

tile aṅkhi āḍa, karite nā pāri, 
tā’hale je mari āmi 
caṇḍīdāse kahe, anugata jane, 
dayā nā chāḍio tumi
IDX.en_translation:
O Friend! I will keep the touchstone of love hidden in my eyes. Stringing it with mellows, I will lift it into my heart. 

From childhood, I knew no other. I have made Your feet the essence. Wealth, people, mind, life, and youth—You are the necklace around my neck. 

In sleeping or dreaming, in sleep or wakefulness, I never forget You. A helpless woman has millions of faults; You should forgive them all. 

Do not push me away by force; I am a helpless woman, and You are everything to me. I have considered and seen that without You, O Friend, I have no one else. 

I cannot turn my eyes from You for even a moment; if I do, I shall die. Chandidasa says: Do not give up Your mercy towards Your surrendered servant.

mathurāya keśī-tīrtha-ghāṭera sakāśa 

govinda-vigraha dhari’, tathāya āchena hari, 
nayane baṅkima-dṛṣṭi, mukhe manda-hāsa 
kibā tri-bhaṅgama ṭhāma, varṇa samujjvala śyāma, 
nava-kiśalaya śobhā śrī aṅge prakāśa 

adhare vaṁśīṭī tā’ra, anarthera mūlādhāra, 
śikhi-cūḍākeo bhāi karo nā viśvāsa 

se mūrti nayane here, keha nāhi ghare phire, 
saṁsārī gṛhīra je go haya sarva-nāśa 
(tāi mora mane baḍa trāsa) 
ghaṭibe vipada bhārī, jeyo nāko he saṁsāri, 
mathurāya keśī-tīrtha-ghāṭera sakāśa
IDX.en_translation:
If you desire playful jokes and fun with your friends, Then heed my words, do not go, do not go, Near Keśītīrtha-ghāṭa in Mathurā. 

Assuming the form of Govinda, Hari is there, With a captivating glance in His eyes and a gentle smile on His face. What a beautiful three-fold bending posture, His complexion brilliantly dark, The beauty of new sprouts manifests on His divine limbs. 

The flute on His lips is the root cause of all unwanted things, Brother, do not even trust His peacock feather crown. 

Seeing that form with one’s eyes, no one returns home, Indeed, it becomes complete ruin for the worldly householder. 
(Therefore, there is great fear in my heart) 
A great danger will occur, do not go, O worldly person, Near Keśī-tīrtha-ghāṭa in Mathurā.

IDX.en_translation:
Everyone says “Bāul, Bāul”, but who truly is a Bāul? Showing their beards and topknots, O brother, they are deceiving the jīvas.

baḍa deuḍe taḍe, ghaṇṭā ārati helāni 

āsa āsa nārāyaṇa, diyabāre daraśana 
kalira kaḍāra rūpa netra paṭe niśi lāni
IDX.en_translation:
The time has come, O Lord, for You to leave Your jeweled throne. At the summit of Nīlācala, You are seated, waiting on the path. 

The lotus-faced Śrīmati Rādhikā experiences the pain of separation in Her heart. Mother Yaśodā’s eyes are always flowing with tears. 

The end of the Dvāpara-yuga has come, and the Jagamohana hall is established. In the great temple, the ārati is being performed with the sound of bells. 

Come, come O Lord Nārāyaṇa, to give us Your divine sight. The dark shadow of the Age of Kali is falling upon our eyes.

IDX.search: bhai re bhaja goracandera carana e tina bhuvane ara dayara thakura nai gora bada patita pavana hena avatare jara nahila bhakati lesa bala tara ki habe upaya ravira kirane jara ankhi parasanna naila vidhata vancita kaila taya
IDX.author: premānanda-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: bhāi-re! bhaja gorācāṅdera caraṇa e tina bhuvane āra, dayāra ṭhākura nāi, gorā baḍa patita-pāvana hena avatāre jā’ra, nahila bhakati leśa, bala tā’ra ki habe upāya ravira kiraṇe jā’ra, āṅkhi parasanna naila, vidhātā vañcita kaila tāya hena-jalada kāya, prema-dhārā variṣaya, karuṇāmaya avatāra gorā hena prabhu peye, je-jana śītala naila, ki jāni kemana mana tā’ra kali-bhava-sāgare, nija-nāma bhelā kari’, āpane gaurāṅga kare pāra tabe je ḍubiyā mare, ke tā’re uddhāra kare, e premānandera parihāra
IDX.en_translation:
O brothers! Worship the lotus feet of Lord Gorācānd. In these three worlds, there is no other Master as merciful as Him. Lord Gaura is truly the deliverer of the most fallen. 

If one has not even a trace of devotion during such an incarnation, tell me, what will be his destination? One whose eyes do not open to the pleasing rays of the sun has surely been deprived by destiny. 

With a body like a monsoon cloud, He showers divine love—He is the most merciful incarnation. Having received such a Master as Lord Gaura, if a person’s heart does not become pacified, I wonder what kind of mind he possesses. 

In the ocean of material existence in this Age of Kali, Lord Gaurāṅga Himself makes His own Holy Name a raft to help souls cross over. Then, if someone still drowns and dies, who can deliver them? This is the conclusion of Premānanda.

IDX.first_line: bhāi re! eka dina śāntipure prabhu advaitera ghare
IDX.search: bhai re eka dina santipure prabhu advaitera ghare dui prabhu bhojane basilasaka kari asvadana prabhu bale bhaktagana ei saka krsna asvadila hena saka asvadane krsnaprema aise mane sei preme kara asvadanajadabuddhi parihari prasada bhojana kari hari hari bala sarvajana

bhāi-re! 
eka-dina śāntipure, prabhu advaitera ghare, 
dui prabhu bhojane basilaśāka kari’ āsvādana, prabhu bale,- “bhaktagaṇa, 
ei śāka kṛṣṇa āsvādila 

hena śāka āsvādane, kṛṣṇaprema āise mane, 
sei preme kara āsvādanajaḍabuddhi parihari, prasāda bhojana kari’,

IDX.en_translation:
O brother! One day in Śāntipur, in the house of Prabhu Advaita, The two Lords sat down to eat. Tasting the greens, Prabhu said, “O devotees, Kṛṣṇa has tasted these greens. 

Tasting such greens, love for Kṛṣṇa comes to mind. Eat with that love. Giving up material intelligence, eating sanctified food, Everyone chant Hari Hari!

IDX.first_line: bhāi re! rāma kṛṣṇa gocāraṇe jāivena dūra vane
IDX.search: bhai re rama krsna gocarane jaivena dura vane eta cinti jasoda rohiniksira sara chana nani dujane khaoyana ani vatsalye ananda mane gani vayasya rakhalagane khaya rama krsna sane nace gaya ananda antarekrsnera prasada khaya udara bhariya jayaara deo ara deo kare
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
bhāi-re! 
rāma-kṛṣṇa gocāraṇe, jāivena dūra vane, 
eta cinti’ jaśodā-rohiṇīkṣīra, sara, chānā, nanī, du’jane khāoyāna āni’, 
vātsalye ānanda mane gaṇi’ 

vayasya rākhālagaṇe, khāya rāma-kṛṣṇa sane, 
nāce gāya ānanda antarekṛṣṇera prasāda khāya, udara bhariyā jāya,‘āra deo’ ‘āra deo’ kare
IDX.en_translation:
O brother! Thinking that Rāma and Kṛṣṇa will go to the distant forest to graze the cows, Yaśodā and Rohiṇī bring condensed milk, cream, cheese, and butter and feed them both, their hearts full of joy and parental affection. 

The cowherd friends eat with Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, dancing and singing with joy in their hearts. They eat Kṛṣṇa’s remnants, filling their stomachs, and keep saying, “Give more! Give more!”

IDX.first_line: bhāi re! śacīra aṅgane kabhu mādhavendra purī prabhu
IDX.search: bhai re sacira angane kabhu madhavendra puri prabhu prasadanna karena bhojanakhaite khaite tanra aila prema sudurbara bale suna sannyasira gana moca ghanta phulavadi dali dalna caccadi sacimata karila randhanatanra suddha bhakti heri bhojana karila hari sudha sama e anna vyanjana
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
bhāi-re! 
śacīra aṅgane kabhu, mādhavendra-purī prabhu, 
prasādānna karena bhojanakhāite khāite taṅ’ra, āila prema sudurbāra, 
bale- “śuna, sannyāsīra gaṇa 

mocā-ghaṇṭa phulavaḍi, ḍāli-ḍālnā-caccaḍi, 
śacīmātā karila randhanataṅ’ra śuddhā bhakti heri’, bhojana karila hari, 
sudhā-sama e anna-vyañjana 

joge jogī pāya jāhā, bhoge āja ha’be tāhā, 
hari bali’ khāo sabe bhāikṛṣṇera prasāda anna, trijagat kare dhanya, 
tripurāri nāce jāhā pāi”
IDX.en_translation:
O brothers! In Śacī’s courtyard, sometimes, Madhavendra Purī Prabhu partook of prasādānna. While eating, irresistible prema arose in him, and he said, “Listen, O assembly of sannyāsīs! 

Mochā-ghaṇṭa (banana flower curry), phulvaṛī (fried lentil balls), ḍāli (lentil soup), ḍālnā (vegetable curry), caccari (mixed vegetable dish)-Mother Śacī cooked them. Seeing her pure bhakti, Hari partook of this food as if it were nectar. 

That which a yogī obtains through yoga, today will be obtained through eating. Saying “Hari”, eat all of you, O brothers! Kṛṣṇa’s prasād blesses the three worlds, at the attainment of which Tripurāri (Lord Śiva) dances.”

IDX.first_line: bhāi re! śrī caitanya nityānanda śrīvāsādi bhakta vṛnda
IDX.search: bhai re sri caitanya nityananda srivasadi bhakta vrnda gauridasa panditera ghareluci cini ksira sara mithai payasa ara pithapana asvadana kare mahaprabhu bhakta gane parama ananda mane ajna dila karite bhojanakrsnera prasada anna bhojane hoiya dhanya krsna bali dake sarva jana
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
bhāi-re! 
śrī-caitanya-nityānanda, śrīvāsādi bhakta-vṛnda, 
gaurīdāsa-paṇḍitera ghareluci, cini, kṣīra, sara, miṭhāi, pāyasa āra, 
piṭhāpānā āsvādana kare 

mahāprabhu bhakta-gaṇe, parama ānanda-mane, 
ājñā dila karite bhojanakṛṣṇera prasāda-anna, bhojane hoiyā dhanya, 
kṛṣṇa bali’ ḍāke sarva-jana
IDX.en_translation:
O brother! Caitanya and Nityānanda, along with Śrīvāsa and other devotees, are at the house of Gaurīdāsa Paṇḍita tasting luci (fried bread), chini (sugar), kṣīra (condensed milk), sara (cream), miṭhāi (sweets), pāyasa (rice pudding), and piṭhā-pānā (cakes and drinks). 

With a greatly joyful heart, Mahāprabhu ordered them to take the meal. Blessed by eating the food offered to Kṛṣṇa, everyone calls out His name!

IDX.search: bhaja bhai caitanya nityananda ghucibe sakala jvala paibe ananda vadana bhariya bhai bala haribola apane vaisnavagana dhari dibe kola
IDX.author: śyāmānanda dāsa
IDX.verses:
bhaja bhāi! caitanya nityānanda 
ghucibe sakala jvālā pāibe ānanda 

vadana bhariyā bhāi! bala haribola 
āpane vaiṣṇavagaṇa dhari’ dibe kola 

minati kariyā kahi śuna sarvajanā 
vraje rādhā-kṛṣṇa-līlā karaha bhāvanā 

emana janama bhāi! nā hoibe āra 
śyāmānanda kahe, keha nahe āpanāra
IDX.en_translation:
O brother! Worship Lord Caitanya and Lord Nityānanda. All miseries will end, and you will attain supreme bliss. 

O brother! With a full mouth, chant “Haribol!” The Vaiṣṇavas themselves will embrace you. 

I humbly request, listen all people: Meditate upon the pastimes of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in Vraja. 

O brother! Such a human birth will not come again. Śyāmānanda says: “No one in this world is truly your own.”

IDX.first_line: bhaja bhaja hari mana dṛḍha kari’
IDX.search: bhaja bhaja hari mana drdha kari mukhe bola tanra nama vrajendra nandana gopi pranadhana bhuvana mohana syama kakhana maribe kemane taribe visama samana dake janhara pratape bhuvana kanpaye na jani mara vipake
IDX.author: locana-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: bhaja bhaja hari, mana dṛḍha kari’, mukhe bola tāṅ’ra nāma vrajendra-nandana, gopī-prāṇadhana, bhuvana-mohana śyāma kakhana maribe, kemane taribe, viṣama śamana ḍāke jāṅhāra pratāpe, bhuvana kāṅpaye, nā jāni mara vipāke kula-dhana pāiyā, unamata haiyā, āpanāke jāna baḍa śamanera dūte, dhari’ pāye hāte, bāṅdhiyā karibe jaḍa kibā jati, satī, kibā nīca jāti, jei hari nāhi bhaje tabe janamiyā, bhramiyā bhramiyā, raurava-narake maje e dāsa locana, bhāve anukṣaṇa, vṛthāi janama gela hari nā bhajinu, viṣaye majinu, hṛdaye rahala śela
IDX.en_translation:
Worship Hari, making your mind firm. Speak His name with your mouth—the son of the King of Vraja, the treasure of the gopīs’ lives, the dark-complexioned Lord who enchants the universe. 

When will you die? How will you be saved? The fierce lord of death calls. By whose prowess the universe trembles, you do not know when you will die in great distress. 

Having obtained family and wealth and becoming intoxicated by them, you consider yourself great. The messengers of the lord of death, catching you by your hands and feet, will bind you and make you helpless. 

Whether an ascetic, a chaste woman, or one of a low caste, whoever does not worship the Lord will wander through countless lives and drown in a hellish planet. 

This servant Locana constantly thinks: “My life has passed in vain! I did not worship the Lord and instead drowned in worldly affairs; a spear of regret remains in my heart.”

IDX.first_line: bhaja bhakata vatsala śrī gaura hari
IDX.search: bhaja bhakata vatsala sri gaura hari sri gaura hari sohi gostha vihari nanda yasomati citta hari bela hala damodara aisa ekhana bhoga mandire vasi karaha bhojana
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
bhaja bhakata-vatsala śrī-gaura-hari 
śrī-gaura-hari sohi goṣṭha-vihārī, 
nanda-yaśomatī-citta-hārī 

belā ha’la dāmodara, āisa ekhana 
bhoga-mandire vasi’ karaha bhojana 

nandera nirdeśe baise giri-varadhārī 
baladeva-saha sakhā baise sāri sāri 

śuktā-śākādi bhāji nālitā kuṣmāṇḍa 
ḍāli ḍālnā dugdha-tumbī dadhi mocā-khaṇḍa 

mudga-vaḍā māṣa-vaḍā roṭikā ghṛtānna 
śaṣkulī piṣṭaka kṣīra puli pāyasānna 

karpūra amṛta-keli rambhā kṣīra-sāra 
amṛta rasālā, amla dvādaśa-prakāra 

luci-cini sarapurī lāḍḍu rasāvalī 
bhojana karena kṛṣṇa ha’ye kutūhalī 

rādhikāra pakka anna vividha vyañjana 
parama ānande kṛṣṇa karena bhojana 

chale-bale lāḍḍu khāya śrī madhumaṅgala 
bagala bājāya āra deya haribola 

rādhikādi-gaṇe heri’ nayanera koṇe 
tṛpta ha’ye khāya kṛṣṇa yaśodā-bhavane 

bhojanānte piye kṛṣṇa suvāsita vāri 
sabe mukha prakṣālaya ha’ye sāri sāri 

hasta-mukha prakṣāliyā jata sakhā-gaṇe 
ānande viśrāma kare baladeva sane 

‘jāmbula’ ‘rasāla’ āne tāmbūla-masālā 
tāhā kheye kṛṣṇa-candra sukhe nidrā gelā 

‘viśālākṣa’ śikhi-puccha cāmara ḍhulāya 
apūrva śayyāya kṛṣṇa sukhe nidrā jāya 

yaśomatī-ājñā peye dhaniṣṭhā-ānīta 
śrī kṛṣṇa-prasāda rādhā bhuñje ha’ye prīta 

lalitādi sakhī-gaṇa avaśeṣa pāya 
mane mane sukhe rādhā-kṛṣṇa-guṇa gāya
IDX.en_translation:
Worship bhakta-vatsala (one who is affectionate to His devotees) Śrī Gaura-hari. Śrī Gaura-hari is the same goṣṭha-vihārī (one who enjoys pastimes in the cowherd village), Nanda and Yaśomatī’s citta-hārī (one who steals the heart). 

It’s time, Dāmodara, please come now. Sit in the bhoga-mandira (offering house) and take your meal. 

Nanda’s order, Girivaradhārī (the one who lifted Govardhana Hill) sits, Baladeva and the sakhās (friends) sit in rows. 

Śukta, various vegetable fries, nālitā (jute leaves), kuṣmāṇḍa (winter melon), Dāli (lentils), ḍālanā (vegetable curry), milk-tumbī (gourd), dadhi (yogurt), mocākhaṇḍa (banana flower curry). 

Mudgavaṛā (lentil fritters), māṣavaṛā (black gram fritters), roṭikā (bread), ghṛtānna (rice with ghee), Śaṣkulī (sweet cakes), piṣṭaka (cakes), kṣīra (sweet rice), puli (dumplings), pāyasānna (sweet rice). 

Karpūra (camphor), amṛtakeli (a type of sweet), rambhā (banana), kṣīrasāra (cream of milk), Amṛta rasālā (sweet nectar), amla (sour dishes) of twelve types. 

Lucī (fried bread), cini (sugar), sarapurī (a type of sweet), lāḍḍu (sweet balls), rasāvalī (sweet dish), Kṛṣṇa eats with great curiosity. 

Rādhikā’s pakva anna (cooked rice) and various vyañjana (curries), Kṛṣṇa eats with supreme joy. 

Trickery, Śrī Madhumaṅgala eats lāḍḍu, He claps his armpits and shouts Haribol. 

Beholding Rādhikā and others from the corner of His eye, Kṛṣṇa eats contentedly in Yaśodā’s bhavana (house). 

After eating, Kṛṣṇa drinks suvasita vāri (fragrant water), Everyone cleans their mouths, sitting in rows. 

Having washed their hands and mouths, all the sakhā-gaṇe (groups of friends), Happily rest with Baladeva. 

“Jāmbula” (jambu fruit) and “rasāla” (mango) are brought, and tāmbūla-masālā (betel nut preparation), Eating that, Kṛṣṇa-candra goes to sleep happily. 

Viśālāksa waves the peacock feather cāmara (fan), Kṛṣṇa sleeps happily on an extraordinary bed. 

Receiving Yaśomatī’s order, brought by Dhaniṣṭhā, Rādhā partakes of Śrī Kṛṣṇa-prasāda (mercy) with pleasure. 

Lalitādi sakhī-gaṇa (Lalitā and other female friends) receive the remnants, In their minds, they happily sing the glories of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa. 

Harilīlā (Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes) is the only source of joy for whom, Bhaktivinoda sings this bhogārati (song glorifying the offering of food).

IDX.search: bhaja mana nanda kumara bhaviya dekhaha bhai gati nahi ara dhana jana putra adi keba apanara atoeva karaha mana hari pada sara
IDX.author: rādhāmohana dāsa
IDX.verses: bhaja mana! nanda-kumāra bhāviyā dekhaha bhāi gati nāhi āra dhana jana putra ādi kebā āpanāra atoeva karaha mana hari-pada sāra kusaṅga chāḍiyā sadā sat-saṅge thāka parama nipuṇa hoi, nāma bali’ ḍāka tāṅ’ra nāma-līlā-gāne sadā hoo matta se caraṇa-dhana pābe, hoibe kṛtārtha rādhāmohana bale, mana! ki baliba tore saṁsāra-yātanā āra nāhi deha more
IDX.en_translation:
O my mind! Worship the Son of Nanda. Reflect and see, O brother—there is no other way. 

Wealth, family, children, and so on—who is truly your own? Therefore, O mind, make the lotus feet of Lord Hari your only essence. 

Giving up bad association, always stay in good company. Becoming very expert, call out the Holy Name. 

Always be intoxicated in singing His Name and pastimes. You will receive the treasure of His lotus feet and your life will be fulfilled. 

Rādhāmohana says: “O my mind! What more shall I say to you? Do not cause me to suffer in this material existence anymore.”

bhaja rādhā kṛṣṇa, gopāla kṛṣṇa 
kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa bala mukhe 
nāme buka bhare jāya, abhāva miṭāya, 
svabhāva jāgāya mahāsukhe 

hari dīnabandhu, ciradina bandhu, 
jīvera cira sukhe duḥkhe 
(tāi) bhajare andha, caraṇāravinda, 
dustara māyā-vipāke 

bhaja mūḍhamati, tava cirasāthī, 
jāṅhāra karuṇā loke loke 
tabe kena pāntha, eta tumi bhrānta,

Worship Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa! Worship Gopāla Kṛṣṇa! Chant “Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa!” with your mouth. The heart fills with the Holy Name, all wants are fulfilled, and one’s true nature awakens in great joy. 

Lord Hari, the Friend of the distressed, is the eternal friend of the soul in both happiness and sorrow. Therefore, O blind one, worship His lotus feet in this insurmountable entanglement of illusion. 

Worship your eternal companion, O foolish mind! His mercy is in every world. Why then, O traveler, are you so bewildered? Where are you running in every direction? 

That playful Lord Hari has come to the city of Nadīyā with the love of Rādhā in His heart. Worship the Supreme Lord always with your mind and soul, for He has come to take you to His heart.

IDX.author: govinda dāsa
IDX.verses: bhajahū re mana, śrī-nanda-nandana, abhaya caraṇāravinda re durlabha mānava-, janama sat-saṅge, taraha e bhava-sindhu re śīta-ātapa, vāta bariṣaṇa, e dina jāminī jāgi’ re biphale sevinu, kṛpaṇa durajana, capala sukha-lava lāgi’ re e dhana, jauvana, putra-parijana, ithe ki āche paratīti re kamala-dala-jala, jīvana ṭalamala, bhajahū hari-pada niti re śravaṇa, kīrtana, smaraṇa, vandana, pāda-sevana, dāsya re pūjana, sakhī-jana, ātma-nivedana, govinda dāsa abhilāṣa re
IDX.en_translation:
O mind, worship the fearless lotus feet of the son of Nanda. Having attained this rare human birth, cross over this ocean of material existence in the association of saintly persons. 

Remaining awake day and night in cold, heat, wind, and rain, I have fruitlessly served miserly and wicked people just for a fleeting drop of happiness. 

What reliability is there in wealth, youth, children, or family? Life is as unsteady as a drop of water on a lotus petal; therefore, always worship the feet of the Lord. 

Hearing, chanting, remembering, offering prayers, serving the Lord’s feet, servitude, worship, friendship, and self-surrender—this is the heartfelt desire of Govinda dāsa.
