IDX.verses:
hare kṛṣṇa hare kṛṣṇa 
kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa hare hare 
hare rāma hare rāma 
rāma rāma hare hare 

iti ṣoḍaśakaṁ nāmnāṁ 
kali-kalmaṣa-nāśanaṁ 
nātaḥ parataropāyaḥ 
sarva-vedeṣu dṛśyate
IDX.translation_intro: Śrīla A.C. Bhaktivedānta Swami Prabhupāda, Mahā-mantra essay written in December 1966 in New York City
IDX.en_translation:
This transcendental vibration by chanting of: Hare Kṛṣṇa Hare Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa Hare Hare Hare Rāma Hare Rāma Rāma Rāma Hare Hare, is the sublime method of reviving our Kṛṣṇa consciousness. As living spiritual souls we are all originally Kṛṣṇa conscious entities, but due to our association with matter from time immemorial, our consciousness is now polluted by the material atmosphere.
In this polluted concept of life, we are all trying to exploit the resources of material nature, but actually we are becoming more and more entangled in her complexities. This illusion is called māyā — or hard struggle for existence for winning over the stringent laws of material nature.
This illusory struggle against the material nature can at once be stopped by the revival of our Kṛṣṇa consciousness. Kṛṣṇa consciousness is not an artificial imposition on the mind. This consciousness is the original energy of the living entity. When we hear the transcendental vibration, this consciousness is revived, and the process is recommended by authorities for this age.
By practical experience, also, we can perceive that by chanting this maha-mantra, or “the great chanting for deliverance,” one can at once feel transcendental ecstasy from the spiritual stratum. When one is factually on the plane of spiritual understanding, surpassing the stages of sense, mind, and intelligence, one is situated on the transcendental plane.
This chanting of Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa, Hare Hare, Hare Rāma, Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma, Hare Hare is directly enacted from the spiritual platform, surpassing all lower stages of consciousness, namely sensual, mental, and intellectual. There is no need of understanding the language of the mantra, nor there is any need of mental speculation, nor an intellectual adjustment for chanting this Mahā-mantra. It springs automatically from the spiritual platform, and as such anyone can take part in this transcendental sound vibration without any previous qualification and feel the ecstasy. We have seen it practically —even a child can take part in the chanting, or even a dog can take part in it.
The chanting should be heard from the lips of a pure devotee of the Lord so that immediate effect can be achieved. As far as possible chanting from the lips of pure devotee should be avoided as much as milk touched by lips of a serpent causes poisonous effect.
The word Harā is a form of addressing the energy of the Lord. Kṛṣṇa and Rāma are forms of addressing directly the Lord, and They mean “the highest pleasure-eternal.” Harā is the supreme pleasure potency of the Lord. This potency, when addressed as Hare, helps us in reaching the supreme Lord.
The material energy, called as māyā, is also one of the multipotencies of the Lord as much as we are also marginal potency of the Lord. The living entities are described as superior energy than matter. When the superior energy is in contact with inferior energy, it becomes an incompatible situation. But when the supreme marginal potency is in contact with the spiritual potency, Harā, it becomes the happy, normal condition of the living entity.
The three words, namely Harā, Kṛṣṇa, and Rāma, are the transcendental seeds of the Mahā-mantra, and the chanting is the spiritual call for the Lord and His internal energy, Harā, for giving protection to the conditioned soul. The chanting is exactly like genuine crying by the child for mother. Mother Harā helps in achieving the grace of the supreme father Hari, or Kṛṣṇa and the Lord reveals Himself to such a sincere devotee. No other means therefore of spiritual relization is as effective in this age as chanting the Mahā-mantra: Hare Rāma, Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma, Hare HareHare Kṛṣṇa Hare Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa Hare Hare Hare Rāma Hare Rāma Rāma Rāma Hare Hare. The sixteen words Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa, Hare Hare Hare Rāma, Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma, Hare Hare are especially meant for counteracting the contaminations of Kali. After searching through all the Vedas, you will not find a better means of self-realization for this age.

IDX.en_translation:
Hare Kṛṣṇa Hare (Refrain) 

Oh, what a Name Nitāi has brought! Nitāi has brought the Name to the marketplace of the Name, And He is giving that Name for the price of faith. 

Hare Kṛṣṇa Hare Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa Hare Hare, Hare Rāma Hare Rāma Rāma Rāma Hare Hare 

Nitāi, seeing the fallen condition of the souls to be so wretched, Has brought the Name all the way from Vraja. 

This Name is chanted by Śiva with his five mouths. (This sweet Hari-nāma) 

This Name is chanted by Brahmā with his four mouths. (This sweet Hari-nāma) 

This Name is chanted by Nārada on his vīṇā. (This sweet Hari-nāma) 

By a mere reflection of this Name (nāmābhāsa), Ajāmila went to Vaikuṇṭha. 

Bhaktivinoda says: “Constantly chanting this holy name, let us go to Vraja!”

IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses: ‘hari’ bala, ‘hari’ bala, ‘hari’ bala, bhāi re harināma āniyāche gaurāṅga nitāi re (modera duḥkha de’khe re) harināma vinā jīvera anya dhana nāi re harināme śuddha ha’la jagāi-mādhāi re (baḍa pāpī chila re) miche māyābaddha haye jīvana-kāṭāi re (āmi āmāra bole re) āśāvaśe ghure’ ghure’ āra kothā jāi re (āśāra śeṣa nāi re) ‘hari’ ba’le deo bhāi āśāra mukhe chāi re (nirāśa to sukha re) bhoga-mokṣa-vāñchā chāḍi’ harināma gāi re (śuddha-sattva haye re) nā ce’yeo nāmera guṇe o saba phala pāi re (tuccha phale prayāsa che’ḍe re) vinoda bale, jāi la’ye nāmera bālāi re (nāmera bālāi che’ḍe re) śabdārthaḥ-bālāi-pratibandhaka, esthale daśa nāmāparādha
IDX.en_translation:
Chant “Hari! Hari! Hari!” O brother! Gaurāṅga and Nitāi have brought the Holy Name. 

Seeing our distress, they brought this Name, for without the Holy Name, the soul has no other wealth. Even the great sinners Jagāi and Mādhāi were purified by it. 

Falsely bound by illusion, we spend our lives; saying “I” and “mine” and driven by desire, where else shall we go? 

There is no end to desire! Therefore, chant “Hari!” and throw ashes on the face of desire. Freedom from desire is true happiness; giving up the quest for enjoyment and liberation, we sing the Holy Name. 

Becoming pure in being, we attain all fruits through the power of the Name without even asking. Giving up the effort for trivial results, Bhaktivinoda says: let us go, casting away the offenses to the Holy Name. 

(Casting aside the offenses to the Name!)

IDX.first_line: hari ba’laba āra madanamohana heriba go
IDX.search: hari balaba ara madanamohana heriba go ei rupete vrajera pathe caliba go jaba go vrajendrapura haba gopikara nupura tadera carane madhura madhura bajiba go
IDX.author: narottama-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: hari ba’laba āra madanamohana heriba go ei rūpete vrajera pathe caliba go jā’ba go vrajendrapura, ha’ba gopīkāra nūpura, tādera caraṇe madhura-madhura bājiba go rādhā-kṛṣṇera rūpamādhurī, heriba du’nayana bhari’, nikuñjera dvārī dvārī rahiba go vipine vinoda khelā, saṅgete rākhālera melā, taṅdera caraṇera dhūlā mākhiba go tomarā sabe vrajavāsī, purāo manera abhilāṣī, āra kabe śrī-kṛṣṇera baṅśī śuniba go ei deha antimakāle, rākhiba śrī-yamunāra jale, jaya rādhā-govinda ba’le bhāsiba go kahe narottama-dāsa, nā pūrila abhilāṣa, (āra) kabe hāma vrajavāsa kariba go
IDX.en_translation:
I will chant the name of Hari and behold the Lord who enchants Cupid. In this way, I will walk on the path to Vraja. 

I will go to the city of the King of Vraja and become the ankle bells of the cowherd girls, sweetly jingling at their feet. 

I will behold the sweet beauty of the forms of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, filling my eyes, and I will remain at every entrance of the groves. 

In the forest are joyful pastimes with a gathering of cowherd boys; I will smear myself with the dust of their feet. 

O residents of Vraja, please fulfill my heart’s desire! When will I hear the flute of Śrī Kṛṣṇa again? 

At the time of death, I will place this body in the waters of the Yamunā and float away while chanting, “All glories to Rādhā and Govinda!” 

Narottama dāsa says: “My desires are not yet fulfilled. When will I truly reside in Vraja?”

IDX.search: hari bale modera gaura elo ela re gauranga canda preme elo thelo nitai advaita sange godrume pasila
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
hari ba’le modera gaura elo 

ela re gaurāṅga-cāṅda preme elo-thelo 
nitāi-advaita-saṅge godrume paśila 

saṅkīrtana-rase mete nāma vilāila 
nāmera hāṭe ese preme jagat bhāsāila 

godruma-vāsīra āja duḥkha dūre gela 
bhaktavṛnda-saṅge āsi’ hāṭa jāgāila 

nadīyā bhramite gorā ela nāmera hāṭe 
gaura ela hāṭe, saṅge nitāi ela hāṭe 

nāce mātoyārā nitāi godrumera māṭhe 
jagat mātāya nitāi premera mālasāṭe 

(torā dekhe jāre) 
advaitādi bhaktavṛnda nāce ghāṭe ghāṭe 
palāya duranta kali paḍiyā vibhrāṭe 

ki sukhe bhāsila jīva gorācāṅdera nāṭe 
dekhiyā śuniyā pāṣaṇḍīra buka phāṭe
IDX.en_translation:
Our Gaura has arrived, chanting Hari. 

Here comes Gaurāṅgacānda, disheveled in ecstatic love. With Nitāi and Advaita, He entered Godruma. 

Intoxicated by the mellow of saṅkīrttana, He distributed the holy name. Coming to the market of the holy name, He inundated the world with love. 

Today, the sorrow of Godruma’s residents is gone. Coming with the bhaktavṛnda, He awakened the market. 

As Gorā traveled Nadīyā, He came to the market of the holy name. Gaura came to the market, and Nitāi came with Him. 

Nitāi dances ecstatically in Godruma’s fields. Nitāi intoxicates the world with an abundance of love. 

(Go and see for yourselves!) Advaita and the bhaktavṛnda dance at every ghāṭa. The troublesome Kali flees in confusion. 

How much joy the jīva is immersed in, in the play of Gorācānda! Seeing and hearing this, the pāṣaṇḍī’s heart breaks.

IDX.verses: hari bo’lbo ār madana-mohan heribo go ei rūpe vrajer pathe calibo go jā’bo go vrajendra-pur, ha’bo gopī pāyer nūpur, nūpur haye runujhunu bājibo go rādhā-kṛṣṇer rūp mādhurī, heribo du’nayan bhori’, nikuñjera dvārī dvārī rahibo go vipine vinoda khelā, saṅgete rākhāler melā, tā’der caraṇera dhūlā mākhibo go tomrā sabe vraja-vāsī, purāo maner abhilāṣī, ār kabe kṛṣṇer vāṁśī śunibo go ei deha antima kāle, rākhibo (śrī) yamunār jale, jay rādhā-govinda bo’le bhāsibo go kahe narottama-dāsa, nā pūrilo abhilāṣ, ār kabe vraje-vās karibo go
IDX.en_translation:
I will chant the names of Hari and behold Madana-mohana. In such as state, I shall travel the path to Vraja. 

I will go to the land of Vraja, become the anklet with small bells on the feet of the gopīs and will there chime sweetly. 

I will gaze upon the sweet beauty of Śrī Śrī Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa to the full satisfaction of my eyes, and I will stand at the entrance of Their pastime groves. 

Charming pastimes will take place in the forests of Vraja, in the playful assembly of the cowherd boys. I will smear the dust of their lotus feet on my body. 

O residents of Vraja, please fulfill my heart’s desire! Oh, when will I hear the sound of Kṛṣṇa’s flute? 

When the time comes for this body’s demise, I will place it in the waters of the Yamunā, and as it floats, I will chant, “All glories to Rādhā-Govinda!” 

Narottama dāsa laments: “My desires are not been fulfilled. Oh, when will I attain reside in Vraja?”

IDX.first_line: hari e ohari rāma adhamaka uddhāra karāhe nārāyaṇa
IDX.search: hari e ohari rama adhamaka uddhara karahe narayana dhanajana namago moi moksa parasada krpa kari kara prabhu moka atmasat
IDX.verses:
hari-e ohari rāma 
adhamaka uddhāra karāhe nārāyaṇa 

dhanajana nāmāgo moi mokṣa parasāda 
kṛpā kari karā prabhu moka ātmasāt 

tumi jagatara svāmī sakalo tomāra 
tumi mātra dātā prabhu, dātā kon āra 

mora buli bhāvi karo mithyā abhimāna 
dāsa kari la’le haya tāra avasāna 

karmadoṣe jate thāko svarga vā narake 
ei kṛpā karā jena nubhulo tomāke 

bhakati parama dhana tayu bharālata 
nukhujoho āna eko tāka diyā moka 

tayu bhakatara saṅga diyā sarvakṣaṇe 
tayu nāma-guṇa śuno sadāya jena kāne
IDX.en_translation:
O Hari! O Rāma! O Nārāyaṇa, please deliver this fallen soul. 

I do not seek wealth, followers, fame, nor even the blessing of liberation. By Your grace, O Lord, please make me Your own. 

You are the Master of the universe, and everything belongs to You. You alone are the Giver, O Lord; who else can truly give? 

Thinking “mine,” I am full of false ego. If You make me Your servant, that ego will come to an end. 

Due to the faults of my past actions, wherever I may reside—whether in heaven or in hell—please grant me this grace: that I may never forget You. 

Devotion is the supreme treasure in Your treasury. I do not ask for anything else; please give that to me. 

Grant me the company of Your devotees at all times, so that I may always hear Your Holy Names and glories with my ears.

IDX.first_line: hari haraye namaḥ kṛṣṇa yādavāya namaḥ
IDX.search: hari haraye namah krsna yadavaya namah yadavaya madhavaya kesavaya namah gopala govinda rama sri madhusudana giridhari gopi natha madana mohana
IDX.author: narottama-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: (hari) haraye namaḥ kṛṣṇa yādavāya namaḥ yādavāya mādhavāya keśavāya namaḥ gopāla govinda rāma śrī madhusūdana giridhārī gopī-nātha madana-mohana śrī caitanya, nityānanda, śrī-advaita goptā (sītā) hari, guru, vaiṣṇava, bhāgavata, gītā śrī rūpa, śrī sanātana, bhaṭṭa-raghunātha śrī jīva, gopāla-bhaṭṭa, dāsa-raghunātha ei chaya gosāir kari caraṇa vandana jāhā haite vighna-nāśa abhīṣṭa-pūraṇa ei chaya gosāī jāṅ’ra, mui tāṅ’ra dāsa tāṅ’ sabāra pada-reṇu mora pañca-grāsa tāṅ’dera caraṇa sevi bhakta-sane vāsa janame janame haya, ei abhilāṣa ei chaya gosāī jabe vraje kailā vāsa rādhā-kṛṣṇa-nitya-līlā karilā prakāśa ānande bala hari, bhaja vṛndāvana śrī guru-vaiṣṇava-pade majāiyā mana śrī guru-vaiṣṇava-pāda-padma kari’ āśa nāma-saṅkīrtana kahe narottama-dāsa
IDX.translation_intro: śrī nāma-kīrtana
IDX.en_translation:
Salutations to Hari, Kṛṣṇa, and the descendant of Yadu! Salutations to Mādhava and Keśava! 

Gopāla, Govinda, Rāma, and Śrī Madhusūdana! The lifter of Govardhana Hill, the Lord of the gopīs, and the one who enchants Cupid! 

Śrī Caitanya, Nityānanda, Śrī Advaita the protector (and His consort, Śrī Sītā Ṭhākurāṇī)! Hari, the spiritual master, the devotee, the scripture, and the Gītā! 

Śrī Rūpa, Śrī Sanātana, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa, Śrī Jīva, Gopāla Bhaṭṭa, and Raghunātha dāsa. 

I offer my obeisances to the lotus feet of these six spiritual masters, by which the destruction of obstacles and the fulfillment of desires occur. 

Whoever follows these six masters—I am their servant. The dust of their lotus feet is my very sustenance. 

To serve their feet and reside with the devotees—this is my desire, birth after birth. 

When these six masters resided in Vraja, they revealed the eternal pastimes of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. 

Joyfully chant the name of Hari and worship Vṛndāvana, immersing your mind in the lotus feet of the spiritual master and the devotees. 

Taking hope in the lotus feet of the spiritual master and the devotees, Narottama dāsa sings this congregational chanting.

IDX.first_line: hari hari! āra kabe pālaṭibe daśā
IDX.search: hari hari ara kabe palatibe dasa e dasa kariya bame jaba vrndavana dhame ei mane kariyachi asa dhana jana putra dare esaba kariya dure ekanta hoiya kabe jaba saba duhkha parihari vrndavane vasa kari madhukari magiya khaiba
IDX.author: narottama-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: hari hari! āra kabe pālaṭibe daśā e-daśā kariyā bāme, jā’ba vṛndāvana-dhāme, ei mane kariyāchi āśā dhana-jana putra-dāre, esaba kariyā dūre, ekānta hoiyā kabe jāba saba duḥkha parihari’, vṛndāvane vāsa kari’, mādhukarī māgiyā khāiba yamunāra jala jena, amṛta samāna hena, kabe piba udara pūriyā kabe rādhā-kuṇḍa-jale, snāna kari’ kutūhale, śyāma-kuṇḍe rahiba paḍiyā bhramiba dvādaśa vane, rasakeli je je sthāne, premāveśe gaḍāgaḍi diyā śudhāiba jane jane, vrajavāsigaṇa-sthāne, nivediba caraṇa dhariyā bhajanera sthāna kabe, nayana-gocara habe, āra jata āche upavana tā’ra madhye vṛndāvana, narottama dāsera mana, āśā kare yugala-caraṇa
IDX.en_translation:
Hari Hari! When will my condition change? Having left this state behind, I will go to the abode of Vṛndāvana—this is the hope I have cherished in my mind. 

Abandoning wealth, followers, children, and wife far away, when will I go, becoming single-minded? Giving up all distress, residing in Vṛndāvana, I will eat by begging alms. 

When will I fill my belly drinking the water of the Yamunā, which is like nectar? When, bathing with curiosity in the waters of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, will I lie down at Śyāma-kuṇḍa? 

I will wander in the twelve forests, in all the places of playful pastimes, rolling on the ground in the ecstasy of love. I will ask each and every person at the places of the residents of Vraja, and I will submit my petition holding their feet. 

When will the place of worship become visible to my eyes, along with all the gardens that exist? Among them is Vṛndāvana; Narottama Dāsa’s mind hopes for the lotus feet of the Divine Couple.

IDX.first_line: hari hari! āra ki emana daśā haba
IDX.search: hari hari ara ki emana dasa haba e bhava samsara tyaji parama anande maji ara kabe vraja bhume jaba sukha maya vrndavana kabe habe darasana se dhuli lagibe kabe gaya preme gadagada haina radha krsna nama laiya kandiya bedaba ubharaya
IDX.author: narottama-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: hari hari! āra ki emana daśā haba e-bhava-saṁsāra tyaji’, parama-ānande maji’, āra kabe vraja-bhūme jā’ba sukha-maya vṛndāvana, kabe ha’be daraśana, se-dhūli lāgibe ka’be gāya preme gadagada haiñā, rādhā-kṛṣṇa-nāma laiyā, kāndiyā beḍāba ubharāya nibhṛte nikuñje jāñā, aṣṭāṅge praṇāma haiyā, ḍākiba ‘hā rādhānātha’ bali’ kabe yamunāra tīre, paraśa kariba nīre, kabe piba karapuṭe tuli’ āra kabe emana haba, śrī-rāsa-maṇḍale jā’ba, kabe gaḍāgaḍi diba tāya vaṁśīvaṭa-chāyā pāñā, parama-ānanda hañā, paḍiyā rahiba tā’ra chāya kabe govardhana giri, dekhiba nayana bhari’, kabe habe rādhā-kuṇḍe vāsa bhramite bhramite kabe, e-deha patana habe, kahe dīna narottama-dāsa
IDX.en_translation:
O Lord Hari! Will such a state ever be mine? Abandoning this material existence and immersed in supreme bliss, when will I go to Vrajabhūmi? 

When will I behold blissful Vṛndāvana? When will its dust touch my body? Overwhelmed with divine love and chanting the names of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, I will wander about weeping loudly. 

Going to a secluded grove and offering my full obeisances, I will call out, “O Lord of Rādhā!” When will I touch the water on the bank of the Yamunā? When will I drink it from my cupped hands? 

When will such a state be mine again? I will go to the place of the rāsa dance. When will I roll on the ground there? Finding the shade of the Vaṁśīvaṭa tree and becoming supremely joyful, I will remain there. 

When will I see Govardhana Hill with my eyes full? When will I reside at Rādhā-kuṇḍa? While wandering around, when will this body fall? Thus says the humble Narottama dāsa.

IDX.search: hari hari biphale janama gonainu manusya janama paiya radha krsna na bhajiya janiya suniya visa khainu golokera prema dhana harinama sankirtana rati na janmila kene taya samsara visanale diva nisi hiya jvale judaite na kainu upaya
IDX.author: narottama-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: hari hari! biphale janama goṅāinu manuṣya-janama pāiyā, rādhā-kṛṣṇa nā bhajiyā, jāniyā śuniyā viṣa khāinu golokera prema-dhana, harināma-saṅkīrtana, rati nā janmila kene tāya saṁsāra-viṣānale, divā-niśi hiyā jvale, juḍāite nā kainu upāya vrajendra-nandana jei, śacī-suta haila sei, balarāma hoila nitāi dīna hīna jata chila, hari-nāme uddhārila, tā’ra sākṣī jagāi-mādhāi hā hā prabhu nanda-suta, vṛṣabhānu-sutā-yuta, karuṇā karaha eibāra narottama-dāsa kaya, nā ṭhelio rāṅgāpāya, tomā vinā ke āche āmāra
IDX.en_translation:
Hari Hari! I spent my life in vain. Having obtained a human birth, not worshipping Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, I knowingly drank poison. 

The treasure of Goloka’s love, the saṅkīrtana of Hari’s Name—why did I not develop attachment for it? My heart burns day and night in the poisonous fire of worldly existence; I did not make a way to cool it. 

He who is Vrajendra-nandana became Śacī-suta; Balarāma became Nitāi. He delivered all the lowly and destitute by the Holy Name; Jagāi and Mādhāi are the witnesses to that. 

Alas, alas! O Lord, Son of Nanda, along with the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu, be merciful this time. Narottama Dāsa says: Do not push me away from Your reddish feet; who do I have except You?

IDX.verses: hari hari! hena dina hoibe āmāra dūhu aṅga paraśiba, dūhu aṅga nirakhiba, sevana kariba dohākāra mālā gāṅthi’ diba nānā phule kanaka-sampūṭa kari’, karpūra tāmbula pūri’, jogāiba adharayugale rādhā-kṛṣṇa vṛndāvana, ei mora prāṇa-dhana, ei mora jīvana-upāya jaya patita-pāvana, deha more ei dhana, tomā vine anya nāhi bhāya śrī-guru karuṇā-sindhu, adhama janāra bandhu, lokanātha lokera jīvana hā hā! prabhu kara dayā, deha more padachāyā, narottama loila śaraṇa
IDX.en_translation:
Hari Hari! Such a day will be mine. I will touch the limbs of Both, I will see the limbs of Both, I will serve Both of Them. 

Stringing garlands of various flowers, I will give them. Making a golden box, filling it with camphor and betel nuts, I will supply it to Their lips. 

Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, Vṛndāvana—this is the treasure of my life, this is the means of my life. Glory to the Savior of the Fallen! Give me this wealth; nothing else shines for me without You. 

Śrī Guru, ocean of mercy, friend of the fallen people, Lokanātha—the life of the people. Alas, alas! Master, be merciful, give me the shade of your feet; Narottama has taken shelter.

IDX.search: hari hari kabe haba vrndavana vasi nirakhiba nayane yugala ruparasi tyajiya sayanasukha vicitra palanka kabe vrajera dhulaya dhusara habe anga
IDX.author: narottama-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: hari hari! kabe haba vṛndāvana-vāsī nirakhiba nayane yugala-rūparāśi tyajiyā śayanasukha vicitra pālaṅka kabe vrajera dhūlāya dhūsara ha’be aṅga ṣaḍrasa bhojana dūre parihari kabe vraje māgiyā khāiba mādhukarī parikramā kariyā beḍāba vane vane viśrāma kariyā jāi yamunā-puline tāpa dūra kariba śītala vaṁśīvaṭe (kabe) kuñje baiṭhaba hāma vaiṣṇava-nikaṭe narottama-dāsa kahe kari’ parihāra kabe vā emana daśā hoibe āmāra
IDX.en_translation:
Hari Hari! When will I become a resident of Vṛndāvana? I will behold with my eyes the beautiful forms of the Divine Couple. 

Forsaking the comfort of sleeping on an elaborate bed, when will my body be covered in the dust of Vraja? 

Leaving aside meals with six tastes (sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter, and astringent), when will I eat by begging for mādhukarī (alms) in Vraja? 

I will wander from forest to forest performing parikramā, and I will rest on the banks of the Yamunā. 

I will relieve my distress in the cool Vaṁśīvaṭa, when will I sit in a kuñja (grove) in the company of Vaiṣṇavas? 

Narottam Dāsa says, making this humble plea, when will such a state be mine?

IDX.first_line: hari hari! kabe hena daśā habe mora
IDX.search: hari hari kabe hena dasa habe mora seviba dohara pada anande vibhora bhramara hoiya sada rahiba carane sri caranamrta sada kariba asvadane
IDX.author: narottama-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: hari hari! kabe hena daśā habe mora seviba dohāra pada ānande vibhora bhramara hoiyā sadā rahiba caraṇe śrī-caraṇāmṛta sadā kariba āsvādane ei āśā kari āmi-yata sakhīgaṇa tomādera kṛpāya haya vāñchita pūraṇa bahudina vāñchā kari’ pūrṇa jāte haya sabe meli dayā kara hoiyā sadaya sevā āśe narottama kānde divāniśi kṛpā kari’ kara more anugata dāsī
IDX.en_translation:
Hari Hari! When will such a state be mine? Overwhelmed with joy, I will serve the feet of the Couple. 

Becoming a bee, I will always remain at the feet; I will always taste the nectar of the holy feet. 

I cherish this hope—all you sakhīs! By your mercy, the desire is fulfilled. 

That which I have desired for many days may be fulfilled—all of you meeting together, be kind, becoming merciful. 

In the hope of service, Narottama weeps day and night; mercifully make me a follower maidservant.

IDX.first_line: hari hari kabe mora habe hena dina
IDX.search: hari hari kabe mora habe hena dina vimala vaisnave rati upajibe vasana hoibe ksina antara bahire sama vyavahara amani manada haba krsna sankirtane sri krsna smarane satata majiya raba
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses: hari hari kabe mora habe hena dina vimala vaiṣṇave, rati upajibe, vāsanā hoibe kṣīṇa antara-bāhire, sama vyavahāra, amānī mānada ha’ba kṛṣṇa-saṅkīrtane, śrī-kṛṣṇa-smaraṇe, satata majiyā ra’ba e dehera kriyā, abhyāse kariba, jīvana jāpana lāgi’ śrī-kṛṣṇa-bhajane, anukūla jāhā, tāhe ha’ba anurāgī bhajanera jāhā, pratikūla tāhā, dṛḍhabhāve teyāgiba bhajite bhajite, samaya āsile, e deha chāḍiyā diba bhakativinoda, ei āśā kari’, basiyā godruma-vane prabhu-kṛpā lāgi’, vyākula antare, sadā kāṅde saṅgopane
IDX.en_translation:
Hari Hari, when will that day be mine? When affection for pure Vaiṣṇavas will arise, And desires will become weak. 

Inside and outside, my behavior will be consistent, I will become one who desires no respect for myself but offers all respect to others. In congregational chanting of Kṛṣṇa’s names, and in remembering Śrī Kṛṣṇa, I will always remain immersed. 

The activities of this body, I will perform out of habit, For the sake of maintaining life. That which is favorable to devotional service to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, To that I will become attached. 

That which is unfavorable to devotional service, That I will firmly give up. While performing devotional service, when the time comes, I will give up this body. 

Bhaktivinoda, cherishing this hope, Sitting in Godruma-vana, For the Lord’s grace, with an anxious heart, He always weeps secretly.

IDX.first_line: hari hari! kabe mora hoibe sudina
IDX.search: hari hari kabe mora hoibe sudina govardhana girivare parama nibhrte ghare rai kanu karaiba sayana bhrngarera jale ranga carana dhoyaiba muchaba apana cikure kanaka samputa kari karpura tambula puri jogaiba duhuka adhare
IDX.author: narottama-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: hari hari! kabe mora hoibe sudina govardhana girivare, parama nibhṛte ghare, rāi kānu karāiba śayana bhṛṅgārera jale rāṅgā-, caraṇa dhoyāiba, muchaba āpana cikure kanaka-sampuṭa kari’, ‘karpūra tāmbūla pūri’ jogāiba dūhuka adhare priya-sakhī-gaṇa-saṅge, sevana kariba raṅge, caraṇa seviba nija kare dūhuka kamala-diṭhi, kautuke heraba, dūhu aṅga pulaka antare mallikā mālatī jūthi, nānā phule mālā gāṅthi, kabe diba dohāra galāya soṇāra kaṭorā kari, kārpūra candana bhari’, kabe diba dohākāra gāya āra kabe emana habe, dūhu-mukha-nirakhiba, līlārasa nikuñja-śayane śrī-kundalatāra saṅge, keli-kautuka raṅge, narottama karibe śravaṇe
IDX.en_translation:
O Lord Hari! When will my auspicious day come? On Govardhana Hill, in a most secluded place, I will make Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa lie down to rest. 

With water from a jeweled pitcher I will wash Their reddish lotus feet and wipe them with my own hair. Taking a golden casket and filling it with camphor and betel, I will offer it to Their lips. 

With my dear companions I will serve Them joyfully, serving Their lotus feet with my own hands. I will behold Their lotus-like glances with delight, and Their forms will cause ecstasy within my heart. 

When will I string garlands of jasmine and various other flowers and place them around Their necks? Taking a golden cup and filling it with camphor and sandalwood paste, when will I anoint Their bodies? 

And when will it happen that I will gaze upon Their faces, reveling in the nectar of Their pastimes as They recline in the secluded grove? With Śrī Kundalatā, in the joy of playful sport, Narottama will listen.

IDX.first_line: hari hari! kabe mora hoibe sudine
IDX.search: hari hari kabe mora hoibe sudine kelikautuka range kariba sevane lalita visakha sane jateka sangira gane mandali kariba doha meli rai kanu kare dhari nrtya kare phiri phiri nirakhi gonaba kutuhali
IDX.author: narottama-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: hari hari! kabe mora hoibe sudine kelikautuka raṅge kariba sevane lalitā-viśākhā sane, jateka saṅgīra gaṇe, maṇḍalī kariba doha meli’ rāi kānu-kare dhari’, nṛtya kare phiri’ phiri’, nirakhi’ goṅā’ba kutūhalī alasa-viśrāma-ghare, govardhana-girivare, rāikānu karibe śayana narottama-dāsa kaya, ei jena mora haya, anukṣaṇa caraṇa sevana
IDX.en_translation:
Hari Hari! When will I have that auspicious day when I will perform service in the playful pastimes? 

With Lalitā and Viśākhā, and all the group of companions, I will make a circle, bringing the Two together. Holding the hands of Rāi and Kānu, They will dance round and round; I will pass the time watching with curiosity. 

In the house of leisurely rest, on the best of hills, Govardhana, Rāi and Kānu will lie down. Narottama Dāsa says: May this be mine—service to the feet at every moment.

IDX.first_line: hari hari! kata dine hena daśā haba
IDX.search: hari hari kata dine hena dasa haba sri rasa manjari sange sri mani manjari range sri rupera anuga haiba susitala vrndavana ratnavedi susobhana tahe manimaya simhasana hema nila kantidhara rai kanu sundara tahe basaiba duijana
IDX.author: narottama-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: hari hari! kata dine hena daśā haba śrī-rāsa-mañjarī saṅge śrī-maṇi-mañjarī rāṅge śrī-rūpera anugā haiba suśītala vṛndāvana ratnavedī suśobhana tāhe maṇimaya siṁhāsana hema nīla-kāntidhara rāi-kānu sundara tāhe basāiba duijana sakhīra ādeśa habe cāmara ḍhulāba kabe tāmbula jogāba cāṅda-mukhe ānandita ha’ba sadā śuddha-bhāve prema-kathā duhāra pīriti rasa-sukhe mallikā mālatī jūthī nānā phule mālā gāṅthi parāiba duhāra galāye rasera ālasa kāle basiyā caraṇa tale sevana kariba duhāra pāye rādhā-kṛṣṇa prāṇapati jīvane maraṇe gati ihā vine āra nāhi mane śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-prāṇa svarūpa-rūpa-sanātana narottama ei nivedana
IDX.en_translation:
O Lord Hari! When will I achieve such a state? In the company of Śrī Rāsa-mañjarī and Śrī Maṇi-mañjarī, I will become a follower of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. 

In the very cool and beautiful Vṛndāvana, on a beautiful, jewel-studded altar, I will see a jewel-studded throne. Upon that throne, I will seat the beautiful Divine Couple, who have golden and dark-blue complexions. 

When will I receive the order of the gopī friends to fan Them with a whisk? When will I offer betel nuts to Their moon-like faces? I will always be joyful, purely devoted to topics of divine love and the happiness of Their mutual affection. 

Stringing garlands of various jasmine flowers, I will place them around Their necks. When They are resting, I will sit at Their lotus feet and render service to both of Them. 

Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa are the Lords of my life, my only shelter in life and in death. Without Them, nothing else remains in my mind. Svarūpa Dāmodara, Rūpa Gosvāmī, and Sanātana Gosvāmī are the very life of Lord Caitanya. This is the humble prayer of Narottama Dāsa.

IDX.first_line: hari hari! ki mora karama abhāga
IDX.search: hari hari ki mora karama abhaga viphale jivana gela hrdaye rahila sela nahi bhela hari anuraga jajna dana tirtha snana punya karma japa dhyana akarane saba gela mohe bujhilama mane hena upahasa haya jena vastrahina alankara dehe
IDX.author: narottama-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: hari hari! ki mora karama abhāga viphale jīvana gela, hṛdaye rahila śela, nāhi bhela hari-anurāga jajña, dāna, tīrtha-snāna, puṇya-karma, japa, dhyāna, akāraṇe saba gela mohe bujhilāma mane hena, upahāsa haya jena, vastrahīna alaṅkāra dehe sādhu-mukhe kathāmṛta, śuniyā vimala cita, nāhi bhela aparādha-kāraṇa satata asatsaṅga, sakali hoila bhaṅga, ki kariba āile śamana śruti-smṛti sadā rabe, śuniyāchi ei sabe, haripada abhaya śaraṇa janama loiyā sukhe, kṛṣṇa nā balinu mukhe, nā karinu se-rūpa bhāvana rādhā-kṛṣṇa dūhu pāya, tanu mana rahu tāya, āra dūre jāuka vāsanā narottama dāse kaya, āra mora nāhi bhaya, tanu-mana saṁpinu āpanā
IDX.en_translation:
O Lord Hari! What unfortunate destiny is mine! My life passed in vain, and a spear remained in my heart, for I did not attain affection for You. 

Sacrifice, charity, bathing in holy places, pious activities, chanting, and meditation—all were lost fruitlessly due to illusion. I realize now that it was like a mockery, like wearing decorations on a body without clothes. 

From the mouths of the saints I heard the nectar of Your words, yet with my impure heart, I did not avoid committing offenses. Constant association with the impious broke everything; what will I do when the messenger of death arrives? 

The scriptures will always declare that Your feet are a fearless shelter—I have heard all of this. Though born in comfort, I did not utter Kṛṣṇa’s name, nor did I meditate on His form. 

May my body and mind remain at the feet of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, and may all other desires depart far away. Narottama dāsa says: I have no more fear, for I have surrendered my body and mind completely.

IDX.first_line: hari hari! kṛpā kari’ rākha nija pade
IDX.search: hari hari krpa kari rakha nija pade kama krodha chaya jane lana phire nanasthane visaya bhunjaya nanamate hoiya mayara dasa kari nana abhilasa tomara smarana gela durearthalabha ei ase kapata vaisnava vese bhramiya bulaye ghare ghare
IDX.author: narottama-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: hari hari! kṛpā kari’ rākha nija pade kāma-krodha chaya jane, lañā phire nānāsthāne, viṣaya-bhuñjāya nānāmate hoiyā māyāra dāsa, kari’ nānā abhilāṣa, tomāra smaraṇa gela dūrearthalābha ei āśe, kapaṭa vaiṣṇava-veśe, bhramiyā bulaye ghare ghare aneka duḥkhera pare, layechile vrajapure, kṛpāḍora galāya bāndhiyādaivamāyā balātkāre, khasāiyā sei ḍore, bhava-kūpe dileka ḍāriyā punaḥ jadi kṛpā kari’, e janāra keśe dhari’, ṭāniyā tulaha vraja-dhāmetabe se dekhiye bhāla, natubā parāṇa gela, kahe dīna dāsa narottame
IDX.en_translation:
O Lord Hari! Please bestow Your mercy and keep me at Your feet. Lust, anger, and the other four enemies take me and drag me to various places, making me enjoy material things in various ways. 

Becoming a servant of illusion and following various desires, Your remembrance went far away. In the hope of gaining wealth and wearing the guise of a deceitful devotee, I wander from house to house. 

After much suffering, You had taken me to the town of Vraja, tying a rope of mercy around my neck. But the divine energy of illusion forcefully untied that rope and threw me back into the well of material existence. 

Again, if You bestow mercy, catching me by the hair and pulling me up to Vrajadhāma—then it will be good. Otherwise, my life is lost. So says the humble servant Narottama.

IDX.search: hari hari viphale janama gonainu manusya janama paiya radha krsna na bhajiya janiya suniya visa khainu golokera prema dhana harinama sankirtana rati na janmila kene tayasamsara visanale divanisi hiya jvale judaite na kainu upaya
IDX.author: narottama-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: hari hari! viphale janama goṅāinu manuṣya-janama pāiyā, rādhā-kṛṣṇa nā bhajiyā, jāniyā śuniyā viṣa khāinu golokera prema-dhana, harināma-saṅkīrtana, rati nā janmila kene tāyasaṁsāra-viṣānale, divāniśi hiyā jvale, juḍāite nā kainu upāya vrajendra-nandana jei, śacī-suta haila sei, balarāma hoila nitāidīna hīna jata chila, hari-nāme uddhārila, tā’ra sākṣī jagāi-mādhāi hā hā prabhu nandasuta, vṛṣabhānu-sutāyuta, karuṇā karaha eibāra narottama-dāsa kaya, nā ṭhelio rāṅgāpāya, tomā vinā ke āche āmāra
IDX.en_translation:
Hari Hari! I spent my life in vain. Having obtained a human birth, not worshipping Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, I knowingly drank poison. 

The treasure of Goloka’s love, the saṅkīrtana of Hari’s Name—why did I not develop attachment for it? My heart burns day and night in the poisonous fire of worldly existence; I did not make a way to cool it. 

He who is Vrajendra-nandana became Śacī-suta; Balarāma became Nitāi. He delivered all the lowly and destitute by the Holy Name; Jagāi and Mādhāi are the witnesses to that. 

Alas, alas! O Lord, Son of Nanda, along with the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu, be merciful this time. Narottama Dāsa says: Do not push me away from Your reddish feet; who do I have except You?

IDX.first_line: hari he! 1 prapañce paḍiyā agati hoiyā
IDX.search: hari he 1 prapance padiya agati hoiya na dekhi upaya ara agatira gati carane sarana tomaya karinu sara karama geyana kichu nahi mora sadhana bhajana nai tumi krpamaya ami ta kangala ahaituki krpa cai
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
hari he! (1) 
prapañce paḍiyā, agati hoiyā, 
nā dekhi’ upāya āra 
agatira gati, caraṇe śaraṇa, 
tomāya karinu sāra 

karama geyāna, kichu nāhi mora, 
sādhana-bhajana nāi 
tumi kṛpāmaya, āmi ta’ kāṅgāla, 
ahaitukī kṛpā cāi 

vākya-mano-vega, krodha-jihvā-vega, 
udara-upastha-vega 
miliyā e-saba, saṁsāre bhāsāye, 
diteche paramodvega 

aneka jatane, se-saba damane, 
chāḍiyāchi āśā āmi 
anāthera nātha, ḍāki tava nāma, 
ekhana bharasā tumi
IDX.translation_intro: From The Harmonist, March 1929. Edited by Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī.
IDX.en_translation:
Hari! Fallen into this world, Rendered helpless, I find no other way of deliverance, Guide of the guideless! The Refuge of Thy feet I seek as essential. 

Capacity for work or Knowledge I have none; I neither serve Thee nor try. Thou art full of mercy, I am destitute, indeed; Thy causeless mercy I crave. 

The activities of speach and mind, Anger, palate, The stomach and organ of generation,- All these joining together, Casting me adrift on the stream of the world, Are giving me great trouble. 

The hope of subduing them, By using every care, I have given up. Lord of the lordless! I call upon Thy Name. Thou art now the Hope.

IDX.first_line: hari he! 2 arthera sañcaye viṣaya prayāse
IDX.search: hari he 2 arthera sancaye visaya prayase ana katha prajalpane ana adhikara niyama agrahe asat sanga samghatane asthira siddhante rahinu majiya hari bhakti raila dure e hrdaye matra parahimsa mada pratistha sathata sphure
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
hari he! (2) 
arthera sañcaye, viṣaya-prayāse, 
āna kathā prajalpane 
āna adhikāra, niyama-āgrahe, 
asat-saṅga-saṁghaṭane 

asthira siddhānte, rahinu majiyā, 
hari-bhakti raila dūre 
e hṛdaye mātra, parahiṁsā-mada, 
pratiṣṭhā, śaṭhatā, sphure 

e saba āgraha, chāḍite nārinu, 
āpana doṣete mari’ 
janama biphala, hoila āmāra, 
ekhana ki kari’ hari 

āmi ta’ patita, patita-pāvana, 
tomāra pavitra nāma 
se-sambandha dhari’, tomāra caraṇe, 
śaraṇa loinu hāma
IDX.translation_intro: From The Harmonist, April 1929. Edited by Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī.
IDX.en_translation:
Hari! Gathering wealth, Striving after things of this world, Idle talk on topics of the hour, Misunderstanding the sphere of my duties, Adherence to the letter of the law, Contriving to mix with worldly people, 

Uncertainty of principle, - Continue to enamour me still. Devotion to Hari is afar off. This heart only breeds Malice against others, pride, Desire for fame and cunning, 

All these inclinations I could not leave. I am ruined by my own fault, This birth of mine Is rendered useless Hari! what now I am to do? 

I am fallen, indeed, Thy Holy Name Is Saviour of those gone astray. By this relationship At Thy feet I take Refuge.

IDX.first_line: hari he! 3 bhajane utsāha bhaktite viśvāsa
IDX.search: hari he 3 bhajane utsaha bhaktite visvasa prema labhe dhairya dhana bhakti anukula karma pravartana asat sanga visarjana bhakti sadacara ei chaya guna nahila amara natha kemane bhajiba tomara carana chadiya mayara satha
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
hari he! (3) 
bhajane utsāha, bhaktite viśvāsa, 
prema-lābhe dhairya-dhana 
bhakti-anukūla, karma-pravartana, 
asat-saṅga visarjana 

bhakti-sadācāra, ei chaya guṇa, 
nahila āmāra nātha! 
kemane bhajiba, tomāra caraṇa, 
chāḍiyā māyāra sātha 

garhita ācāre, rahilāma maji’, 
nā karinu sādhu-saṅga 
la’ye sādhu-veśa, āne upadeśi, 
e baḍa māyāra raṅga 

e hena daśāya, ahaitukī kṛpā, 
tomāra pāiba, hari! 
śrī guru-āśraye, ḍākiba tomāya, 
kabe vā minati kari’
IDX.translation_intro: From The Harmonist, April 1929. Edited by Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī.
IDX.en_translation:
Hari! Zeal in serving, Faith in devotion, The treasure of patience in attainment of love, Devising act That conduces to devotion, Abandonment of worldly association, 

Approved devotional practice, These six good qualities, Lord, have never been mine. How worship Thy feet, Giving up all affinity with Thy delusive power? 

Of improper activities I am so enamoured; Association with sadhus I have not practised. Assuming the garb of a sadhu I instruct others. This is a funny contrivance of Maya! 

In such condition I shal! receive, Hari, Thy cause-less mercy. Under the guidance of the good preceptor, O, when shall I call upon Thee With humble entreaty?

IDX.first_line: hari he! 4 dāna pratigraha mitho gupta kathā
IDX.search: hari he 4 dana pratigraha mitho gupta katha bhaksana bhojana dana sangera laksana ei chaya haya ihate bhaktira prana tattva na bujhiye jnane va ajnane asate e saba kari bhakti harainu samsari hoinu sudure rahile hari
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
hari he! (4) 
dāna-pratigraha, mitho gupta-kathā, 
bhakṣaṇa, bhojana-dāna 
saṅgera lakṣaṇa, ei chaya haya, 
ihāte bhaktira prāṇa 

tattva nā bujhiye, jñāne vā ajñāne, 
asate e’ saba kari’ 
bhakti hārāinu, saṁsārī hoinu, 
sudūre rahile hari 

kṛṣṇa-bhakta-jane, e saṅga-lakṣaṇe, 
ādara kariba jabe 
bhakti-mahādevī, āmāra hṛdaya-, 
āsane basibe tabe 

joṣit-saṅgī jana, kṛṣṇābhakta āra, 
dūhu-saṅga parihari’ 
tava bhakta-jana-, saṅga anukṣaṇa, 
kabe vā hoibe hari
IDX.translation_intro: From The Harmonist, August 1929. Edited by Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī.
IDX.en_translation:
Hari! Making and receiving gifts, Mutual confidential talk, Accepting and offering food, These six are indications Of intimate association; These are the life of devotion. 

Not understanding the truth,- Consciously or unconsciously, Enacting these with sinners I have missed devotion, Am become a worldling; Thou, Hari, art left afar.

Those who are addicted to women, Those who are averse to Krishna,- Abandoning the society of both, When shall I cultivate, O Hari, Constant association with Thy devotees?

Hari- If one, initiated, or no, who is free From the offence of evil association, Sing Thy Name,- In my mind I will him esteem, Knowing him to be my kin.

O, when shall I have the quality Of a guileless mind Towards the Vaishnava? O, when shall I hie To Thy abode of Braja After crossing the ocean of this world?

The Vaishnava is Thy own, An expression of Thy Divine power. May I obtain bis mercy! Then my steps Will turn toward Thee And I shall attain the shade of Thy feet.

Lord Hari, seeing His own incomparable self reflected in a mirror in Vraja and desiring to taste His own sweetness completely—just as Rādhā or Her dearmost companions do—took another golden form and was born in the land of Bengal. Will the Son of Mother Śacī ever again come before my eyes? 

He is sweet like a bath in the honey of love within Advaita Ācārya’s heart. His feet are repeatedly worshipped by Govinda Dāsa’s excellent service. His face is offered ārati by Svarūpa Dāmodara’s millions of life-breaths. Will the Son of Mother Śacī ever again come before my eyes? 

Wearing a loincloth and over it an outer saffron cloth, His grand body, like a golden mountain, is completely served by its own effulgence. Joyfully and loudly singing His own sweet Holy Names, will the Son of Mother Śacī ever again come before my eyes? 

That which was unknown even to previous sages—the creeper of devotion, hidden in the Vedas and bearing the fruit of pure, brilliant ecstatic love—the merciful Lord manifested that with great mercy in Bengal. Will the Son of Mother Śacī ever again come before my eyes? 

The Lord accepted the devotees from Bengal as His own. Instructing them like a father, He said: “Chant the Names of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa according to a counting method, O devotees!” Will the Son of Mother Śacī ever again come before my eyes? 

Seeing the Lord of Purī in front of Him with great streams of love, His tall and effulgent body is bathed by the flowing tears from His eyes. He always stands at the Garuḍa pillar in the temple. Will the Son of Mother Śacī ever again come before my eyes? 

Joyfully biting His lower lip with His teeth and placing His left hand on His hip, He shines beautifully. With countless ecstatic shivers and eager to dance, He rises up in love. Will the Son of Mother Śacī ever again come before my eyes? 

Overwhelmed by separation from the Moon of Gokula on the banks of a river, He creates another river with the incessant flow of His tears. Repeatedly falling into unconsciousness, He makes the entire world appear like a corpse. Will the Son of Mother Śacī ever again come before my eyes? 

This eight-verse prayer of the Son of Mother Śacī bestows all desires. He who recites this with a very clear mind due to increasing humility—Lord Caitanya, being overwhelmed by intense mercy, will immerse him in the great ocean of love, which is famous for bestowing divine nectar.

IDX.author: jayadeva gosvāmī
IDX.verses:
he govinda he gopāla 
keśava mādhava dīna-dayāla 

tumi parama dayāla prabhu, parama dayāla 
keśava mādhava dīna dayāla 

pīta-vasana pari mayūrera śikha dhari 
muralīra vāṇī-tule bole rādhā-nāma 

tumi moder gopāla prabhu, moder gopāla 
keśava mādhava dīna-dayāla 

bhava-bhaya-bhañjana śrī madhusūdana 
vipada-bhañjana tumi nārāyaṇa
IDX.en_translation:
O Govinda! O Gopāla! O Keśava! O Mādhava! O You who are compassionate to the fallen! 

You are supremely merciful, my Lord, supremely merciful. O Keśava! O Mādhava! O You who are compassionate to the fallen! 

Wearing yellow garments and holding a peacock feather, He plays His flute and utters the Name of Rādhā. 

You are our Gopāla, my Lord, our Gopāla! O Keśava! O Mādhava! O You who are compassionate to the fallen! 

He is the destroyer of the fear of material existence, Lord Madhusūdana. You are the dispeller of all dangers, Lord Nārāyaṇa.

govinda dāmodara mādhaveti

govinda āve mam gṛha khele

govinda dāmodara mādhaveti 

mātā yaśodā hariko jagāve,

govinda dāmodara mādhaveti

arthānurāgī dhana sañcayommē 
ye hī nirālī dhvani gā rahe haīṅ, 
govinda dāmodara mādhaveti 

le ke karommē dohani anokhī, 
gau dugdha kāḍhe avalā navelī 
gau dugdha dhārā saṅga gā rahī hai, 
govinda dāmodara mādhaveti 

jāge pujārī hari mandirommē, 
jāke jagāveṁ hariko sabere 
he kṣīrasindhu ava netra kholo, 
govinda dāmodara mādhaveti 

soyā kisīkā suta pālanemē, 
ḍorī karo se jaba kheñcatī hai 
ho prema magnā usane pukārā, 
govinda dāmodara mādhaveti 

royā kisīkā suta pālanemē, 
ho prema magnā usane pukārā 
rovo na gāvo prabhu saṅga mere, 
govinda dāmodara mādhaveti 

koī navelī patiko jagāve, 
prāṇeśa jāgo ava nīnda tyāgo 
belā yahī hai hari gīta gāvo, 
govinda dāmodara mādhaveti
IDX.en_translation:
O Kṛṣṇa! O Yādava! O friend! O Govinda! O Dāmodara! O Mādhava! When someone drops the churning rod into the yogurt, the thought of the butter-thief Kṛṣṇa immediately comes to mind. 

With a choked voice she calls out: “O Govinda! O Dāmodara! O Mādhava!” O Kṛṣṇa! O Yādava! O friend! O Govinda! O Dāmodara! O Mādhava! 

A woman cleaning her courtyard prays: “May Lord Govinda come and play in my house.” While meditating, she sings these words: “O Govinda! O Dāmodara! O Mādhava!” 

Mother Yaśodā awakens Lord Hari: “Wake up, get up, O Mohana! Open Your eyes! The cowherd boys are standing at the door calling for You: O Govinda! O Dāmodara! O Mādhava!” 

The one devoted to knowledge in his books, and the one devoted to wealth while accumulating riches—they too are singing this unique sound: “O Govinda! O Dāmodara! O Mādhava!” 

Holding a milking pot in her hands, a young woman milks the cow. Along with the stream of milk, she sings: “O Govinda! O Dāmodara! O Mādhava!” 

The priests wake up in the Lord’s temples and go to awaken Him in the morning: “O Ocean of milk! Now please open Your eyes! O Govinda! O Dāmodara! O Mādhava!” 

When a mother pulls the string of her child’s cradle, she calls out in love: “O Govinda! O Dāmodara! O Mādhava!” 

When a child cries in the cradle, the mother calls out in love: “Do not cry! Sing with me, O Lord: O Govinda! O Dāmodara! O Mādhava!” 

A young woman awakens her husband: “O Lord of my life! Wake up and abandon sleep! This is the time to sing the Lord’s song: O Govinda! O Dāmodara! O Mādhava!”

IDX.verses: hede he nāgaravara, śuna he muralīdhara, nivedana kari tuyā pāya caraṇa-nakhara-maṇi, jena cāṅdera gāṅthani, bhāla śobhe āmāra galāya śrīdāma-sudāma-saṅge, jakhana vane jāo raṅge, takhana āmi duyāre dāṅḍāye mane kari saṅge jāi, gurujanāra bhaya pāi, āṅkhi rahe tuyā pāne ceye cāi navīna meghapāne, tuyā bandhu paḍe mane! elāile keśa nāhi bāṅdhi randhana-śālāte jāi, tuyā vadhu guṇa gāi, dhūyāra chalanā kari’ kāndi maṇi noo, māṇika noo, āṅcale bāṅdhile roo, phula noo je keśe kari veśe nārī nā karita vidhi, tuyā hena guṇanidhi, loiyā phiritāma deśe deśe aguru candana hoitāma, tuyā aṅge mākhā roitāma, ghāmiyā paḍitāma rāṅgā pāya ki mora manera sādha, vāmana haye cāṅde hāta, vidhi ki sādha pūrābe āmāya narottama-dāse kaya, śuna ohe dayāmaya, tumi āmāya nā chāḍiha dayā je dina tomāra bhāve, āmāra parāṇa jābe, sei dina dio padachāyā
IDX.en_translation:
O best among the charming lovers! Listen, O flute-player! I offer this plea at Your feet. The jewels of Your toenails are like a string of moons; how well they would adorn my neck! 

When You go to the forest with joy in the company of Śrīdāma and Sudāma, I stand at my doorway. I think of going with You, but I fear my elders; thus my eyes remain fixed upon You. 

I look at the new clouds and remember You, my beloved! My hair has come loose, yet I do not tie it. I go to the kitchen and sing Your glories, pretending that my tears are caused by the smoke. 

You are not a jewel or a ruby that I can tie in the end of my cloth, nor are You a flower to adorn my hair. If fate had not made me a woman, I would take such a treasure of virtues as You and wander from country to country. 

I wish I were aloe wood or sandalwood paste, so I could remain smeared on Your body. Sweating, I would fall upon Your reddish feet. What a desire is in my mind—like a dwarf reaching for the moon! Will fate ever fulfill this desire for me? 

Narottama dāsa says: listen, O compassionate Lord! Please do not withdraw Your mercy from me. On the day my life departs, immersed in Your love, please grant me the shade of Your feet.

I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Śrīla Bhakti Vilāsa Tīrtha Gosvāmī Mahārāja. His beautiful body is like molten gold, he is established in truth, and he possesses a pure character. He is full of compassion and is always joyful. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Śrīla Tīrtha Mahārāja. He is expert in destroying the miseries of material existence. His beautiful face is adorned with a gentle smile, and his charming speech is filled with the true principles of devotional service. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Śrīla Tīrtha Mahārāja. He enriched the glories of Śrīdhāma Māyāpura and was very knowledgeable in the path of Deity worship. He graced the renowned Caitanya Maṭha like a blooming lotus. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Śrīla Tīrtha Mahārāja. He established the beautiful house of Lord Caitanya’s teachings and was adorned with profound spiritual glories. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Śrīla Tīrtha Mahārāja. His peaceful mind is free from the three-fold miseries, and he shines with the marks of a great personality. He is the joy of the transcendental sannyāsī community. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Śrīla Tīrtha Mahārāja. He is the abode of ultimate welfare and follows the path of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. He is intoxicated by drinking the nectar of Lord Gaura’s pastimes. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Śrīla Tīrtha Mahārāja. He is bathed in the most brilliant nectar of divine love and is knowledgeable in the confidential mysteries of the Vṛndāvana forest. He is enchanted by the Names of Śrīmati Rādhikā and Lord Mādhava. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Śrīla Tīrtha Mahārāja. He is supremely worthy of refuge and is exceedingly expert in the knowledge of transcendental sound. He is my very life.

When will that time come, when Vilāsa Mañjarī and Anaṅga Mañjarī, seeing me, will with great mercy speak these essential words: 

“Come, come, friend! We will acknowledge you today among Śrī Lalitā’s associates. Leaving aside household concerns, worship Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, abandoning worldly shame.” 

Hearing those sweet words, I will take shelter at their lotus feet, and both of them, with mercy, will take me to Lalitā’s abode. 

Beautiful Lalitā, becoming merciful, will make me her maidservant. In her own bower’s cottage, she will give me residence, knowing my desire to serve.

IDX.en_translation:
All glories to the beautiful Lord who sports in the groves! His complexion is like a sapphire, His ears are adorned with fully blossomed nīpa flowers, and He wears a garland of berries on His broad chest. 

All glories to the charming Lord who sports in the groves! He is like the chakora bird for the moon-like face of Rādhā, the thief of the steadfastness of all the cowherd girls, and skillful in His dancing. 

All glories to the Lord who sports in the groves! He is renowned for destroying the festival of Indra, thereby removing his pride, and for lifting a mountain to protect the cowherd community with His pastimes. 

All glories to the Lord who sports in the groves! With the enchanting movements of His flute, He declares the festival of Cupid. His character is praised by flocks of parrots and mynas. 

All glories to the Lord who sports in the groves! His lower garment surpasses the luster of pure gold, His topknot is adorned with peacock feathers, and He delights the young women of Vraja with His fresh youth. 

All glories to the Lord who sports in the groves! He is smeared with fragrant sandalwood paste for decoration, His waist is resplendent with a golden belt, and He is like an elephant playing with the beauty of Rādhā. 

All glories to the Lord who sports in the groves! His forehead shines brightly with sacred markings, His garland of jasmine flowers sways playfully, and He secretly meets the beautiful-browed maidens in mountain caves. 

All glories to the Lord who sports in the groves! With the dance of His restless and charming sidelong glances, He disrupts all the duties of the cowherd women, and He is the lover of the love-intoxicated daughter of Vṛṣabhānu. 

Whoever recites this charming eight-verse song about the sweet pastimes of the Lord who sports in the groves will attain great fortune and devotion to the worship of His lotus feet.

If your heart is always intent on drinking the nectar-like taste of Hari’s lotus feet, abandoning the home full of the mood of Kali-yuga, worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Wealth, youth, life, and the happiness of a kingdom are not eternal; they are constantly perishing. Give up all mundane talks, which are useless. Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

And O friend, the happiness of association with women, in the end, is fearful and takes away one’s human goals. Being intoxicated by the nectar-like taste of Hari-nāma, worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

The taste of mundane poetry is not true poetic taste. The taste of Gaura, who purifies Kali-yuga, is indeed the true taste. Enough of cultivating other topics. Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Whose beautiful left side is accompanied by Vṛṣabhānu-sutā; the hero on the bank of the Yamunā, son of Nanda; engaged in the joyous sweet music of the flute- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Situated in the midst of Hari-kīrttana with His own associates, surrounded by them, Hari with a golden luster; the sole ocean of mercy for the people of Gaura-deśa- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Whose home is surrounded by Girirājasutā; the master of the nine continents, captivating the minds of ascetics; praised by hosts of demigods, with His beloved- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Holding the mood of a club for the dogs of Kali; intent on giving the great medicine of Hari-nāma; embodying a beautiful form, full of compassion for the distressed fallen- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Whose mercy makes no distinction between enemy and friend, constantly arising from His lotus-like face; that Akṛṣṇa here, the son of Vraja-rāja- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Here, the all-pervading Lord praised in the Upaniṣads; the son of Dvijarāja, Hari with a golden luster; plays in His own abode with His friends- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

The best of all avatāras, fully complete; the Supreme Truth, full of self-manifested pastimes here; the hidden rasa of the ocean of Vraja-dhāma- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Whose mercy is not dependent on Vedic knowledge, social status, or wealth, powerful in generating devotion without these. O friend, He is indeed the path of causeless ecstatic love- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Even when in the grip of a crocodile, in the middle of a lake, He delivered that distressed living entity. He is unborn; whose strength is inconceivable, a desire-tree of auspiciousness- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

With a mind pleased by the penance of Surabhīndra, Hari, possessing a beautiful complexion, appeared. That eternal happiness, who steals the patience of the sages- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

All desires, and the mentality of non-difference; give up all of this, both inauspicious and auspicious. With favor and beloved service, worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Intent on the duty of serving Hari’s servants; delighted in drinking the nectar of Hari-nāma’s rasa; endowed with humility, meekness, and compassion- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Chant Yādava, Mādhava, Kṛṣṇa, Hare! Chant Rāma, Janārddana, Keśava, O! Always the beloved Lord of Vṛṣabhānu-sutā- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Chant “Lord of the forest and mountains on the bank of the Yamunā!” Chant “Sound of the clusters of groves in Gokula forest!” Chant “O Gaura-Hari, the elixir of Rāsa!”- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Go to the nine-part forest of Gaura. Read the pastimes of Gaura-Hari with joy. Roll on the bank of the Gaṅgā marked with Gaura’s footsteps- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Remember the playful arts of Gaura and Gadādhara. Become a follower of Gaura and Gadādhara. Hear the charming narrations of Gaura and Gadādhara- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest.

IDX.search: jamalarjuna bhanjanam asrita ranjanam ahiganjana ghana lasya bharam pasupala purandaram abhisrta kandaram atisundaram aravinda karam vara gopa vadhu jana viracita pujanam uru kujana nava venu dharam smara narma vicaksanam akhila vilaksana tanu laksanam atidaksataram pranatasani panjaram namvara pinjaram arikunjara harim indumukham go mandala raksinam anukrta paksinam atidaksinam amitatma sukham guru gairika manditam anunaya panditam avakhandita puruhuta makham vraja kamala virocanam alika surocana gorocanam atitamra nakham

jamalārjuna-bhañjanam āśrita-rañjanam ahigañjana-ghana-lāsya-bharaṁ 
paśupāla-purandaram abhisṛta-kandaram atisundaram aravinda-karam 
vara-gopa-vadhū-jana-viracita-pūjanam uru-kūjana-nava-veṇu-dharaṁ 
smara-narma-vicakṣaṇam akhila-vilakṣaṇa-tanu-lakṣaṇam atidakṣataram 

praṇatāśani-pañjaram namvara-piñjaram arikuñjara-harim indumukhaṁ 
go-maṇḍala-rakṣiṇam anukṛta-pakṣiṇam atidakṣiṇam amitātma-sukham 
guru-gairika-maṇḍitam anunaya-paṇḍitam avakhaṇḍita-puruhūta-makhaṁ 
vraja-kamala-virocanam alika-surocana-gorocanam atitāmra-nakham 

unmada-rati-nāyaka-śāṇita-sāyaka-vinidhāyaka-cala-cilli-latam 
uddhata-saṅkocanam ambuja-locanam agha-mocanam amarāli-natam 
nikhilādhika-gauravam ujjvala-saurabham atigaurabha-paśupīṣu rataṁ 
mṛdu-pada-pallavam abhram u vallabha-ruci-durlabha-sa-vilāsa-gatam 

bhuja-mūrdhni viśaṅkaṭam adhigata-śaṅkaṭa-nata-kaṅkaṭam aṭavīṣu calaṁ 
navanīpa-karambita-vana-rolambitam avalambita-kala-kaṇṭha-kalam 
durjana-tṛṇa-pāvakam anucara-śāvaka-nikarāvakam aruṇoṣṭha-dalaṁ 
nija-vikrama-carcita-bhuja-guru-garvita-gandharvita-danujārdi-balam 

śruti-ratna-vibhūṣaṇa-ruci-jita-pūṣaṇam alidūṣaṇa-nayanānta-gatiṁ 
yamunā-taṭa-talpita-puṣpam analpita-mada-jalpita-dayitāpta-ratim 
vandemahi vandita-nandam amandita-kulam andhita-khala-kaṁsa-matiṁ 
tvām iha dāmodara haladhara-sodara hara no daram anubaddha-ratim
IDX.en_translation:
Breaker of the twin Arjuna trees, You delight those who take shelter of You. Your heavy dancing shames the dark clouds. You are the best among the protectors of the cowherds; approaching the caves, You are exceedingly beautiful, with lotus-like hands. Worshiped by excellent cowherd girls and holding a new flute with abundant sweet sounds, You are an expert in amorous pastimes and possess all extraordinary bodily characteristics. 

You are a fortress for the surrendered, wearing yellow garments—a lion to Your elephant-like enemies, with a moon-like face. Protector of the cowherd community, imitating the birds, You are very benevolent and possess unlimited inner happiness. Adorned with red chalk and expert in persuasion, You thwarted Indra’s sacrifice. You illuminate the lotus of Vṛndāvana with an excellent vermilion mark and exceedingly reddish nails. 

Your moving, creeper-like eyebrows set the sharpened arrows of the god of intoxicated love in motion. Humbling the arrogant, with lotus-like eyes, You are the liberator from sins, bowed to by hosts of demigods. You possess supreme glory and a brilliant fragrance, greatly delighting in the cowherd girls. With tender sprout-like feet, Your playful gait and dark beauty are difficult to attain even by the desires of Your most beloved devotees. 

With broad shoulders and strong arms adorned with captivating bracelets, You move through the forests. Playing amidst forests intertwined with fresh kadamba flowers and surrounded by buzzing bees, Your sweet voice is echoed by the sweet-throated birds. You are a fire to the grass-like wicked and the protector of Your young followers, with reddish petal-like lips. Your arms are anointed with Your own valor, and Your strength torments the proud demons. 

Adorned with the jewels of the Vedas, Your splendor conquers the sun-god, and Your sidelong glances shame the bees. Your beloveds attain deep love through Your intoxicating words, and flowers are spread for You on the banks of the Yamunā. We worship You, who are worshiped by Nanda, whose family is glorious, and who blinded the intelligence of the wicked king Kaṁsa. O Dāmodara, brother of Balarāma, remove our fear and grant us constant devotion.

IDX.first_line: janama saphala tā’ra kṛṣṇa daraśana jā’ra
IDX.search: janama saphala tara krsna darasana jara bhagye hoiyache ekabaravikasiya hrnnayana kari krsna darasana chade jiva cittera vikara vrndavana kelicatura vanamalitribhanga bhangima rupa vamsidhari aparupa rasa mayanidhi gunasali
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
janama saphala tā’ra, kṛṣṇa daraśana jā’ra, 
bhāgye hoiyāche ekabāravikaśiyā hṛnnayana, kari’ kṛṣṇa-daraśana, 
chāḍe jīva cittera vikāra 

vṛndāvana-kelicatura vanamālītribhaṅga-bhaṅgima rūpa, vaṁśīdhārī aparūpa, 
rasa-mayanidhi guṇaśālī 

varṇa nava-jaladhara, śire śikhi-picchavara, 
alakā tilaka śobhā pāyaparidhāne pītavāsa, vadane madhura hāsa, 
hena rūpa jagata mātāya 

indranīla jini’, kṛṣṇarūpakhāni, 
heriyā kadambamūlemana ucāṭana, nā cale caraṇa, 
saṁsāra gelāma bhule 

(sakhi he) sudhāmaya, se rūpamādhurīdekhile nayana, haya acetana, 
jhare prema-maya vāri 

kibā cūḍā śire, kibā vaṁśī kare, 
kibā se tribhaṅga-ṭhāmacaraṇa-kamale, amiyā uchale, 
tāhāte nūpuradāma 

sadā āśā kari’, bhṛṅga-rūpa dhari’, 
caraṇa-kamale sthānaanāyāse pāi, kṛṣṇa-guṇa gāi, 
āra nā bhajiba āna
IDX.en_translation:
Successful is the birth of one who has had the vision of Kṛṣṇa even once by great fortune. By opening the eyes of the heart and beholding Kṛṣṇa, the soul abandons all mental perversions. 

He is the expert lover adorned with forest flowers in His Vṛndāvana pastimes; with His unparalleled threefold-bending form and holding His flute, He is a treasure-trove of mellows endowed with all good qualities. 

His complexion is like a fresh rain cloud, and on His head is a beautiful peacock feather; curly locks and a sacred tilaka adorn Him. Dressed in yellow garments with a sweet smile on His face, such a form enchants the world. 

Surpassing the beauty of sapphire, gazing at Kṛṣṇa’s beautiful form at the base of a kadamba tree, my mind becomes agitated, my feet cannot move, and I forget the material world. 

O my friend! Nectarine and sweet is that beautiful form. Upon seeing it, the eyes become unconscious and tears of divine love flow. 

Oh, what a crown on His head! Oh, what a flute in His hand! Oh, what a charming threefold-bending posture! Nectar overflows from His lotus feet, which are adorned with anklets. 

I always hope to assume the form of a bee and easily attain a place at His lotus feet. I will sing the glories of Kṛṣṇa and serve no one else.

IDX.first_line: jāṅra nāma śravaṇe saṁsāra bandha ghuce
IDX.search: janra nama sravane samsara bandha ghuce hena prabhu avatari kaliyuge nace janra nama loi suka narada bedaya sahasra vadana prabhu jara guna gaya
IDX.author: vṛndāvana-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
jāṅra nāma śravaṇe saṁsāra-bandha ghuce 
hena prabhu avatari kaliyuge nāce 

jāṅra nāma loi śuka-nārada beḍāya 
sahasra vadana prabhu jāra guṇa gāya 

sarva-mahā-prāyaścitta je prabhura nāma 
se prabhu nācaye dekhe jata bhāgyavāna 

khrīkṛṣṇacaitanya nityānandaṭāda jāna 
vṛndāvana dāsa tachu padayuge gāna
IDX.en_translation:
By hearing whose Name the bondage of material existence is removed—such a Lord has incarnated and dances in this Age of Kali. 

Taking whose Name, the great sages Śukadeva and Nārada wander and preach; the Lord with a thousand mouths sings whose glories. 

The Name of that Lord is the greatest atonement for all sins; that Lord now dances, and only the fortunate ones are able to see this. 

Know Them to be Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya and Lord Nityānanda. Vṛndāvana Dāsa sings at Their lotus feet.

IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
jaśomatī-nandana, vrajavara-nāgara, 
gokula-rañjana kāna 
gopī-parāṇadhana, madana-manohara, 
kālīya-damana-vidhāna 

amala harināma amiya-vilāsā 
vipina-purandara, navīna-nāgaravara, 
vaṁśī-vadana, suvāsā 

vraja-jana-pālana, asurakula-nāśana, 
nanda-godhana-rākhooyālā 
govinda, mādhava, navanīta-taskara, 
sundara nanda-gopālā 

jāmuna-taṭacara, gopī-vasanahara, 
rāsa-rasika kṛpāmaya 
śrī-rādhā-vallabha, vṛndāvana-naṭavara, 
bhakativinoda-āśraya
IDX.en_translation:
The son of Yaśomatī, the chief lover of Vraja, Kṛṣṇa, who delights Gokula. The wealth of the gopīs’ lives, the enchanter of Cupid, and the subduer of the serpent Kāliya. 

Pure Harināma is a nectarine pastime. He is the Lord of the forests, the ever-fresh supreme lover, the flute-player adorned with beautiful garments. 

The protector of the people of Vraja, the destroyer of the demon dynasty, and the protector of Nanda’s cows. He is Govinda, Mādhava, the butter thief, and the beautiful cowherd boy of Nanda. 

He roams on the banks of the Yamunā, stole the garments of the gopīs, and enjoys the rāsa dance, full of mercy. He is the beloved of Śrī Rādhā, the supreme dancer of Vṛndāvana, and the shelter of Bhaktivinoda.

IDX.first_line: jat kiṅkarīṣu bahuśaḥ khalu kāku vāṇī
IDX.search: jat kinkarisu bahusah khalu kaku vani nityam parasya purusasya sikhanda mauleh tasyah kada rasa nidher vrsabhanu jayas tat keli kunja bhavanangana marjani syam jo brahma rudra suka narada bhisma mukhyair alaksito na sahasa purusasya tasya sadyo vasi karana curnam ananta saktim tam radhika carana renum anusmarami
IDX.verses:
jat-kiṅkarīṣu bahuśaḥ khalu kāku-vāṇī 
nityaṁ parasya puruṣasya śikhaṇḍa-mauleḥ 
tasyāḥ kadā rasa-nidher vṛṣabhānu-jāyās 
tat-keli-kuñja-bhavanāṅgana-marjanī syām 

jo brahma-rudra-śuka-nārada-bhīṣma-mukhyair 
ālakṣito na sahasā puruṣasya tasya 
sadyo-vaśī-karaṇa-cūrṇam ananta-śaktiṁ 
taṁ rādhikā-caraṇa-reṇum anusmarāmi 

jasyāḥ kadāpi vasanāñcala-khelanottha- 
dhanyāti-dhanya-pavanena kṛtārtha-mānī 
jogīndra-durgama-gatir madhusūdano ‘pi 
tasyā namo ‘stu vṛṣabhānu-bhuvo diśe ‘pi 

pādābjayos tava vinā vara-dāsyam eva 
nānyat kadāpi samaye kila devi jāce 
sakhyāya te mama namo ‘stu namo ‘stu nityaṁ 
dāsyāya te mama raso ‘stu raso ‘stu satyam 

hā devi kāku-bhara-gadgadayādya vācā 
jāce nipatya bhuvi daṇḍavad udbhaṭārtiḥ 
asya prasādam abudhasya janasya kṛtvā 
gāndharvike nija-gaṇe gaṇanāṁ vidhehi 

anārādhya rādhā-padāmbhoja-reṇum 
anāśritya vṛndāṭavīṁ tat-padāṅkam 
asambhāṣya tad-bhāva-gambhīra-cittān 
kutaḥ śyāma-sindho rasasyāvagāhaḥ 

bhajāmi rādhām aravinda-netrāṁ 
smarāmi rādhāṁ madhura-smitāsyām 
vadāmi rādhāṁ karuṇa-bharārdrāṁ 
tato mamānyāsti gatir na kāpi 

mahā-bhāva-svarūpā tvaṁ kṛṣṇa-priyā-varīyasi 
prema-bhakti-prade devi rādhike tvāṁ namāmy aham 

rādhe vṛndāvanādhīśe karuṇāmṛta-vāhini 
kṛpayā nija-pādābja-dāsyaṁ mahyaṁ pradīyatām 

vande nanda-vraja-strīṇāṁ, pāda-reṇum abhīkṣṇaśaḥ 
jāsāṁ hari-kathodgītaṁ, punāti bhuvana-trayam 

tavaivāsmi tavaivāsmi, na jīvāmi tvayā vinā 
iti vijñāya devi tvaṁ, naya māṁ caraṇāntikama
IDX.en_translation:
When will I be the sweeper of the courtyard of the play-grove of the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu, the ocean of rasa? The Supreme Person with a peacock-feather crown (Kṛṣṇa) always speaks many plaintive words to Her maidservants. 

I remember that dust of Rādhikā’s feet, which is the infinite power, the powder that instantly subdues that Person who is not easily perceived by Brahmā, Rudra, Śuka, Nārada, Bhīṣma, and others. 

Even Madhusūdana, whose path is difficult for the best of yogīs to attain, considers Himself successful by the most fortunate breeze arising from the playful movement of the corner of Her cloth. Obeisances to Her, and even to the direction of Vṛṣabhānu’s daughter. 

O Devi! I indeed never beg for anything else at any time except for the excellent service of Your lotus feet. Obeisances to Your friendship; obeisances always. May my taste be for Your service; may it be true. 

Alas, O Devi! Today, with a voice choked with piteous words, falling on the ground like a stick, I beg with intense distress: bestowing mercy on this ignorant person, O Gāndharvikā, please count me among Your own people. 

Without worshipping the dust of Rādhā’s lotus feet, without taking shelter of the forest of Vṛndā which bears Her footprints, without conversing with those whose hearts are deep with Her mood—how can one enter the ocean of the rasa of Śyāma? 

I worship Rādhā who has lotus eyes; I remember Rādhā who has a sweet smile on Her face; I speak of Rādhā who is melted by the burden of compassion. Therefore, I have no other goal. 

You are the form of Mahābhāva, the best of Kṛṣṇa’s beloveds. O Devi Rādhikā, bestower of loving devotion, I bow to You. 

O Rādhe! Queen of Vṛndāvana! River of the nectar of mercy! Please mercifully give me the service of Your lotus feet. 

I repeatedly offer obeisances to the dust of the feet of the women of Nanda’s Vraja, whose loud singing of the topics of Hari purifies the three worlds. 

I am Yours alone, I am Yours alone, I cannot live without You. Knowing this, O Devi, lead me to the vicinity of Your feet.

IDX.author: vidyāpati
IDX.verses:
jatane jateka dhana, pāpe vaṭāralo, 
meli meli parijana khāya 
maraṇaka beri, koi nā puchoi, 
karama saṅge cali jāya 

e hari vando tuyā pada-nāya 
tuyā pada parihari, pāpa-payonidhi, 
pāra haba kon upāya 

jāvata janama hāma, tuyā pada nā sevinu, 
juvatī matimaya meli 
amṛta tyaji kiye, halāhala piyanu, 
sampade vipadahi bheli 

bhaṇahū vidyāpati, leha mane gaṇi, 
kahile ki bāḍhaba kāje 
sāṅjhaka beri, seva koi māgoi, 
heroite tuyā pada lāje
IDX.en_translation:
Whatever wealth I accumulated with effort, I earned through sin, and my family consumed it. At the time of death, no one will care; only my past actions will go with me. 

O Lord Hari! I worship Your lotus feet. Having abandoned Your feet, how can I cross this ocean of sin? 

Throughout my life, I did not serve Your feet, being absorbed in the intoxication of youth and delusion. Abandoning nectar, I drank poison, and my prosperity has turned into misfortune. 

Vidyāpati says: “Consider this in your heart—what more will be gained by speaking? At the end of my life, who will ask for service? I am ashamed to even look at Your lotus feet.”
