prema se kaho! śrī kṛṣṇa caitanya, prabhu nityānanda, śrī advaita, gadādhara, śrīvāsādi gaura-bhakta-vṛnda kī jaya! śrī antardvīpa māyāpura, sīmantadvīpa, godrumadvīpa, madhyadvīpa, koladvīpa, ṛtudvīpa, jahnudvīpa, modradrumadvīpa, rudradvīpātmaka śrī navadvīpa-dhāma kī jaya! śrī śrī rādhā-kṛṣṇa gopa, gopī, go, govardhana, dvādaśa vanātmaka śrī vraja-maṇḍala kī jaya! śrī rādhā-kuṇḍa, śyāma-kuṇḍa, gaṅgā, yamunā, tulasī, bhakti-devī kī jaya! śrīmatī vṛndā-devī kī jaya! śrī paurṇamāsī yogamāyā kī jaya! śrī gopīśvara mahādeva kī jaya! śrī jagannātha, baladeva, subhadrā, sudarśana cakra jiu kī jaya! śrī kṣetra-maṇḍala kī jaya! sarva-vighna-vināśakārī śrī nṛsiṁhadeva bhagavān kī jaya! bhakta-pravara śrī prahlāda mahārāja kī jaya! cāri-dhāma kī jaya! cāri-sampradāya kī jaya! cāri-ācārya kī jaya! ākara maṭha-rāja śrī caitanya maṭha kī jaya! śrī śrī keśavajī gauḍīya maṭha o tat-śākhā maṭha samūha kī jaya! grantha-rāja śrīmad-bhāgavatam kī jaya! bṛhat-mṛdaṅga kī jaya! śrī harināma-saṅkīrtana kī jaya! ananta-koṭi vaiṣṇava-vṛnda kī jaya! samāgata bhakta-vṛnda kī jaya! śrī nitāi-gaura-premānande! hari hari bol!
IDX.en_translation:
Glory to Śrī Guru and Śrī-Gaurāṅga, and victory to the expert in musical arts who lifts Govardhana Hill and plays joyful pastimes, Rādhā-Vinoda-bihārī! 

Victory to the one who has entered the eternal pastimes and resides at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, His Divine Grace Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī, King among renunciates! 

Glory to the one who has entered the eternal pastimes and resides at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, His Divine Grace Bhaktivedānta Vāmana Gosvāmī, King among renunciates! 

Victory to the one who has entered the eternal pastimes and resides at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, His most respectful Divine Grace Bhaktivedānta Svāmī, King among renunciates! 

Glory to the one who has entered the eternal pastimes and resides at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, His most respectful Divine Grace Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī, King among renunciates! 

Victory to the one who has entered the eternal pastimes and resides at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, His most respectful Divine Grace Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Prabhupāda! 

Glory to the one who has entered the eternal pastimes, the topmost supreme devotee of the Lord, His Divine Grace Gaurakiśora dāsa Bābājī, King among renunciates! 

Victory to the one who has entered the eternal pastimes, His Divine Grace Saccidānanda Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura! 

Glory to the one who has entered the eternal pastimes, the universal emperor of all Vaiṣṇavas, His Divine Grace Jagannātha dāsa Bābājī, King among renunciates! 

Victory to the illustrious Gauḍīya Vedānta teacher, His Divine Grace, Master Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa! 

Glory to Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura! 

Victory to the trio of masters, Śrīla Narottama Ṭhākura, Śrīnivāsa Ācārya, and Śyāmānanda Prabhu! 

Glory to His Grace the literary poet Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī Prabhu! 

Victory to the six Gosvāmī of Vṛndāvana: Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī, Sanātana Gosvāmī, Bhaṭṭa Raghunātha Gosvāmī, Śrī Jīva Gosvāmī, Gopāla-bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī, and Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī! 

Glory to the assembly of Śrī Gaura’s intimate associates, beginning with Śrī Svarūpa Dāmodara and Rāya Rāmānanda! 

Victory to the master of the Holy Name, Śrīla Haridāsa Ṭhākura! 

Proclaim with love: Glory to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Prabhu Nityānanda, Śrī Advaita Ācārya, Gadādhara Paṇḍita, Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura, and all the assembly of Gaura’s devotees! 

Glory to Śrī Navadvīpa-dhāma, the sacred abode which is comprised of the nine islands: Śrī Māyāpura at the center, surrounded by Sīmantadvīpa, Godrumadvīpa, Madhyadvīpa, Koladvīpa, Ṛtudvīpa, Jahnudvīpa, Modadrumadvīpa, and Rudradvīpa! 

Glory to Śrī Vraja-maṇḍala, which consists of twelve forests and is home to Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, the cowherd boys, the damsels, the cows, and Govardhana Hill! 

Victory to the Śrī Rādhā-kuṇḍa and Śyāma-kuṇḍa ponds, Gaṅgā and Yamunā rivers, Tulasī the Goddess of devotion! 

Glory to the forest messenger, Śrīmatī Vṛndā-devī! 

Victory to the spiritual master of the vraja-vāsīs, Śrī Paurṇamāsī Yogamāyā! 

Glory to the gatekeeper of Vṛndāvana, Śrī Gopīśvara Mahādeva! 

Victory to the respected Śrī Jagannātha, Baladeva, Subhadrā, and Sudarśana Cakra! 

Glory to Śrī Kṣetra-maṇḍala, Jagannātha Purī! 

Victory to the destroyer of all obstacles, the half-man half-lion Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva! 

Glory to the foremost among the highest of devotees, King Prahlāda! 

Victory to the four sacred abodes! <highlight>[Badarī-nārāyaṇa, Jagannātha Purī, Rāmeśvaram, and Dvārakā Purī]</highlight> 
Glory to the four authorized disciplic successions! <highlight>[Śrī Sampradāya, Brahma Sampradāya, Rudra Sampradāya, and Kumāra Sampradāya]</highlight> 
Victory to the four foundational teachers! <highlight>[Śrī Rāmānujācārya, Śrī Madhvācārya, Śrī Viṣṇusvāmī, and Śrī Nimbāditya]</highlight> 

Glory to the original fountainhead and supreme leader of all monasteries, Śrī Caitanya Maṭha! 

Victory to Śrī Śrī Keśavajī Gauḍīya Maṭha and the entire assembly of its branch monasteries! 

Glory to the absolute pinnacle of all sacred scriptures, Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam! 

Victory to the large-scale distribution of transcendental literature! 

Glory to the congregational chanting of the Holy Names of Śrī Hari! 

Victory to the endless millions of Vaiṣṇavas! 

Glory to the assembled devotees! 

In the divine love of Śrī Nitāi-Gaura, chant: Hari, Hari!

IDX.search: jaya godrumapati gora nitai jivana advaitera dhana vrndavana bhava vibhora
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
jaya godrumapati gorā 

nitāi-jīvana, advaitera dhana, 
vṛndāvana-bhāva-vibhorā 

gadādhara-prāṇa, śrīvāsa-śaraṇa, 
kṛṣṇabhakta-mānasa-corā
IDX.en_translation:
All glories to Gaura-candra, the Lord of Godruma! 

He is the life of Nitāi and the treasure of Advaita, absorbed in the mood of Vṛndāvana. 

He is the life of Gadādhara and the shelter of Śrīvāsa—the thief of the minds of the devotees of Kṛṣṇa.

IDX.search: jaya govinda jaya gopala kesava madhava dinadayalasyama sundara kanhaiyalala girivara dhari nanda dulala acyuta kesava sri dhara madhava gopala govinda hariyamuna puliname vamsi bajave natavara vesadhari
IDX.verses:
jaya govinda, jaya gopāla, 
keśava, mādhava, dīnadayālaśyāma-sundara kanhaiyālāla, 
girivara-dhārī nanda-dulāla 

acyuta, keśava, śrī-dhara mādhava, 
gopāla govinda, hariyamunā pulinamē vaṁśī bajāve, 
naṭavara veśadhārī
IDX.en_translation:
All glories to Govinda, all glories to Gopāla! Keśava, Mādhava, the Friend of the distressed! Śyāmasundara, the beloved Kanhaīyālāla, the Lifter of Govardhana Hill, the beloved Son of Nanda! 

Acyuta, Keśava, Śrīdhara, Mādhava, Gopāla, Govinda, Hari! On the banks of the Yamunā, He plays the flute, appearing as the supreme dancer.

IDX.author: govinda dāsa
IDX.verses: jaya jaga-tāraṇa-kāraṇa dhāma ānanda-kanda nityānanda nāma ḍagamaga locana-kamala ḍhulāyata sahaje athira gati jiti matoyāra bhāiyā abhirāma bali ghana ghana ḍāka-i gaura prema-bhare cala-i nā pāra gada gada ādhamadhura vacanāmṛta lahu lahu hāsa-vikaśita ganta pāṣaṇḍa khaṇḍana śrī-bhuja-maṇḍana kanaka- khacita avalamvana daṇḍa kali-yuga kālabhujaṅgama daṁśala dagadhala sthāvara jāṅgama dekhi prema-sudhā-rasa jaga bhari barikhala govinda-dāsa ke kāṁhe upekhi
IDX.en_translation:
All glories to the abode that is the cause of the world’s deliverance, the root of all bliss, whose Name is Nityānanda. 

His lotus-like eyes sway unsteadily with ease. His wavering gait outdoes even an intoxicated person. Calling out “O brother Abhirāma!” again and again, Gaura is unable to walk, overwhelmed with divine love. 

Faltering, half-sweet, nectarous words gently flow from His mouth, His face blossoming with a soft smile. The destroyer of atheists, He holds a golden staff inlaid with gold, which adorns His beautiful arms. 

Seeing all beings, both moving and non-moving, bitten and scorched by the serpent of the Age of Kali, He showered the entire world with the nectarean essence of divine love. Why then does He neglect Govinda Dāsa?

IDX.search: jaya jaya adbhuta so pahu advaita suradhuni sannidhane ankhi mudi rahe prema nadi vahe vasana titila ghame nija pahu mane ghana garajane uthe jode jode lampha dake bahu tuli kande phuli phuli dehe viparita kampa
IDX.author: vṛndāvana-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: jaya jaya adbhuta, so pahū advaita, suradhunī sannidhāne āṅkhi mudi’ rahe, prema-nadī vahe, vasana titila ghāme nija pahū mane, ghana garajane, uṭhe joḍe joḍe lampha ḍāke bāhu tuli’, kāṅde phuli’ phuli’, dehe viparīta kampa advaita-huṅkāre, suradhunī-tīre, āilā nāgara-rāja tāṅhāra pīrite, āilā tvarite, udaya nadīyā-mājha jaya sītānātha, karala vekata, nandera nandana hari kahe vṛndāvana, advaita-caraṇa, hiyāra mājhāre dhari
IDX.en_translation:
All glories, all glories to the amazing one! There, the master Advaita, near the Suradhunī, remains with closed eyes. A river of love flows, his clothes are drenched in sweat. 

In his own mind, the master, with a deep roar, leaps again and again. He calls with raised arms, he weeps profusely, his body trembles violently. 

By the roar of Advaita, on the bank of the Suradhunī, the Nāgara-rāja arrived. Out of love for him, he quickly came, appearing in Nadīyā. 

All glories to Sītānātha! He made manifest Hari, the son of Nanda. Vṛndāvana says, holding the lotus feet of Advaita within my heart.

IDX.author: locana-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: jaya jaya advaita ācārya dayāmaya jā’ra huhuṅkāre gaura-avatāra haya premadātā sītānātha karuṇā-sāgara jā’ra prema-rase āilā vrajera nāgara jāhāre karuṇā kari’ kṛpā dite cāya prema-rase se-jana caitanya-guṇa gāya tāhāra padete jebā loila śaraṇa se-jana pāila gauraprema-mahādhana emana dayāra nidhi kene nā bhajilu locana bale nija-māthe vajara pāḍilu
IDX.en_translation:
Glory, glory to the merciful Advaita Ācārya! By whose roaring call the Avatāra Gaura appeared. 

The giver of love, the Lord of Sītā, the ocean of compassion. By the nectar of whose love, the Hero of Vraja came. 

To whomsoever He desires to give mercy, that person sings the qualities of Caitanya in the mellows of love. 

Whoever took shelter at His feet, that person attained the great treasure of Gaura-prema. 

Why did I not worship such a reservoir of mercy? Locana says, “I have struck a thunderbolt on my own head.”

IDX.search: jaya jaya gadadhara pandita gosai janra krpa bale se caitanya guna gai hena se gaurangacandre janhara piriti gadadhara prananatha jahe lage khyati
IDX.author: śivānanda
IDX.verses: jaya jaya gadādhara paṇḍita gosāi jāṅ’ra kṛpā-bale se caitanya-guṇa gāi hena se gaurāṅgacandre jāṅhāra pirīti ‘gadādhara-prāṇanātha’ jāhe lāge khyāti gauragata-prāṇa, prema ke bujhite pāre kṣetra-vāsa, kṛṣṇa-sevā jāṅ’ra lāgi’ chāḍe gadāira gaurāṅga, gaurāṅgera gadādhara śrī-rāma-jānakī jena eka kalevara jena ekaprāṇa rādhā-vṛndāvana-candra tena gaura-gadādhara premera taraṅga kahe śivānanda paṁhu jāṅ’ra anurāge śyāma-tanu gaurāṅga hoiyā prema māge
IDX.en_translation:
All glories, all glories to Śrīla Gadādhara Paṇḍita Gosvāmī! By the power of his mercy, I sing the glories of Lord Caitanya. 

Such is his love for Lord Gaurāṅgacandra that he is famously known as “Gadādhara-prāṇanātha” (the Lord of Gadādhara’s life). 

His life is completely absorbed in Lord Gaura. Who can truly understand his love? For the sake of Lord Gaura, he gave up his residence in Jagannātha Purī and even his direct service to Lord Kṛṣṇa. 

Gaurāṅga belongs to Gadādhara, and Gadādhara belongs to Gaurāṅga. They are just like Śrī Rāma and Śrīmati Sītā-devī, appearing in one divine form. 

Just as Śrīmati Rādhā-rāṇī and Vṛndāvanacandra are one soul, so are Lord Gaura and Śrīla Gadādhara Paṇḍita—a vast wave of divine love. 

Śivānanda Sena says: “In whose deep affection Lord Kṛṣṇa, whose body is the color of a dark cloud, became Gaurāṅga and now begs for divine love.”

IDX.search: jaya jaya gadadhara premera sagara gaurangera priyottama pandita pravara madhava misrera putra sri gadadhara nama sisu haite samsare virakta bhagyavan
IDX.author: śrī-caitanya-bhāgavata
IDX.verses:
jaya jaya gadādhara premera sāgara 
gaurāṅgera priyottama paṇḍita pravara 

“mādhava miśrera putra-śrī-gadādhara nāma 
śiśu haite saṁsāre virakta bhāgyavān 

viṣṇu-bhakti-tejomaya divya kalevara 
ākṛti, prakṛti-dui parama sundara 

āpane caitanya baliyāche bāra bāra 
‘gadādhara mora vaikuṇṭhera paribāra’ 

niravadhi gadādhara thākena saṁhati 
prabhu-gadādharera viccheda nāhi kati 

ki bhojane, ki śayane, paryaṭane 
gadādhara prabhure sevena anukṣaṇe 

gadādhara sammukhe paḍena bhāgavata 
śuni prabhu hana premarase mahāmatta 

gadādhara-vākye mātra prabhu sukhī haya 
bhrame gadādhara saṅge vaiṣṇava-ālaya 

paṇḍite prabhura prasāda kahana nā jāya 
‘gadādhara-prāṇanātha’ nāma haila jāya 

gadādhara-pāda-padme mora namaskāra 
gaura-candra-saṅge jāṅra kīrtana vihāra”
IDX.en_translation:
Glory, glory to Gadādhara, the ocean of love! The dearest of Gaurāṅga, the best of Paṇḍitas. 

The son of Mādhava Miśra, named Śrī Gadādhara. From childhood, he was detached from the world and fortunate. 

A divine body full of the brilliance of devotion to Viṣṇu. Both his form and nature were supremely beautiful. 

Caitanya Himself has said again and again: “Gadādhara is My family from Vaikuṇṭha.” 

Gadādhara remains constantly in His company. There is never any separation between the Lord and Gadādhara. 

Whether eating or sleeping or travelling, Gadādhara serves the Lord at every moment. 

Gadādhara reads the Bhāgavata in front of Him. Hearing it, the Lord becomes greatly maddened in the rasa of love. 

The Lord becomes happy only by the words of Gadādhara. He wanders to the homes of Vaiṣṇavas with Gadādhara. 

The Lord’s mercy on the Paṇḍita cannot be described. His name became “Gadādhara-Prāṇanātha” (Lord of Gadādhara’s life). 

My obeisances to the lotus feet of Gadādhara, whose kīrtana-pastime is with Gaura-candra.

All glories, all glories to the beautiful ārati of Śrī Gaurāṅga being performed in a forest on the banks of the Jāhnavī (Gaṅgā), attracting the minds and hearts of all. 
<highlight>(Captivating the minds and hearts of all people. The beautiful ārati of Śrī Gaurāṅga captivates the minds and hearts of everyone. In the forest on the bank of the Jāhnavī, it captivates the minds and hearts of all people.)</highlight> 

On the right of Gaurāṅga is the moonlike Nityānanda Prabhu (nitāi-cānda), on the left is Gadādhara Paṇḍita, and on the sides are Advaita Prabhu and Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita, who holds the umbrella. 
<highlight>(Śrīvāsa holds the ceremonial umbrella. During Gaurāṅga’s ārati, Śrīvāsa holds the ceremonial umbrella.)</highlight> 

Śrī Gaurāṅga is seated on a jeweled throne. 
<highlight>(The jeweled throne is filled with radiant effulgence.)</highlight> 
Brahmā is performing the ārati along with other demigods. 
<highlight>(The hosts of demigods perform the ārati. During the ārati of Gaura and Nityānanda, the demigods perform the ārati. Brahmā and the other demigods perform Śrī Gaurāṅga’s ārati.)</highlight> 

Narahari Sarakāra Ṭhākura and others fan with cāmaras as many others like Saṣjaya Paṇḍita, Mukunda Daṭṭa and Vāsudeva Ghoṣa sing songs. 
<highlight>(Vāsu Ghoṣa sings devotional songs. Crying, “All glories to Nitāi! All glories to Gaura!” Vāsu Ghoṣa sings. Singing with the hope, “May I receive Gaura’s mercy,” Vāsu Ghoṣa sings. Praying, “Please bestow Your mercy upon me,” Vāsu Ghoṣa sings.)</highlight> 

The sounds of the conch, bell and karatālas mix with the sweet sound of the mṛdaṅgas, producing the most relishable ambrosia for the ears. 
<highlight>(Sweetly, imitating a sweet, honey-like sound, the instruments resound. During the ārati of Gaura and Nityānanda, the instruments resound with sweet, honey-like tones. The conch, bell, khol, and karatālas resound with sweet, honey-like melodies.)</highlight> 

Śrī Gaurāṅga’s brilliant face conquers the glow of many millions of moons, and the garland of forest flowers about His neck splendorously shines. 
<highlight>(The garland glitters and sparkles brilliantly. The garland of forest flowers around Gaura’s neck sparkles with dazzling brilliance. The garland sways by itself, even without anyone moving it. The garland woven by Gadādhara sways on its own, though no one moves it. The forest-flower garland around Gaura’s neck sways by itself, though untouched.)</highlight> 

Śiva, Śukadeva Gosvāmī and Nārada Muni’s voices have become choked up with prema. Thus, Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura is seeing the glories of Śrī Gaurāṅga. 
<highlight>(Only such a person beholds Gaurāṅga’s divine treasure glories. One who knows nothing but to call out “Gaura! Gaura!” truly beholds Gaurāṅga’s divine treasure. One who has dedicated his very life at Gaurāṅga’s lotus feet truly beholds His divine treasure. One who knows only to cry, “O Gaura!” truly beholds Gaurāṅga’s divine treasure.)</highlight>

IDX.first_line: jaya jaya gurudeva śrī bhakti prajñāna
IDX.search: jaya jaya gurudeva sri bhakti prajnana parama mohana rupa arta vimocana murtimanta sri vedanta asubha nasana bhakti grantha sri vedanta tava vighosana
IDX.author: bhaktivedānta trivikrama gosvāmī mahārāja
IDX.verses: jaya jaya gurudeva śrī-bhakti-prajñāna parama mohana rūpa ārta-vimocana mūrtimanta śrī-vedānta aśubha-nāśana “bhakti-grantha śrī-vedānta” tava vighoṣaṇa vedānta samiti-dīpe śrī-siddhānta-jyoti ārati tomāra tāhe haya niravadhi śrī-vinodadhārā-taile dīpa prapūrita rūpānuga-dhūpe daśa-dik āmodita sarvaśāstra sugambhīra karuṇā-komala jugapat suśobhana vadana-kamala svarṇa-kānti vinindita śrī-aṅga-śobhana jativāsa paridhāne jagat-kalyāṇa nānā chāṅde sajjana cāmara ḍhulāya gaura-jana ucca-kaṇṭhe sumadhura gāya sumaṅgala nīrājana kare bhakta-gaṇa duramati dūra haite dekhe trivikrama
IDX.en_translation:
All glories, all glories to Śrī Gurudeva Bhakti-prajñāna! Your supremely enchanting form delivers the distressed. 

You are the personification of Śrī Vedānta, the destroyer of inauspiciousness. You proclaimed, “Bhakti is the scripture, Śrī Vedānta.” 

In the lamp of the Vedānta Samiti, the light of siddhānta (philosophical conclusion) shines; Your ārati is performed there incessantly. 

The lamp is filled with the oil of the current of Śrī Vinoda; The ten directions are perfumed by the incense of the followers of Rūpa. 

Grave in all scriptures, soft with mercy; simultaneously, Your lotus face is very beautiful. 

The beauty of Your divine limbs defeats the luster of gold; Wearing the dress of a sannyāsī, You bring auspiciousness to the world. 

In various styles, the saintly persons wave the cāmara; The associate of Gaura sings very sweetly in a loud voice. 

The devotees perform the auspicious nīrājana; From a distance, the wicked-minded Trivikrama watches.

IDX.search: jaya jaya harinama cidanandamrta dhama paratattva aksara akara nija jane krpa kari namarupe avatari jive daya karile apara jaya hari krsna nama jagajana suvisrama sarvajana manasa ranjana munivrnda nirantara je namera samadara kari gaya bhariya vadana
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses: jaya jaya harināma, cidānandāmṛta dhāma, paratattva akṣara-ākāra nija-jane kṛpā kari’, nāmarūpe avatari’, jīve dayā karile apāra jaya hari-kṛṣṇa-nāma, jagajana suviśrāma, sarvajana-mānasa-rañjana munivṛnda nirantara, je nāmera samādara, kari’ gāya bhariyā vadana ohe kṛṣṇa-nāmākṣara, tumi sarvaśaktidhara, jīvera kalyāṇa-vitaraṇe tomā vinā bhavasindhu, uddhārite nāhi bandhu, āsiyācha jīva-uddhāraṇe āche tāpa jīve jata, tumi saba kara hata, helāya tomāre ekabāra ḍāke jadi kona jana, ha’ye dīna akiñcana, nāhi dekhi’ anya pratikāra tava svalpasphūrti pāya, ugratāpa dūre jāya, liṅga-bhaṅga haya anāyāse bhakativinoda kaya, jaya harināma jaya, pa’ḍe thāki tuyā pada-āśe
IDX.en_translation:
All glories, all glories to the Holy Name, the abode of conscious bliss and nectar, the Supreme Truth in the form of syllables! Out of mercy for Your own people, You have descended in the form of the Name and bestowed unlimited compassion upon the souls. 

All glories to the names of Hari and Kṛṣṇa, the supreme rest for all living beings and the delight of everyone’s mind! Groups of sages constantly honor this Name and sing it with a full voice. 

O imperishable Name of Kṛṣṇa, You possess all potencies for bestowing welfare upon the souls. Without You, there is no friend to deliver us from the ocean of material existence; You have come for the soul’s deliverance. 

Whatever miseries exist for the soul, You destroy them all if a person calls out to You just once, becoming humble and destitute, seeing no other remedy. 

Upon receiving Your slightest manifestation, fierce miseries vanish and the subtle body is easily destroyed. Bhaktivinoda says: victory to the Holy Name! I remain in the hope of Your feet.

IDX.first_line: jaya jaya jadu kula jalanidhi candra
IDX.search: jaya jaya jadu kula jalanidhi candra vraja kula gokula ananda kanda jaya jaya jaladhara syamara anga helana kalpa taru lalita tri bhanga
IDX.author: govinda dāsa
IDX.verses: jaya jaya jadu-kula-jalanidhi-candra vraja-kula gokula ānanda-kanda jaya jaya jaladhara śyāmara aṅga helana kalpa-taru lalita tri-bhaṅga sudha-i sudhāmaya murali-vilāsa jaga-jana-mohana madhurima hāsa avanī vilambita vani vana-bāla madhukara jhaṅkaru tatahi rasāla taruṇa aruṇa ruci pada aravinda nakha-maṇi nichani dāsa-govinda
IDX.en_translation:
All glories, all glories to the Moon of the Yadu dynasty, the very root of joy for the residents of Vraja and Gokula! 

All glories, all glories to Him whose body is dark like a cloud, who effortlessly surpasses the wish-fulfilling tree, and who stands in a charming threefold bending posture! 

Nectarean are His pastimes with the flute, and His sweet smile enchants everyone in the world. 

His forest garland sways low to the earth, and the bees hum there, attracted by the sweet aroma. 

Govinda Dāsa offers his adoration to the jewel-like nails of His lotus feet, which are as radiant as the rising sun.

IDX.first_line: jaya jaya jaga jana locana phānda
IDX.search: jaya jaya jaga jana locana phanda radha ramana vrndavana canda abhinava nila jalada tanu dhala dhala pincha mukuta sire sajani re kancana vasanaratanamaya abharana nupura ranarani bajani re
IDX.author: govinda dāsa
IDX.verses: jaya jaya jaga-jana-locana-phānda rādhā-ramaṇa vṛndāvana-cānda abhinava nīla jalada tanu ḍhala ḍhala piñcha mukuṭa śire sājani re kāñcana vasanaratanamaya ābharaṇa nūpura raṇaraṇi bājanī re indīvara-yuga subhaga vilocana añcala cañcala kusuma-śare avicala kula ramaṇī-gaṇa mānasa jara jara antare madana-bhare vani vana-māloājānu-lambita parimale ali-kula māti rahu bimbādhara pare mohana muralī gā-ota govinda-dāsa-pahu
IDX.en_translation:
All glories, all glories to the moon of Vṛndāvana, Rādhā-ramaṇa, who captivates the eyes of all the people in the world! 

His fresh, blue body is dazzling like a cloud, and a peacock-feather crown adorns His head. He wears golden garments and jeweled ornaments, and His anklets make a jingling sound. 

His beautiful lotus-like eyes dart restless glances like Cupid’s flower-arrows. The hearts of all the ladies of Vraja are overwhelmed with love by His glances. 

A forest garland hangs down to His knees, and its fragrance intoxicates the bees. Upon His red lips, an enchanting flute sings—so says the Master of Govinda Dāsa.

IDX.search: jaya jaya jagannatha sacira nandana tri bhuvana kare janra carana vandana nilacale sankha cakra gada padmadharanadiya nagare danda kamandalu kara
IDX.author: vasudeva ghoṣa
IDX.verses: jaya jaya jagannātha śacīra nandana tri-bhuvana kare jāṅ’ra caraṇa vandana nīlācale śaṅkha-cakra-gadā-padmadharanadīyā nagare daṇḍa-kamaṇḍalu-kara keha bale, - ‘pūravete rāvaṇa vadhilā’golokera vaibhava līlā prakāśa karilā śrī-rādhāra bhāve ebe gorā avatāra‘hare kṛṣṇa’-nāma gaura karilā pracāra vāsudeva ghoṣa bale kari’ joḍa hātajei gaura, sei kṛṣṇa, sei jagannātha
IDX.en_translation:
All glories to Jagannātha, the Son of Śacī! The three worlds worship His feet. 

In Nīlācala, He is the Holder of conch, disc, club, and lotus; in the town of Nadīyā, He is the Holder of the staff and water-pot. 

Someone says, “Previously He killed Rāvaṇa.” He manifested the opulent pastimes of Goloka. 

Now, in the mood of Śrī Rādhā, He is the Golden Avatar; Gaura preached the Name “Hare Kṛṣṇa”. 

Vāsudeva Ghoṣa says with folded hands: He who is Gaura is Kṛṣṇa, is Jagannātha.

IDX.search: jaya jaya mahaprabhu jaya gaura candra aya visvambhara jaya karunara sindhu jaya sacisuta jaya pandita nimani jaya misra purandara jaya saci ai

IDX.verses: jaya jaya mahāprabhu jaya gaura-candra aya viśvambhara jaya karuṇāra sindhu jaya śacīsūta jaya paṇḍita nimāñi jaya miśra purandara jaya śacī āi jaya jaya navadvīpa jaya suradhunī jaya lakṣmī viṣṇupriyā prabhura gṛhiṇī jaya jaya navadvīpavāsī-bhaktagaṇa jaya jaya nityānanda advaita-caraṇa nityānanda pada dvandva sadā kari āśa nāma saṁkīrtana gāila kṛṣṇa-dāsa
IDX.en_translation:
All glories to Mahāprabhu! All glories to Gaura-candra! All glories to Viśvambhara, the maintainer of the universe and the ocean of mercy! 

All glories to the Son of Mother Śacī, the learned Paṇḍita Nimāi! All glories to Jagannātha Miśra and Mother Śacī! 

All glories to Navadvīpa and the River Ganges! All glories to Lakṣmī-devī and Viṣṇupriyā-devī, the wives of the Lord. 

All glories to the residents of Navadvīpa and all the devotees! All glories to the lotus feet of Lord Nityānanda and Advaita Ācārya! 

I always desire the twin lotus feet of Lord Nityānanda. Kṛṣṇa-dāsa sings this congregational chanting of the Holy Name.

IDX.en_translation:
All glories to the Son of Nanda, the Master of the family of Vraja! All glories to the Lord of the Yadus, the ultimate destination of the three worlds! 

All glories to the Abode of the universe, the Master of the senses! All glories to Him who is like the sun for the lotus-like devotees! 

All glories to Him whose lotus feet are caressed by the Goddess of Fortune! All glories to the blissful joy of the minds of the great sages! 

All glories to the Ocean of good qualities! All glories to the Merciful One! All glories to Him who is affectionate to His devotees and full of divine mellows! 

All glories to the Destroyer of great fear and sin! All glories to the fierce Subduer of atheists! 

All glories to the great Lion who defeats the elephant-like demons! All glories to the Honeybee for the lotus-like faces of the gopīs! 

All glories to the Swan in the minds of the great yogīs! All glories to the Destroyer of the cycle of material existence for the devotees! 

All glories to the Auspiciousness of the universe, the Abode of all good qualities! All glories to Him whose Name is beyond the reach of the Vedas! 

All glories to the complete Absolute Truth, Lord Kṛṣṇa, who performs wonderful pastimes! All glories to Lord Jagannātha, the incarnation of Nīlācala! 

All glories to Śrī Gaurāṅga, the personification of consciousness! He is the Bestower of loving devotion and the only shelter of the devotees.

IDX.verses: jaya jaya nityānanda rohiṇī-kumāra patita uddhāra lāgi’ du’bāhu pasāra gada gada madhura madhura ādho bola jā’re dekhe tā’re preme dhari’ deya kola ḍagamaga locana ghuraye nirantara sonāra kamale jena phiraye bhramara dayāra ṭhākura nitāi para-duḥkha jāne hari-nāmera mālā gāṅthi’ dila jagajane pāpī-pāṣaṇḍī jata karila dalana dīna-hīna-jane kailā prema vitaraṇa ‘āhā re gaurāṅga’-bali’ paḍe bhūmitale śarīra bhijila nitāira nayanera jale vṛndāvana-dāsa mane ei vicārila dharaṇī upare kibā sumeru paḍila
IDX.en_translation:
Glory, glory to Nityānanda, the Son of Rohiṇī! He spreads His two arms to deliver the fallen. 

Choked up, sweet, sweet broken words; whomever He sees, He holds him with love and embraces him. 

His overwhelmed eyes roll constantly; as if a bee wanders in a golden lotus. 

The merciful Lord Nitāi knows the pain of others; He strung a garland of the Holy Name and gave it to the people of the world. 

He crushed all the sinners and atheists; He distributed love to the lowly and destitute people. 

Saying “Alas! O Gaurāṅga!”, He falls to the ground; Nitāi’s body became wet with the water of His eyes. 

Vṛndāvana Dāsa considered this in his mind: Has Sumeru fallen upon the earth?

All glories, all glories to Nityānanda, Advaita, and Gaurāṅga! Glory to Nitāi-Gaurāṅga! Glory to Nitāi-Gaurāṅga! 

Glory to the Son of Yaśodā, the Son of Śacī, Gaura-candra! Glory to the Son of Rohiṇī, Balarāma, Nityānanda! 

Glory to the Avatar of Mahāviṣṇu, Śrī Advaitacandra! Glory to Gadādhara, Śrīvāsa, and the group of Gaura’s devotees! 

Glory to Svarūpa, Rūpa, Sanātana, Rāya Rāmānanda! Glory to the residents of Khaṇḍa—Narahari, Murāri, Mukunda! 

Glory to Rāya Bhavānanda, who dances with five sons! Glory to Sena Śivānanda, who dances with three sons! 

Glory to the twelve Gopālas and the sixty-four Mahantas! All of you, mercifully give the lotus feet of Gaura.

IDX.verses: jaya jaya prabhupādera ārati nehāri yoga-māyāpura-nitya-sevā-dānakārī sarvatra pracāra-dhūpa saurabha manohara baddha-mukta alikula mugdha carācara bhakati-siddhānta-dīpa jvāliyā jagate pañca-rasa-sevā-śikhā pradīpta tāhāte pañca mahādīpa jathā pañca mahājyotiḥ triloka-timira nāśe avidyā-durmati bhakativinoda-dhārā jala-śaṅkha-dhāra niravadhi vahe tāhā rodha nāhi āra sarva-vādya-mayī ghaṇṭā bāje sarva-kāla bṛhat-mṛdaṅga-vādya parama rasāla viśāla lalāṭe śobhe tilaka ujjvala gala-deśe tulasī-mālā kare jhalamala ājānu-lambita bāhu dīrgha kalevara tapta-kāñcana-varaṇa parama sundara lalita-lāvaṇya-mukhe sneha-bharā hāsi aṅga-kānti śobhe jaiche nitya-pūrṇa-śaśī jati-dharme paridhāne aruṇa-vasana mukta kaila meghāvṛta gauḍīya-gagana bhakati-kusume kata kuñja viracita saundarya-saurabhe tāra viśva-vimohita sevādarśe narahari cāmara ḍhulāya keśava ati ānande nīrājana gāya
IDX.en_translation:
All glories, all glories! Beholding the ārati of Prabhupāda, who bestows eternal service at Yogapīṭha in Māyāpura. 

The enchanting fragrance of his preaching acts like incense, captivating the bees of the bound and liberated souls, and the entire moving and non-moving world. 

Igniting the lamp of Bhaktisiddhānta (devotional conclusions) in the world, the flame of service in the five mellows shines brightly within it. 

Just as the five great lamps serve as five great lights, they destroy the darkness of the three worlds—ignorance and wicked intelligence. 

The current of Bhaktivinoda flows like water from a conchshell; it flows incessantly, with no obstruction. 

The bell, consisting of all instruments, rings at all times; the great mṛdaṅga plays, supremely sweet. 

On his broad forehead shines a bright tilaka, and a necklace of tulasī beads glitters on his neck. 

His long arms reach down to his knees, his body is tall, and his complexion is like molten gold—supremely beautiful. 

A smile filled with affection is on his charming, graceful face; his bodily effulgence shines like the eternal full moon. 

Wearing the saffron cloth of the renounced order, he cleared the cloud-covered Gauḍīya sky. 

How many groves he has created with the flowers of devotion; the whole universe is enchanted by their beauty and fragrance. 

In the vision of service, Narahari waves the cāmara, and Keśava sings the nīrājana with great joy.

All glories, all glories to the union of the Divine Couple, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa! Lalitā and the other friends perform the āratī. 

Kṛṣṇa, whose form enchants even Cupid, is beautiful with His three-fold bending posture. He is adorned with yellow garments and a charming crest of peacock feathers. 

To the left of charming Mādhava stands the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu. Dressed in blue garments, fair-complexioned, she is blessed with beauty and excellent qualities. 

Various kinds of ornaments glitter. Their radiant faces captivate Hari’s mind. 

Viśākhā and the other friends sing in various melodies. All the intimate joking friends wave the whisks. 
<highlight>(They gently wave the cāmaras. During the ārati of Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, they gently wave the cāmaras. Crying, “All glories to Rādhe! Śrī Rādhe!” they gently wave the cāmaras. Lalitā, Viśākhā, and the other sakhīs gently wave the cāmaras.)</highlight> 

With hope for the lotus feet of Śrī Rādhā and Mādhava, Bhaktivinoda joyfully floats in the mood of a female friend.

IDX.verses:
“jaya jaya śrī-advaita patita-pāvana 
mui saba patitera karaha mocana 

kṛṣṇa nā karena jāṅra saṅkalpa anyathā 
je karite pāre kṛṣṇa-sākṣāt sarvathā 

kṛṣṇa-candre jāṅra vākya karena pālana 
se tomā-smaraṇe sarvabandha-vimocana 

jama, kāla, mṛtyu jāṅra ājñā śire dhare 
jāṅra pada vāñche jogeśvare munīśvare 

sei tomā hena jane ke jāne saṁsāre 
tumi kṛpā karile se bhaktiphala dhare 

bhaktira bhāṇḍārī tumi, vine bhakti dile 
kṛṣṇa-bhakti, kṛṣṇabhakta, kṛṣṇa kāre mile 

amāyāya kṛṣṇa-bhakti deha he-āmāre 
janma janma āra jena kṛṣṇa pāsare 

advaita-caraṇe mora ei namaskāra 
tāna priya, tāṅhe mati rahuka āmāra”
IDX.en_translation:
All glories, all glories to Śrī Advaita, the patita-pāvana! Please deliver all of us who are fallen. 

Kṛṣṇa never allows His resolve to be otherwise; He can directly manifest Kṛṣṇa in all respects. 

Whose words Kṛṣṇa-candra obeys; by remembering You, all bondage is released. 

Whose command Yama, Kāla, and Mṛtyu obey; whose lotus feet are desired by the greatest yogeśvaras and munīśvaras. 

Who in this world can truly know such a person as You? Only by Your mercy can one attain the fruit of devotion. 

You are the treasurer of devotion; without Your giving devotion, who can attain Kṛṣṇa-bhakti, a Kṛṣṇa-bhakta, or Kṛṣṇa Himself? 

Please sincerely bestow upon me Kṛṣṇa-bhakti, so that in birth after birth, I may never forget Kṛṣṇa. 

To the lotus feet of Advaita, I offer this namaskāra; may my mind remain fixed on Him, who is so dear.

jaya rūpa-sanātana jaya gadādhara

jaya vraja-dhāma-vāsī vaiṣṇava-nicoya 

jaya jaya navadvīpa-vāsī bhakta-gaṇa 
sabe mili’ kṛpā more kara vitaraṇa 

nikhila-vaiṣṇava-jana dayā prakāśiyā 
śrī-jāhnavā-pade more rākhaha ṭāniyā 

āmi to’ durbhaga ati vaiṣṇava nā cini 
more kṛpā karibena vaiṣṇava āpani 

śrī-guru-caraṇe more bhakti kara dāna 
je caraṇa-bale pāi tattvera sandhāna 

brāhmaṇa sakala kari’ kṛpā mora prati 
vaiṣṇava-caraṇe more deha dṛḍha-mati 

ucca nīca sarva-jīva caraṇe śaraṇa 
loilāma āmi dīna hīna akiñcana 

sakalake kariyā kṛpā deha’ more vara 
vaiṣṇave karuṇā ei granthera ādara 

grantha-dvārā vaiṣṇava-janera kṛpā pāi 
vaiṣṇava-kṛpāya kṛṣṇa-lābha haya bhāi 

vaiṣṇava-vimukha jā’re tāhāra jīvana 
nirarthaka jāna’ bhāi prasiddha vacana 

śrī-vaikuṇṭha-dhāme āche niḥśreyasa vana 
tāhe śobhā pāya kalpa-taru agaṇana 

tāhā mājhe e kalyāṇa-kalpa-taru-rāja 
nitya-kāla nitya-dhāme karena virāja 

skandha-traya āche tā’ra apūrva darśana 
upadeśa upalabdhi ucchvāsa gaṇana 

su-bhakti-prasūna tāhe ati śobhā pāya 
kalyāṇa nāmaka phala agaṇana tāya 

je sujana e viṭapī karena āśraya 
kṛṣṇa-sevā-su-kalyāṇa-phala tāṅ’ra haya 

śrī-guru-caraṇa-kṛpā-sāmarthya labhiyā 
e hena apūrva vṛkṣa dilāma āniyā 

ṭāniyā ānite vṛkṣa e karkaśa mana 
naśilo ihāra śobhā śuno sādhu-jana 

tomāra sakala ha-o e vṛkṣera mālī 
śraddhā-vari diyā punaḥ kara rūpaśālī

kariba sakale mili’ tāhā āsvādana

bhakti-bale kara’ dūra kutarka-anala
IDX.en_translation:
All glories, all glories to Śrī-caitanya, the savior of the fallen! All glories to Nityānanda Prabhu, the deliverer of the helpless! 

All glories, all glories to Advaitacandra! 

All glories to Śrī Jīva residing in Braja-dhāma! 

All glories, all glories to the devotee community residing in Navadvīpa! All of you together, please bestow your mercy upon me. 

By manifesting mercy, all Vaiṣṇavas, Please pull me and keep me at the feet of Śrī Jāhnavā Devī. 

I am very unfortunate and do not recognize any Vaiṣṇava; May you, the Vaiṣṇavas, show mercy upon me. 

Please bestow devotion upon me at the feet of my Śrī-guru, By the strength of those feet, I obtain the understanding of truth. 

May all Brāhmaṇas show mercy towards me, And grant me firm faith at the feet of the Vaiṣṇavas. 

High and low, all living entities take shelter at their feet, I, who am poor, fallen, and insignificant, have taken that shelter. 

All of you, showing mercy, please grant me this boon: Compassion towards Vaiṣṇavas, and adoration for this book. 

Through this book, I receive the mercy of the Vaiṣṇavas, the attainment of Kṛṣṇa occurs, O brother! 

Know, O brother, that the life of one who is averse to Vaiṣṇavas Is useless; this is a famous saying. 

In Śrī-Vaikuṇṭha-dhāma there is a forest of supreme welfare, In which innumerable wish-fulfilling trees shine beautifully. 

Among them, this king of wish-fulfilling trees named Kalyāṇa, Eternally resides in the eternal abode, shining brightly. 

It has three branches, a wonderful sight: Instruction, realization, and expression of ecstasy. 

Beautiful flowers of devotion greatly enhance its beauty, And innumerable fruits named Kalyāṇa are found there. 

For any good person who takes shelter of this tree, The excellent fruit of service to Kṛṣṇa becomes his. 

Having obtained the power of the mercy of the feet of my Śrī-guru, I have brought such an uncommon tree here. 

To pull and bring this tree, my harsh mind Destroyed its beauty; please listen, O saintly people! 

May all of you become the gardeners of this tree, And by offering the water of faith, make it beautiful again. 

It will bear the auspicious fruit of yugala-sevana; We will all together relish that. 

Dance, chant “Hari”, and partake of the fruit of service; By the strength of devotion, drive far away the fire of bad arguments.

IDX.verses: jaya jaya śrī-guru, prema-kalpataru, adbhuta jāṅko parakāśahiyā ageyāna, timiravara jñāna-, sucandra kiraṇe karu nāśa iha locana ānanda-dhāmaayācita mo-hena, patita heri jo pahū, jāci deyala harināma duramati agati, satata asate mati, nāhi sukṛti laba leśaśrī-vṛndāvana, yugala-bhajana-dhana, tāhe karala upadeśa niramala-gaura-, premarasa siñcane, pūrala jagajana āśaso caraṇāmbuje, rati nāhi hoyala, royata vaiṣṇava-dāsa
IDX.en_translation:
All glories to the spiritual master, the wish-fulfilling tree of divine love, whose manifestation is wondrous. The darkness of ignorance in the heart is destroyed by the rays of the beautiful moon of his knowledge. 

He is the abode of joy for these eyes. Without being asked, and seeing a fallen soul like me, he mercifully gave the Holy Name. 

I am of wicked mind and without any goal; my thoughts are always fixed on the mundane. I do not possess even a trace of pious merit. Yet he gave me the instruction to attain Vṛndāvana and the treasure of worshiping the Divine Couple. 

By sprinkling the pure nectar of divine love, he fulfilled the hopes of the people of the world. In those lotus feet I have no attachment—so cries Vaiṣṇava dāsa.

IDX.verses: jaya jaya śrī-kṛṣṇacaitanya dayāsindhu patita uddhāra hetu jaya dīna-bandhu jaya premabhaktidātā, dayā kara more dante tṛṇa dhari’ ḍāke e-dāsa pāmare pūrvete sākṣāt jata pātakī tārilā se vicitra nahe jāte avatāra kailā mo-hena pāpiṣṭhe ebe karaha uddhāra āścarya dayāla-guṇa ghuṣuka saṁsāra vicāra karile muñi nahe dayāpātra āpana svabhāva-guṇe karaha kṛtārtha viśeṣa pratijñā śuni’ ei kaliyuge ei bharasāya rādhāmohana dayā māge
IDX.en_translation:
All glories, all glories to Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, an ocean of mercy! All glories to the Friend of the distressed, for delivering the fallen! 

All glories to the giver of loving devotion! Please bestow Your mercy upon me. This fallen servant calls out, holding a blade of grass in his teeth. 

In the past, You directly delivered many sinful persons. This is not surprising, for You have appeared as an incarnation specifically for that purpose. 

Now, please deliver a wretch as sinful as me. Let Your astonishingly merciful qualities be proclaimed throughout the entire world. 

Upon reflection, I am not worthy of Your mercy. Please fulfill me by Your own merciful nature and divine qualities. 

Hearing Your special promise in this Age of Kali, and with this hope alone, Rādhāmohana begs for Your mercy.

All glories to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya and Nityānanda! All glories to Advaitacandra, and all glories to the assembly of Lord Gaura’s devotees! 

Please, all of you together, bestow your mercy; do not disdain this fallen and degraded soul. 

In these three worlds, Your lotus feet are the essence; reflecting in my mind, I see that there is no other shelter. 

In the hope of attaining those feet, distress arises in my mind; with an anxious heart, I always lament. 

How will I attain them? I find no way. I cannot even remember the lotus feet of Prabhu Lokanātha. 

You are indeed a merciful Lord; please glance upon me just once and remove the darkness from Narottama’s heart.

IDX.search: jaya jaya sri srivasa thakura pandita narada kheyati jara bhuvana vidita ki kahiba srivasera udara caritra tribhuvana haya jara smarane pavitra

IDX.verses:
jaya jaya śrī-śrīvāsa ṭhākura paṇḍita 
nārada-kheyāti jā’ra bhuvana vidita 

“ki kahiba śrīvāsera udāra caritra 
tribhuvana haya jāra smaraṇe pavitra 

satya sevilena caitanyere śrīnivāsa 
jāṅra ghare caitanyera sakala vilāsa 

kṛṣṇa-avatāra jena vasudeva-ghare 
jateka vihāra saba-nandera mandire 

jagannātha-ghare haila gaura-avatāra 
śrīvāsa-paṇḍita-gṛhe jateka vihāra 

sarvavaiṣṇavera priya paṇḍita śrīvāsa 
tāna bāḍī gele mātra sabāra ullāsa 

ki kahiba śrīvāsera bhāgyera mahimā 
jāṅra dāsadāsīra bhāgyera nāhi sīmā 

cāri vede jāṅre dekhibāre abhilāṣa 
tāhā dekhe śrīvāsera jata dāsī-dāsa 

putraśoka nā jānila je gaurāṅga-preme 
bhāse āro śrī-kṛṣṇera saṅkīrtana-vāṇe 

e saba saṁsāra-duḥkha tāṅhāra ki dāya 
je tāṅhāre smare seha kabhu nāhi pāya 

śrīvāsera caraṇe rahuka namaskāra 
gaura-candra-nityānanda-nandana jāṅhāra’’
IDX.en_translation:
All glories, all glories to Śrī Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura Paṇḍita, whose fame is known throughout the world like that of Nārada. 

What can I say about the magnanimous character of Śrīvāsa? By remembering him, the three worlds become pure. 

Indeed, Śrīnivāsa served Caitanya. In his house were all the pastimes of Caitanya. 

Just as the incarnation of Kṛṣṇa was in Vasudeva’s house, but all His many pastimes were in Nanda’s temple. 

In Jagannātha’s house was the incarnation of Gaura, but all His many pastimes were in Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita’s home. 

Śrīvāsa is dear to all Vaiṣṇavas. Just by going to his house, everyone becomes joyful. 

What can I say about the glory of Śrīvāsa’s fortune? There is no limit to the fortune of his servants and maidservants. 

He whom the four Vedas desire to see, Him see all the servants and maidservants of Śrīvāsa. 

He did not feel the sorrow of his son in that love for Gaurāṅga. He rather floated in the current of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s saṅkīrtana. 

What concern are all these worldly miseries to him? Whoever remembers him also never experiences them. 

Let my obeisances remain at the feet of Śrīvāsa, he whose sons are Gaura-candra and Nityānanda.

jaya jaya sundara nanda-kumāra 
saurabha-saṅkaṭa-, vṛndāvana-taṭa-, 
vihita-vasanta-vihāra 

abhinava-kuṭmala-, guccha-samujjvala-, 
kuñcita-kuntala-bhāra 
praṇayi-janerita-, vandana-sahakṛta-, 
cūrṇita-vara-ghanasāra 

caṭula-digañcala-, racita-rasocchala-, 
rādhā-madana-vikāra 
bhuvana-vimohana-, mañjula-nartana, 
gati-valgita-maṇihāra 

adhara-virājita-, mandatara-smita-,

IDX.en_translation:
Glory, glory to the beautiful Nanda-kumāra (son of Nanda)! On the banks of Vṛndāvana, filled with fragrance, He performs His spring pastimes (vihāra). 

His curly hair is adorned with fresh buds and radiant bunches of flowers. He is worshipped by His beloved devotees and powdered with excellent camphor. 

His playful glances, overflowing with sweet mellows (rasa), stir the Cupid (Madana) of Rādhā. His beautiful dance enchants the world, and His jewel necklace sways with His movements. 

A gentle smile graces His lips, captivating His own family (parivāra). He is the delightful avatāra (descent) who resides in the hearts of His own cowherd people (vallavajana) and eternal friends (suhṛt sanātana).

His body is smeared with musk and camphor. His curly hair is adorned with a peacock feather. 

The sound of His flute steals Rādhā’s patience. The corners of His eyes create the god of love’s emotional disturbances. 

He enchants Rādhā’s companions with His mellows. He sports in the heart of Sanātana.

All glories to the son of Nanda, the beloved of the gopīs, the hero of Rādhā, the clever dark-complexioned Lord. He is the son of Śacī, the chief of Nadiyā, and the captivating abode for the minds of gods and sages. 

All glories to Him whose body possesses the luster of His own beloved; all glories to the enjoyment of His beloved’s sentiments. All glories to the auspiciousness for the eyes of the companions of Vraja; all glories to the delight for the eyes of the residents of Nadiyā. 

All glories to Śrīdāma, Sudāma, Subala, and Arjuna—His form like a fresh monsoon cloud increases divine love. All glories to beautiful Balarāma and the dear companions; all glories to the incomparable Gaura, who enchants the universe. 

All glories to the one of immense strength, the beloved younger brother of Balarāma; all glories to the joy of Śrī Nityānanda. All glories to the one who removes the fears of the saintly devotees; this is the hope and attachment of Govinda dāsa.

Glory to Rādhā, glory to Kṛṣṇa, glory to Vṛndāvana. Śrī Govinda, Gopīnātha, Madana-mohana. 

Śyāma-kuṇḍa, Rādhā-kuṇḍa, Govardhana Hill. Glory to the Kālindī Yamunā, glory to Mahāvana. 

Keśī-ghāṭa, Vaṁśīvaṭa, the twelve forests. Where the son of Nanda performed all His pastimes. 

Glory to Śrī Nanda and Yaśodā, glory to the cowherd men. Glory to Śrīdāma and others, glory to the cows and calves. 

Glory to Vṛṣabhānu, glory to the beautiful Kīrtidā. Glory to Paurṇamāsī, glory to the young cowherd women. 

Glory, glory to Gopīśvara in the midst of Vṛndāvana. Glory, glory to Kṛṣṇa’s friend, the brāhmaṇa boy (Madhu-maṅgala). 

Glory to Rāma-ghāṭa, glory to the son of Rohiṇī. Glory, glory to all the residents of Vṛndāvana. 

Glory to the wives of the brāhmaṇas, glory to the Nāga-kanyās. Who attained the feet of Govinda through devotion. 

Glory to the Śrī Rāsa-maṇḍala, glory to Rādhā-Śyāma. Glory, glory to the rāsa-līlā, which enchants everyone. 

Glory, glory to the ujjvala-rasa, the essence of all rasas. Which is preached in Vraja in the mood of paramour love. 

Remembering the lotus feet of Śrī Jāhnavā, the lowly Kṛṣṇa Dāsa sings the saṅkīrtana of the Name.

All glories, all glories, all glories to Ṭhākura Śrī Narottama, the great king of prema-bhakti! His minister, who is non-different from him in heart, is Rāmacandra Kavirāja. 

The crown jewel of divine love, adorned with a succession of spiritual emotions, shines on every limb of his body. He sits upon a royal throne in Khetarī, accompanied by an assembly of devotees. 

He constantly deliberates on the Bhāgavatam and the works of Sanātana and Rūpa. This brilliant mellow of the Divine Couple, Rādhā and Mādhava, is the essence of supreme bliss. 

Through Śrī Saṅkīrtana and being intoxicated with the nectar of his subject, he transcends considerations of both pious and impious activities. Yoga, speculative knowledge, and various vows all weep before the presence of the Bhāgavatam. 

The scriptures of the Bhāgavatam, which bestow the wealth of devotion, are themselves glorified by Gaura. All the schools of Sāṅkhya, Mīmāṁsā, and logic tremble seeing his spiritual prowess. 

The thieves of non-devotion flee far away; they do not dare reveal themselves near him. To the poor and lowly people, the wealth of devotion is freely given. Only Govinda Dāsa feels deprived of this treasure.

IDX.en_translation:
All glories to Your birth in Vraja, where even the Goddess of Fortune seeks to reside upon its dust. Yet, alas, You do not abandon us here! How can we, Your devotees, be otherwise, O Lord? 

Your beauty is superior to the finest autumn lotuses, from which You steal the very goddess of beauty with Your gaze. 

Alas! How can we, who are outside Your grace, attain such purity? Even though You were bound by our pleas, and even those lotuses were blessed by You. 

Having entered Your service again, why do You now slay us with that gaze? If death were to come by Your glance alone, it would be superior to death by a weapon. 

From various fears, You have preserved all of Gokula along with its forests. We consider it Your protection, for how can that protection be lost due to Your love? 

O protector of the humble! O Son of the Queen of Vraja! Our intelligence is perishable. Your apparent neglect of us appears bitter because of our suffering. 

You are the universal protector and are not easily angered like others. Therefore, being entreated by Lord Brahmā, You appeared in the most pure lineage. 

May that hand of Your Master, which is renowned and dispels the fear of the cycle of birth and death, place its auspicious touch upon our heads. 

O hero! In the depths of Vraja, You pacify the angry gopīs with a smile alone. Therefore, do not punish us in any other way; simply manifest the glorious splendor of Your face. 

Although Your feet are the abode of the Goddess of Fortune and are a great banner of merit for the distressed, You still follow the cows and dance on the heads of the venomous serpent. 

Even though You were in great distress in that state, You became our tranquil support. Alas! Why do You not protect us, whose hearts are consumed by the fire of separation from You? 

With Your sweet pastimes, delightful words, and joyful fragrance, we have been thirsty for a long time for Your nectarean speech. 

Your nectarean stories are the life of the distressed and are praised by the poets for destroying all impurities. Those who do not propagate them are wicked and deprive us of knowledge. 

Your smiling, dancing eyes and Your delightful moods dispels all sorrow, and Your presence in the forest is our very life. 

When You go to graze the cows, our minds are broken by fate. The thought of the soft grass and sprouts touching Your feet becomes our only meditation. 

Alas! Our inner hearts are ablaze! Remember Your own people, who consider themselves humble. May Your lotus feet be firmly placed in our hearts, O charmer! 

Alas! When You go to the forest each day, we see Your beautiful face with curly locks and that moment feels like a vast age to us. 

What more can be said about this in Vraja? Even for a moment, Your sight is desired. Alas, how can we gopīs not be anxious there? 

Entangled in the net of Your songs and having left our own people, what woman would You abandon in the night in this wilderness? 

O beloved! Your smiling, loving glances and Your broad chest—which is the abode of fortune—seeing all this, our own foolishness is revealed to us. 

At the end of the day, with the darkness of Your hair and the spreading dust from the cows, You manifest the moon-like glory of Your face and cause us to remember You again and again. 

Due to the increase of its own pleasure, the flute becomes a witness. Grant us, O hero, that nectar from Your lips which destroys all sorrow and is our life-giving food. 

Even though You conceive of love in that way, it is in truth an artistic creation. How can we, who are constantly in the mood of affection, ever have other desires? 

Your manifestation among the residents of Gokula is the destroyer of their sins. Grant us, who are filled with longing for You, the soothing cure for our heart’s disease. 

Your supremely beautiful lotus feet, which we gently place upon our breasts, are pained when You wander in the forest. Our minds become bewildered by the thought of thorns and stones pricking them. 

Thus, the gopīs, singing and lamenting in various ways, wept aloud, eager to see Lord Kṛṣṇa. 

Then, the Lord, whose lotus face was smiling, appeared before them wearing yellow garments and a garland—He who is the direct bewilderer of even Cupid himself.

IDX.en_translation:
Where has that master gone, that revered teacher who brought the wealth of divine love and abundant mercy? 

Where are Svarūpa Dāmodara and Rūpa Gosvāmī? Where is Sanātana Gosvāmī? Where are Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī and Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī, the deliverers of the fallen? 

Where are my two Bhaṭṭas? Where is Kṛṣṇa-dāsa Kavirāja? Where has the fair-complexioned king of dancers gone all at once? 

I will smash my head against a stone; I will enter the fire. Where will I find Gaurāṅga, the treasure house of all qualities? 

Not finding the association of those companions with whom He performed His divine pastimes, Narottama dāsa cries.

Whichever rati takes birth in someone, that kind of rasa is theirs. The principal rasas are of five kinds. Again, the seven secondary rasas are subservient qualities of rati; the relation of rati is the shelter of bhāva. 

Among the five principal rasas, O brother, I sing the glories of madhura, calling it the supreme rasarāja. All the qualities that are in other rasas are present in madhura, and it becomes more powerful due to many more. 

All the secondary rasas that exist are like sañcārī, and they nourish śṛṅgāra. One who is a follower of Śrī Rūpa and is absorbed in devotional service, their steadiness is only in madhura. 

The madhura and ujjvala rasa is always under the sway of śṛṅgāra. The son of Vraja-rāja is the viṣaya. Aiśvarya is very hidden within it; it becomes intoxicated by the influence of mādhurya. Its āśraya are the devotees.

Rādhā’s face, and the eyes of Śyāma are the cakora. The rope of the love of the sakhīs is attached to the feet.

One fills a plate with various sweets, holding it before Their mouths. With the gopī friends, with much joy, They happily ate Their meal. 

Preparing betel nuts, one sakhī took it and placed it in both Their mouths. They offered hair adorned with flowers, worshipping Them from head to foot, again and again. 

On a bed of flowers, gently, Rādhikā and Śyāma sat. From weariness, with closed eyes, seeing this, even Cupid is enchanted.

Lord Kṛṣṇa, whose body is like a fresh rain cloud, swings with Rādhā on His left. Their beauty is entwined like lightning and a cloud. Moon-like necklaces adorned with star-like jewels sway on Their necks as They swing. Their bodies are gracefully entwined. 

To the rhythmic syllables of the drum, the mṛdaṅga plays an enchanting sound. The gentle sound, conquering all other sounds, spreads throughout the villages and towns—it is beyond description. 

The jeweled ornaments and ankle bells make a jingling sound as They swing. Rādhāmohana expresses hope at Their feet, and Uddhava Dāsa has complete reliance upon Them. His heart is filled with this composition.

“Wake up, O soul, wake up!” says Gorāchānda. How long will you sleep in the lap of the witch Māyā? 

Having come into this material world, thinking, “I will worship,” You remained deluded by the burden of ignorance. 

To deliver you, I have descended as an Avatāra. Who else but Me is your friend? 

I have brought the medicine to destroy Māyā. Take the Harināma-mahāmantra by humbly asking for it. 

Bhaktivinoda, falling at the feet of the Lord, Humbly begged for and received that Harināma-mantra.

By the good fortune of all living entities, the two brothers have appeared on this earth: the moon-like Gaura and Nitāi, who enchant the entire universe.

The three worlds were filled with the nectar of the Holy Name and divine love. Only this servant Locana remains deprived.

jñānī jñānayoge, kariyā jatane, 
brahmera sākṣāt kare 
brahma-sākṣātkāra, aprārabdha karma, 
sampūrṇa jñānete hare 

tabu ta’ prārabdha, nāhi haya kṣaya, 
phalabhoga vinā kabhu 
brahmabhūta jīva, phalabhoga lāgi’, 
janama-maraṇa labhu 

kintu ohe nāma, tava sphūrti ha’le, 
ekāntī janera āra 
prārabdhāprārabdha, kichu nāhi thāke, 
vede gāya bāra bāra 

tomāra udaye, jīvera hṛdaya, 
sampūrṇa śodhita haya 
karmajñāna-bandha, saba dūre jāya, 
anāyāse bhava-kṣaya 

bhakativinoda, bāhu tule kaya, 
nāmera niśāna dhara 
nāmaḍaṅkā-dhvani, kariyā jāibe, 
bheṭibe muralīdhara
IDX.en_translation:
A wise person, through the path of knowledge and with great effort, realizes the Absolute Truth. This realization completely removes the accumulated reactions to past actions through perfect knowledge. 

Even then, the results of current actions are not destroyed; they must still be experienced. A soul absorbed in that Absolute Truth must take birth and death to experience those results. 

But, O Name! When You manifest, for a one-pointed devotee, all karmic reactions cease to exist. The Vedas sing this again and again. 

With Your appearance, the heart of the soul becomes completely purified. All the bondage of action and knowledge goes far away, and material existence is destroyed effortlessly. 

Bhaktivinoda raises his arms and says: “Hold the banner of the Name! By making the sound of the Holy Name resound, you will meet the flute-player!”

IDX.first_line: joga jāga saba chāra ‘śraddhā’ sakalera sāra
IDX.search: joga jaga saba chara sraddha sakalera sara sei sraddha hrdaye jahara udiyache ekabindu krame bhaktirasa sindhu labhe tara haya adhikara jnana karma devadevi bahu jatanete sevi praptaphale haile tucchajnana sadhujana sangavese sri krsnakathaya sese visvasa ta haya balavan
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
joga jāga saba chāra, ‘śraddhā’ sakalera sāra, 
sei śraddhā hṛdaye jāhāra 
udiyāche ekabindu, krame bhaktirasa-sindhu-, 
lābhe tā’ra haya adhikāra 

jñāna, karma, devadevī, bahu jatanete sevi’, 
prāptaphale haile tucchajñāna 
sādhujana-saṅgāveśe, śrī-kṛṣṇakathāya śeṣe, 
viśvāsa ta’ haya balavān 

sei ta’ viśvāse bhāi, “śraddhā” bali sadā gāi, 
bhaktilatā-bīja bali tāre 
karmī jñānī jane jāre, śraddhā bale bāre bāre, 
sei vṛtti śraddhā hoite nāre 

‘nāmera vivāda mātra’, śuniyā ta’ jvale gātra, 
lauhe jadi balaha kāñcana 
tabu lauha lauha raya, kāñcana ta’ kabhu naya, 
maṇi-sparśa nahe jatakṣaṇa 

kṛṣṇa-bhakti cintāmaṇi, tāṅra sparśe lauha-khani, 
karmajñānagata śraddhā-bhāva 
hañā jāya hemabhāra, chāḍiyā ta’ ku-vikāra, 
se kevala maṇira prabhāva
IDX.en_translation:
All yogas and sacrifices are insignificant; faith is the essence of all. One in whose heart a single drop of that faith has arisen, gradually becomes qualified to attain the ocean of the nectar of devotion. 

Even after much endeavor in serving knowledge, fruitive activities, and demigods, when the obtained results are considered insignificant, then through the association of saintly persons and finally hearing topics of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, firm belief becomes strong. 

O brother, we always sing of that firm belief as “faith”, and call it the seed of the creeper of devotion. What the fruitive worker and empiric philosopher repeatedly call faith, that tendency cannot be true faith. 

Hearing that it is “just a dispute of names,” one’s body burns. If you call iron gold, still, iron remains iron, it is never truly gold, until it receives the touch of a divine gem. 

Devotion to Kṛṣṇa is the wish-fulfilling gem. By its touch, an iron mine—the mood of faith related to karma and jñāna—becomes a heap of gold, leaving behind all impurities. That is solely the power of the gem.

IDX.search: joga pithopari sthita astasakhi suvestita vrndaranye kadamba kanane radhasaha vamsi dhari visvajana cittahari prana mora tanhara carane sakhi ajnamata kari dohara sevana palya dasi sada bhavi dohara carana
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses: joga-pīṭhopari sthita, aṣṭasakhī-suveṣṭita, vṛndāraṇye kadamba-kānane rādhāsaha vaṁśī-dhārī, viśvajana-cittahārī, prāṇa mora tāṅhāra caraṇe sakhī-ājñāmata kari dohāra sevana pālya-dāsī sadā bhāvi dohāra caraṇa kabhu kṛpā kari’, mama hasta dhari’, madhura vacana bale tāmbūla loiyā, khāya duijane, mālā laya kutūhale adarśana haya kakhana ki chale nā dekhiyā dohe hiyā mora jvale jekhāne sekhāne, thākuka du’jane, āmi ta’ caraṇa-dāsī milane ānanda, virahe jātanā, sakala samāna vāsi rādhā-kṛṣṇa prāṇa mora jīvane maraṇe more rākhi’ māri’ sukhe thākuka du’jane bhakativinoda, āna nāhi jāne, paḍi’ nijasakhī-pāya rādhikāra gaṇe, thākiyā satata, yugala-caraṇa cāya
IDX.en_translation:
Situated on the altar of union, surrounded by the eight chief companions in the kadamba groves of Vṛndāvana, is the flute-bearer with Rādhā, the captivator of everyone’s heart. My very life is at His feet. 

According to the companions’ command, I serve them both. As a nurtured maidservant, I always meditate on Their feet. 

Sometimes, by Their grace, They take my hand and speak sweet words. Taking betel, They both eat, and they take garlands with eagerness. 

When they disappear by some pretense, my heart burns at not seeing them. 

Wherever They may be, let them remain. I am indeed a maidservant of Their feet. In union, there is joy; in separation, there is distress—I consider all these feelings to be equal. 

Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa are my life in both life and death. Whether protecting me or killing me, let them remain happy. 

Bhaktivinoda knows nothing else. Falling at the feet of his own companions and always remaining among Rādhā’s associates, he desires the feet of the Divine Couple.

IDX.first_line: ka kaliyuge śrī kṛṣṇa caitanya avatāra
IDX.search: ka kaliyuge sri krsna caitanya avatara kha khelivara prabandhe kaila khola karatala ga gadagadi jana prabhu nija sankirtane gha ghare ghare harinama dena sarva jane
IDX.author: narottama-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: ka, kaliyuge śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya avatāra kha, khelivāra prabandhe kaila khola-karatāla ga, gaḍāgaḍi jāna prabhu nija saṅkīrtane gha, ghare ghare harināma dena sarva-jane ṅ, uccaiḥsvare kāṅde prabhu jīvera lāgiyā ca, cetana karāna jīve kṛṣṇa-nāma diyā cha, chala chala kare āṅkhi nayanera jale ja, jagat pavitra kaila gaura-kalevare jha, jhala jhala mukha jena pūrṇa śaśadhara ña, emata ta’ dekhi nāi dayāra sāgara ṭa, ṭalamala kare aṅga bhāvete vibhola ṭha, ṭhamake ṭhamake cale bale hari-bola ḍa, ḍorahi kaupīna kṣīṇa kaṭira upare ḍha, ḍhaliyā ḍhaliyā paḍe gadādharera kroḍe ṇa, āna parasaṅga gorā nā śune śravaṇe ta, tāna māna gāna rase majāila mane tha, thira nāhi haya prabhura nayanera jala da, dīna hīna janere dhariyā deya kola dha, dhoyāiyā pūrava pirīti parasaṅga na, nā jāni kāhāra bhāve hoila tri-bhaṅga pa, premarase bhāsāila akhila-saṁsāra pha, phuṭala śrī-vṛndāvana suradhunī-dhāra ba, brahmā, maheśvara jāṅ’re kare anveṣaṇa bha, bhāviyā nā pā’na jāṅ’re sahasra-locana ma, matta-mātaṅga-gati madhura mṛdu hāsa ja, jaśomatī mātā jāṅ’ra bhuvane prakāśa ra, ratipati jini rūpa ati manorama la, līlā lāvaṇya jāṅ’ra ati anupama ba, vasudeva-suta sei śrī-nanda-nandana śa, śacīra nandana ebe bale sarva-jana ṣa, ṣaḍbhuja rūpa hailā atyāścaryamaya sa, sāvadhāna, prāṇanātha gorā-rasamaya ha, hari hari bala bhāi, kara mahāyajña kṣa, kṣititale janmi’ keha nā haiya avijña e’ cautriśa padāvalī je kare kīrtana dāsa narottama māge tāṅhāra caraṇa
IDX.en_translation:
Ka - In the Age of Kali, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya is the incarnation. Kha - He took up the mṛdaṅga drum and karatālas to arrange His pastimes. 

Ga - The Lord rolls on the ground in His congregational chanting. Gha - He gives the Holy Name to everyone in every home. 

Ṅa - The Lord cries loudly for the sake of the living entities. Ca - He awakens the living entities by giving them the Holy Name of Kṛṣṇa. 

Cha - His eyes are filled with tears. Ja - He purified the universe with His golden body. 

Jha - His face shines like the full moon. Ña - I have never seen such an ocean of mercy. 

Ṭa - His body trembles, overwhelmed with ecstatic emotion. Ṭha - He walks with a graceful gait and chants “Haribol!” 

Ḍa - He wears a loincloth and a belt on His thin waist. Ḍha - Swaying to and fro, He falls into the lap of Gadādhara Paṇḍita. 

Ṇa - Lord Gaura does not hear any other topics with His ears. Ta - His mind is absorbed in the nectar of melodies, beats, and songs. 

Tha - The tears in the Lord’s eyes are never still. Da - Embracing the poor and lowly people, He gives them His mercy. 

Dha - He washes everything with the topics of previous divine love. Na - I do not know in whose mood He became bent in three places. 

Pa - He flooded the entire world with the mellows of divine love. Pha - Śrī Vṛndāvana blossomed in the flow of the celestial Ganges. 

Ba - He is the one whom Lord Brahmā and Lord Śiva search for. Bha - The thousand-eyed Indra cannot find Him even by meditation. 

Ma - His gait is like a maddened elephant, and His smile is sweet and gentle. Ya - Mother Yaśodā is manifest in this world. 

Ra - His form defeats Cupid and is very enchanting. La - His pastimes and beauty are very incomparable. 

Va - He is that same Son of Vasudeva and Son of Nanda. Śa - Everyone now calls Him the Son of Śacī. 

Ṣa - He manifested a six-armed form, which is very wonderful. Sa - Be careful, the Lord of my life, Gaura, is full of divine mellows. 

Ha - Chant “Hari! Hari!” brother, and perform this great sacrifice. Kṣa - Being born on the surface of the earth, do not remain ignorant. 

Whoever chants these thirty-four verses, Narottama Dāsa begs for his lotus feet.

IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses: kabe āhā gaurāṅga baliyā bhojana-śayane, dehera jatana, chāḍiba virakta hañā navadvīpa-dhāme, nagare nagare, abhimāna parihari’ dhāmavāsī-ghare, mādhukarī la’ba, khāiba udara bhari’ nadī-taṭe giyā, añjali añjali, piba prabhu-padajala taru-tale paḍi’, ālasya tyajiba, pāiba śarīre bala kākuti kariyā, ‘gaura-gadādhara’, ‘śrī-rādhā-mādhava’-nāma kāṅdiyā kāṅdiyā, ḍāki’ uccarave, bhramiba sakala dhāma vaiṣṇava dekhiyā, paḍiba caraṇe, hṛdayera bandhu jāni’ vaiṣṇava ṭhākura, ‘prabhura kīrtana’, dekhāibe dāsa māni’
IDX.en_translation:
Alas, when, chanting “Gaurāṅga”, will I become detached and give up caring for my body in eating and sleeping? 

In Navadvīpa-dhāma, from town to town, abandoning false pride, I will beg alms (madhukarī) at the homes of the residents of the dhāma and eat to fill my belly. 

Going to the riverbank, palmful by palmful, I will drink the water of the Lord’s feet. Lying under a tree, I will give up laziness and gain strength in my body. 

Piteously chanting the names “Gaura-Gadādhara”, “Śrī Rādhā-Mādhava”, weeping and weeping, calling out loudly, I will wander throughout the dhāma. 

Seeing a Vaiṣṇava, I will fall at his feet, knowing him to be a friend of my heart. The Vaiṣṇava Ṭhākura, accepting me as his servant, will show me the Lord’s kīrtana.

IDX.en_translation:
When in the wood-lands of Gaura By the bank of the celestial stream With the cry of “Oh Kṛṣṇa, Oh Rādhā!” Shall I roam weeping, Renouncing the pleasures of the body, Under all diverse creepers and Trees? 

At the homes of the basest By begging I will feed, Sip the water of the Sarasvatī, From bank to bank I will roll on the ground With the tumult of cry of Kṛṣṇa? 

To the denizens of the Abode of God Making obeisance I will beg for the trace of mercy: With the particles of dust from the feet of the Vaiṣṇavas Anointing my body, Assuming the garb of the wholly free? 

The denizens of Braja and Gauḍa I will not deem as different, I will be a dweller of Braja-dhāma’s own beauty Will manifest to the eye, I will be the handmaid of Rādhā!

IDX.translation_intro: From The Harmonist, October 1932. Edited by Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī.
IDX.en_translation:
( Tune-Surat, Khambaj, Eltala ) Say, oh will that day be ever mine When all offence ceasing, The relish of the pure Name Will be infused into my heart by the pewer of mercy! 

Owning myself humbler Than the blade of grass, Welcoming the quality of fortitude in my heart, Giving honour to all, Being myself free from all vanity, Oh, when shall I taste the essence of the mellow liquid of the Name! 

Wealth, attendants, And the beautiful maid of poesy, I shall not covet for my happiness. In all my successive births, Be Thou pleased, O Gaur-Hari, To give me causeless devotion to Thy Feet! 

To articulate the Name Of Sree Krishna Horripilation of the body, thickness of the voice, Pallor and shivering Will make their appearance; A constant stream of tears will flow from my eyes. 

Oh, when shall I at Nabadwip, By the bank of the Celestial Stream, Call artlessly upon Gaur and Nityananda, And run about, Dancing and singing, Like one mad, giving up all consideration! 

Oh, when will Nityananda, Taking mercy on me, Absolve me from the infatuation of the world; And giving me the shelter Of His Own Feet Allow me entry into the Mart of the Name! 

And I shall buy and plunder  The mellow liquid of the Name of Hari, Intoxicated by the sweetness of the Name, lose all discretion; And by touching the feet Of those immersed in the mellow liquid Be ceaselessly mellowed by the liquid sweet! 

Oh, when will pity for jiva Manifest its appearance, And with an humble mind, forgetting his own happiness, Bhaktivinode, By humble solicitation, Will propagate the tidings of Divine Command!

IDX.verses:
kabe ha’be hena daśā mora 
tyaji’ jaḍa-āśā, vividha bandhana, 
chāḍiba saṁsāra-ghora 

vṛndāvanābhede, navadvīpa-dhāme, 
bāṅdhiba kuṭīrakhāni 
śacīra nandana-, caraṇa āśraya, 
kariba sambandha māni’ 

jāhnavī-puline, cinmaya-kānane, 
basiyā vijana-sthale 
kṛṣṇa-nāmāmṛta, nirantara piba, 
ḍākiba ‘gaurāṅga’ ba’le 

hā-gaura-nitāi, torā du’ṭī bhāi, 
patitajanera bandhu 
adhama patita, āmi he durjana, 
hoo more kṛpā-sindhu 

kāṅdite kāṅdite, ṣolakrośa-dhāma, 
jāhnavī ubhaya-kūle 
bhramite bhramite, kabhu bhāgya-phale, 
dekhi kichu taru-mūle 

hā hā manohara, ki dekhinu āmi, 
baliyā mūrchita ha’ba 
samvit pāiyā, kāṅdiba gopane, 
smari’ dūhu kṛpā-laba
IDX.en_translation:
When will such a state be mine? Giving up material desires and diverse attachments, I will abandon the dense darkness of this material world. 

In the abode of Navadvīpa, which is non-different from Vṛndāvana, I will build a small cottage. Taking the lotus feet of the son of Śacī as my shelter, I will establish that relationship. 

On the banks of the Ganges, in a spiritual forest, sitting in a secluded spot, I will continuously drink the nectar of Kṛṣṇa’s name, calling out “Gaurāṅga!” 

O Gaura and Nitāi, You two brothers are the friends of the fallen! I am the lowest of the fallen, a wicked person; please become an ocean of mercy for me. 

Weeping, I will wander on both banks of the Ganges through the sixteen-krośa abode. At some point, by good fortune, I will see something at the foot of a tree. 

“Oh, oh, how beautiful! What have I seen?” Saying this, I will faint. Regaining consciousness, I will cry secretly, remembering a drop of Their mercy.
