IDX.verses: kabe kṛṣṇa-dhana pāba, hiyāra mājhāre thoba, juḍāiba tāpita-parāṇa sājāiyā diba hiyā, basāiba prāṇa-priyā, nirakhiba se candra-bayāna he sajani! kabe mora hoibe sudina se prāṇa-nāthera saṅge, kabe vā phiriba raṅge, sukhamaya yamunā-pulina lalitā-viśākhā lañā, tāṅhāre bheṭiba giyā, sājāiyā nānā upahāra sadaya hoiyā vidhi, milāibe guṇa-nidhi, hena bhāgya hoibe āmāra? dāruṇa vidhira nāṭa, bhāṅgila premera hāṭa, tilamātra nā rākhila tā’ra kahe narottama-dāsa, ki mora jīvane āśa, chāḍi’ gela vrajendra-kumāra
IDX.en_translation:
When will I obtain the treasure of Kṛṣṇa? I will place Him in the core of my heart, and soothe my distressed soul. I will decorate my heart, and seat the beloved of my life there; I will gaze upon His moon-like face. 

Oh friend! When will that auspicious day be mine, when with that Lord of my life, I will playfully wander on the blissful banks of the Yamunā? 

Taking Lalitā and Viśākhā, I will go and meet Him, having prepared various offerings. When will providence be merciful and unite me with that treasure-house of qualities? Will such fortune ever be mine? 

The cruel play of fate has broken the marketplace of love, not even a sesame seed’s worth remains of it. Naroṭṭamadasa says, what hope is there in my life, since the Prince of Vraja has left me?

IDX.first_line: kabe mora mūḍha mana chāḍi’ anya dhyāna
IDX.search: kabe mora mudha mana chadi anya dhyana sri krsna carane pabe visramera sthana kabe ami janiba apane akincana amara apeksa ksudra nahi anya jana
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
kabe mora mūḍha mana chāḍi’ anya dhyāna 
śrī-kṛṣṇa-caraṇe pā’be viśrāmera sthāna 

kabe āmi jāniba āpane akiñcana 
āmāra apekṣā kṣudra nāhi anya jana 

kabe āmi ācaṇḍāle kariba praṇati 
kṛṣṇa-bhakti māgi’ la’ba kariyā minati 

sarvajīve dayā mora katadine ha’be 
jīvera durgati dekhi’ lotaka paḍibe 

kāṅdite kāṅdite āmi jā’ba vṛndāvana 
vraja-dhāme vaiṣṇavera loiba śaraṇa 

vrajavāsi-sannidhāne juḍi’ dui kara 
jijñāsiba līlā-sthāna hoiyā kātara 

ohe vrajavāsi! more anugraha kari’ 
dekhāo kothāya līlā karilena hari 

tabe kona vraja-jana sakṛpa-antare 
āmāre jā’bena la’ye vipina-bhitare 

balibena, dekha ei kadamba-kānana 
jathā rāsa-līlā kailā vrajendra-nandana 

ai dekha nandagrāma nandera āvāsa 
ai dekha baladeva jathā kailā rāsa 

ai dekha jathā haila dukūla-haraṇa 
ai sthāne bakāsura hoila nidhana 

eirūpa vraja-janasaha vṛndāvane 
dekhiba līlāra sthāna satṛṣṇa-nayane 

kabhu vā yamunā-tīre śuni’ vaṁśīdhvani 
avaśa hoiyā lābha kariba dharaṇī 

kṛpāmaya vraja-jana ‘kṛṣṇa’ ‘kṛṣṇa’ bali’ 
pāna karāibe jala pūriyā añjali 

harināma śune punaḥ pāiyā cetana 
vraja-jana-saha āmi kariba bhramaṇa 

kabe hena śubhadina hoibe āmāra 
mādhukarī kari’ beḍāiba dvāra dvāra 

yamunā-salila piba añjali bhariyā 
devadvāre rātrikāle rahiba śuiyā 

jakhana āsibe kāla e bhautika pura 
jalajantu-mahotsava hoibe pracura 

siddhadehe nija kuñje sakhīra caraṇe 
nityakāla thākiyā seviba kṛṣṇa-dhane 

ei se prārthanā kare e pāmara chāra 
śrī-jāhnavā more dayā kara’ eibāra
IDX.en_translation:
When will my foolish mind abandon all other thoughts and find a place of rest at the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa? 

When will I truly know myself as insignificant, realizing that there is no one smaller than me? 

When will I offer my obeisances even to the outcasts and beg for devotion to Kṛṣṇa with humble prayers? 

When will compassion for all living beings awaken in me? Seeing the suffering of all souls, tears will fall from my eyes. 

Weeping, I will go to Vṛndāvana and take shelter of the devotees in that sacred land. 

Joining my hands before the residents of Vraja, I will anxiously inquire about the places of the Lord’s pastimes. 

“O residents of Vraja! Please be merciful to me and show me where the Lord performed His pastimes.” 

Then some compassionate resident of Vraja will take me into the forest. 

He will say, “Look, this is the kadamba forest where the son of the King of Vraja performed the rāsa dance. 

“Look, there is Nandagrāma, the home of Nanda; look, there Baladeva performed the rāsa dance. 

“Look, there the stealing of the clothes took place; in that very spot, the demon Bakāsura was killed.” 

In this way, with the residents of Vraja, I will see the places of these pastimes with eager eyes. 

Sometimes, on the bank of the Yamunā, hearing the sound of the flute, I will become overwhelmed and fall to the ground. 

The merciful residents of Vraja, repeatedly chanting “Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa!”, will offer me water from their cupped hands. 

Hearing the Holy Name and regaining consciousness, I will travel with the residents of Vraja. 

When will such an auspicious day be mine, that I will wander from door to door begging for alms? 

I will drink the water of the Yamunā from my cupped hands, and at night I will lie down at the temple gate. 

When my time comes to leave this material body, a great festival for aquatic creatures will take place. 

With a perfected spiritual body, in my own grove at the feet of the companions, I will eternally remain and serve the treasure that is Kṛṣṇa. 

This lowly wretch makes this prayer: O Śrī Jāhnavā, please bestow Your mercy upon me now.

IDX.first_line: kabe mui vaiṣṇava ciniba hari hari
IDX.search: kabe mui vaisnava ciniba hari hari vaisnava carana kalyanera khani matiba hrdaye dhari vaisnava thakura aprakrta sada nirdosa anandamayakrsna name prita jade udasina jivete dayardra haya
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses: kabe mui vaiṣṇava ciniba hari hari vaiṣṇava-caraṇa, kalyāṇera khani, mātiba hṛdaye dhari’ vaiṣṇava-ṭhākura, aprākṛta sadā, nirdoṣa, ānandamayakṛṣṇa-nāme prīta, jaḍe udāsīna, jīvete dayārdra haya abhimāna-hīna, bhajane pravīṇa, viṣayete anāsaktaantara-bāhire, niṣkapaṭa sadā, nityalīlā-anurakta kaniṣṭha, madhyama, uttama prabhede, vaiṣṇava trividha gaṇikaniṣṭhe ādara, madhyame praṇati, uttame śuśrūṣā śuni je jena vaiṣṇava, ciniyā loiyā, ādara kariba jabevaiṣṇavera kṛpā, jāhe sarva-siddhi, avaśya pāiba tabe vaiṣṇava-caritra, sarvadā pavitra, jei ninde hiṁsā kari’bhakativinoda, nā sambhāṣe tā’re, thāke sadā mauna dhari
IDX.en_translation:
When will I recognize a vaiṣṇava, O Hari, Hari! The feet of a vaiṣṇava, is a mine of auspiciousness, I will hold them in my heart with ecstasy. 

Vaiṣṇava-ṭhākura is always transcendental, Faultless, full of joy. Pleased by the name of Kṛṣṇa, indifferent to material things, Compassionate to all living beings. 

Devoid of false ego, expert in devotional service, Unattached to worldly objects. Always sincere, both internally and externally, Attached to the eternal pastimes of the Lord. 

Dividing vaiṣṇavas into neophyte, intermediate, and advanced, I consider vaiṣṇavas to be of three types. Affection for the neophyte, obeisances to the intermediate, And I hear of rendering service to the advanced. 

When I recognize each vaiṣṇava according to their stage, And offer them respect, Then by the mercy of the vaiṣṇava, which is the source of all perfection, I will certainly attain it. 

The character of a vaiṣṇava is always pure. Whoever slanders them out of envy, Bhaktivinoda does not converse with such a person, And always remains silent.

IDX.first_line: kabe śrī caitanya more karibena dayā
IDX.search: kabe sri caitanya more karibena daya kabe ami paiba vaisnavapada chaya kabe ami chadiba e visayabhimana kabe visnu jane ami kariba sammana
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses: kabe śrī-caitanya more karibena dayā kabe āmi pāiba vaiṣṇavapada-chāyā kabe āmi chāḍiba e viṣayābhimāna kabe viṣṇu-jane āmi kariba sammāna galavastra kṛtāñjali vaiṣṇava-nikaṭe dante tṛṇa kari’ dāṅḍāiba niṣkapaṭe kāṅdiyā kāṅdiyā jānāiba duḥkhagrāma saṁsāra-anala haite māgiba viśrāma śuniyā āmāra duḥkha vaiṣṇava ṭhākura āmā’ lāgi’ kṛṣṇe āvedibena pracura vaiṣṇavera āvedane kṛṣṇa dayāmaya e hena pāmara-prati ha’bena sadaya vinodera nivedana vaiṣṇava-caraṇe kṛpā kari’ saṅge laha ei akiñcane
IDX.en_translation:
When will Śrī Caitanya show mercy to me? When will I obtain the shade of the feet of the devotees? 

When will I abandon this false ego of material enjoyment? When will I offer respect to the devotees of the Lord? 

With a cloth around my neck and with folded hands, I will approach the devotees. Holding a blade of grass in my teeth, I will stand before them sincerely. 

Weeping uncontrollably, I will reveal the multitude of my miseries. From the fire of material existence, I will beg for relief. 

Having heard my miseries, the revered devotee will appeal greatly to Kṛṣṇa for me. 

By the appeal of that devotee, the merciful Kṛṣṇa will become kind toward such a fallen soul. 

This is the humble submission of Bhaktivinoda at the feet of the devotees: “Please be merciful and take this insignificant one along with you.”

IDX.first_line: kadācit kālindī taṭa vipina saṅgīta taralo
IDX.search: kadacit kalindi tata vipina sangita taralo mudabhiri nari vadana kamalasvada madhupah rama sambhu brahma marapati ganesarcitapado jagannathah svami nayanapatha gami bhavatu me bhuje savye venum sirasi sikhi piccham katitate dukulam netrante sahacari kataksam vidadhate sada srimad vrndavana vasati lila paricayo jagannathah svami nayanapatha gami bhavatu me
IDX.author: śrī śaṅkarācārya
IDX.verses:
kadācit kālindī-taṭa-vipina-saṅgīta-taralo 
mudābhīrī-nārī-vadana-kamalāsvāda-madhupaḥ 
ramā-śambhu-brahma-marapati-gaṇeśārcitapado 
jagannāthaḥ svāmī nayanapatha-gāmī bhavatu me 

bhuje savye veṇuṁ śirasi śikhi-picchaṁ kaṭitaṭe 
dukūlaṁ netrānte sahacari-kaṭākṣaṁ vidadhate 
sadā śrīmad-vṛndāvana-vasati-līlā-paricayo 
jagannāthaḥ svāmī nayanapatha-gāmī bhavatu me 

mahāmbhodhes-tīre kanaka-rucire nīla-śikhare 
vasan prāsādāntaḥ sahaja-balabhadreṇa balinā 
subhadrā-madhyasthaḥ sakala-sura-sevāvasarado 
jagannāthaḥ svāmī nayanapatha-gāmī bhavatu me 

kṛpā-pārāvāraḥ sajala-jalada-śreṇi-ruciro 
ramā-vāṇī-rāmaḥ sphuradamala-paṅkeruha-mukhaḥ 
surendrairārādhyaḥ śrutigaṇaśikhā gītacarito 
jagannāthaḥ svāmī nayanapatha-gāmī bhavatu me 

rathārūḍho gacchan pathi milita-bhūdeva-paṭalaiḥ 
stuti-prādurbhāvaṁ pratipadamupākarṇya sadayaḥ 
dayāsindhurbandhuḥ sakala jagatāṁ sindhu-sutayā 
jagannāthaḥ svāmī nayanapatha-gāmī bhavatu me 

paraṁbrahmāpīḍaḥ kuvalaya-dalotphulla-nayano 
nivāsī nīlādrau nihita-caraṇo‛nanta-śirasi 
rasānandī rādhā-sarasa-vapurāliṅgana-sukho 
jagannāthaḥ svāmī nayanapatha-gāmī bhavatu me 

na vai jāce rājyaṁ na ca kanaka-māṇikya-vibhavaṁ 
na jāce‛haṁ ramyāṁ sakala-jana-kāmyāṁ varavadhūm 
sadā kāle kāle pramatha-patinā gīta-carito 
jagannāthaḥ svāmī nayanapatha-gāmī bhavatu me 

hara tvaṁ saṁsāraṁ drutatarama-sāraṁ sura-pate! 
hara tvaṁ pāpānāṁ vitatima-parāṁ jādava-pate! 
aho dīne‛nāthe nihita-caraṇo niścitamidaṁ 
jagannāthaḥ svāmī nayanapatha-gāmī bhavatu me 

jagannāthāṣṭakaṁ puṇyaṁ 
jaḥ paṭhet prayataḥ śuciḥ 
sarva-pāpa-viśuddhātmā 
viṣṇulokaṁ sa gacchati
IDX.en_translation:
Sometimes He is vibrant with music in the forest groves on the banks of the Yamunā, a bee joyfully relishing the lotus-like faces of the cowherd women; whose feet are worshiped by Lakṣmī, Śiva, Brahmā, Indra, and Gaṇeśa—may that Jagannātha, the Lord of the Universe, be the object of my vision. 

With a flute on His left arm, a peacock feather on His head, a fine garment around His waist, and the sidelong glances of His companions at the corners of His eyes; He is ever famous for His pastimes of residing in glorious Vṛndāvana—may that Jagannātha, the Lord of the Universe, be the object of my vision. 

Residing within His temple on the golden, beautiful Blue Peak on the shore of the great ocean, with His strong elder brother Balabhadra; He stands with Subhadrā in the middle, granting the opportunity for service to all the gods—may that Jagannātha, the Lord of the Universe, be the object of my vision. 

He is an ocean of mercy, charming like a fresh cloud; the beloved of Lakṣmī and Sarasvatī, with a glowing, pure lotus-like face; He is worshiped by the chief of the gods, and His glories are sung by the highest Vedic texts—may that Jagannātha, the Lord of the Universe, be the object of my vision. 

Riding on His chariot and proceeding along the path, He is met by groups of priests; He graciously hears the manifestation of their praise at every step; He is an ocean of compassion, a friend to all the worlds, accompanied by Lakṣmī—may that Jagannātha, the Lord of the Universe, be the object of my vision. 

He is the crown jewel of the Supreme Absolute, with eyes wide open like blooming blue lotus petals; He resides on the Blue Mountain, placing His feet on the head of the cosmic serpent; He experiences the joy of divine mellows, blissful from embracing the charming form of Rādhā—may that Jagannātha, the Lord of the Universe, be the object of my vision. 

I do not pray for a kingdom, nor for the opulence of gold and jewels; I do not pray for a beautiful bride desired by all; His glories are always sung by Śiva in every age—may that Jagannātha, the Lord of the Universe, be the object of my vision. 

O Lord of the gods! Quickly remove this worthless material existence! O Lord of the Yādavas! Remove the vast multitude of my sins! Oh, it is certain that His feet are placed on the helpless and destitute—may that Jagannātha, the Lord of the Universe, be the object of my vision. 

One who recites these eight sacred verses on Jagannātha with devotion and purity, with a soul purified from all sins, goes to the abode of Viṣṇu.

IDX.first_line: kadamba tarura ḍāla nāmiyāche bhūme bhāla
IDX.search: kadamba tarura dala namiyache bhume bhala phutiyache phula sari sari parimale bharala sakala vrndavana keli kare bhramara bhramari rai kanu vilasoi range kiba rupa lavani vaidagdhakhani dhani manimaya abharana ange
IDX.author: narottama-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: kadamba tarura ḍāla, nāmiyāche bhūme bhāla, phuṭiyāche phula sāri sāri parimale bharala, sakala vṛndāvana, keli kare bhramarā bhramarī rāi-kānu vilāsoi raṅge kibā rūpa lāvaṇi, vaidagdhakhani dhani, maṇimaya ābhāraṇa āṅge rādhāra dakṣiṇa kara, dhari’ priya giridhara, madhura madhura cali’ jāya āge pāche sakhī-gaṇa, kare phula variṣaṇa, kona sakhī cāmara ḍhulāya parāge dhūsara sthala, candra kare suśītala, maṇimaya vedīra upare rāi-kānu kara joḍi’, nṛtya kare phiri’ phiri’, paraśe pulake tanu bhare tāra madhye hemapīṭha, aṣṭadale veṣṭita, aṣṭadale pradhānā nāyikā tā’ra madhye ratnāsane, basi āchena duijane, śyāma saṅge sundarī rādhikā orūpa lāvaṇyarāśi, amiya paḍeche khasi’, hāsya parihāsa-sambhāṣaṇe narottama-dāsa kaya, nityalīlā sukhamaya, sadāi sphuruka mora mane mṛgamada-candana, kare kari’ sakhī-gaṇa, barikhaye phula gandharāje śramajala bindu bindu, śobhā kare mukha-indu, adhare muralī kibā bāje hāsya-vilāsa-rasa, sarala madhura bhāṣa, narottama-manoratha bharu duhūka vicitra veśa, kusume racita keśa, locana-mohana līlā karu
IDX.en_translation:
The branches of the kadamba tree have bent beautifully to the ground, and flowers have blossomed in rows upon rows. The entire Vṛndāvana is filled with fragrance, while bees playfully hum. 

Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa enjoy playfully with great joy. Oh, what beauty and charm! A treasure-mine of cleverness, Their bodies are adorned with jeweled ornaments. 

Holding Rādhā’s right hand, her dear Giridhara walks very sweetly. Before and behind Them, the companions shower flowers, while some fan Them with whisks. 

The ground is dusty with pollen, and the moon makes it very cool; upon a jeweled platform, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa dance with joined hands, turning around and around, Their bodies filled with ecstatic thrills at each other’s touch. 

In its midst is a golden seat surrounded by eight petals; among them are the principal companions. Upon a jeweled throne, both of Them are seated—beautiful Rādhikā with her dark Lord. 

From that abundance of beauty and charm, nectar overflows in Their laughter, jokes, and conversations. Narottama dāsa says: the eternal pastimes are full of joy; may they always manifest in my mind. 

Holding musk and sandalwood paste in their hands, the companions shower Them with fragrant flowers. Drops of perspiration adorn Their moon-like faces. Oh, how beautifully the flute plays on His lips! 

The mellow of playful laughter and simple sweet speech—may Narottama’s heart’s desires be fulfilled. In Their wonderful dresses, with Their hair adorned with flowers, They perform eye-enchanting pastimes.

IDX.search: kadaye ninduka saba kari haya haya eka bara nadiyaya ele dhirava tara paya na jani mahima guna kahiyachi kata ei bara lagaila paile haba anugata

IDX.verses: kādaye ninduka saba kari hāya hāya eka-bāra nadīyāya ele dhirava tāra pāya nā jāni mahimā guṇa kahiyāchi kata ei-bāra lāgāila pāile haba anugata deśe deśe kata jīva tarāila śuni caraṇe dharile dayā karibe āpani nā budhiyā kahiyāchi kata kuvacana ei-vara pāile tāra laiba śaraṇe gaurangera sange jata pāriṣada-gaṇe tārā saba suniyāchi patita-pāvana ninduka pāṣanda jata pāila prakāśa kādiyā ākula bhela vṛndāvana-dāsa
IDX.en_translation:
All the critics cry out “Alas! Alas!” If one comes to Nadīyā just once, he takes shelter of Your feet. 

Not knowing Your glorious qualities, I have spoken so much. This time, if I attain You, I will become submissive. 

I hear that You have delivered so many souls in every land. If I hold onto Your feet, You Yourself will show mercy. 

Not understanding, I have spoken so many abusive words. This time, if I attain You, I will take shelter of Him. 

All the associates with Gaurāṅga, I have heard that they all are patita-pāvana. 

All the critics and miscreants obtained enlightenment. Vṛndāvana Dāsa became overwhelmed, weeping.

A certain beautiful cowherd woman, separated by a quarrel, her body distressed by the heat of separation, anxiously spoke to her friend: 

Alas, Gauri! Will He walk the path of my eyes? Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the ocean of mercy, Kṛṣṇa, the beloved of Gokula? 

Govinda, the supreme bliss, the auspiciousness of Nanda’s home, the ruby from the mine of Yaśodā, the moon of the ocean of the king of cowherds. 

His splendor mocks the brilliance of a fresh raincloud. He is covered by a yellow garment (pītāmbara) that defeats the pride of gold. 

The luster of His toenails steals the pride of Kandarpa’s beauty. His feet shine with the marks of the flag, lotus, thunderbolt, barley, and goad. 

His anklets chirp like wagtails in the cage of His feet. His knees are brilliant, holding the shape of a jewelry box or blue gems. 

His thighs have the beauty of the trunk of an intoxicated elephant. His broad hips are surrounded by a girdle of jeweled bells. 

The sweetness of His waist destroys the pride of the lion. His broad chest is like a great emerald mountain. 

His conch-like neck is adorned with a king of jewels. The power of His arms challenges the jeweled pillars of Indra. 

His face defeats the beauty of millions of full moons. He is an ocean of waves of charm, His lips comparable to vermillion. 

His eyes are filled with the beauty of a blossoming lotus. Shark-shaped earrings dance, swinging at the edge of His cheeks. 

His radiant form expands with the onset of fresh youth. The prowess of His sidelong glances surpasses millions of bows of Cupid. 

His noble speech is laden with the sweetness of nectar. He is the fragrant elephant of the caves and bowers of the dense forest of Vṛndāvana. 

He is the fresh cloud on the lap of the high peaks of blessed Govardhana. He is the auspicious swan playing in the Yamunā. 

He is the delight of Nandīśvara, the dancer on the banks of Bhāṇḍīra. He is the killer of Śaṅkhacūḍa, and He made the lord of mountains His playing ball. 

He is as deep as millions of oceans, as powerful as millions of lions. He delights the son of Rohiṇī and has intense friendship with Śrīdāmā. 

He is dear to Subala due to love, the heart-throb of His friends. He has taken a great vow to ignite the bliss of the people of Nanda’s Vraja. 

His circle of flute music gathers the herds of cows. He is eager for the sport of fighting with tall bulls. 

He is the personification of the erotic sentiment of the forest, the chosen deity of amorous love. His bright form is marked by a bunch of raised peacock feathers. 

He is worshipped with a garland of five colors hovered over by moving bees. His belt is strung with golden jasmine flowers and red raṅgaṇa flowers. 

His body is a wave of beauty painted with various mineral pigments. His ornaments are made of heaps of guñjā berries, and His bed is of tender leaves. 

The fragrance of His body increases the intoxication of the young women. He inflames the desire of the lotus-eyed girls of Vṛndāvana. 

He is muddy with the kunkuma from the breasts of the cowherd women who are agitated by Cupid. The stream of sweetness from His moon-like face blocks the eyes of chaste women. 

He is the plunderer of the garments of the unmarried girls. He is expert in mature, playful joking. He is the ocean of nectar for Rādhā, anointed with abundant, charming cleverness. 

He is the autumn season for the moonlight of Candrāvalī’s intelligence. He possesses the fortune of being a steady and charming lover (dhīra-lalita), beautiful with the joy of Cupid. 

He is the moon for the cakora bird of Candrāvalī. He is the honey for the mādhavī creeper of Rādhikā. He is charming in His pastimes with Lalitā, and the moon for the star Viśākhā. 

He is a row of lotuses for the face of Padmā. His lotus feet are served by Śaibyā. He sleeps in the heart of Bhadrā, and yearns for the love of Śyāmalā. 

He is the garden of extraordinary, astonishing pastimes. He is the magnet for the wealth of love, the beloved who has made a vow of iron-like attraction. 

He is the thief of the flute, the snatcher of the bodices of the golden-limbed girls. He is the all-in-all of Rādhā’s tryst, the guru of extensive amorous skills. 

His body is bound by the creeper of Rādhā’s playful words and desire to hear them. He is eager to be blocked by Rādhikā, who takes away His garland of kadamba flowers. 

He delights in union with Rādhā, hidden in the lap of the bower. He is struck by the lotus-earring of the dignified Rādhā during their wild sports. 

His armor is the crushed kunkuma from the battle of love. He has a form with three bends, and His lips are joined with the flute. 

The elegance of His flute music spreads the essence of celestial melodies. He is the king of thousands of groups of gopīs, maddened by the intense mellows of the rāsa dance. 

The corner of His eye agitates millions of Cupid’s five arrows. He has begun a dance in the circle on the bank of the Yamunā. 

He is the lake for the bee of Vṛṣabhānu’s daughter, the wish-fulfilling cow. He creates a smile on Rādhikā’s face with His hidden, meaningful jokes. 

His soul is hidden in the dress of a woman, astounding the mind. His lotus mouth is mixed with betel containing camphor. 

He is skilled in arranging reconciliation through the messenger of the proud Candrāvalī. He is struck by Rādhā’s frown when blocked at the banks of the deceitful toll-station. 

He is embarrassed by the reproaches disguised as laughter from Rādhā’s expert friends. He is the embodied love of the cowherd women, the form of welfare and bliss. 

He is eager for the tinkling sound of Bhadrā’s bells as she happily goes to the tryst. His path is watched by Padmā who is preparing the bed. 

He has become the object of the anxious Lalitā’s conjectures. He increases the burden of lamentation of the cheated Viśākhā. 

He is sought after by Śyāmā, who regrets her quarrel. He relishes the angry words of the fiercely intelligent, betrayed Śaibyā. 

He is delighted by the message of Candrāvalī, who is distressed by separation. He is expert in decorating the blossoming Rādhā, who controls her Lover. 

He is held by the hem of the garment by Rādhā, who won the wager of kissing the flute. His heart is bewildered by the whirlpool of Rādhā’s love. 

Thus, with a mind maddened by love, she described the Crusher of Kaṁsa. Seeing Him appearing before her, she attained a festival of mature bliss. 

May the wise lovingly dive into this “Premendu-sāgara” (Ocean of the Moon of Love), consisting of one hundred and eight names, which is a Mandara mountain for the tongue.

udañcan-mārtaṇḍa-dyuti-hara-dukūlāñcita-kaṭiḥ

sa devaś caitanyākṛtir atitarāṁ naḥ kṛpayatu

IDX.en_translation:
In this age of Kali, learned persons worship Him—who is fair-complexioned but is Kṛṣṇa Himself—through sacrificial rites consisting of the loud chanting of His names. They declare Him to be the worshipable object for all who have accepted the renounced order of life. May that Lord, in the form of Caitanya, bestow upon us His abundant mercy. 

He performs dear pastimes that are a source of joy even for the sinful, perfectly removing the sorrow of Mother Śacī with sounds of victory. His waist is adorned with silken cloth that surpasses the effulgence of the rising sun. May that Lord, in the form of Caitanya, bestow upon us His abundant mercy. 

Eager to enjoy a certain boundless, sweet flood of mellows belonging to His loving devotees, He has stolen Their mood. He covered His own dark complexion and manifested Their golden effulgence here. May that Lord, in the form of Caitanya, bestow upon us His abundant mercy. 

Though difficult to worship with love for a long time by those attached to a demoniac mentality, He bestows a divine nature upon the surrendered, being the supreme deity in the three worlds. He is glorious and naturally sweet with bliss and constantly triumphs. May that Lord, in the form of Caitanya, bestow upon us His abundant mercy. 

He is the refuge of the people of Bengal and manifested the glories of Navadvīpa, adorning the community of learned priests glorified by the world. By accepting them, He purifies the status of the highest order of renunciants on earth. May that Lord, in the form of Caitanya, bestow upon us His abundant mercy. 

Having first drunk the sweet nectar of the Holy Name through His mouth, He emits it through the doors of His eyes under the guise of profuse tears. His body is thrilled to manifest the essence of divine love on earth. May that Lord, in the form of Caitanya, bestow upon us His abundant mercy. 

Manifesting a body with the effulgence of new gold, He is adorned at the waist with a water pot, and His gait is like that of a young elephant king. He gives instruction to His dear ones by the charm of His own remnants. May that Lord, in the form of Caitanya, bestow upon us His abundant mercy. 

His smiling glance completely takes away the sorrow of the worlds, and the very beginning of His speech causes hosts of auspiciousness to sprout. The shelter of His feet bestows floods of divine love upon everyone. May that Lord, in the form of Caitanya, bestow upon us His abundant mercy. 

The glories of the son of Śacī are as dense as the fresh fragrance of a cluster of flowers. May that fortunate person who reads these eight verses with a joyful heart be made happy at every step with unobstructed auspiciousness, as the Lord bestows devotion at His own lotus feet.

IDX.en_translation:
Her eye turns in every direction, like a lotus flower moved by a gentle breeze. 

(Rādhā) enters the pleasure grove; with every step, the obstacles of manasija (the god of love) arise. 

Placing soft, slow steps, like the gait of an elephant. 

Spoken by the poet Rāmānanda Rāya, this delights Rudra-gajādhipa (Gajapati Mahārāja Pratāparudra).

IDX.search: kali ghora timire garasala jaga jana dharama karama rahu dura asadhane cintamani vidhi milaola ani gora bada dayara thakura bhaire bhai gora guna kahana na jaya kata sata anana kata caturanana varaniya ora nahi paya
IDX.author: nayanānanda dāsa
IDX.verses: kali-ghora timire, garāsala jaga-jana, dharama karama rahu dūra asādhane cintāmaṇi, vidhi milāola āni’, gorā baḍa dayāra ṭhākura bhāire bhāi, gorā-guṇa kahana nā jāya kata śata ānana, kata caturānana, varaṇiyā ora nāhi pāya cāriveda ṣaḍ-, daraśana paḍi’, se jadi gaurāṅga nāhi bhaje vṛthā tā’ra adhyayana, locanavihīnajana, darapaṇe andhe kibā kāje veda vidyā dui, kichui nā jānata, se jadi gaurāṅga jāne sāra nayanānanda bhaṇe, sei ta’ sakali jāne, sarvasiddhi karatale tā’ra
IDX.en_translation:
In the dense darkness of the Age of Kali, the people of the world are swallowed up, and righteousness and pious activities remain far away. Without any effort on our part, destiny has brought us a wish-fulfilling gem. Lord Gorā is a very merciful Master. 

O brothers! The qualities of Lord Gorā cannot be described. Even with hundreds of mouths, or even the four-faced Brahmā himself, one cannot reach the limit of His glories. 

Having studied the four Vedas and the six systems of philosophy, if one does not worship Lord Gaurāṅga, his study is in vain. For a person without eyes, of what use is a mirror? 

Even if one knows nothing of the Vedas or other knowledge, if he knows Lord Gaurāṅga as the essence, Nayanānanda says: “He indeed knows everything. All perfection is in the palm of his hand.”

IDX.verses:
kali-yuga-pāvana viśvambhara 
gauḍa-cita-gagana-śaśadhara 
 
kīrtana-vidhātā, paraprema-dātā, 
śacī-suta puraṭa-sundara
IDX.en_translation:
All glories to Viśvambhara, the purifier of the Kali age! He is the moon in the sky of the hearts of the devotees of Bengal. 

He is the ordainer of congregational chanting and the giver of supreme divine love—the son of Śacī, beautiful as pure gold.

kalikukkura-kadana jadi cāo (he) 
kaliyuga-pāvana, kalibhaya-nāśana, 
śrī-śacī-nandana gāo (he) 

gadādhara-mādana, nitā’yera prāṇa-dhana, 
advaitera prapūjita gorā 
nimāñi viśvambhara, śrīnivāsa-īśvara, 
bhaktasamūha-cita-corā 

nadīyā-śaśadhara, māyāpura-īśvara, 
nāma-pravartana sura 
gṛhi-jana-śikṣaka, nyāsikula-nāyaka, 
mādhava rādhā-bhāva-pura 

sārva-bhauma-śodhana, gajapati-tāraṇa, 
rāmānanda-poṣaṇa vīra 
rūpānanda-vardhana, sanātana-pālana, 
haridāsa-modana dhīra 

vrajarasa-bhāvana, duṣṭamata-śātana, 
kapaṭi-vighātana kāma 
śuddhabhakta-pālana, śuṣkajñāna-tāḍana, 
chalabhakti-dūṣaṇa rāma
IDX.en_translation:
If you wish to conquer the dogs of the Kali age, sing the glories of the son of Śacī, who purifies the age and destroys its fears. 

He is the enchanter of Gadādhara and the life-treasure of Nitāi; the fair-complexioned Lord worshiped by Advaita, Nimāi, and Viśvambhara—the Lord of Śrīnivāsa and the thief of the hearts of all devotees. 

He is the moon of Nadiyā, the Lord of Māyāpur, and the hero who inaugurates the chanting of the Holy Name. He is the teacher of householders, the leader of the renunciants, and the Lord who is fully imbued with the emotions of Rādhā. 

He purified Sārvabhauma and delivered King Pratāparudra; He is the heroic protector of Rāmānanda Rāya, the one who increases the bliss of Rūpa Gosvāmī, the maintainer of Sanātana Gosvāmī, and the sober Lord who enchants Haridāsa Ṭhākura. 

He cultivates the mellows of Vraja and destroys wicked philosophies. He is the desire to defeat the deceitful and the protector of pure devotees—the Lord who chastises dry speculation and condemns hypocritical devotion.

IDX.author: rūpa gosvāmī
IDX.verses:
kandarpa-koṭi-ramyāya sphurad-indīvara-tviṣe 
jagan-mohana-līlāya namo gopendra-sūnave 

kṛṣṇalā-kṛta-hārāya kṛṣṇa-lāvaṇya-śāline 
kṛṣṇākūla-karīndrāya kṛṣṇāya karavai namaḥ 

sarvānanda-kadambāya kandamba-kusuma-sraje 
namaḥ premāvalambāya pralambāri-kanīyase 

kuṇḍala-sphurad-aṁsāya vaṁśāyatta-mukha-śriye 
rādhā-mānasa-haṁsāya vrajottaṁsāya te namaḥ 

namaḥ śikhaṇḍa-cūḍāya daṇḍa-maṇḍita-pāṇaye 
kuṇḍalī-kṛta-puṣpāya puṇḍarīkekṣaṇāya te 

rādhikā-prema-mādhvīka-mādhurī-muditāntaram 
kandarpa-vṛnda-saundaryaṁ govindam abhivādaye 

śṛṅgāra-rasa-śṛṅgāraṁ karṇikārātta-karṇikam 
vande śriyā navābhrāṇāṁ vibhrāṇaṁ vibhramaṁ harim 

sādhvī-vrata-maṇi-vrāta-paśyato-hara-veṇave 
kahlāra-kṛta-cūḍāya śaṅkha-cūḍa-bhide namaḥ 

rādhikādhara-bandhūka-makaranda-madhuvratam 
daitya-sindhura-pārīndraṁ vande gopendra-nandanam 

varhendrāyudha-ramyāya jagaj-jīvana-dāyine 
rādhā-vidyud-vṛtāṅgāya kṛṣṇāmbhodāya te namaḥ 

premāndha-vallavī-vṛnda-locanendīvarendave 
kāśmīra-tilakāḍhyāya namaḥ pītāmbarāya te 

gīrvāṇeśa-madoddāma dāva-nirvāṇa-nīradam 
kandūkī-kṛta-śailendraṁ vande gokula-bāndhavam 

dainyārṇave nimagno’smi mantu-grāva-bharārditaḥ 
duṣṭe kāruṇya-pārīṇa mayi kṛṣṇa kṛpāṁ kuru 

ādhāro’py aparādhānām aviveka-hato’py aham 
tvat-kāruṇya-pratīkṣo’smi prasīda mayi mādhava
IDX.en_translation:
Salutations to the son of Nanda, who is charming like millions of Cupids, whose effulgence is like a blooming blue lotus, and whose pastimes enchant the world. 

I offer my obeisances to Kṛṣṇa, who wears a garland of berries, who possesses dark beauty, and who is like a powerful, dark elephant. 

Salutations to Him who is a cluster of all joys, who wears a garland of kadamba flowers, who is the support of divine love, and who is the younger brother of Balarāma. 

Salutations to You, whose shoulders shine with earrings, whose face is beautiful with the flute, who is the swan in the mind of Rādhā, and who is the best jewel of Vraja. 

Salutations to You, who wears a peacock feather on His crown, whose hand is adorned with a staff, who wears flowers as earrings, and whose eyes are like lotuses. 

I bow down to Govinda, whose heart is delighted by the sweetness of the nectar-like love of Rādhikā, and whose beauty is like a multitude of Cupids. 

I offer obeisances to Hari, who is the ornament of the mellow of conjugal love, who has yellow flowers in His ears, and who assumes the charm of fresh dark clouds with His splendor. 

Salutations to Him whose flute steals the vows of chaste women just by its sight, who has a white lotus on His crown, and who is the slayer of Śaṅkha-cūḍa. 

I offer obeisances to the son of Nanda, who is like a bee to the honey of the red flower of Rādhikā’s lips and like a lion to the elephants of the demons. 

Salutations to You, who are beautiful with a peacock feather like a rainbow, the giver of life to the universe, whose body is surrounded by Rādhā like lightning, and who are like a dark cloud. 

Salutations to You who wear yellow garments, who are like the moon to the lotuses of the eyes of the love-blinded cowherd girls, and who are adorned with a mark of saffron. 

I offer obeisances to the friend of Gokula, who is like a cloud extinguishing the fire of Indra’s pride and who made Govardhana Hill into a play-ball. 

O Kṛṣṇa, O ocean of mercy! I am immersed in the ocean of misery, afflicted by the heavy burden of my offenses. Please bestow Your mercy upon me, the wicked one. 

O Mādhava! Even though I am a repository of offenses and slain by ignorance, I am awaiting Your mercy. Please be pleased with me.

IDX.first_line: kānta sane vihariyā svakīya mandire giyā
IDX.search: kanta sane vihariya svakiya mandire giya snana kari nija ramyavese krsnasukhalokanande rahe dhani paranande sakhigana saha krsnavese gocarana hoite kanta asibena haye sranta sei sranti karibare dura nanavidha bhaksyapeya prastuta karena temha upahara dibena pracura
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
kānta-sane vihariyā, svakīya mandire giyā, 
snāna kari nija ramyaveśe 
kṛṣṇasukhālokānande, rahe dhanī parānande, 
sakhīgaṇa saha kṛṣṇāveśe 

gocāraṇa hoite kānta, āsibena haye śrānta, 
sei śrānti karibāre dūra 
nānāvidha bhakṣyapeya, prastuta karena teṁha , 
upahāra dibena pracura 

śrī-rādhā-ramaṇa hari, sakhāgaṇa saṅge kari’, 
dhenuvṛnda loiyā takhana 
śrī-rādhā-darśana-sukha, labhi’ vraja-abhimukha, 
calilena śrī-vaṁśīvadana 

pitāmātā ādi sabe, āgubāḍi āsi’ tabe, 
ānande dekhaye kṛṣṇamukha 
śrī-gātra-mārjana kari’, jaśomati laye hari, 
ādara kariyā pāya sukha
IDX.en_translation:
Having sported with Her Beloved and then returned to Her own home, Rādhā bathes and dresses in beautiful attire. In the joy of seeing Lord Kṛṣṇa’s happiness, She remains in supreme bliss with Her gopī friends, completely absorbed in thoughts of Him. 

Her Beloved will soon return tired from herding the cows, and to remove that tiredness, She prepares various kinds of food and drink and offers many gifts. 

Lord Hari, the Beloved of Rādhā, taking His cowherd friends and the cows, then returns toward Vraja after having attained the happiness of seeing Śrīmati Rādhikā. 

All His family members, including His father and mother, come forward to meet Him and happily gaze upon the Lord’s face. After Mother Yaśodā wipes His beautiful body, she shows Him great affection and finds great happiness.

IDX.first_line: karaṅga kaupīna lañā chēḍā kānthā gāye diyā
IDX.search: karanga kaupina lana cheda kantha gaye diya teyagiba sakala visaya krsne anuraga habe vrajera nikunje kabe jaiya kariba nijalaya hari hari kabe mora hoibe sudina phalamula vrndavane khana diba avasane bhramiba hoiya udasina
IDX.author: narottama-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: karaṅga kaupīna lañā, chēḍā kānthā gāye diyā, teyāgiba sakala viṣaya kṛṣṇe anurāga ha’be, vrajera nikuñje kabe, jāiyā kariba nijālaya hari hari! kabe mora hoibe sudina phalamūla vṛndāvane, khāñā dibā avasāne, bhramiba hoiyā udāsīna śītala yamunā-jale, snāna kari’ kutūhale, premāveśe ānandita hañā bāhura upara bāhu tuli’, vṛndāvane kuli-kuli, kṛṣṇa bali’ beḍāba kāndiyā dekhiba saṅketa-sthāna, juḍābe tāpita prāṇa, premāveśe gaḍāgaḍi diba kaṅhā rādhā prāṇeśvari, kaṅhā girivaradhāri, kaṅhā nātha baliyā ḍākiba mādhavī-kuñjera’pari, sukhe vasi’ śuka-śārī, gāibeka rādhā-kṛṣṇa-rasa tarumūle vasi’ tāhā, śuni’ juḍāiba hiyā, kabe sukhe goṅāba divasa śrī-govinda-gopīnātha, śrīmatī-rādhikā-sātha, dekhiba ratana-siṁhāsane dīna narottama-dāsa, karaye durlabha āśa, ei mati haibe kata-dine
IDX.en_translation:
Taking a water pot and a loincloth and wearing a torn quilted cloth, I will give up all worldly attachments. When will my devotion to Kṛṣṇa arise, and when will I make my home in the groves of Vraja? 

O Lord Hari! When will that auspicious day be mine? Eating fruits and roots in Vṛndāvana, I will wander with detachment at the end of the day. 

Joyfully bathing in the cool waters of the Yamunā, absorbed in ecstatic love, I will become joyful. Raising my arms and calling out "Kṛṣṇa!" along the banks of Vṛndāvana, I will wander while weeping. 

I will see the secret meeting places, and my distressed heart will be soothed; absorbed in ecstatic love, I will roll on the ground. "Where is Rādhā, my life's queen? Where is the lifter of Govardhana Hill? Where is my Lord?" I will call out. 

In the bower of mādhavī flowers, parrots and mynah birds will sit happily and sing of the sweet mellows of the divine love of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. Sitting at the foot of a tree and hearing that, my heart will be soothed. When will I pass my days in such happiness? 

I will behold Śrī Govinda and Gopīnātha, along with Śrīmatī Rādhikā, on a jeweled throne. Humble Narottama dāsa cherishes this rare hope: when will such a state of mind come to pass?

IDX.search: karpanya panjika va vijnapti nivedana ami ati dinamati vrajakunje nivasati radha krsna yugala carane kandiya kandiya aja chadi saba lokalaja nivediba jata ache mane tumi krsna nilamani nava meghaprabha jini vrajananda kara vitarana tumi radhe nava gauri gorocana garva hari vraje hara krsna candra mana
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses: kārpaṇya pañjikā vā vijñapti-nivedana āmi ati dīnamati, vrajakuñje nivasati, rādhā-kṛṣṇa-yugala caraṇe kāṅdiyā kāṅdiyā āja, chāḍi’ saba lokalāja, nivediba jata āche mane tumi kṛṣṇa nīlamaṇi, nava-meghaprabhā jini’, vrajānanda kara vitaraṇa tumi rādhe nava gaurī, gorocanā-garva hari’, vraje hara kṛṣṇa-candra-mana tumi kṛṣṇa pītāmbare, parājīyā kārtasvare, vrajavane nitya-kelirata tumi rādhe nīlāmbarī, palāśera garva hari’, kṛṣṇakeli-sahāya satata tumi kṛṣṇa harinmaṇi, juvāvṛnda-śiromaṇi, rādhikā tomāra prāṇeśvarī vrajāṅganā-śiraḥśobhā, dharmilla-mallikā-prabhā, tumi rādhe kṛṣṇapriyaṅkarī ramāpati-śobhā jini’, kṛṣṇa tava rūpakhāni, jagat mātāya vrajavane ramā-jini, vrajāṅganā-, gaṇamadhye suśobhanā, tumi rādhe kṛṣṇacittāṅgane tavāṅga-saurabhakaṇa, vaṁśīgīta anukṣaṇa, ohe kṛṣṇa! rādhā-mana hare rādhe! aṅgagandha tava, tomāra suvīṇārava, kṛṣṇacitta unmādita kare tomāra capalekṣaṇa, hare rādhā-dhairyadhana, tumi kṛṣṇa caura-śiromaṇi bāṅkā dṛṣṭi bhaṅgī tava, śrī-kṛṣṇa-hṛdayāsaba, tumi rādhe kalāvatī dhanī parihāse rādhikāra, kathā nāhi sare jāra, tumi kṛṣṇa naṭakulaguru kṛṣṇa-narma ukti śuni’, romāñcita tanukhāni, tava rādhe rasakalpataru aprākṛta-guṇamaṇi, vinirmita-giriśreṇī, tumi kṛṣṇa sarva guṇamaya umādi ramaṇījana-, vāñchanīya guṇagaṇa, rādhe! tava svābhāvika haya āmi ati mandamati, kari he kākuti nati, niṣkapaṭe e prārthanā kari vṛndāvana-adhīśvara, tumi kṛṣṇa prāṇeśvara, tumi rādhe! vrajavaneśvarī tomādera kṛpā pāi, erūpa jogyatā nāi, jadio āmāra vrajavane dūhe mahākṛpāmaya, jāni’ kainu padāśraya, kṛpā kara e adhama jane kevala ayogya nahi, aparādhī āmi hoi, tathāpi karaha kṛpā dāna loke kṛpāviṣṭa jana, kṣame aparādhagaṇa, tumi dūhe mahā-kṛpāvān kṛpāhetu bhaktisāra, leśābhāsa nāhi tā’ra, kṛpā-adhikārī nahi āmi dūhe mahālīleśvara, hañā sei līlāpara, kṛpā kara vraja-jana-svāmi suduṣṭa abhakta jane, śivādi devatāgaṇe, prasanna hoila kṛpā kari’ mahālīla sarveśvara, dūhu mama prāṇeśvara, dayā kara doṣa parihari’ adhame uttama māni, muḍha-vijña, abhimānī, duṣṭa hañā śiṣṭa-abhimāna ei doṣe doṣī hañā, gela ciradina vañā, nā karinu bhajana-vidhāna tathāpi e dīna-jane, jadi nāma-uccāraṇe, nāmābhāsa karila jīvane sarvadoṣa-nivāraṇa, dūhu-nāma-saṁjalpana- prasāde prasīda dui jana bhakti-lavamātre kṣaya, sarva aparādha haya, kṣamāśīla dūhera kṛpāya e āśā mane dhari’, caraṇe prārthanā kari, śodha doṣa kṣamiyā āmāya sādhana-sampattihīna, ohe ei jīva dīna, atikaṣṭe dhṛṣṭatāra chāra dūhupāda-nipatita, prārthanā karaye hita, prasannatā houka dohāra dante tṛṇa dhari’ hāya, kāṅditeche ubharāya, e pāpīra kampita śarīra ‘hā nātha! hā nātha’! bali’, ha’ye āji kṛtāñjali, prasāda arpiyā kara sthira e durbhāgā hā hā svare, prasāda prārthanā kare anutāpe gaḍāgaḍi jāya he rādhe! he kṛṣṇa-candra! śuna mama kākuvāda, tūhu kṛpā vinā prāṇa jāya phutkāra kariyā kāṅde, āhā āhā kākunāde, bale hoo prasanna āmāya ei ta’ ayogya jane, kṛpā kara nijaguṇe, karuṇāsāgara rākha pāya mukhete aṅguṣṭha diyā, uccaiḥsvare ārta hañā, kāṅdite kīdite bale, nātha! karuṇā-kaṇikādāne, rakṣā kara mora prāṇe, kara ei dīne ātmasātha ei tava mūḍha jana, dīnavākye satrundana, prārthanā karaye dṛḍhamane he karuṇā-sunidhāna! anugati kara dāna, karuṇormicchaṭā vrajavane bhāva cittasukhakara, jata āche sumadhura, prakaṭāprakaṭa līlāsthale rādhā-kṛṣṇa-premasāra, sakalera sārātsāra, sei bhāva jeṁi kṛpābale jadi e dāsīra prati, prasanna karuṇāmati, dūhu-padasevā kara dāna āra kichu nāhi cāi, yugala caraṇa pāi, śītala houka mora prāṇa anātha-vatsala tumi, adhama anātha āmi, tvadīya sākṣāt-dāsya māgi e prasāda kara dāna, rākha anāthera prāṇa, chāḍi’ saba tava dāsya māgi śirete añjali dhari’, opade vijñapti kari, āmāra abhīṣṭa nivedana ekabāra dāsya diyā, śītala kara he hiyā, tabe māni sārthaka jīvana kabe dūhe ei vane, vilokiba sammilane, amūlyāṅga parimala-ghrāṇa āmāra nāsikā-dvāre, praveśiyā cittapure, acaitanya karibe vidhāna dūhāra nūpura-dhvani, haṁsa-kaṇṭhasvara jini’, madhura madhura mama kāṇe praveśiyā kona kṣaṇe, mama cita surañjane, mātāibe sevārasa-pāne cakrādi saubhāgyāmpada, vilakṣita dūhupada, cihna ei vṛndāvana-vane dekhiyā e dāsī kabe, bhāsibe ānandotsave, dūhu-kṛpā peye saṁgopane sakala-saundaryāspada, nīrājita dūhupada, he rādhe! he nandera nandana! mamākṣi-gocare kabe, sarvādbhūta mahotsave, karibe ānanda vitaraṇa prācīnāśā, phalapūrti, tūhu padāmbuja-sphurti, sei dūhujana-daraśana janme ki ha’be mama, e utkaṇṭhā suviṣama, vicalita kare mama mana kabe āmi vṛndāvana-, kuñjāntare daraśana, kariba sundara dūhu jane surata-līlāya rata, āmā hoite adūrata, preme magna ha’ba daraśane ghaṭanāvaśataḥ kabe, dūhuyoga asambhave, paraspara sandeśa āniyā bāḍāiba dūhu sukha, jābe tabe manoduḥkha, beḍāiba ānande mātiyā kabe ei vṛndāvane, dūhu dūhā adarśane, phire jāba dūhe anveṣiyā sammilana karāiba, hāra-padakādi pāba, parituṣṭa dūhāre kariyā dūhe hāra dhari’ paṇe, dyūtakrīḍā-samāpane, ‘āmi jayī’, ‘āmi jayī’ bali’ karibe kalaha tabe, hāra-saṁgrahete kabe, āmi tāhā dekhiba sakali āhā! kabe dui jane, kuñjamājhe suśayane, kusuma-śayyāya virāmibe se samaye dūhupada-, samvāhana susampada, e dāsīra saubhāgya milibe kandarpa-kalahodgāre, chīṅḍibe kaṇṭhera hāre, latāgṛhe paḍibe khasiyā se hāra gāṅthibe kabe, e dāsī niyukta ha’be dūhukṛpā-ājñā śire pāñā kelikallolera jabe, dūhu-keśa srasta habe, dujanāra iṅgita pāiyā śikhipiñcha kare dhari’, kuntala-maṇḍita kari’, āmi raba ānande ḍubiyā kandarpa-krīḍāya jabe, dūhu-srak srasta ha’be, tabe āmi dūhu-ājñā pāñā ubhaya-lalāṭamājhe, kariba tilaka-sāje, matta ha’ba se śobhā dekhiyā kṛṣṇa! tava vakṣe āmi, vanamālā diyā svāmi! rādhe! tava nayane kajjala kuñjamājhe kona dina, pā’ba sukha samīcīna, preme citta ha’be ṭalamala kabe jāmbunada-varṇa, loiyā tāmbūlīparṇa, śīrāśūnya karpūrādi juta vīṭikā nirmāṇa kari’, dūhu mukhe diba dhari’, preme citta ha’be paripluta kothā e durāśā mora, kothā e duṣkarma ghora, e prārthanā, jadi bala kena he rādhe! he ghanaśyāma! dūhujana-guṇagrāma-, mādhurī balāya more hena dūhāra je kṛpāguṇe, pāinu dhāma-vṛndāvane, se kṛpā abhīṣṭa pūraṇa karuna āmāya nātha! pāñā tūhu-sakhī sātha, kuñjasevā pāi anukṣaṇa ohe rādhe! ohe kṛṣṇa! sei vrajarasatṛṣṇa, kārpaṇya-pañjikā-kathā-chale jalpanā karaye sadā, tā’ra vāñchā-pūrti tadā, karuna dūhu kṛpā-bale śrī-rūpamañjarī-pada, śire dhari’ susampada, kamala-mañjarī kare āśā śrī-godruma-vrajavane, dūhu-līlā-sandarśane, pūrṇa hou rasera pipāsā iti kārpaṇya-pañjikā samāpta
IDX.en_translation:
Kārpaṇya-pañjikā Or A Humble Petition I, with a very humble mind, residing in a grove of Vraja, today offer whatever is in my heart at the lotus feet of the Divine Couple, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, while weeping and abandoning all social shame. 

You, Lord Kṛṣṇa, are a blue jewel, conquering the splendor of new clouds, and You bestow joy upon Vraja. You, Rādhā, are ever fair, stealing the pride of gorocana; in Vraja You captivate the mind of the moon-like Kṛṣṇa. 

You, Lord Kṛṣṇa, in yellow garments, conquering the luster of gold, are always engaged in eternal pastimes in the forest of Vraja. You, Rādhā, in blue garments, stealing the pride of the palāśa flower, are always assisting Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes. 

You, Lord Kṛṣṇa, are a jewel among men and the crest-jewel of all youth; Śrīmati Rādhikā is the Mistress of Your life. You, Rādhā, are the ornament on the heads of the gopīs, and with the splendor of jasmine in Your hair, You are Kṛṣṇa’s most beloved. 

Conquering the beauty of Lord Viṣṇu, Your beautiful form, Lord Kṛṣṇa, intoxicates the entire world in Vraja. Conquering the Goddess of Fortune, You, Rādhā, are the most beautiful among the gopīs and reside in the courtyard of Kṛṣṇa’s heart. 

The particles of fragrance from Your body, O Kṛṣṇa, and the song of Your flute always captivate Rādhā’s mind. O Rādhā! The fragrance of Your body and the sweet sound of Your vīṇā enchant Kṛṣṇa’s heart. 

Your restless glances steal Rādhā’s treasure of patience; You, Lord Kṛṣṇa, are the crest-jewel of thieves. Your crooked glances and gestures are like wine for Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s heart; You, Rādhā, are the wealthy possessor of all arts. 

In jest, Rādhikā’s words sometimes fail Her; You, Lord Kṛṣṇa, are the Master of all dancers. Hearing Kṛṣṇa’s humorous words, Her body becomes thrilled; You, Rādhā, are the wish-fulfilling tree of divine mellows. 

A jewel of transcendental qualities, You, Lord Kṛṣṇa, are full of all good qualities. Those qualities desired even by the goddesses are natural for You, O Rādhā. 

I am very dull-minded, yet I make these humble entreaties and obeisances sincerely. O Master of Vṛndāvana! You, Lord Kṛṣṇa, are the Lord of my life. You, Rādhā, are the Empress of the forests of Vraja. 

I have no qualification to receive Your mercy, although I am in Vṛndāvana. You both are supremely merciful; knowing this, I have taken shelter of Your feet. Please bestow mercy upon this lowly person. 

Not only am I unqualified, I am also an offender; still, please grant me Your mercy. Merciful people in this world forgive offenses; You both are the most merciful. 

Of that devotion which is the cause of mercy, there is not even a trace in me; I am not worthy of Your mercy. You both are the great Lords of pastimes; being devoted to those pastimes, please show mercy, O Masters of the residents of Vraja! 

Even to very wicked and undevoted persons, and to Lord Śiva and the other demigods, You are pleased to show mercy. O great Masters of all pastimes! Both of You are the Lords of my life; please show kindness, overlooking my many faults. 

Considering a lowly person like me to be great, being ignorant but thinking myself wise and proud, and being wicked but appearing well-behaved—being guilty of all these faults, my whole life has passed in delusion. I did not perform the prescribed devotional service. 

Still, if this poor person has made even a faint appearance of the Holy Name in his life—that Name which removes all faults—then by the grace of Your Names, please be pleased with me. 

Even by a trace of devotion, all offenses are destroyed by the mercy of You both, who are so forgiving. Holding this hope in my heart, I pray at Your feet; please purify my faults by forgiving me. 

Devoid of the wealth of spiritual practice, this poor soul, fallen at Your feet, prays for his welfare. May Your kindness be upon me. 

Alas, holding a blade of grass in my teeth and weeping profusely, my body trembles. Crying “O Master! O Master!”, I offer my prostrated obeisances; please offer me Your mercy and stabilize my heart. 

This unfortunate soul prays for Your mercy and rolls on the ground in repentance. O Rādhā! O moon-like Kṛṣṇa! Please hear my humble entreaty; without Your mercy, my life will depart. 

Crying with piteous gasps, I beg You: “Please be pleased with me.” To this unqualified person, please show mercy out of Your own compassion; O ocean of mercy, please keep me at Your feet. 

Placing my thumb in my mouth in total submission and crying loudly in distress, I say: “O Master! By granting me a particle of mercy, please save my life. Take this poor person as Your own.” 

This foolish person of Yours, with humble words and weeping, prays with a firm mind. O treasure house of mercy! Please bestow upon me the privilege of following You. Let waves of mercy sprinkle upon the forest of Vraja. 

I pray for that sentiment which brings joy to the heart, which is the most sweet essence of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa’s love. May I attain that sentiment by Your mercy. 

If You are pleased with this maidservant, please grant the service of both Your feet. I desire nothing else; to attain the lotus feet of the Divine Couple, may my heart become cool. 

You are affectionate to the helpless, and I am a fallen and helpless person. I beg for Your direct service. Please bestow this mercy and save the life of this helpless one. Giving up everything else, I beg for Your service. 

Offering my obeisances, I make this humble request at Your feet. This is my cherished desire. By once granting me Your service, please cool my heart. Only then will I consider my life successful. 

When will I behold both of You in this forest in a meeting? The invaluable fragrance of Your bodies, entering the city of my heart through my nose, will render me unconscious in ecstasy. 

The sound of Your ankle bells, sweeter than the voice of swans, is sweet to my ears. When will it enter my heart and intoxicate me with the mellow of Your service? 

Auspicious signs like the disc are observed on both Your feet in the forest of Vṛndāvana. When will this maidservant, seeing them, float in a festival of joy, having secretly received the mercy of both of You? 

O Rādhā! O Son of Nanda! When will You bestow joy upon me by appearing within my sight in an all-surpassing great festival? 

Will the ancient hope of seeing Your lotus feet ever be fulfilled in my life? This intense anxiety disturbs my mind constantly. 

When will I see the beautiful Divine Couple in Vṛndāvana, within the groves, engaged in Their intimate pastimes? I will be immersed in love upon seeing Them. 

When, by chance, will I increase the happiness of both by bringing messages between You? Then all my mental distress will vanish, and I will wander about, intoxicated with joy. 

When, in this Vṛndāvana, will I search for You and bring You together when You are separated? I will arrange Your meeting and receive garlands and medallions after satisfying both of You. 

When You wager a garland at the conclusion of a game of dice, and both say, “I am victorious!”, then You will quarrel. When You collect the garland, I will witness it all. 

Alas! When will You both rest beautifully in the groves, lying on a bed of flowers? At that time, massaging Your feet will be my greatest fortune; when will this maidservant attain that luck? 

In the outburst of Cupid’s quarrel, the garlands around Your necks will break and fall off. When will this maidservant be engaged to re-string that garland, receiving Your merciful command? 

When, in the waves of pastimes, Your hair becomes disheveled, I will receive a hint from You and, holding a peacock feather, I will adorn Your locks while remaining immersed in joy. 

When in the sports of love Your garlands become disheveled, I will receive Your command and make tilaka decorations on both Your foreheads; I will become intoxicated seeing that beauty. 

O Kṛṣṇa! When will I put a forest garland on Your chest? O Rādhā! When will I apply eyeliner to Your eyes? When will I find such perfect happiness in the groves? My heart will overflow with divine love. 

When, taking a yellow betel leaf, free from veins, with camphor and other spices, will I prepare a betel quid and place it in Your mouths? My heart will be inundated with love. 

Where is this desperate hope of mine, and where are my grave misdeeds? If you ask why I make this prayer—O Rādhā! O dark Lord Kṛṣṇa! The beauty of Your qualities and glories compels me to speak this way. 

By Your mercy I have attained the abode of Vṛndāvana. May that mercy fulfill my desire, O Master! Attaining the companionship of Your sakhīs, may I constantly receive service in the groves. 

O Rādhā! O Kṛṣṇa! This soul, thirsty for the mellows of Vraja, always speaks through this humble appeal. May both of You fulfill his desire by the power of Your mercy. 

Holding the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī upon her head, Kamala Mañjarī hopes that by seeing Your pastimes in Vraja, her thirst for transcendental mellows may be fulfilled. 

Thus ends the Kārpaṇya-pañjikā.

IDX.first_line: kata paricaryā kari’ juvadvaye tuṣṭa kari’
IDX.search: kata paricarya kari juvadvaye tusta kari vrnda dohara sadhila milana sakhigana mili tabe sei prema mahotsave gana narma praheli natana sulapana rasalasya kari nanavidha dasya yugalavilasa dekhe kata prestha sabigana gheri badaya rati madhuri ujjvala sevaya thake rata gandhamalya sutambula vyajanadi himajala pada samvahana adi jata

IDX.verses:
kata paricaryā kari’, juvadvaye tuṣṭa kari’, 
vṛndā dohāra sādhila milana 
sakhīgaṇa mili tabe, sei prema-mahotsave, 
gāna narma prahelī naṭana 

sulapana rasalāsya, kari nānāvidha dāsya, 
yugalavilāsa dekhe kata 
preṣṭha sabīgaṇa gheri’, bāḍāya rati-mādhurī, 
ujjvala-sevāya thāke rata 
gandhamālya sutāmbūla, vyajanādi himajala, 
pāda-samvāhanā ādi jata 

jāra jei sevā kare, premānande ataḥpare, 
rādhā-kṛṣṇe deya nānā sukha 
viśrānti ālāpa-chale, nibhṛta nikuñjasthale, 
nidrā āsi’ hoila sevonmukha 

sukusuma-śayyopari, nidrā jāya rādhā-hari, 
cāridike supta sakhīgaṇa 
sukhanidrā-bhāva lakhi’, vaneśvarī vṛndāsakhī, 
nibhṛta karila vṛndāvana 

vṛndāra śāsana māni’, nistabdha sakala prāṇī, 
vanavāsī paśupakṣīgaṇa 
kuñje rādhā-dāmodara, sakhīsaṅge nidrāpara, 
vṛndā ekā praharī takhana
IDX.en_translation:
Vṛndā-devī performed many services to satisfy the Divine Couple and arranged Their meeting. Then the gopīs gathered in that great festival of divine love, singing, joking, and dancing. 

With graceful dancing and by performing various services, they watched many of the Divine Couple’s pastimes. The dearest gopīs surrounded Them, increasing the sweetness of Their love while remaining engaged in brilliant service with fragrant garlands, betel nuts, and cool water. 

Each gopī performed her specific service, and thus they all gave various kinds of happiness to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. Under the pretext of rest and conversation in the secluded grove, sleep came, ready to offer its service. 

Upon a bed of beautiful flowers, Lord Hari and Śrīmati Rādhā-rāṇī sleep, while all around Them the gopīs also sleep. Observing Their peaceful slumber, Vṛndā-devī made the forest of Vṛndāvana completely secluded and silent. 

Obeying Vṛndā’s command, all the forest creatures, animals, and birds became silent. In the grove, Lord Dāmodara and Rādhā were asleep with Their companions, and Vṛndā-devī alone remained as the guard.

IDX.search: ke go tumi kangala vese desa videse ghure bedao ati bada vyathara vyathi tai nayana jala vaksa bhasao adhama patita acandale snehera kole loo go tule divya premera ankhi khule bhava vanchita pada dekhaiya dao
IDX.verses:
ke go tumi kāṅgāla-veśe, deśa-videśe ghure beḍāo 
ati baḍa vyathāra vyathi, (tāi) nayana-jala vaksa bhāsāo 

adhama patita ācaṇḍāle, snehera kole loo go tule, 
divya-premera āṅkhi khule, bhava-vāñchita-pada dekhāiyā dāo 

emana dayāla ke go tumi, vilāle prema-cintāmaṇi, 
dhara loo ba’le premera khani, ācaṇḍāle bilāiyā dāo 

ācaṇḍāle prema vilāle, tri-tāpa-jvālā juḍāile, 
(māyā- ) mugdha-jīvera bhava-kṣudhā, ciratare miṭāiyā dāo 

yamunāra kūle kadambera mūle, bājāte bāṅśī rādhā ba’le 
sei nā tumi gaura haye, nade ese jīva tarāo
IDX.en_translation:
Who are You in the dress of a beggar, wandering in countries and foreign lands? You feel great pain for the suffering (so) You float Your chest in the water of Your eyes. 

You take the lowly, fallen, down to the Caṇḍāla, into the lap of affection. Opening the eyes of divine love, You show the feet desired by the world. 

Who are You, such a merciful person? You distributed the touchstone of love. Saying “Take, take,” You distributed the mine of love down to the Caṇḍāla. 

You distributed love down to the Caṇḍāla, You cooled the burning of the three-fold miseries. You satisfied the material hunger of the (māyā-)bewildered living beings forever. 

On the bank of the Yamunā, at the root of the Kadamba, You used to play the flute calling “Rādhā”. Are You not He, becoming Gaura, coming to Nadīyā to deliver the living beings?

IDX.search: ke jabi ke jabi bhai bhavasindhu para dhanya kali yugera caitanya avatara amara gaurangera ghate adana kheya vaya jada andha atura avadhi para haya

IDX.verses: ke jābi ke jābi bhāi bhavasindhu-pāra dhanya kali-yugera caitanya-avatāra āmāra gaurāṅgera ghāṭe adāna-kheyā vaya jaḍa, andha, ātura avadhi pāra haya harināmera naukākhāni śrī-guru-kāṇḍārī saṅkīrtana-keroyāla du’bāhu pasāri saba jīva haila pāra premera vātāse paḍiyā rahila locana āpanāra doṣe
IDX.en_translation:
Who will go, O brother, who will go across the ocean of material existence? Glorious is the incarnation of Caitanya in this age of Kali! 

At the bank of my Gaurāṅga’s river, a free ferry operates. Even the inert, the blind, and the distressed cross over. 

The boat of the Holy Name has the spiritual master as its helmsman, with congregational chanting as its oar, spreading His two arms wide. 

All souls have crossed over by the breeze of divine love; only Locana remains behind, due to his own fault.

IDX.first_line: kena āra kara dveṣa videśi jana bhajane
IDX.search: kena ara kara dvesa videsi jana bhajane bhajanera linga nana nana dese nana jane keha mukta kacche bhaje keha hatu gadi puje keha va nayana mudi thake brahma aradhane

IDX.verses:
kena āra kara dveṣa, videśi-jana-bhajane 
bhajanera liṅga nānā, nānā deśe nānā jane 

keha mukta-kacche bhaje, keha hāṭu gāḍi’ pūje 
keha vā nayana mudi’ thāke brahma-ārādhāne 

keha jogāsane pūje, keha saṅkīrtane maje 
sakalei bhajiche sei ekamātra kṛṣṇa-dhane 

atoeva bhrātṛbhāve, thāka sabe susadbhāve 
hari-bhakti sādha sadā, e jīvane vā maraṇe
IDX.en_translation:
Why do you still harbor hatred for the worship of foreign people? The forms of worship are varied, differing across lands and peoples. 

Some worship with loose garments, some worship kneeling down, and some remain with eyes closed in worship of the Absolute. 

Some worship in yogic postures, while some delight in congregational chanting. All of them are worshiping that one and only Kṛṣṇa, the sole treasure. 

Therefore, all of you, remain in a brotherly spirit with good will. Always practice devotion to God, whether in this life or in death.

IDX.en_translation:
Why don’t my mind and heart weep when chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa and saying Hari? O bird, I don’t know for what offense you do not chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa with your mouth. 

O forest bird, I caught you and kept you in the temple of my heart. O bird, if taught, you will learn this Hari, which is sweet as honey. 

O bird, you can say all names, why do you not chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa? Why don’t my mind and heart weep when chanting the Hare Kṛṣṇa and saying Hari? 

Come, O bird, let’s go to the land of true beauty, where worldly-minded people cannot come and go. 

O bird, at the time of your death, you will be placed on a bamboo stretcher. O, four people will carry you on their shoulders to the cremation ground. 

O, when they place fire in your mouth and raise your tongue, what will you do then? Tell me.

IDX.en_translation:
O friend! What can I say of today’s endless joy? My Lord Mādhava is in the temple forever. 

As much happiness as the moonlight gave, that much more happiness arose by seeing my Beloved’s face. 

If I were to receive a great treasure, I would never send my Beloved to a distant land. 

My Beloved is like a shawl in winter, shade in summer, an umbrella in the rainy season, and a boat upon the ocean. 

Vidyāpati says: “Listen, beautiful woman—for good people, sorrow lasts only for a few days.”

IDX.en_translation:
How shall I, a wicked soul, obtain service? My affection has not developed for my spiritual master and the devotees. 

My mind became engrossed in endless illusion. Not even a trace of affection for the devotees was born. 

Forgetting myself in material enjoyments, I became blind day and night. Illusion, like a witch, roams about to put a noose around my neck. 

Once caught, there is no escape. Without the mercy of saintly persons, there is no other way. 

O Lord, who overlooks the faults of others, please deliver the fallen! This time, please grant liberation to Narottama.

IDX.en_translation:
Where are You, O Rādhā, the embodiment of love? All glories to You! 

By appearing before me, please save my life. Your destitute servant calls You. 

Rādhā, who enjoys pastimes in Vṛndāvana! Rādhā, who enchants Kṛṣṇa’s mind! 

Rādhā, the crest-jewel of the eight principal companions! Rādhā, the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu! 

A great soul regularly and always calls out: “Rādhe! Rādhe!” 

Sometimes he calls at Keśī-ghāṭa, and again he calls at Vaṁśīvaṭa. 

Sometimes he calls in Nidhuvana, and again he calls in the forest groves. 

Sometimes he calls at Rādhā-kuṇḍa, and again he calls at Śyāma-kuṇḍa. 

Sometimes he calls in Kusumavana, and again he calls at Govardhana. 

Sometimes he calls in Tālavana, and again he calls in Tamālavana. 

With dirty clothes on his body, he rolls in the dust of Vraja. 

With “Rādhā! Rādhā!” on his lips, he floats in the tears from his eyes. 

From lane to lane in Vṛndāvana, he cries and wanders, calling Your name. 

For fifty-six units of time, day and night, he knows nothing except Rādhā and Govinda. 

After that, he sleeps for four units of time, and in his dreams he sees Rādhā and Govinda.

kṛpā kara vaiṣṇava ṭhākura! 
sambandha jāniyā, bhajite bhajite, 
abhimāna hou dūra 

‘āmi ta’ vaiṣṇava’, e buddhi hoile, 
amānī nā ha’ba āmipratiṣṭhāśā āsi’, hṛdaya dūṣibe, 
hoiba niraya-gāmī 

tomāra kiṅkara, āpane jāniba,‘guru’-abhimāna tyaji’tomāra ucchiṣṭa, pada-jala-reṇu, 
sadā niṣkapaṭe bhaji 

‘nije śreṣṭha’ jāni, ucchiṣṭādi-dāne, 
ha’be abhimāna-bhāratāi śiṣya tava, thākiyā sarvadā, 
nā loiba pūjā kāra 

amānī mānada, hoile kīrtane, 
adhikāra dibe tumitomāra caraṇe, niṣkapaṭe āmi, 
kaṅdiyā luṭiba bhūmi
IDX.en_translation:
Please bestow your mercy, O revered devotee! Knowing my relationship with the Lord, as I continuously worship, may all pride be cast far away. 

If the thought “I am a devotee” arises, I will not be humble. The desire for prestige will come and pollute my heart, and I will be destined for hell. 

I will consider myself your servant, giving up the pride of being a master. I will always sincerely worship your remnants and the dust from your feet. 

Knowing myself to be superior while giving remnants to others, the burden of pride would increase. Therefore, remaining always as your disciple, I will not accept anyone's worship. 

If I am humble and offer respect to others during the chanting of the Holy Name, you will grant me the qualification. At your feet, I will sincerely cry and roll on the ground.

IDX.verses: kṛṣṇa-bhakti vinā kabhu nāhi phalodaya miche saba dharmādharma jīvera upādhimaya joga-yāga-tapodhyāna, sannyāsādi brahmajñāna nānā kāṇḍa-rūpe jīvera bandhana-kāraṇa haya vinodera vākya dhara, nānā kāṇḍa tyāga kara nirupādhi kṛṣṇa-prema hṛdaye deha āśraya
IDX.en_translation:
Without devotion to Kṛṣṇa, there is never a favorable outcome. All religious and irreligious acts are useless when full of the material designations of the living entity. 

Yoga, sacrifice, austerities, meditation, renunciation, and knowledge of the Absolute in the form of various activities only become the cause of the soul’s bondage. 

Accept the words of Bhaktivinoda and give up these various activities. Give shelter to pure love for Kṛṣṇa in your heart.

IDX.en_translation:
From Kṛṣṇa came the four-faced Brahmā, who is inclined to the service of Kṛṣṇa. From Brahmā came the intelligence of Nārada. From Nārada came Vyāsa; Madhva calls himself the servant of Vyāsa. Pūrṇaprajña (Madhva) is the destination of Padmanābha. 

In the lineage of Nṛhari and Mādhava, Akṣobhya accepted Paramahaṁsa as his disciple. Akṣobhya’s disciple is known by the name “Jaya Tīrtha”. His servant was Jñānasindhu. 

From him came Dayānidhi, and his servant is Vidyānidhi. Rājendra came from him. His servant is known by the name “Jaya Dharma”. Know this disciplic succession well. 

Renowned in the service of Jayadharma was Śrī Puruṣottama Yati. From him came the learned Brahmaṇya Tīrtha. Vyāsa Tīrtha was his servant. Lakṣmīpati was the servant of Vyāsa. From him came Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī. 

The best disciple of Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī was Śrī Īśvara Purī, and also Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu and the powerful Śrī Advaita Ācārya. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the spiritual master of the universe, the great Golden Lord, made Śrī Īśvara Purī glorious. 

Mahāprabhu Śrī Caitanya is none other than Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, the life of the followers of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. The dearmost of Viśvambhara was Śrīla Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, and the Gosvāmīs Śrīla Rūpa and Śrīla Sanātana. 

Dear to Rūpa were the great souls Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī and Śrīla Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī. Their dear poet was Śrīla Kṛṣṇa-dāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī. Kṛṣṇa-dāsa’s dearmost was Śrīla Narottama Dāsa Ṭhākura, dedicated to service, whose feet were the hope of Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura. 

Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura, along with the devotees Śrīla Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa and Śrīla Jagannātha Dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja; their dear Śrīla Saccidānanda Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura. The great mahā-bhāgavata, the excellent Śrīla Gaura-kiśora Dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja, whose delight was in the worship of Hari. 

[Composed by his disciples] The excellent “Śrī Vārṣabhānavī”, always intent on the service of the Object of service—his name is “Dayita-dāsa” (Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura Prabhupāda). 

The intimate associate of Prabhupāda, the follower of Svarūpa and Rūpa, is Śrīla Bhaktiprajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja. 

Knower of Gauḍīya Vedānta, destroyer of the darkness of Māyāvāda, the abode of the practice and preaching of Gaura’s message. 

Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Svāmī Prabhupāda preached the message of Gaura, fulfilling the desire of Prabhupāda. 

The great souls dear to Keśava are Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Vāmana Gosvāmī Mahārāja and Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja. 

The message of Gaura is the treasure of their lives. All these devotees of Hari are Gaurāṅga’s own; my desire is for their remnants.

The qualities, names, and pastimes associated with Kṛṣṇa and His devotees; all the innumerable emotions like adornments, relationships, and neutral factors—these are what the experts call the stimulants that awaken the divine mellows. 

The three qualities are mental, verbal, and bodily. The names include Kṛṣṇa and Śrī Rādhā-Mādhava. His dancing, flute playing, and movements; His milking of cows, cow worship, and His vigorous dance in the cowherd village for cow protection. 

Garlands, anointments, garments, and ornaments—these four types are the adornments that enhance beauty. The sounds of the flute, horn, and vīṇā, sweet songs, art, and pleasant fragrances, His footprints, ornaments, and musical sounds. 

The peacock feather, cows, shepherd’s staff, flute, horn, and loving glances; minerals from the mountains, remnants, and cow-dust at twilight. Vṛndāvana and all its dependent places, Govardhana, the Yamunā River, and all the places of divine pastimes such as the Rāsa dance. 

Birds, bees, deer, groves, Tulasi plants, clusters of creepers, Karnikara and Kadamba trees, and other trees. All these are related to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the great opulence of the forest of Vṛndāvana, and they stimulate the charming mellow. 

Moonlight, dense clouds, lightning, the autumn season, the full moon, the fragrant breeze, and flocks of birds. These are called neutral stimulants, all mercifully creating the experience of the divine mellow.

By Lord Kṛṣṇa’s mercy, Govardhana Hill attained sovereignty over all mountains and received tribute even from His enemy Indra. May He grant the desire of my heart. 

Govardhana Hill, who, due to the abundant joy experienced from the exquisite touch of Lord Kṛṣṇa’s lotus-like hands, did not even feel the strike of Indra’s thunderbolt—may He grant the desire of my heart. 

May Śrī Govardhana, where Lord Kṛṣṇa engaged in a playful dispute with the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu to collect a toll, and where the desire to hear of these pastimes is great—may He grant the desire of my heart. 

May that Śrī Govardhana, where the elephant-like wind, having bathed in the nearby lakes, beautifully plays by stirring the pollen of the Kadamba and other trees—may He grant the desire of my heart. 

Govardhana Hill, which, by the natural fragrance of its own stones, repeatedly causes one to wonder: “Did my Lord sleep here with musk?”—may He grant the desire of my heart. 

May that Govardhana Hill, where the deer, desiring to see Lord Hari, follow the path guided by the echo of His flute, grant the desire of my heart. 

May that Govardhana Hill, where Lord Kṛṣṇa, having seated Rādhā in a boat along the Mānasa-gaṅgā, and the boat having playfully submerged in the middle, shone beautifully as He embraced Her—may He grant the desire of my heart. 

Without the shelter of the feet of the best of Kṛṣṇa’s servants, Govardhana Hill, what would devotion be? Therefore, I take shelter of Śrī Govardhana, who lovingly serves His own Lords, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. May He grant the desire of my heart. 

Whoever reads these eight verses describing the great glories of the best of Kṛṣṇa’s servants with a softened heart, he directly attains, without delay, servitude at the lotus feet of Śrīmati Rādhikā and Lord Mādhava.

Kṛṣṇa! You will accrue merit, brother! When you perform this pious act, Rādhā-rāṇī will be pleased; I tell you this as a certainty. 

Śrī Siddhānta Sarasvatī is very dear to the Son of Śacī; there is no one equal to him in the service of Kṛṣṇa. That great Guru, the best in the world, distributes Kṛṣṇa-bhakti in place after place. 

His desire is powerful—that the name of Gaurāṅga should spread in the West. In all the cities of the earth, from the ocean to the rivers, may everyone take the name of Kṛṣṇa. 

Then there will be joy, then there will be victory in all directions, by the great mercy of Caitanya. All the miserable people polluted by Māyā in the world will be happy, and the desire of the Vaiṣṇava will be fulfilled. 

To perform that task, if you give me the order—although I am unworthy, very low and fallen—I beg for your suitable mercy; today you are the authority for everyone. 

If I get your strength, the object of Guru-sevā is obtained, and my life becomes successful. If I get that service, then I will be happy; by good fortune, your association is obtained. 

“O Lord, I am a person fallen into the blind well of material existence, constantly engaged in lust. I was accepted by the celestial sage (Nārada) and made his own. How can I give up the service of Your servant?” 

You are my eternal companion; forgetting You, I have suffered the kicks of Māyā birth after birth. Today, again, if this opportunity arises—if there is a connection—then I can meet You. 

In meeting You, brother, I again find that happiness, wandering all day grazing the cows. Running in so many forests, rolling on the ground in the forest—when will that day be mine? 

(Today, in that opportunity, I remembered You. With great hope, I called out. I am Your eternal servant, so I have so much hope. Without You, I have no other shelter.)

IDX.en_translation:
Kṛṣṇa! You will accrue merit, brother! When you perform this pious act, Rādhā-rāṇī will be pleased; I tell you this as a certainty. 

Śrī Siddhānta Sarasvatī is very dear to the Son of Śacī; there is no one equal to him in the service of Kṛṣṇa. That great Guru, the best in the world, distributes Kṛṣṇa-bhakti in place after place. 

His desire is powerful—that the name of Gaurāṅga should spread in the West. In all the cities of the earth, from the ocean to the rivers, may everyone take the name of Kṛṣṇa. 

Then there will be joy, then there will be victory in all directions, by the great mercy of Caitanya. All the miserable people polluted by Māyā in the world will be happy, and the desire of the Vaiṣṇava will be fulfilled. 

To perform that task, if you give me the order—although I am unworthy, very low and fallen—I beg for your suitable mercy; today you are the authority for everyone. 

If I get your strength, the object of Guru-sevā is obtained, and my life becomes successful. If I get that service, then I will be happy; by good fortune, your association is obtained. 

“O Lord, I am a person fallen into the blind well of material existence, constantly engaged in lust. I was accepted by the celestial sage (Nārada) and made his own. How can I give up the service of Your servant?” 

You are my eternal companion; forgetting You, I have suffered the kicks of Māyā birth after birth. Today, again, if this opportunity arises—if there is a connection—then I can meet You. 

In meeting You, brother, I again find that happiness, wandering all day grazing the cows. Running in so many forests, rolling on the ground in the forest—when will that day be mine? 

(Today, in that opportunity, I remembered You. With great hope, I called out. I am Your eternal servant, so I have so much hope. Without You, I have no other shelter.)

lokamukhe guṇa śravaṇiyā

sakhīsaṅge calilā dhāiyā 

nikuñjakānane karila abhisāra 
nā mānila nivāraṇa, gṛhakārya agaṇana, 
dharmādharma nā karila vicāra 

yamunāpuline giyā, sakhīgaṇe sambodhiyā, 
jijñāsila priyera uddeśa 
chāḍila prāṇera bhaya, vanete praveśa haya, 
vaṁśīdhvani kariyā nirdeśa 

nadī jathā sindhu-prati, dhāya ati vegavatī, 
seirūpa rasavatī satī 
ati vege kuñjavane, giyā kṛṣṇa-sannidhāne, 
ātmanivedane kaila mati 

kena mora durbalā lekhanī nāhi sare 
abhisāra āramtiyā sakampa antare 

milana, sambhoga, vipralambhādi-varṇana 
prakāśa karite nāhi sare mama mana 

durbhāgā nā bujhe rāsalīlā-tattvasāra 
śūkara jemana nāhi cine muktāhāra 

adhikārahīna-jana-maṅgala cintiyā 
kīrtana karinu śeṣa, kāla vicāriyā
IDX.en_translation:
Hearing Kṛṣṇa’s flute song, seeing His beautiful form in a painting, and hearing of His qualities, her heart was afflicted by initial attraction; showing symptoms of madness, she ran swiftly with her companions. 

She made her tryst toward the forest bower. She heeded no prevention, nor her countless household duties, nor did she consider right or wrong. 

Going to the bank of the Yamunā and addressing her companions, she inquired about the whereabouts of her beloved. Abandoning all fear for her life, she entered the forest, guided by the sound of the flute. 

Just as a river swiftly rushes toward the ocean, that chaste woman, full of mellows, went with great speed to the forest grove near Kṛṣṇa; with a mood of self-surrender, she gave herself to Him. 

Why does my feeble pen not move, as I begin to describe the tryst with a trembling heart? 

My mind does not move to reveal the meeting, the enjoyment, the separation, and other such topics. 

An unfortunate person cannot understand the essence of the divine rāsa dance, just as a hog cannot recognize a pearl necklace. 

Thinking of the welfare of those who are not yet qualified, I conclude this narration here, considering the time.

IDX.verses: kṛṣṇavārtā vinā āna, ‘asadvārtā’ bali’ jāna, sei veśyā ati bhayaṅkarī śrī-kṛṣṇaviṣayā mati, jīvera durlabha ati, sei veśyā mati laya hari’ śuna, mana, bali he tomāya ‘mukti’-nāme śārdūlinī, tā’ra kathā jadi śuni, sarvātmasampatti gili’ khāya tadubhaya tyāga kara, muktikathā parihara, lakṣmīpati-rati rākha dūre se-rati prabala ha’le, paravyome deya phele, nāhi deya vāsa vrajapure vraje rādhā-kṛṣṇa-rati, amūlya-dhanada ati, tā’i tumi bhaja ciradina rūpa-raghunātha-pāya, sei rati prārthanāya, e bhaktivinoda dīna hīna
IDX.en_translation:
Without topics concerning Lord Kṛṣṇa, know all other talk to be “unreal talk.” Such talk is like a very dreadful prostitute. Devotion concerning Lord Kṛṣṇa is extremely rare for the soul, and that prostitute steals away that devotion. 

Listen, O my mind, I tell you: if one listens to the tigress named “liberation,” she swallows all his spiritual wealth. 

Abandon both sense gratification and liberation, and give up talk of impersonal liberation. Keep devotion for Lord Nārāyaṇa far away. If that devotion becomes strong, it throws one into the spiritual sky of Vaikuṇṭha, but does not grant residence in Vraja. 

Devotion for Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in Vraja is an extremely priceless bestower of wealth. Therefore, you should always worship that. At the feet of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī and Śrīla Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī, praying for that devotion, this Bhaktivinoda is poor and humble.
