Engaged in the congregational chanting of Kṛṣṇa’s names, singing and dancing—they are oceans of the nectar of divine love. Dear to both the sober and the restless, they are doers of good, free from envy, and revered. Full of the mercy of Lord Caitanya and relieving the earth of its burden—I offer my obeisances to Rūpa, Sanātana, Raghunātha dāsa, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa, Jīva, and Gopāla Bhaṭṭa. 

Expert in deliberating on various scriptures and establishers of true religious principles, they are benefactors of humanity, respected in the three worlds, and abodes of refuge. Like intoxicated bees relishing the bliss of worshiping the lotus feet of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa—I offer my obeisances to Rūpa, Sanātana, Raghunātha dāsa, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa, Jīva, and Gopāla Bhaṭṭa. 

Endowed with abundant faith in the process of describing Lord Caitanya’s qualities, they are the cutters of the miseries and sins of embodied beings through the nectar of the Lord’s glories. Expert in increasing the ocean of bliss and delivering others from impersonal liberation—I offer my obeisances to Rūpa, Sanātana, Raghunātha dāsa, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa, Jīva, and Gopāla Bhaṭṭa. 

Having quickly given up all ranks of powerful leaders and always considering them insignificant, out of compassion they became the masters of the humble and poor. Taking shelter of simple loincloths and patched coverings, they are constantly immersed in the waves and surges of the nectar-ocean of the mood of the gopīs—I offer my obeisances to Rūpa, Sanātana, Raghunātha dāsa, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa, Jīva, and Gopāla Bhaṭṭa. 

In Vṛndāvana, which is filled with cooing cuckoos, swans, and cranes, crowded with peacocks, and adorned with trees whose roots are bound with jewels—they worship Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa day and night and joyfully bestow the ultimate benefit upon all souls. I offer my obeisances to Rūpa, Sanātana, Raghunātha dāsa, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa, Jīva, and Gopāla Bhaṭṭa. 

They utilized their time by chanting the Holy Names a fixed number of times and by offering obeisances. They conquered sleep, eating, and recreation, and were extremely humble. Enchanted by the sweet bliss of remembering the qualities of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa—I offer my obeisances to Rūpa, Sanātana, Raghunātha dāsa, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa, Jīva, and Gopāla Bhaṭṭa. 

On the bank of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, on the bank of the Yamunā, and at the Vaṁśīvaṭa tree, they were always overwhelmed by the madness of divine love, affected by various stages of ecstasy and always intoxicated. Sometimes they were joyfully overwhelmed by transcendental emotions while singing the excellent qualities of the Lord. I offer my obeisances to Rūpa, Sanātana, Raghunātha dāsa, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa, Jīva, and Gopāla Bhaṭṭa. 

“O Rādhā! O Goddess of Vraja! O Lalitā! O Son of Nanda! Where are You? Are You under the wish-fulfilling trees of Govardhana, or in the forest along the Yamunā?” Shouting in this way everywhere in Vraja and greatly agitated by the distress of separation—I offer my obeisances to Rūpa, Sanātana, Raghunātha dāsa, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa, Jīva, and Gopāla Bhaṭṭa.

premamṛṣṭa cakṣe saba dekhe kutūhale 

māṁsamayī dṛṣṭiyoge vahirmutha jana 
māyikāvaraṇa mātra kare daraśana 

māyāra je deśa kāla nāhika tathāya 
cidāvṛtti deśakāla tathā śobhā pāya 

parama dayālu kṛṣṇa jīve dayā kari 
prakaṭa karila saba svayaṁ avatari’ 

māyābaddha jīva tathā jāya anukṣaṇa 
kṛṣṇakṛpā vinā nāhi pāya daraśana 

je jīvera karmakṣaye sādhusaṅga haya 
seimātra vrajavana darśana karaya 

bahirmukha jīva tathā rahite nā pāre 
śīghra jaḍamāyā ākarṣiyā laya tāre 

vraja-dhāme jei jīva jāya ekabāra

IDX.en_translation:
The groves, the ponds, the lakes, Govardhana Hill, the trees and creepers, the River Yamunā—all of Vṛndāvana. 

Everything there is made of spiritual jewels and gems; there is not even a trace of material illusion there. 

The soul who becomes perfect by the grace of the gopīs sees everything with eyes cleansed by pure love and with great eagerness. 

An externally oriented person, with material vision, sees only a covering of illusion. 

There is no material place or time there; rather, the spiritual dimension of place and time is beautifully manifest. 

The supremely merciful Lord Kṛṣṇa, showing mercy to the living entities, manifested everything Himself by His descent. 

The soul bound by illusion goes there constantly, but without the Lord’s mercy, he cannot see anything. 

The soul whose past actions are exhausted obtains the association of the saintly. Only such a person can truly see the forest of Vraja. 

An externally oriented soul cannot remain there; the material illusion quickly pulls them away. 

That soul who goes to the holy land of Vraja even once gradually accumulates strong spiritual merit. 

When such merit becomes strong, the association of the saintly occurs. All the scriptures declare that the attainment of Vraja comes through the association of the saintly.

Anointed with vermilion, She whose golden lotus-like beauty defeats all pride. She whose fragrance, surpassing the scent of a blossoming lotus, proclaims Her fame. She who fulfills all the desires of the son of the king of the cowherds. May that Rādhā, the beloved of Kṛṣṇa, grant me service to Her lotus feet. 

She whose colorful silken garments defeat the luster of sapphire. She is a garden of blossoming flowers for Kṛṣṇa, the maddened bee, to sport in. Rādhā, who is like the sun for the eternal union with Kṛṣṇa. May She grant me service to Her lotus feet. 

Her tenderness surpasses the beauty of young sprouts. She whose cool form is served by the moon, sandalwood, lotus, and camphor. She who relieves the fever of the Lord of the cowherds by Her touch. May She grant me service to Her lotus feet. 

Even the goddess of fortune, who is worshiped by all the worlds, is not equal to Her in the wealth of beauty, youth, and other qualities. In character, affection, and pastimes, She is supreme. May She grant me service to Her lotus feet. 

She is skilled in all the excellent arts of the rāsa dance, singing, and joking. Adorned with the charming beauty of love, attire, and all good qualities. She who is superior even to all the young gopīs of the world. May She grant me service to Her lotus feet. 

Always endowed with the wealth of ever-new beauty, sports, and Kṛṣṇa’s moods, She makes the young gopīs tremble in their bond of love for Him. She is perfectly absorbed in the form, attire, and pastimes of Kṛṣṇa. May She grant me service to Her lotus feet. 

Filled with emotions like perspiration, trembling, thrills of ecstasy, and a choked voice, She is adorned with the ornaments of various moods like indignation, joy, and charm. She bestows a multitude of jeweled ornaments that please Kṛṣṇa’s eyes. May She grant me service to Her lotus feet. 

She who is pleased by the multitude of emotions like extreme humility and restlessness, which arise from even a half-moment’s separation from Kṛṣṇa. She who becomes entirely perfect upon obtaining Kṛṣṇa’s company. May She grant me service to Her lotus feet. 

He who praises the beloved of Kṛṣṇa with these eight verses—She who is difficult for even the greatest goddesses to behold—is quickly made a recipient of the nectar of service to Her feet by Her, making all Her companions joyful.

Kuvera Paṇḍita was greatly delighted to see the face of his son. He performed the birth rituals as prescribed by religious duty, and his happiness increased manifold. 

The child was endowed with all auspicious markings and a golden complexion. He had the beauty of a lotus, and His graceful arms reached down to His knees, captivating the minds of all people. 

He had a deep navel, was supremely beautiful, and His eyes surpassed the beauty of lotus flowers. His feet were reddish, and His toenails were like mirrors, conquering the luster of millions of moons and jewels. 

Everyone was astonished to see these charming signs of a Great Personality, and they felt that through Him, the world would be delivered. 

All the women of the town, beholding the child’s face, floated in an ocean of bliss. Their hearts could not contain their joy, and they went again and again to gaze at Him without blinking. 

They jokingly said to His mother, “Who can describe the limit of the fortune of one who has such a son? Who in the world is equal to her?” 

All the women spoke with voices choked with emotion, understanding the reason for the world’s deliverance. This is the hope of Vaiṣṇava Dāsa.

The permanent sentiment of conjugal love finds its manifestation in what I will now describe; listen attentively: complaint, the object of desire, the two aspects of the sense of relationship, His specific qualities, and similes. 

Taking refuge in one’s inherent nature, love descends into the heart, nurturing the conjugal sentiment. For others, these six factors become the cause of their love, but the cowherd girls of Vraja do not view it this way. 

Their spontaneous love, along with Their sense of relationship, always keeps them capable of selfless service. For them, there is no other endeavor except the service of Kṛṣṇa; there is never any attempt for Their own happiness. 

That love matures and attains the stage of the highest ecstatic love, to which there is no equal attainment. Such a desire for union, which is entirely wonderful and astonishing, I find no words to describe.

Kṛṣṇa is very merciful; to help us conquer the tongue, O brother, He has given us His own prasāda. Accept that nectar-like food, sing the glories of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, and with love, call out Caitanya-Nitāi.

She is a jewel of the highest ecstatic love, whose transcendental form is manifested, glorious, and adorned as the chief of the companions. She is a stream of nectar of compassion, youth, and beauty, in which she—the chaste lady who conquers the goddess of fortune—is bathed. 

Her silken garment is shyness, her beauty is the essence of saffron, and her body is adorned with musk. Trembling, tears, thrills of ecstasy, paralysis, perspiration, a faltering voice, and madness are her nine jewels. 

Adorned with a beautiful flower garland of twenty-five qualities, her silken dress is a mood of both patience and impatience. Her braided hair conceals her pique, she shines with the mark of good fortune, and the glory of Kṛṣṇa’s names is the delight of her ears. 

Her lips are red with the betel of attachment, her clear eyeliner is her charming crookedness, and she is playful, perfumed with the camphor of smiles. In the inner chambers of fame and glory, she shines upon the throne of pride, wearing the swaying garland of the uniqueness of love. 

Her blouse of loving anger covers her breasts; she conquers the moon and is the melody of the lute. Playfully placing her lotus hands on the shoulders of two companions, she distributes the nectar of Kṛṣṇa. 

Such feet of Rādhikā are your great wealth; with a blade of grass in my teeth, I beg at your feet. This humble Bhaktivinoda asks for a particle of the nectar of service to Rādhā. O Rūpa, O Raghunātha! Please give it to him.

O my mind! Remain conscious and do not forget the wealth of pure and simple truth. Otherwise, under the sway of illusion, you will eventually have to weep eternally. 

In a pure soul there is no materialism, brother; understand this clearly. The pure soul is naturally happy in Vṛndāvana. When he worships Kṛṣṇa-candra, he drowns in joy and relishes sweet mellows at every moment. 

Within his material body he practices devotion and detachment from worldly knowledge; the journey of his body is conducted in a religious mood. Whether he lives at home or in the forest, he calls out “Kṛṣṇa!” with a single mind. 

This indeed is called simple worship—with a pure mind, the one way to attain Kṛṣṇa. Whoever abandons this and imposes something artificial only perishes; he performs no true worship.

O mind! Speak the topics of Gaura. Gaura’s Name is the abode of nectar, the giver of the form of love. 

Gaura in sleep, Gaura in dreams, Gaura is the star of the eye. Gaura in life, Gaura in death, Gaura is the necklace of the neck. 

Keeping Gaurāṅga within my heart, I will remain sitting in solitude. With the desire of the mind, I will place that Moon of Beauty eye to eye. 

Without Gaura, I do not survive in life; I have made Gaura the essence. Let life go saying “Gaura”; I will not want anything else. 

Gaura’s gait, Gaura’s form, the smile on Gaura’s face; Gaura’s love, Gaura’s form—remained entered in my heart. 

Gaura is Dharma, Gaura is Karma, Gaura is the essence of the Vedas. At Gaura’s feet I have offered my life; Gaura will take me across. 

He in whose heart the Sound of Gaura and the Wealth of Gaura awaken—Narahari Dāsa, the servant of His servant’s servant, begs for shelter at the feet.

Glories to the auspicious forms of Śrī Guru and Gaura, and all glories to Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa’s auspicious amorous love.

 All glories to Their auspicious niśānta-līlā which heralds the end of night and Their auspicious awakening, bringing auspiciousness to all! Glories to maṅgala-ārati, which awakens a sphūrti of that niśānta-līlā within the devotees’ hearts!

 While You sleep, the jīvas lie sleeping deep in their ignorance, but upon Your rising, the whole world awakens! <highlight>[Meaning, if You manifest in their hearts, then all tattva and all siddhānta will be revealed to them.]</highlight>

 In the pond, which is filled with many varieties of flowers, the lotuses sway in the center. The breezes spread their auspicious aromas in all directions, bringing pure delight and joy to all.

 Large cymbals, gongs, bells, conches, karatālas and auspicious mṛdaṅgas play the supreme rasa.

 Performing maṅgala ārati within the company of devotees, the unfortunate Keśava (the servants of Srī Keśava) sings nāma-saṅkīrtana.

IDX.translation_intro: maṅgalācaraṇa expanded prayers
IDX.en_translation:
I offer my obeisances to the lotus feet of my Spiritual Master, to the preceptors, and to the Vaiṣṇavas; to Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī with his elder brother (Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī), to Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī, along with Śrīla Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī and his associates. 

I offer obeisances to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Deva, along with Śrī Advaita Ācārya, Śrī Nityānanda Avadhūta, and His associates; and to the lotus feet of Śrī Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, accompanied by Śrīmatī Lalitā-devī, Śrīmatī Viśākhā-devī, and their associates. 

[Samaṣṭigata Praṇāma] 
I offer my obeisances time and again unto Śrī Gurudeva, Śrī Gauracandra, Śrīmatī Rādhikā, Her associates and Her abode Śrī Vṛndāvana-dhāma, to Śrī Kṛṣṇa and His devotees, and to all Vaiṣṇavas. 

[Śrī Guru Praṇāma] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto my Spiritual Master, who opened my eyes, which were blinded by the darkness of ignorance, with the torchlight of knowledge. 

[Śrīla Nārāyaṇa Praṇāma] 
I offer praṇāma to oṁ viṣṇupāda Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja, who is very dear to Śrīmatī Rādhikā. 

O Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja, you are expert in describing kṛṣṇa-līlā and are fully endowed with the qualities of magnanimity and sweetness. You are the best of all great souls. I bow my head to you. 

Tridaṇḍī-sannyāsī Śrīla Nārāyaṇa Mahārāja, the crown-jewel of devotees, always keeps in his heart the lotus feet of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, especially when Kṛṣṇa serves Śrīmatī Rādhikā. He deeply meditates on Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and the internal reasons for His descent. I bow down to the lotus feet of Śrīla Nārāyaṇa Mahārāja, who possesses innumerable transcendental qualities. 

[Śrī Nārāyaṇa Vandanā] 
I offer obeisances to the best of Gurus, the excellent follower of Rūpa, who is a connoisseur of the mellows of Vraja—to that Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja, who is surrendered. 

I offer obeisances to the lotus feet of the Guru, who is the beloved of the Lord on earth, who bestows Rūpānuga-bhakti, the embodiment of mercy, Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja. 

Who always bestows service in the delightful Seva-kuñja in Vraja, at Govardhana Hill, and at Rādhā-kuṇḍa, which is full of the bliss of rasa. 

I offer obeisances to that Guru named Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja, the beloved of the Lord, by the mere remembrance of whose feet Dāmodara becomes pleased. 

[Śrīla Vāmana Vandanā] 
I offer praṇāma to oṁ viṣṇupāda Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktivedānta Vāmana Gosvāmī Mahārāja, who is most dear to Śrī Keśava (alternately: Śrī Śrīmad Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja) 

Obeisances to the servant of the saintly, the beloved of the saintly on earth, the friend of the devotees, known as “Rādhānātha-vallabha”. 

Most dear to Śrīla Saccidānanda Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, Śrīla Narottama Dāsa Ṭhākura, and Narahari Sarakāra Ṭhākura; the well-wisher of Śrī Vedānta, the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, and the Six Gosvāmīs. 

Dear to the abode of Māyāpura, the servant of the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavas, more humble than a blade of grass—the beautiful personality, Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Vāmana Gosvāmī Mahārāja. 

[Śrīla Svāmī Vandanā] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto His Divine Grace A.C. Bhaktivedānta Svāmī Prabhupāda, who is very dear to Lord Kṛṣṇa on this earth, having taken shelter at His lotus feet. 

Our respectful obeisances are unto you, O spiritual master, servant of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Prabhupāda. You are kindly preaching the message of Lord Caitanyadeva and delivering the Western countries, which are filled with impersonalism and voidism. 

[Śrīla Keśava Vandanā] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto Viṣṇupāda Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktiprajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī, who is like a lion among the Ācāryas. 

Whose character is superhuman, the protector of those who take shelter of him, always distressed by the suffering of the jīvas, the giver of the Name and Love. 

The embodiment of shelter in Gaura, whose only desire is Kṛṣṇa, the excellent follower of Rūpa, whose form is like Vinoda. 

The intimate associate of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Prabhupāda, possessor of all good qualities, the destroyer of the darkness of Māyāvāda, the knower of the meaning of Vedānta. 

[Śrīla Prabhupāda Vandanā] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto His Divine Grace Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Prabhupāda, who is very dear to Lord Kṛṣṇa on this earth, having taken shelter at His lotus feet. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to Śrī Vārṣabhānavī-devī-dayita Dāsa, who is favored by Śrīmatī Rādhā-rāṇī and who is the ocean of transcendental mercy and the deliverer of the science of Kṛṣṇa. 

I offer my respectful obeisances unto you, the personified energy of Śrī Caitanya’s mercy, who deliver devotional service which is enriched with conjugal love of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, coming exactly in the line of revelation of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. 

I offer my respectful obeisances unto you, who are the personified teachings of Lord Caitanya. You are the deliverer of the fallen souls. You do not tolerate any statement which is against the teachings of devotional service enunciated by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. 

[Śrīla Gaura-kiśora Vandanā] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto Śrīla Gaura-kiśora Dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja, who is renunciation personified and always merged in the ocean of the mellow of separation from Kṛṣṇa. 

[Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Vandanā] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto Śrīla Saccidānanda Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, who is the personification of the energy of Lord Caitanya and the best of the followers of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. 

[Śrīla Jagannātha Vandanā] 
Obeisances to you, Śrīla Jagannātha Dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja, the Emperor of the Vaiṣṇavas, dear to the saintly, who indicated the place of Gaura’s appearance. 

[Śrī Vaiṣṇava Vandanā] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto all the Vaiṣṇava devotees of the Lord. They are just like desire trees who can fulfill the desires of everyone, and they are oceans of mercy and the purifiers of the fallen souls. 

[Śrī Pañca-tattva Praṇāma] 
I offer my obeisances unto the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa, who appears in the form of a devotee (Lord Caitanya), as His expansion (Lord Nityānanda), His incarnation (Advaita Ācārya), His internal potency (Gadādhara), and His marginal potency (Śrīvāsa). 

[Śrī Nityānanda Praṇāma] 
May Śrī Nityānanda Rāma be the object of my constant remembrance. Saṅkarṣaṇa, Śeṣa Nāga and the Viṣṇus who lie on the Kāraṇa Ocean, Garbha Ocean, and ocean of milk are His plenary portions and the portions of His plenary portions. 

I offer praṇāma unto Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu who bestows the bliss of divine love, who eliminates the filth of the age of Kali, and who is the master of Jāhnavā-devī. 

[Śrī Gaurāṅga Praṇāma] 
Obeisances to the most munificent incarnation, who bestows love of Kṛṣṇa—to Kṛṣṇa Himself, who has assumed the name Kṛṣṇa Caitanya and a golden complexion. 

[Śrī Śukadeva Praṇāma] 
I offer obeisances to Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī, who can enter the hearts of all living entities. When he left home without undergoing the purificatory processes such as accepting the sacred thread, his father Vyāsa cried out, “Oh my son!” As if they were absorbed in that same feeling of separation, only the trees echoed in response to his call. 

[Śrī Kṛṣṇa Praṇāma] 
O my dear Kṛṣṇa, ocean of mercy, You are the friend of the distressed and the source of creation. You are the master of the cowherd men and the lover of the gopīs, especially Rādhā-rāṇī. I offer my respectful obeisances unto You. 

[Śrī Rādhā Praṇāma] 
Reverential obeisances unto you, O Rādhā, whose complexion is like molten gold and who are the Queen of Vṛndāvana. You are the daughter of King Vṛṣabhānu, and You are very dear to Lord Kṛṣṇa. 

O Svāminī Śrī Rādhe, I am Yours, I am Yours! I cannot live without You! Knowing this, please bestow the shelter of Your lotus feet. 

[Sambandha-adhideva Praṇāma] 
Glory to the all-merciful Rādhā and Madana-mohana! They are the only shelter of my depraved and crippled intelligence. Their lotus feet are my everything. 

[Abhidheya-adhideva Praṇāma] 
In a temple of jewels in Vṛndāvana, underneath a desire tree, Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Govinda, served by Their most confidential associates, sit upon an effulgent throne. I offer my humble obeisances unto Them. 

[Prayojana-adhideva Praṇāma] 
Śrī Śrīla Gopīnātha, who originated the transcendental mellow of the rāsa dance, stands on the shore in Vaṁśīvaṭa and attracts the attention of the cowherd damsels with the sound of His celebrated flute. May they all confer upon us their benediction. 

[Śrī Tulasī Praṇāma] 
I offer my repeated obeisances unto Vṛndā, Tulasī-devī, who is very dear to Lord Keśava. O goddess, you bestow devotional service to Kṛṣṇa and you possess the highest truth. 

Devoid of devotion and guilty of committing unlimited offences, I am being tossed about in the ocean of material existence by the turbulent waves of lust, anger, greed and so forth. Therefore, O merciful Vṛndā-devī, I take shelter of you and offer obeisances unto your lotus feet. 

[Śrī Pañca-tattva] 
Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, Prabhu Nityānanda, Śrī Advaita, Gadādhara, Śrīvāsa and all the devotees of Lord Gaura. 

[Mahā-mantra] 
Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa, Hare Hare; Hare Rāma, Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma, Hare Hare.

IDX.translation_intro: maṅgalācaraṇa
IDX.en_translation:
I offer my obeisances to the lotus feet of my Spiritual Master, to the preceptors, and to the Vaiṣṇavas; to Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī with his elder brother (Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī), to Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī, along with Śrīla Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī and his associates. 

I offer obeisances to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Deva, along with Śrī Advaita Ācārya, Śrī Nityānanda Avadhūta, and His associates; and to the lotus feet of Śrī Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, accompanied by Śrīmatī Lalitā-devī, Śrīmatī Viśākhā-devī, and their associates. 

[Śrī Guru Praṇāma] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto my Spiritual Master, who opened my eyes, which were blinded by the darkness of ignorance, with the torchlight of knowledge. 

[Śrīla Nārāyaṇa Praṇāma] 
I offer praṇāma to oṁ viṣṇupāda Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja, who is very dear to Śrīmatī Rādhikā. 

O Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja, you are expert in describing kṛṣṇa-līlā and are fully endowed with the qualities of magnanimity and sweetness. You are the best of all great souls. I bow my head to you. 

Tridaṇḍī-sannyāsī Śrīla Nārāyaṇa Mahārāja, the crown-jewel of devotees, always keeps in his heart the lotus feet of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, especially when Kṛṣṇa serves Śrīmatī Rādhikā. He deeply meditates on Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and the internal reasons for His descent. I bow down to the lotus feet of Śrīla Nārāyaṇa Mahārāja, who possesses innumerable transcendental qualities. 

[Śrī Nārāyaṇa Vandanā] 
I offer obeisances to the best of Gurus, the excellent follower of Rūpa, who is a connoisseur of the mellows of Vraja—to that Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja, who is surrendered. 

I offer obeisances to the lotus feet of the Guru, who is the beloved of the Lord on earth, who bestows Rūpānuga-bhakti, the embodiment of mercy, Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja. 

Who always bestows service in the delightful Seva-kuñja in Vraja, at Govardhana Hill, and at Rādhā-kuṇḍa, which is full of the bliss of rasa. 

I offer obeisances to that Guru named Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja, the beloved of the Lord, by the mere remembrance of whose feet Dāmodara becomes pleased. 

[Śrīla Vāmana Vandanā] 
I offer praṇāma to oṁ viṣṇupāda Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktivedānta Vāmana Gosvāmī Mahārāja, who is most dear to Śrī Keśava (alternately: Śrī Śrīmad Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja) 

Obeisances to the servant of the saintly, the beloved of the saintly on earth, the friend of the devotees, known as “Rādhānātha-vallabha”. 

Most dear to Śrīla Saccidānanda Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, Śrīla Narottama Dāsa Ṭhākura, and Narahari Sarakāra Ṭhākura; the well-wisher of Śrī Vedānta, the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, and the Six Gosvāmīs. 

Dear to the abode of Māyāpura, the servant of the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavas, more humble than a blade of grass—the beautiful personality, Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Vāmana Gosvāmī Mahārāja. 

[Śrīla Svāmī Vandanā] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto His Divine Grace A.C. Bhaktivedānta Svāmī Prabhupāda, who is very dear to Lord Kṛṣṇa on this earth, having taken shelter at His lotus feet. 

Our respectful obeisances are unto you, O spiritual master, servant of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Prabhupāda. You are kindly preaching the message of Lord Caitanyadeva and delivering the Western countries, which are filled with impersonalism and voidism. 

[Śrīla Keśava Vandanā] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto Viṣṇupāda Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktiprajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī, who is like a lion among the Ācāryas. 

Whose character is superhuman, the protector of those who take shelter of him, always distressed by the suffering of the jīvas, the giver of the Name and Love. 

The embodiment of shelter in Gaura, whose only desire is Kṛṣṇa, the excellent follower of Rūpa, whose form is like Vinoda. 

The intimate associate of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Prabhupāda, possessor of all good qualities, the destroyer of the darkness of Māyāvāda, the knower of the meaning of Vedānta. 

[Śrīla Prabhupāda Vandanā] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto His Divine Grace Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Prabhupāda, who is very dear to Lord Kṛṣṇa on this earth, having taken shelter at His lotus feet. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to Śrī Vārṣabhānavī-devī-dayita Dāsa, who is favored by Śrīmatī Rādhā-rāṇī and who is the ocean of transcendental mercy and the deliverer of the science of Kṛṣṇa. 

I offer my respectful obeisances unto you, the personified energy of Śrī Caitanya’s mercy, who deliver devotional service which is enriched with conjugal love of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, coming exactly in the line of revelation of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. 

I offer my respectful obeisances unto you, who are the personified teachings of Lord Caitanya. You are the deliverer of the fallen souls. You do not tolerate any statement which is against the teachings of devotional service enunciated by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. 

[Śrīla Gaura-kiśora Vandanā] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto Śrīla Gaura-kiśora Dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja, who is renunciation personified and always merged in the ocean of the mellow of separation from Kṛṣṇa. 

[Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Vandanā] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto Śrīla Saccidānanda Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, who is the personification of the energy of Lord Caitanya and the best of the followers of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. 

[Śrīla Jagannātha Vandanā] 
Obeisances to you, Śrīla Jagannātha Dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja, the Emperor of the Vaiṣṇavas, dear to the saintly, who indicated the place of Gaura’s appearance. 

[Śrī Vaiṣṇava Vandanā] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto all the Vaiṣṇava devotees of the Lord. They are just like desire trees who can fulfill the desires of everyone, and they are oceans of mercy and the purifiers of the fallen souls. 

[Śrī Pañca-tattva Praṇāma] 
I offer my obeisances unto the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa, who appears in the form of a devotee (Lord Caitanya), as His expansion (Lord Nityānanda), His incarnation (Advaita Ācārya), His internal potency (Gadādhara), and His marginal potency (Śrīvāsa). 

[Śrī Nityānanda Praṇāma] 
May Śrī Nityānanda Rāma be the object of my constant remembrance. Saṅkarṣaṇa, Śeṣa Nāga and the Viṣṇus who lie on the Kāraṇa Ocean, Garbha Ocean, and ocean of milk are His plenary portions and the portions of His plenary portions. 

[Śrī Gaurāṅga Praṇāma] 
Obeisances to the most munificent incarnation, who bestows love of Kṛṣṇa—to Kṛṣṇa Himself, who has assumed the name Kṛṣṇa Caitanya and a golden complexion. 

[Śrī Kṛṣṇa Praṇāma] 
O my dear Kṛṣṇa, ocean of mercy, You are the friend of the distressed and the source of creation. You are the master of the cowherd men and the lover of the gopīs, especially Rādhā-rāṇī. I offer my respectful obeisances unto You. 

[Śrī Rādhā Praṇāma] 
Reverential obeisances unto you, O Rādhā, whose complexion is like molten gold and who are the Queen of Vṛndāvana. You are the daughter of King Vṛṣabhānu, and You are very dear to Lord Kṛṣṇa. 

[Sambandha-adhideva Praṇāma] 
Glory to the all-merciful Rādhā and Madana-mohana! They are the only shelter of my depraved and crippled intelligence. Their lotus feet are my everything. 

[Abhidheya-adhideva Praṇāma] 
In a temple of jewels in Vṛndāvana, underneath a desire tree, Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Govinda, served by Their most confidential associates, sit upon an effulgent throne. I offer my humble obeisances unto Them. 

[Prayojana-adhideva Praṇāma] 
Śrī Śrīla Gopīnātha, who originated the transcendental mellow of the rāsa dance, stands on the shore in Vaṁśīvaṭa and attracts the attention of the cowherd damsels with the sound of His celebrated flute. May they all confer upon us their benediction. 

[Śrī Tulasī Praṇāma] 
I offer my repeated obeisances unto Vṛndā, Tulasī-devī, who is very dear to Lord Keśava. O goddess, you bestow devotional service to Kṛṣṇa and you possess the highest truth. 

[Śrī Pañca-tattva] 
Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, Prabhu Nityānanda, Śrī Advaita, Gadādhara, Śrīvāsa and all the devotees of Lord Gaura. 

[Mahā-mantra] 
Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa, Hare Hare; Hare Rāma, Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma, Hare Hare.

If Your servant is destroyed, there will be dishonor on earth. A stain will befall the moon of Your glory.

IDX.en_translation:
O brother, you are engaging in mānuṣa-bhajana (worship of humans), singing songs of bhāva (ecstatic emotion). You keep the good hidden, but it will be revealed in the house of Yama (the lord of death). 

If the female is hijṛe (lacking spiritual feminine qualities) and the male is khojā (lacking spiritual masculine qualities), then it becomes karttābhaṛā (worship of a worldly master). By this pretense, you are enjoying, deceiving your own mind. 

You say “Guru (spiritual master) is truth” with your mouth, but, brother, you are immersed in material happiness. Your association is with outward things; how will you become pure? 

The jīva (living entity) gets absorbed in yoṣitsanga (association with women) and arthalobha (greed for wealth), leading to mental agitation. Do such things suit a bāula (mendicant/devotee)? A moth dies seeing fire. 

Cāṅda-Bāula humbly requests: giving up all these, purely chant “Hari”; then you will cross the bhavasāgara (ocean of material existence).

By your mercy, may the Names of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa manifest on my tongue. Kṛṣṇa-dāsa says: “May Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa awaken in my heart.”

The Jāhnavī says, “My good fortune is boundless; my vow has become successful.” 

Gorā gives the dead child into the waters of the Ganges. Swelling up, Jāhnavī-devī takes the child into her lap. 

Swelling up, she touches Gorā’s lotus feet. With the child in her lap, the goddess trembles with divine love. 

Seeing the emotional state of the Jāhnavī, all the devotees continuously make the auspicious sound of the holy name. 

From heaven, the demigods shower flowers. Then the sky becomes covered, filled with celestial airplanes. 

In this way, becoming absorbed in various emotional states, all the people performed the funeral rites and then took a bath. 

In supreme bliss, all went to their homes. Bhaktivinoda is immersed in the fullness of the mood of Gorā.

vraja-nava-yuva-rājasyāṣṭakaṁ tuṣṭa-buddhiḥ

By the beauty of His limbs He crushes the pride of the god of love, and the splendor of His clothing surpasses the beauty of the lotus filament. He is the moon-like child whose immaturity is overshadowed by His rising youth; may the youthful prince of Vraja fulfill my desires. 

He is like the churning rod that churns the very life of His father, and He is like the personified affection of His mother, Yaśodā. He is the nectar-like vision for the assembly of elders and cowherd girls; may the youthful prince of Vraja fulfill my desires. 

He is the original teacher of captivating and skillful deeds, awakened in the entire world, and the resting place of supreme strength. He is the friend who delights everyone with His incomparable qualities; may the youthful prince of Vraja fulfill my desires. 

By the twitching of His bow-like eyebrows, He creates waves of agitation in young women that are difficult even for Cupid with his countless arrows. He is the ocean for the fish-like lives of His dear companions; may the youthful prince of Vraja fulfill my desires. 

He churns the deep lake of Rādhā’s heart like a wild elephant, disturbed by the playful hooks of His eyes. He is the six-legged bee playing to taste the nectar of the mellow of divine love; may the youthful prince of Vraja fulfill my desires. 

With the success of His union with Rādhikā, which arises at every step, His body is bound by Their mutual affection. He is an ocean of continuous streams of the honey of sweetness; may the youthful prince of Vraja fulfill my desires. 

His great mind-elephant, which is unrestrained in the three worlds, is held captive by the abundant, crooked glances of Rādhā. With a smiling face due to the joyful jokes of Viśākhā, may the youthful prince of Vraja fulfill my desires. 

“O friend, look! Even though it was crushed in the confusion of Your secret meeting, Your belt of friends shines in the morning!” Thus, by revealing these secrets, He makes Rādhā shy; may the youthful prince of Vraja fulfill my desires. 

One who diligently studies these eight verses of the youthful prince of Vraja—which are full of excellent pastimes—will have his name recorded in the list of Her intimate associates by the Queen of Vṛndāvana, who is an expert in divine mellows.

ḍubila ḍubila bali siñce sabe pāni 

pāriṣadagaṇa sabe hari hari bale 
pūrava soṅari kahe bhāse prema-jale 

gadādhara mukha heri mṛdu mṛdu hāse 
vāsudeva ghoṣa kahe manera ullāse
IDX.en_translation:
Without understanding what mood was in Gaurāṅgacāñda's mind, He went to the bank of the River Ganges with His associates. 

Taking His dear Gadādhara and others with Him, Gaura ascended the boat, absorbed in ecstatic love. 

He Himself became the helmsman and steered the boat. Everyone splashed water, saying, "It's sinking! It's sinking!" 

All the associates chanted "Hari! Hari!" Remembering pastimes, they spoke, floating in the waters of divine love. 

Seeing Gadādhara's face, He smiled gently. Vāsudeva Ghoṣa says with joy in his heart.

I have no desire for yogic perfections or liberation. Nor do I desire to be an associate in the spiritual world. Even if I do not attain divine love, may my residence certainly be in Vṛndāvana. 

Where Lord Brahmā prayed to be born even as a blade of grass, and Uddhava, the crest-jewel of pure devotees, also prayed, seeing its supreme sweetness—in that place, may my residence certainly be in Vṛndāvana. 

“What austerities have you performed, O Earth?” Even the gopīs glorified the Earth, saying: “Because the marks of Lord Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet are imprinted upon you.” In that place, may my residence certainly be in Vṛndāvana. 

Where the attachment to the gopīs alone reaches its complete perfection, and because of which the Vedas declare “He is the personification of all mellows”—therefore, may my residence certainly be in Vṛndāvana. 

Bounded by Bhaṇḍīravana, Govardhana, and the site of the Rāsa dance, marked by these three boundaries within a radius of forty miles—though measured, it is immeasurable in its glories. In that place, may my residence certainly be in Vṛndāvana. 

Where the sovereignty belongs to the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu, by whom the joy of divine love arises in people, and in which my hope is very strong—therefore in that place, may my residence certainly be in Vṛndāvana. 

Where the pastimes of the great Rāsa dance take place, which even the Goddess of Fortune could not attain through many austerities—in that place, filled with splendid and beautiful groves, may my residence certainly be in Vṛndāvana. 

Where deer and antelopes always play fearlessly, cuckoos and parrots chirp sweetly, and peacocks dance—in that place, may my residence certainly be in Vṛndāvana. 

Those who loudly recite these eight verses of Vṛndāvanāṣṭakam with steadfast intelligence will directly attain service to the lotus feet of the Mistress of Vṛndāvana at the end of their lives.

Śacī-nandana, the treasure and life of the devotees, dances. With Him dances dear Nityānanda. Advaita, Śrīnivāsa, and Haridāsa also dance. Vāsughoṣa and Rāya Rāmānanda likewise dance. 

Seeing Nityānanda’s face, the Lord chants “Hari! Hari!” and rolls on the earth in divine love. Dear Gadādhara comes and sits on the Lord’s left side, frequently looking at Narahari’s face. 

The Lord does not open His eyes, saying, “Where is my sakhī? Where will I get the audience of Rādhā?” “Tell me, tell me, Narahari, I can no longer control myself,” Saying this, He became unconscious. 

“Just now I was there, who brought me here? In the forest grove with the mellows of the Rāsa dance.” All happiness and opulence is gone, now there is only calamity— thus the servant Locana Dāsa laments.

In Nadiyā, drink the nectar of Gorā’s pastimes. Drink it, give up sorrow and fear, and steady your mind. 

This temporary world, O brother, only Kṛṣṇa is the essence. According to Gorā’s teachings, worship Kṛṣṇa constantly. 

Whoever is fortunate to grasp the lotus feet of Gorā and worships Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa in Vraja, that person is my life. 

“Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-Gorācānd” and “Nadiyā-Vṛndāvana”- just make this the essence, and you will attain eternal wealth. 

I am devoid of knowledge and intelligence, fallen, insignificant, and contemptible. I am without fruitive action or knowledge, and without good conduct. 

My Guru and the Vaiṣṇavas gave me titles. But for one devoid of devotion, these titles have now become a disease. 

Striving to remove that disease, I have taken shelter of the lotus feet of the Vaiṣṇavas. 

Holding the dust of the lotus feet of the Vaiṣṇavas on my head, Bhaktivinoda sings this song, “The Slayer of Sorrow”.

From the rising mountain of Nadīyā, the full moon of Lord Gaura-hari mercifully arose. The darkness of sin was destroyed, the three worlds rejoiced, and the whole world was filled with the sound of Lord Hari’s Name. 

At that time, Advaita Ācārya rose up in his own home and danced with a joyful heart. Taking Haridāsa Ṭhākura with him, he danced in the joy of congregational chanting, though no one knew why. 

Seeing the eclipse, he smiled and quickly came to the bank of the Ganges to bathe. Taking the eclipse as a pretext, he gave various gifts to the brāhmaṇas with strong conviction. 

Seeing the world filled with joy, Haridāsa Ṭhākura hinted: “Seeing your wonderful mood, my mind is very pleased. I see that some great event is about to manifest.” 

Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita was filled with great joy and went to bathe in the Ganges. His mind overwhelmed with joy, he performed congregational chanting and gave various donations. 

In this way, devotees and renunciants wherever they resided received great strength. They danced and performed congregational chanting, their minds overwhelmed with joy, and gave donations on the pretext of the eclipse. 

The women of the village, filling plates with various gifts, all came to see. Seeing the form of the child who glowed like raw gold, they gave their blessings, experiencing great happiness. 

The celestial women, assuming the guise of village women, also came to see, filling their vessels with various articles. 

In the sky, the demigods and celestial musicians danced and sang praises with their instruments. Dancers and musicians from all of Navadvīpa also came and danced with great joy. 

Who was coming and who was going, who was dancing and who was singing—no one could keep track. Sorrow and lamentation were dispelled, the people were filled with delight, and Jagannātha Miśra became overwhelmed with joy. 

Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita and other devotees came to Jagannātha Miśra and reminded him of his duties. He had the birth ceremony performed according to scriptural injunctions and then gave various donations. 

All the gifts he received, and whatever he had in his house, he gave in charity to the priests. He honored all the dancers, singers, and poor people by giving them wealth. 

Mālinī-devī, the wife of Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita, along with the wives of other devotees, joyfully offered worship with vermillion, turmeric, oil, and various fruits. 

Sītā-Ṭhākurāṇī, the venerable wife of Advaita Ācārya, receiving her husband’s order, went with gifts to see the crest-jewel of children. 

She brought golden ornaments, silver coins, bangles, divine conch-shells, and various necklaces of gold coins. 

She brought tiger-claw pendants set in gold, silk waist-threads, and all manner of ornaments for the hands and feet. She also brought multi-colored silk saris and much wealth in gold and silver coins. 

Filling vessels with auspicious articles like grass, turmeric, saffron, and sandalwood, she rode in a covered palanquin with her attendants and baskets full of clothes and ornaments. 

She arrived at the house of Mother Śacī with many gifts of food and clothing. Seeing the child’s form, she saw directly the Lord of Gokula, only the complexion was different. 

All His limbs were perfectly formed, appearing like a golden Deity and endowed with all auspicious marks. Seeing the child’s divine effulgence, her heart melted with parental love. 

She placed grass and paddy on His head and gave many blessings, saying: “May You two brothers live long.” Fearing that witches might cast an evil eye, she named Him “Nimāi.” 

On the day of the mother and son’s first bath, she gave them clothes and ornaments, honoring Jagannātha Miśra as well. Having accepted the hospitality of Mother Śacī and Jagannātha Miśra, Sītā-Ṭhākurāṇī returned home with a joyful heart. 

Thus, Mother Śacī and Jagannātha Miśra, having received their Son, had all their desires fulfilled. Their house was filled with wealth and grain, and they became more joyful day by day. 

Jagannātha Miśra was a peaceful and pure devotee; he had no pride in his wealth. By the influence of his Son, much wealth came to them, and he gave it all in charity to the priests for the pleasure of the Lord. 

Calculating the astrological moment with joy, the grandfather of the Lord secretly told Jagannātha Miśra: “I see the marks of a great personality upon His limbs; He will surely deliver the entire world.” 

Thus the Lord mercifully made His advent in Mother Śacī’s house. Whoever hears this narrative will receive the mercy of Lord Gaura and eventually attain His lotus feet. 

Having attained a human birth, one who does not hear the glories of Lord Gaura makes such a birth useless. Having found a river of nectar, if one chooses to drink from a poisonous pit, why did they not simply die after taking birth? 

I worship the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya, Nityānanda, Advaita Ācārya, Svarūpa Dāmodara, Rūpa Gosvāmī, and Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī. Kṛṣṇa-dāsa Kavirāja has thus sung the pastimes of the Lord’s birth.

What is the state of mind of the very virtuous and devoted wives of Nadīyā? Their minds are not with their own sons for even a moment, as they praise the character and pastimes of the Son of Śacī. 

Seeing the end of the night, forsaking their beds, they cannot hold patience for even half a moment. Filling plates with various items, row after row, they set off to offer them to the Moon of Nadīyā. 

As they enter Śacī-mātā’s house, a sea of joy overflows in their hearts. Everyone sees, in the lap of His mother, Gorā, the Moon of Gokula, playing. 

Their eyes are soothed, and holding Him in their laps, the women forget their own bodies. Narahari says, “Oh, wonderful! Oh, wonderful! Who has created such a loving sentiment?”

I offer my obeisances unto Viṣṇupāda Śrī Śrīmad Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī, who is like a lion among the ācāryas. 

He perfectly fulfills the desire of Śrī Sarasvatī in every way; he is non-different from Śrī Sarasvatī and is the deliverer of the fallen. 

He is harder than a thunderbolt in destroying conclusions opposed to bhakti; he is fearless for the sake of truth and causes one to reject bad association. 

His character is superhuman, and he protects those who take shelter of him; he is always distressed by the suffering of the jīvas and bestows love for the Holy Name. 

He is the manifestation of Viṣṇupāda, and his only desire is to serve Kṛṣṇa; he is immersed in thoughts of Gaura and holds Śrī Guru in his heart. 

He possesses affectionate vision, seeing the whole universe as pervaded by Viṣṇu; I offer obeisances to you, Gurudeva, who are the embodiment of Kṛṣṇa’s opulence. 

He is the founder of the Śrī Gauḍīya Vedānta Samiti and the one who brought about the prosperity of service in Śrī Māyāpura Dhāma. 

He always protected the Navadvīpa Parikramā; I offer my obeisances to that Śrī Guru who is merciful to the fallen. 

Please give me your strength; this is the earnest prayer of this fallen soul. May my mind run rapidly toward your lotus feet.

I bow down to that Supreme Controller, whose form is eternal bliss and knowledge, whose ears are adorned with swinging earrings, and who is splendidly manifest in Gokula. He is fleeing from Mother Yaśodā due to fear, being pursued by her to the point of being caught. 

He is crying again and again, rubbing His two eyes with His two lotus-like hands, His eyes filled with fear. His neck, marked with three lines, is trembling due to His frequent breaths, and the garland around His belly is tied by the devotion of Yaśodā. 

To this Lord, who immerses His own people in pools of joy through such pastimes and who reveals that He is conquered by His devotees who possess knowledge of His supremacy, I offer my obeisances again and again with love. 

O Lord! I do not pray for liberation, nor for its ultimate limit, nor any other boon from the bestowers of boons. O Lord! May Your form as a cowherd child always be manifest in my mind. What need is there for anything else? 

O Lord! May Your lotus-like face—encircled by dark-blue, soft, curly hair and repeatedly kissed by Mother Yaśodā, with reddish bimba fruit-like lips—always be manifest in my mind. What is the use of millions of other gains? 

O Lord! I offer my obeisances to You, O Dāmodara! O Ananta! O Viṣṇu! Be pleased, O Master! I am submerged in a network of miseries. O Lord! Please bestow Your merciful glance upon me, who am extremely poor and ignorant. Become visible before my eyes! 

Just as the two sons of Kuvera, though bound in material forms, were liberated by You and made into devotees, similarly, please bestow upon me Your own loving devotion. I have no desire for liberation in this world, O Dāmodara! 

My obeisances to the rope which is a brilliant abode! And to Your belly, which is the abode of the entire universe! My obeisances to Rādhikā, Your beloved! My obeisances to You, O Lord, whose pastimes are endless!

I offer my obeisances unto You, the son of Jagannātha Miśra, who are the Absolute Truth in the past, present, and future. I offer my respectful obeisances unto You, along with Your servants, Your followers, and Your associates. 

I worship Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, who is very eager to bestow mercy upon His devotees. He is satisfied by anything whatsoever offered by a devotee with faith. 

I worship Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, an ocean of mercy, who descended in Bengal for the purpose of bestowing loving devotion. 

Repeated obeisances to the maintainer of the universe, the golden Lord, the Supreme Soul, the son of Śacī, and the husband of the goddess of fortune. 

O beautiful young moon of Navadvīpa! O Lord Viśvambhara, best among men! O son of Śacī, thief of my thoughts! O Lord of Viṣṇupriyā, please be pleased! 

Repeated obeisances to You, whose form is full of joyful pastimes, who are beautiful with a divine golden luster, and who bestow the great mellow of divine love. 

I surrender to the one ancient Supreme Person, an ocean of mercy, who—for the purpose of teaching renunciation and His own devotional service—assumed the form of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya. 

All glories to the Lord who was born from the womb of Śacī! All glories to Him whose only principle is to give devotional love! All glories to His golden form that rivals Mount Meru! Blessed is the name of Kṛṣṇa Caitanya! 

O Lord Caitanya! I have fallen into the ocean of worldly miseries, swallowed up by the crocodiles and sharks of lust, anger, and greed. I am chained by bad desires and am without shelter. Please give me the support of Your feet. 

May the son of Śacī, Lord Hari—resplendent with a cluster of beautiful golden effulgence—mercifully descend in this age to bestow the opulence of His own devotion in the most elevated and brilliant mellow, which was never given before. May He always manifest in the cave of your heart. 

Rādhā is the transformation of Kṛṣṇa’s love, His internal pleasure potency. Although They are one in nature, They formerly appeared on earth in two separate bodies. Now those two have attained unity as Caitanya. I offer obeisances to that form of Kṛṣṇa, who is covered by the mood and luster of Rādhā. 

Out of a desire to know the glory of Rādhā’s love, the wonderful sweetness She experiences through Me, and the happiness She derives from My experience, the moon-like Lord Hari was born from the womb of Śacī.

I offer my obeisances to Lord Narasimha, who gives joy to Prahlada Maharaja and whose nails are like chisels on the stonelike chest of the demon Hiranyakasipu. 

Lord Nrsimhadeva is here, and He is also there on the opposite side. Wherever I go, there I see Lord Nrsimhadeva. He is outside and within my heart. Therefore I take shelter of Lord Nrsimhadeva, the original Supreme Personality of Godhead. 

O Kesava! O Lord of the universe! O Lord Hari, who have assumed the form of half-man, half-lion! All glories to You! Just as one can easily crush a wasp between one’s fingernails, so in the same way the body of the wasp-like demon Hiranyakasipu has been ripped apart by the wonderful pointed nails on Your beautiful lotus hands. 

All glories to Nrsimhadeva! All glories to Nrsimhadeva! All glories to Nrsimhadeva! All glories to the Lord of Prahlada, the bee who sits on the lotus face of the Goddess of Fortune. 

I worship Lord Nrsimha, within whose mouth resides the Goddess of Learning, on whose chest resides the Goddess of Fortune, and within whose heart resides the Divine Will. 

I offer my obeisances to Lord Hari, who has the face of a lion, whose effulgence is like that of the autumn moon, who destroys the ignorance of His devotees, and who gives pleasure to the heart of Prahlada. 

Although very ferocious, the lioness is very kind to her cubs. Similarly, although very ferocious to non-devotees like Hiranyakasipu, Lord Nrsimhadeva is very soft and kind to devotees like Prahlada Maharaja.

Whose leaves and tender flower buds embrace the lotus feet of the Lord of Fortune. 

Blessed Tulasī, you have performed perfect penance and are the great chief queen of Lord Śālagrāma.

His cheeks are adorned with swaying earrings, and a peacock feather flies from His topknot. His graceful arms are skilled in the rhythm of His playful dancing. 

He has lotus-like eyes and He removes all sins; His speech is pleasing to the ears. Govinda Dāsa takes refuge at His pure, tender, and sprout-like lotus feet.

O Govardhana! You assumed the form of an umbrella held by the arm of my Lord, and thus crushed the arrogant pride of the fierce king of the gods. O peerless, vast King of Mountains! Please grant me residence near you. 

O Govardhana! In your every cave, the youthful Divine Couple joyfully perform Their passionate loving pastimes. Knowing this and aspiring to serve Them, please grant me residence near you. 

O Govardhana! With great delight, You allow my Beloved to play with Balarāma and His friends amidst Your incomparable jeweled altars, gem-studded thrones, trees, waterfalls, caves, peaks, and valleys. Please grant me residence near you. 

O Govardhana! You make manifest the beautiful and fragrant dark altar, which is a witness to the tax-collecting pastime of the ocean of divine mellows—the youthful Divine Couple—thus bringing joy to the most discerning devotees. Please grant me residence near you. 

O Govardhana! You secretly embrace Rādhā-kuṇḍa—the unique and most beloved friend of Hari—and thus confidentially witness the pastimes of the divine youthful couple there. Please grant me residence near you. 

O Govardhana! You constantly nourish the cows with your fresh grass, pure water, and the shade of your trees at every step, thus making your name meaningful throughout the three worlds. Please grant me residence near you. 

O Govardhana! By providing refuge in your form as a new home, you protected the cowherd village from the prolonged wrath of Indra, and thus received great honor from Kṛṣṇa, the enemy of Agha and Baka. Please grant me residence near you. 

O King of Mountains! The nectar of your name—“the best among the servants of Hari”—emanated from the moon-like face of Śrī Rādhā, and the Vedas clearly declare you to be the ornament of Vraja. Please grant me residence near you. 

O Govardhana! You are the sole bestower of happiness upon the cowherd men, animals, and birds of Vraja, who are saturated with the mellow of friendship with Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa and Their associates. Due to your boundless compassion, please accept me and grant me residence near you. 

O Govardhana! By the causelessly merciful son of Śacī, who is most dear to you, I—who am deceitful and wicked—have been offered to you. Therefore, disregarding my fitness or unfitness, please grant me residence near you. 

One who diligently recites these ten verses—which bestow divine mellows in praise of Śrīla Govardhana, the chief of all mountains—will quickly attain residence in this blissful place and directly achieve the jewel of service to the auspicious Divine Couple.

IDX.en_translation:
O Hari Nama! the Tips of Thy Lotus Feet have eternally been adored by the glowing radiance diffused from the gemmed chaplets of the Upanishads, the crest jewels of the Vedas. Thou art eternally worshipped by the liberated souls. O Hari Nama! clearing myself of all offences, I entirely take shelter in Thee. 

O Holy Name! all glory to Thee who art eternally chanted by the saints. To confer eternal bliss upon the people Thou hast appeared before them as the Transcendental Word. Thou killest all sorts of terrible sufferings of him who happens to chant even Thy dimly reflected Name known as Namabhasa. 

O Sun of Blessed Name! even the slightest reflection of Thy Radiant Self is suficient to dispel the gloom of ignorance from the minds of those who are steeped in the foul sink of worldliness, and confer spiritual vision of pure devotion on those who are blind of the inner sight. Who is there so expert in the world that can sing the glories of Thy Name to finish? 

O Holy Name! the seed of deeds, which necessitates rebirth for their fruition, is not totally destroyed despite veritable at-one-ment with Brahman by dint of constant meditation. But O Name! no sooner dost Thou gain a free scope on the tongue of Thy chanter than all the seeds of deeds of his prenatal existence are destroyed. Such the Vedas loudly declare. 

O Killer of the demon Agha! O Son of Yashoda! O Son of Nanda! O Lotus-Eyed! O Moon of the Gopees! O Lord of Brindaban! O Merciful to the bowed! O Kṛṣṇa! Thou hast manifested Thy self in such various Forms out of Thy infinite mercy. Let my ardour of love go on increasing, in a great measure, for Thee. 

O Holy Name! Thou hast a double Form, viz., Vachya (Signified) i.e., the Transcendental Personality, and Vachaka (Significant) i. e., the Transcendental Word or Name- such Kṛṣṇa, Govinda, etc., -identical with the Vachya. To us the latter Vachaka is more compassionate than the former Vachya against whom we fallen souls as have sinned. Because as soon as we chant the Vachaka, i.e., Thy Holy Name, keeping clear of offences against the Name, we are at once immersed the blissful ocean of Divine Love. 

O Holy Name! O Kṛṣṇa! Thou killest the offences of Thy devotees who have taken shelter in Thy Lotus Feet. Thou art veritable Living Entity of the most Beautiful self conscious concentrated Bliss. Thou art, O Name! the Entity of the great Rejoicings of Gokula. O Kṛṣṇa! I offer my humble greetings, time and again, to Thee- the Divine Form of all Exquisiteness in the fullest degree. 

O Holy Name of Kṛṣṇa! Thou art the very life of Narada’s guitar and the Elixir of the ambrosial ripples of the ocean surcharged with Divine mellowness. I beseech Thee, O Holy Name! do Thou ever find a full scope in my tongue with all the ardour of Divine Love.

Detachment, dejection, pride, humility, weariness, and the madness of exertion; arrogance, fear, apprehension, and forgetfulness; agitation, laziness, and sickness; delusion, death, and inertia; bashfulness, dissimulation, and memory. 

Deliberation, mental fickleness, anxiety, joy, and steadfastness; fierceness, envy, sleepiness, and deep slumber—know all these groups of emotions, thirty-three in total, are recognized as transitory states. 

In the unparalleled sweet mellow, fierceness and laziness do not appear; all other emotions remain as they should. Arising in the bliss of emotional absorption, they are especially eager to move toward the permanent sentiment. 

Through the support of speech, body, and goodness, they convey the union of the mellow, like the enduring waves of an ocean. Quickly fulfilling their own purpose and making the ocean full, they then subside and are seen no more.

IDX.en_translation:
Nitāi is the treasure of my life, Nitāi is my identity. Without Nitāi, I have no other destination. 

I will throw ashes in the face of worldly happiness. I will beg in the town, singing of Nitāi. 

I will not go anywhere where Nitāi is absent. I will not look at the face of a person averse to Nitāi. 

Hara (Śiva) holds on his head the Ganges, which is the water of His (Nitāi’s) feet. Not worshipping such a Nitāi, one dies in misery. 

Locana says: Whoever does not accept my Nitāi, I will set fire to the middle of his face.

śrī-śrīdhara māte dālāla keśava bhāratī, śrī-vidyā vācaspati 

paricāraka āchena kṛṣṇa-dāsa prabhṛti

O brother, who will go to the marketplace of the Holy Name? Come quickly! Those two wicked persons, Jagāi and Mādhāi, have already come and looted all the goods of the marketplace. 

The respected proprietors of this marketplace are Advaita and Sanātana. The expert treasurer is Gadādhara Paṇḍita. 

The watchmen are Haridāsa and others, including Śrī Sañjaya. Śrīdhara serves as a broker, along with Keśava Bhāratī and Vidyā Vācaspati. 

Kṛṣṇa-dāsa and others are the attendants. Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita is the treasurer, and Kedāra has joined as the sweeper. 

The value of this marketplace is determined by the manifestation of the nine kinds of devotional service. Divine love is the essence of all currency; there is no restriction of more or less, for it is available equally to all. 

O people, all this is understood in the mind: the very purpose of this divine love. A single saintly instruction, full of nectar, is the good message in the form of the Holy Name. In this there is no partiality; all eat from the same plate, even the most fallen.

One who has no connection with Nitāi has wasted their life; that (two legged) animal is most wicked. If one does not utter Nitāi’s name and is absorbed in worldly pleasures, what good will their knowledge or family lineage do for them?

Nitāi’s feet are the ultimate truth, and His servants are eternal. Always yearn for Nitāi’s feet. Narottama is very unhappy; O Nitāi, please make me happy, and keep me by your reddish lotus feet.

IDX.en_translation:
I shall now speak the Nṛsiṁha-kavaca, which was spoken by Prahlāda in ancient times. It gives all protection, is pious, and destroys all disturbances. 

It bestows all opulence and grants heaven and liberation. Having meditated on Nṛsiṁha, the Lord of gods, seated on a golden throne. 

With open mouth, three eyes, and luster like the autumn moon; embraced by Lakṣmī on His left side, and surrounded by opulences. 

Four-armed, with soft limbs, adorned with golden earrings; with a chest beautified by a lotus, and marked with jeweled armlets. 

Resembling molten gold, wearing yellow, spotless garments; the crest-jewel of Indra and the gods, with the brilliance of shining rubies. 

His two feet shine with weapons like the conch and disc; He is praised by Garuḍa with humility and joy. 

Having placed Him in the lotus of one’s own heart, one should recite the Kavaca. May Nṛsiṁha, who appeared for the protection of the world, protect my head. 

May He who is all-pervading and resides in the pillar protect the fruit of my words. May Nṛsiṁha, whose eyes are the moon, sun, and fire, protect my eyes. 

May Nṛhari, who is dear to the prayers of the best of sages, protect my memory. May Siṁha-nāsa protect my nose, and He who is dear to the face of Lakṣmī protect my face. 

May the Lord of all knowledge, Nṛsiṁha, protect my tongue. May He whose face is like the moon and who is always worshiped by Prahlāda protect my mouth. 

May Nṛsiṁha protect my neck, and the Sustainer of the earth and Maker of Ananta protect my shoulders. May Nṛsiṁha, whose arms are adorned with divine weapons, protect my arms. 

May Nṛsiṁha, the bestower of boons to the gods, protect my hands from all sides. May Hari, who is attainable by yogīs, protect my heart, His residence. 

May He who tore open the chest and abdomen of Hiraṇyākṣa protect my middle. May Nṛhari protect my navel, He who is praised by Brahmā who sits on His own navel. 

May He in whose hips are millions of universes protect my hips. May He who sees the secret form of the secret mantras protect my private parts. 

May Manobhava protect my thighs, and He who appears in a human form protect my knees. May the Man-Lion, who removes the burden of the earth, protect my calves. 

May the Lord Nṛhari, the giver of the kingdom of the gods, protect my feet. May the Thousand-headed Person protect my body entirely. 

May the Ferocious One protect me from the East, and the Elder Brother of the Great Hero (Maha-vīra-agraja) from the Southeast (Agni). May Mahā-viṣṇu protect me from the South, and the Greatly Blazing One from the Southwest. 

May the Lord of all protect me from the West, He whose faces are in all directions. May Nṛsiṁha protect me from the Northwest, and the Ornamented Form from the North. 

May the Auspicious One, the giver of all auspiciousness, protect me from the Northeast. May the Man-Lion, the Death of death, protect me from the fear of material existence. 

This Nṛsiṁha-kavaca is adorned by the mouth of Prahlāda. One who reads it daily with devotion is freed from all sins. 

He becomes wealthy and has sons in this world, and lives a long life. Whatever desire he wishes for, he undoubtedly obtains it. 

He attains victory everywhere; he becomes victorious everywhere. It is the preventer of the influence of earthly, aerial, and celestial planets. 

It is the supreme remover of poison born of scorpions and snakes. It is the cause of driving away Brahma-rākṣasas and Yakṣas. 

Whether written on the arm or on a palm leaf, this auspicious Kavaca—if one wears it on the wrist, all his activities are perfected. 

One attains victory over one’s own self among gods, demons, and humans. A man who recites it with regulation at one sandhyā or three sandhyās (junctions of the day). 

He finds all-auspiciousness, enjoyment, and liberation. Reading thirty-two thousand times for pure souls. 

The perfection of the mantra of this Kavaca is born. By this King of Mantras, having made ashes (bhasma) with the mantras. 

One who applies the tilaka removes the fear of planets. Chanting three times and enchanting water given. 

The man who drinks the mantra and practices meditation on Nṛsiṁha—his diseases are destroyed, even those born in the abdomen. 

Roaring and making others roar, cracking the surface of the earth with His own arms, killing, ripping, and heating. Throwing and casting down the sons of Diti in heaven and on earth. Crying and causing anger, constantly destroying and filling in every direction. Seeing and filling—I bow to the Divine Lion with hundreds of multitudes of hands. 

Thus ends the Śrī Nṛsiṁha-kavaca spoken by Prahlāda in the Śrī Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa.

O my most merciful Śrīla Narottama Dāsa Ṭhākura! He is the very personification of divine love. How tender is his form, like a śiriṣa blossom, surpassing even the golden luster of a physical body. 

In his youth, no worldly pleasure appealed to him. Hearing the qualities of Lord Gaura, he always wept. Abandoning kingly enjoyments and with great longing, he journeyed to Vraja. 

Entering Vṛndāvana with a joyful mind, he surrendered himself to Śrīla Lokanātha Dāsa Gosvāmī. Lokanātha Dāsa, being merciful, accepted him as his own and initiated him with the Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa mantra. 

Seeing Narottama’s endeavor, everyone in Vṛndāvana was happy and showered him with affection as if he were their very life. He and Śrīnivāsa Ācārya had such a deep connection—their lives were one, and only their bodies were distinct. 

Seeing the Deity of Śrī Rādhā-vinoda, his eyes were always soothed, as Lord Lokanātha was engaged in His service. Through the study of devotional scriptures, great joy increased in his mind, and all his desires were fulfilled. 

By his Guru’s permission, he left Vraja and entered the land of Gauḍa. By the grace of his Master, he traveled to the homes of devotees in Navadvīpa and Jagannātha Purī. 

What a sweet tradition he established in the village of Khetari! He served Lord Gaura, Rādhā-ramaṇa, Śrī Vallabhīkānta, Rādhākānta, Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, and Śrī Vrajamohana. 

These six Deities seemed to be directly performing Their pastimes. Who would not be enchanted by such beauty? With his dear companion Rāmacandra, Narottama floats in the waves of the mellows of divine love. 

O Lord Gaurāṅga! O Vallabhīkānta! O Lord Kṛṣṇa! O Vrajamohana! O Rādhā-ramaṇa! O Rādhā! O Rādhākānta! I offer my obeisances unto You. 

Who can describe all the qualities of Narottama? His congregational chanting is like a shower of divine love. Advaita Ācārya, Lord Nityānanda, and Lord Gaura-candra with Their associates all dance in his kīrtana—the fortunate ones witnessed this. 

Narottama is supremely dear to the associates of Lord Gaura and is of great wisdom. His fame resounds in the service of the devotees. What an astonishingly merciful soul! To whom does he not give the spotless jewel of pure devotion? 

Even the atheistic and demoniac persons he intoxicated with the qualities of Lord Gaura, overwhelmed with ecstatic love. His supernatural activities are unique; his fame is proclaimed in every land. 

The lowly Narahari says: “Will such a day ever come when I will be completely surrendered at the feet of Narottama? Raising both arms repeatedly and crying out “O Master Narottama!”, will I weep and roll in the dust?”

IDX.en_translation:
O Holy Name, Your glories are boundless. I repeatedly offer my obeisances at Your feet. 

You are the great festival and the ocean of bliss for Gokula. I fall at Your feet, full of longing. 

You are Kṛṣṇa in Your complete form, the source of all spiritual mellows. Falling at Your feet, I sing Your qualities. 

Whoever takes exclusive shelter at Your feet, You certainly destroy their many miseries. 

You destroy all their offenses, and You even eradicate offenses to the Holy Name. 

Washing away all faults from their heart, You sit on the throne of their heart, O supreme refuge. 

You are supremely enchanting, the embodied form of concentrated spiritual bliss. The Vedas sing Your praises, proclaiming You to be the very essence of rasa. 

Bhaktivinoda, at the feet of Rūpa Gosvāmī, always prays for the clear manifestation of the Holy Name at every moment.

O Lord of love! O Lord Gaura-candra! How shall I express the anguish of my soul, O Lord? I have lost my very self. 

What more can I say? I have forgotten the very purpose for which You brought me into this world. To speak of it now, after so long, fills me with regret and sorrow. 

No attachment for Your worship has arisen in me; my evil mind is always intoxicated by material illusion. By staying near materialistic people repeatedly, I have become like them. 

Who am I? Why have I come here? I never think about these things. Sometimes enjoying and sometimes renouncing, my mind only dances in deception. 

What will be my fate? I never consider it, nor do I seek the company of Your devotees. All the inauspicious signs of one who is averse to the Lord are present within me. 

By the mercy of my spiritual master, the dream is broken. Now I understand that only You are my own; Your devotees are my only true friends in this prison house of material existence. 

I shall not worship anyone but Your devotees; I take refuge in Your lotus feet. Deliver me, O Lord, from the net of illusion by grabbing this servant by the hair! 

Do You not show mercy even to sinners? Jagāi and Mādhāi were great sinners, yet I have learned that You, the Lord of love, deliver even such as them. 

I am devoid of devotion, fallen and insignificant. Please place Your two feet on the head of this offender. At Your fearless feet I take refuge forever.

O revered Vaiṣnava Ṭhākura! O ocean of mercy! Please be merciful to me, your humble servant. Purify me by giving the shade of your lotus feet. Your feet I clasp submissively. 

Please help me to control the six urges <footnote>(speech, mind, anger, tongue, belly, and genitals)</footnote>, purify me of the six faults <footnote>(overeating or collecting more funds than required, over-endeavoring for material objectives, unnecessarily talking of mundane affairs, being too attached or too neglectful of scriptural rules and regulations, associating with worldly minded people, and lusting after mundane achievements)</footnote>, and please instill in your servant the six good qualities <footnote>(enthusiasm, patience, confidence, determination to perform activities favorable to devotional service, the resolution to abandon the association of non-devotees, and the discipline required to always follow in the footsteps of predecessor ācāryas)</footnote>. Oh, bestow upon me the six kinds of holy association! <footnote>(giving and receiving gifts, accepting and offering spiritual food, revealing one’s inner thoughts, and posing confidential questions regarding devotional service)</footnote> I am seated here in the hope of having your company. 

On my own, I find I have no strength to chant the holy name of Lord Hari. Please be merciful by awarding me with a particle of faith and giving me the great treasure of the holy name of Kṛṣṇa. 

Kṛṣṇa is yours, therefore you are able to give Him to others. This is certainly within your power. I am indeed wretched and fallen, simply running after you crying “Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa!”

pāpa-paṅke nimagno‛smi trāhi māṁ madhusūdana 

mohito‛jñāna-tamasā putra-dāra gṛhādiṣu 
tṛṣṇayā pīḍyamāno‛smi trāhi māṁ madhusūdana!

dvādaśārṇat mahāstotraṁ sarva-kāma-phala-pradaṁ 
garbhavāsa-nirāsāya śukena paribhāṣitaṁ 

dvādaśārṇaṁ nirāhāro jaḥ paṭhet harivāsare 
sa gacched vaiṣṇavaṁ dhāma jatra jogeśvara hariḥ

IDX.en_translation:
By the utterance of “Om”, the sleep of illusion flees far away. O Lord of the Universe! I am seized by that. Save me, O Madhusūdana! 

There is no other goal, O Lord! You alone are my shelter. I am drowned in the mud of sin. Save me, O Madhusūdana! 

Bewildered by the darkness of ignorance, absorbed in son, wife, home, etc., I am tormented by thirst. Save me, O Madhusūdana! 

Devoid of devotion and destitute, afflicted with misery and grief, O Lord! Shelterless and helpless, save me, O Madhusūdana! 

I am exhausted by coming and going on the long paths of material existence. I do not wish to come again. Save me, O Madhusūdana! 

Many doors of the womb have been seen by me, one by one. From the great misery of residence in the womb, save me, O Madhusūdana! 

Therefore, O God! I am surrendered, devoted to You for the sake of deliverance. I am drowned in the ocean of misery. Save me, O Madhusūdana! 

Whatever was promised by speech was not accomplished by action. I am drowned in that ocean of sin. Save me, O Madhusūdana! 

No pious deed was done by me, but sin was done. I am drowned in the ocean of material existence. Save me, O Madhusūdana! 

Obtained by me wandering in thousands of other bodies—animal-ness and human-ness—save me, O Madhusūdana! 

I speak like a madman, I prattle before You. I am afraid of old age and death. Save me, O Madhusūdana! 

Wherever I have been born, among women or among men, give me unalloyed devotion there. Save me, O Madhusūdana! 

Having gone, having gone, the moon, sun, and other planets return. Those who think of the Twelve Syllables never return. 

There are many Stotras granting desired objects indeed. There is nothing superior to the Twelve Syllables spoken by Vāsudeva. 

The great Stotra of the Twelve Syllables, bestowing the fruit of all desires, was spoken by Śuka for the removal of residence in the womb. 

He who recites the Twelve Syllables without food on the day of Hari goes to the abode of Viṣṇu where Hari, the Lord of Yoga, is. 

Thus ends the Śrī Madhusūdana Stotra composed by Śrīla Śukadeva Gosvāmī.

O brothers! Lord Kṛṣṇa is the only friend of these three worlds. The individual soul is bound by its own past actions and is fallen into illusion and blinded. He is an ocean of mercy to deliver us. 

The Lord has surrendered all His own potencies and qualities to His Name; there is no consideration of more or less. There is no difference between the Name and the Lord Himself; by the qualities of the Name we obtain the Lord, for the Name easily delivers us. 

There is no consideration of time or place for it, nor of purity or impurity; there is no prohibition in chanting the Name. Alas! What is my misfortune! At the feet of such a merciful Lord, no attachment has arisen in me. 

O my mind! I fall at your feet—abandoning all useless endeavors, chant “Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa!” constantly. This is very easily obtained; if you develop love for the Name, then you will experience true divine love and bliss.

O my mind! Will such a birth ever happen again? I do not know by what great piety you obtained this excellent human birth, but you have negligently failed to understand its true purpose. 

Observe that half of your life is spent in sleep, and a fourth is lost to disease, sorrow, and useless talk. Another fourth is consumed by the pursuit of learning, wealth, and honor, or lost to lust, anger, and evil desires. Thus, it passes in vain. 

In previous ages, life was very long and death did not come prematurely. Much effort was made then to perform the duties of the age through meditation, sacrifice, and worship. 

But in the Age of Kali, life is short—perhaps a hundred years, and even that is not certain. Still, you waste it in useless activities. What will you say, and with what shame, when the God of Death questions you? 

This Age of Kali is so beneficial because one can simply chant “Hare Kṛṣṇa!” yet you have not developed love for such a Name. Premānanda says: “The cycle of eight million four hundred thousand species will make you wander through endless misfortune.”

O my mind! Reflect deeply and understand your situation. The ones for whom you grieve, wandering everywhere—how will those people ever give you true happiness? 

As long as you have strength and provide wealth, they are with you. But when that usefulness is gone, if you call, they won’t even listen, brother; they won’t even inquire about you when they see you are helpless. 

Seeing your plight, they will laugh, and your good words will seem bitter to them. With a crooked face and an upturned nose, they won’t even give you food when you are hungry, and they will add harsh words, saying: “What a nuisance this person has become!” 

Day by day, their affection for you will wane. What good are family members then? Do not rely on them. Those who once stood with folded hands will now speak harshly, saying: “Who is your friend at this time, O brother?” 

Treating others as your own, you have wasted your entire life. Who are you, and who truly belongs to you? Premānanda says: “Without Lord Kṛṣṇa, there is no refuge. Say “Kṛṣṇa!” and you will overcome this sorrow.”

O my mind! Wealth, family, life, and youth—they are here one moment and gone the next. Do you not see this with your own eyes? How then can you call them your own?

Whatever life you have is merely the breath in your nostrils. Once it leaves, it is no more. Whether you are old or young, there is no fixed time for death. Where then remains the pride of youth? 

All of this is the illusion of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Why do you forget Him, O brother? By His Name, the three worlds are delivered. Premānanda says: “If you chant the Name of Kṛṣṇa constantly, then how can you ever really die?”

tāra mājhe raha anukṣaṇa
