IDX.verses:
śrī-rudra uvāca: 
jitaṁ ta ātmavid-varya-svastaye svastirastu me 
bhabatārādhasā rāddhaṁ sarvasmā ātmane namaḥ 

namaḥ paṅkaja-nābhāya bhūta-sūkṣmendriyātmane 
vāsudevāya śāntāya kūṭasthāya svarociṣe 

saṅkarṣaṇāya sūkṣmāya durantāyāntakāya ca 
namo viśva-prabodhāya pradyumnāyāntarātmane 

namo namo‛niruddhāya hṛṣīkeśendriyātmane 
namaḥ parama-haṁsāya pūrṇāya nibhṛtātmane 

svargāpavarga-dvārāya nityaṁ śuciṣade namaḥ 
namo hiraṇya-vīryāya cāturhotrāya tantave 

nama ūrja iṣe trayyāḥ pataye jajña-retase 
tṛptidāya ca jīvānāṁ namaḥ sarva-rasātmane 

sarva-sattvātma-dehāya viśeṣāya sthavīyase 
namastrailokya-pālāya saha ojo-balāya ca 

artha-liṅgāya nabhase namo‛ntarbahirātmane 
namaḥ puṇyāya lokāya amusmai bhūrivarcase 

pravṛttāya nivṛttāya pitṛ-devāya karmaṇe 
namo‛dharma-vipākāya mṛtyave duḥkhadāya ca 

namasta āśīṣāmīśa manave kāraṇātmane 
namo dharmāya bṛhate kṛṣṇāyākuṇṭha-medhase 
puruṣāya purāṇāya sāṅkhya-yogeśvarāya ca 

śakti-traya-sametāya mīḍhuṣe‛haṅkṛtātmane 
ceta-ākṛti-rūpāya namo vāco vibhūtaye 

darśanaṁ no didṛkṣūṇāṁ dehi bhāgavatārcitam 
rūpaṁ priyatamaṁ svānāṁ sarvendriya-guṇaañjanam 

snigdha-prāvṛḍghana-śyāmaṁ sarva-saundarya-saṁgraham 
cārvāyata-caturbāhu sujāta-rucirānanam 
padma-kośa-palāśākṣaṁ sundara-bhru sunāsikam 
sudvijaṁ sukapolāsyaṁ sama-karṇa-vibhūṣaṇam 

prīti-prahasitāpāṅgamalakai rūpa-śobhitam 
lasat-paṅkaja-kiñjalka-dukūlaṁ mṛṣṭa-kuṇḍalam 
sphurat-kirīṭa-valaya-hāra-nūpura-mekhalam 
śaṅkha-cakra-gadā-padma-mālā-maṇyuttamardhimat 

siṁha-skandha-tviṣo bibhratsaubhaga-grīva-kaustubham 
śriyānapāyinyā kṣipta-nikaṣāśmorasollasat 

pūra-recaka-saṁvigna-bali-valgudalodaram 
pratisaṁkrāmayadviśvaṁ nābhyāvarta-gabhīrayā 

śyāma-śroṇyadhirociṣṇu-dukūla-svarṇa-mekhalam 
sama-cārvaṅghri-jaṅghoru-nimna-jānu-sudarśanam 

padā śarat-padma-palāśa-rociṣā 
nakha-dyubhirno‛ntaraghaṁ vidhunvatā 
pradarśaya svīyamapāsta-sādhvasaṁ 
padaṁ guro mārga-gurustamojuṣām 

etad-rūpamanudhyeyamātma-śuddhimabhīpsatām 
jad-bhakti-yogo‛bhayadaḥ svadharmamanutiṣṭhatām 

bhabān bhakti-matā labhyo durlabhaḥ sarva-dehinām 
svārājyasyāpyabhimata ekāntenātmavid-gatiḥ 

taṁ durārādhyamārādhya satāmapi durāpayā 
ekānta-bhaktyā ko vāñchet-pāda-mūlaṁ vinā bahiḥ 

jatra niviṣṭa-maraṇaṁ kṛtānto nābhimanyate 
viśvaṁ vidhvaṁsayan vīrya-śaurya-visphūrjita-bhruvā 

kṣaṇārdhenāpi tulaye na svargaṁ nāpunarbhavam 
bhagavat-saṅgi-saṅgasya martyānāṁ kimutāśīṣaḥ 

athānaghāṅghrestava kīrti-tīrthayo- 
rantarbahiḥ-snāna-vidhūta-pāpmanām 
bhūteṣbanukrośa-susattva-śīlināṁ 
syāt-saṅgamo‛nugraha eṣa nastava 

na jasya cittaṁ bahirartha-vibhramaṁ 
tamoguhāyāṁ ca viśuddhamāviśat 
jad-bhakti-yogānugṛhītamañjasā 
munirrvicaṣṭe nanu tatra te gatim 

jatredaṁ vyajyate viśvaṁ viśvasminnavabhāti jat 
tat tvaṁ brahma paraṁ jyotirākāśamiva vistṛtam 

jo māyayedaṁ puru-rūpayāsṛjad 
bibharti bhūyaḥ kṣapayatyavikriyaḥ 
jad-bhadra-buddhiḥ sadivātmaduḥsthayā 
tvamātma-tantraṁ bhagavan pratīmahi 

kriyā-kalāpairidameva joginaḥ 
śraddhānvitāḥ sādhu jajanti siddhaye 
bhūtendriyā antaḥkaraṇopalakṣitaṁ 
vede ca tantre ca ta eva kovidāḥ 

tvameka ādyaḥ puruṣaḥ supta-śakti- 
stayā rajaḥ-sattva-tamo vibhidyate 
mahānahaṁ khaṁ marudgnibārdharāḥ 
surarṣayo bhūta-gaṇā idaṁ jataḥ 

sṛṣṭaṁ sva-śaktyedamanupraviṣṭa- 
ścacaturvidhaṁ puramātmāṁśakena 
atho vidustaṁ puruṣaṁ santamanta- 
rbhṛṅkte hṛṣīkairmadhu sāraghaṁ jaḥ 

sa eṣa lokānaticaṇḍa-vego 
vikarṣasi tvaṁ khalu kālayānaḥ 
bhūtāni bhūtairanumeya-tattvo 
ghanāvalī-vāyurivaaviṣahyaḥ 

pravṛddhamuccairiti kṛtya-cintayā 
pravṛddha-lobhaṁ viṣayeṣu lālasam 
tvamapramattaḥ sahasābhipadyase 
kṣullelihāno‛hirivākṣumantakaḥ 

kastvat-padābjaṁ vijahāti paṇḍito 
jaste‛vamāna-vyayamāna-ketanaḥ 
viśaṅkayāsmada-gururarcati sma jad 
vinopapattiṁ manavaścaturdaśa 

atha tvamasi no brahman paramātman vipaścitām 
viśvaṁ rudra-bhaya-dhvastamakutaścidbhayā gatiḥ 

idaṁ japata bhadraṁ vo viśuddhā nṛpa-nandanāḥ 
svadharmamanutiṣṭhanto bhagavatyarpitāśayāḥ 

tamevātmānamātmasthaṁ sarva-bhūteṣvavasthitam 
pūjayadhvaṁ gṛṇantaśca dhyāyantaścāsakṛddharim 

jogādeśamupāsādya dhārayanto muni-vratāḥ 
samāhita-dhiyaḥ sarva etadabhyasatādṛtāḥ 

idamāha purāsmākaṁ bhagavān viśvasṛkpatiḥ 
bhṛgbādīnāmātmajānāṁ sisṛkṣuḥ saṁsisṛkṣatām 

te vayaṁ noditāḥ sarve prajā-sarge prajeśvarāḥ 
anena dhvasta-tamasaḥ sisṛkṣmo vividhāḥ prajāḥ 

athaidaṁ nityadā jukto japannavahitaḥ pumān 
acirācchreya āpnoti vāsudeva-parāyaṇaḥ 

śreyasāmiha sarveṣāṁ jñānaṁ niḥśreyasaṁ param 
sukhaṁ tarati duṣpāraṁ jñāna-naur-vyasanārṇavam 

ja imaṁ śraddhayā jukto mad-gītaṁ bhagavat-stavam 
adhīyāno durārādhyaṁ harimārādhayatyasau 

vindate puruṣo‛musmād jad jadicchatyasatvaram 
mad-gīta-gītāt-suprītāt śreyasāmeka-vallabhāt 

idaṁ jaḥ kalya utthāya prāñjaliḥ śraddhayāmvitaḥ 
śṛṇuyācchrāvayenmartyo mucyate karma-bandhanaiḥ 

gītaṁ mayedaṁ naradeva-nandanāḥ 
parasya puṁsaḥ paramātmanaḥ stavam 
japanta ekāgra-dhiyastapo mahat 
caradhvamante tata āpsyathepsitam
IDX.en_translation:
Śrī Rudra said: O Best of the Self-Realized! Victory to You! O Self of all, let there be auspiciousness for me. I offer my obeisances to You, who are served by You. 

Obeisances to the Lotus-naveled One, the Soul of the subtle elements and senses. To Vāsudeva, the peaceful, the unchanging, the self-effulgent. 

To Saṅkarṣaṇa, the subtle, the endless, and the destroyer. Obeisances to the awakener of the universe, Pradyumna, the inner soul. 

Obeisances, obeisances to Aniruddha, the Master of the senses, the Soul of the senses. Obeisances to the Paramahaṁsa, the Full, the concealed Soul. 

Obeisances to Him who is the door to heaven and liberation, who always dwells in the pure heart. Obeisances to Hiraṇya-vīrya, the expander of the Cātur-hotra sacrifice. 

Obeisances to Ūrja (strength), Iṣa (food), the Lord of the three Vedas, the source of sacrifice. To the giver of satisfaction to the jīvas, obeisances to the Soul of all rasas. 

To Him whose body is all-existence, the Specific, the Grossest. Obeisances to the Protector of the three worlds, along with Ojas (vitality) and Bala (strength). 

To the Meaning-gendered, the Sky, obeisances to the Inner and Outer Soul. Obeisances to the Pious World, to that One of great splendor. 

To the active, the renounced, the Worshipable Deity of the forefathers, to Karma. Obeisances to the result of irreligion, to Death, and to the giver of misery. 

Obeisances to You, the Lord of benedictions, to Manu, to the Causal Soul. Obeisances to Dharma, the Great, to Kṛṣṇa of stunted intelligence. To the Person, the Ancient, the Lord of Sāṅkhya and Yoga. 

To Him endowed with the three energies, to the Showerer, to the Ego-soul. To the form of Consciousness, obeisances to the manifestation of Speech. 

Give us, who are eager to see, the vision worshipped by the devotees. The form most dear to Your own, the collyrium for all the senses and qualities. 

Dark like a glistening raincloud, the reservoir of all beauty. With four beautiful long arms, and a well-formed, charming face. Eyes like lotus petals, beautiful eyebrows, beautiful nose. Beautiful teeth, beautiful cheeks and face, adorned with equal earrings. 

Beautified by sidelong glances laughing with love and by locks of hair. With a garment like the filaments of a shining lotus, and polished earrings. With shining crown, bracelets, necklaces, anklets, and girdle. Endowed with the excellent opulence of conch, disc, club, lotus, garland, and jewels. 

Bearing the Kaustubha on a beautiful neck, with the shoulders of a lion. Shining on the chest, defeating the touchstone with the never-departing Śrī (Lakṣmī). 

With an abdomen beautiful with folds agitated by breathing in and out. Deep with a navel-whirlpool that seems to draw the universe back in. 

With a golden belt on a shining cloth over dark hips. With symmetrical, beautiful feet, shins, thighs, and knees—beautiful to see. 

By Your feet, which have the luster of autumn lotus petals, and by the light of Your nails which destroys our inner sin. Show us Your own feet, which remove fear, O Guru! You are the Guru of the path for those in darkness. 

This form should be meditated upon by those desiring self-purification. Whose bhakti-yoga grants fearlessness to those performing their own duty. 

You are attainable by one who has devotion, but rare for all embodied beings. Even for the King of Heaven, the goal of the knowers of the Self is desired in solitude. 

Having worshipped Him who is difficult to worship, with unalloyed devotion rare even for the saintly. Who would desire anything outside, without the root of Your feet? 

Where death does not think to enter, absorbed. Destroying the universe with eyebrows flashing with heroism and valor. 

I do not weigh heaven or liberation against even half a moment of the association of those attached to the Lord. What to speak of the benedictions of mortals? 

Therefore, let us have the association of those whose sins have been washed away by bathing internally and externally in the holy rivers of Your glories and Your sinless feet. Who are endowed with compassion and good character towards living beings. This is Your mercy upon us. 

Whose mind, bewildered by external objects, does not enter the cave of darkness, being purified. By whose bhakti-yoga, graced easily, the sage sees Your path there. 

Where this universe is manifested, which shines in the universe. You are that Brahman, the Supreme Light, expanded like the sky. 

Who created this with the Maya of many forms, maintains it again, and destroys it, being unchanging. By whom the intelligence is different, as if existing, due to the bad state of the self. We understand You, the Lord, to be independent. 

With these activities, the yogis endowed with faith worship this very thing perfectly for perfection. Characterized by the elements, senses, and inner instrument, in the Veda and Tantra, they alone are the knowers. 

You are the One, the Original Person, whose energy is asleep. By that, passion, goodness, and ignorance are divided. From whom came this: the Mahat, the Ego, the Sky, Air, Fire, Water, Earth, the Suras, Sages, and hosts of beings. 

Created by Your own energy, having entered this fourfold city with a portion of Yourself. Then they know that Person to be existing within, who enjoys the honey made by bees with the senses. 

He, this one, of very fierce speed, You pull the worlds, driving Time. Beings by beings, the Truth inferred, like the wind the clouds, unbearable. 

Thinking loudly “This is to be done,” greedy, lusty for objects. You, always alert, suddenly seize the madman, like a hungry snake a mouse licking its lips. 

What learned person abandons Your lotus feet, when You remove the banner of disrespect? Out of fear, our Guru worshiped, without argument, the fourteen Manus. 

Now You are ours, O Brahman, O Supreme Soul of the wise! The universe is destroyed by the fear of Rudra; You are the destination of the fearless. 

Chant this, may it be well with you, O pure sons of the King! Performing your own duty, with minds offered to the Lord. 

Worship, praise, and meditate on that very Self situated in the self, situated in all beings—Hari. 

Accepting the order of yoga, observing the vow of silence, holding. With concentrated minds, all of you practice this with respect. 

This the Lord, the Master of the creators of the universe, spoke to us in the past. Desiring to create, to the sons like Bhṛgu who were desiring to create. 

We, all the Prajāpatis, urged by that in the creation of progeny. By this, our darkness destroyed, we desire to create various progeny. 

Now, a person constantly engaged in chanting this with attention. He quickly attains the ultimate good, devoted to Vāsudeva. 

Of all benedictions here, knowledge is the supreme beatitude. He crosses the ocean of misery, difficult to cross, on the boat of knowledge, happily. 

He who studies this hymn to the Lord sung by me with faith. He worships Hari, who is difficult to worship. 

A person obtains from Him whatever he desires quickly. From Him, the only beloved of benedictions, who is well-pleased by the song sung by me. 

A mortal who, rising at dawn, with folded hands and endowed with faith. Hears or causes to hear this, is released from the bondages of karma. 

This hymn of the Supreme Person, the Supreme Soul, sung by me, O sons of the King! Chanting with one-pointed minds, perform great austerity; at the end, you will obtain the desired from Him.

IDX.first_line: śrī rūpa mañjarī kabe madhura vacane
IDX.search: sri rupa manjari kabe madhura vacane radha kunda mahima varnibe samgopane e caudda bhuvanopari vaikuntha nilaya tada peksa mathura parama srestha haya
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
śrī-rūpa mañjarī kabe madhura vacane 
rādhā-kuṇḍa-mahimā varṇibe saṁgopane 

e caudda bhuvanopari vaikuṇṭha nilaya 
tada-pekṣā mathurā parama śreṣṭha haya 

māthuramaṇḍale rāsalīlā sthāna jathā 
vṛndāvana śreṣṭha ati śuna mama kathā 

kṛṣṇalīlā-sthala govardhana śreṣṭhatara 
rādhā-kuṇḍa śreṣṭhatama sarva-śakti-dhara 

rādhā-kuṇḍa-mahimā ta’ kariyā śravaṇa 
lālāyita ha’ye āmi paḍiba takhana 

sakhīra caraṇe kabe kariba ākuti 
sakhī kṛpā kari’ dibe svārasikī sthiti
IDX.en_translation:
When will Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī, with sweet words, describe the glories of Rādhā-kuṇḍa to me in a secret place? 

Above the fourteen planetary systems lies the spiritual abode of Vaikuṇṭha. Yet, Mathurā is far superior to that. 

Within the district of Mathurā, Vṛndāvana is the most excellent place, where the Rāsa dance takes place. Please hear my words. 

Govardhana Hill, the site of Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes, is even more excellent. But Rādhā-kuṇḍa is the most excellent of all, possessing all spiritual potencies. 

Hearing the glories of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, I will fall down, overcome with great longing. 

When will I plead at the lotus feet of the sakhīs? By their mercy, the sakhīs will grant me my eternal position in the flow of divine love.

IDX.first_line: śrī rūpa paścāte āmi rahiba bhīta hañā
IDX.search: sri rupa pascate ami rahiba bhita hana dohe punah kahibena ama pane cana sadaya hrdaye dohe kahibena hasi kothaya paile rupa ei nava dasi
IDX.author: narottama-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
śrī-rūpa-paścāte āmi rahiba bhīta hañā 
dohe punaḥ kahibena āmā pāne cāñā 

sadaya-hṛdaye dohe kahibena hāsi 
kothāya pāile rūpa! ei nava dāsī 

śrī-rūpa-mañjarī tabe dohavākya śuni 
mañjunālī dila more ei dāsī āni’ 

ati namracitta āmi ihāre jānila 
sevākārya niyā tabe hethāya rākhila 

hena tattva dohākāra sākṣāte kahiyā 
narottame sevāya dibe niyukta kariyā
IDX.en_translation:
I will remain behind Śrī Rūpa, being afraid. Both will again say, looking at me. 

Smiling with kind hearts, Both will say: “Where did you get this new maidservant, Rūpa?” 

Then Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī, hearing the words of Both: “Mañjunālī brought this maidservant and gave her to me. 

I knew her to be very humble in heart; therefore I kept her here engaged in service.” 

Speaking such truths in the presence of Both, she will engage Narottama in service.

IDX.search: sri rupa vadane sri sacikumara svanama mahima karala pracara jo nama so hari kichu nahi bheda so nama satyamiti gayati veda
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
śrī-rūpa-vadane, śrī-śacīkumāra 
svanāma-mahimā karala pracāra 

jo nāma so hari, kichu nāhi bheda 
so nāma satyamiti gāyati veda 

sabu upaniṣad, ratnamālā-dyuti, 
jhakamaki’ caraṇa-samīpe 
maṅgala-ārati, karaba anukṣaṇa, 
dviguṇita-pañcapradīpe 

cauddabhuvana māha, deva-nara-dānava, 
bhāga jākara balabān 
nāmarasa-pīyuṣa, piyoi anukṣaṇa, 
choḍata karama-geyāna 

nityamukta punaḥ, nāma-upāsanā, 
satata karoi sāmagāne 
goloke baiṭhata, gāoye nirantara, 
nāma-viraha nāhi jāne 

sabu rasa-ākara, ‘hari’ itidvyakṣara, 
sabubhāve karala āśraya 
nāmacaraṇe pa’ḍe, bhakativinoda kahe, 
tuyā pade māgahu nilaya
IDX.en_translation:
Through the mouth of Śrī Rūpa, the son of Śacī proclaimed the glories of His own Holy Name. 

That Name is Hari; there is no difference. The Vedas sing that the Name is the Truth. 

All the Upaniṣads, like the radiance of a garland of jewels, sparkle at His lotus feet. I will constantly perform auspicious worship with twice five lamps. 

In the fourteen worlds, among demigods, men, and demons, those whose fortune is strong constantly drink the nectar of the Holy Name, giving up fruitive activities and speculative knowledge. 

Eternally liberated souls worship the Holy Name, always singing in Vedic melodies. Seated in Goloka, they sing ceaselessly; they know no separation from the Holy Name. 

The two syllables “Hari”, the source of all mellows, are the shelter in all circumstances. Falling at the feet of the Holy Name, Bhaktivinoda says: “At Your feet, I beg for a dwelling.”

IDX.first_line: śrī śrī guru gaurāṅga gāndharvikā giridhārī

śrī-śrī-guru-gaurāṅga-gāndharvikā-giridhārī 
śrī-śrī-rādhā-vinoda-vihārī-jīu kī jaya, 

[ <eng>now your dīkṣā-guru’s name should be glorified</eng> ] 

jaya nitya-līlā-praviṣṭa oṁ 
viṣṇu-pāda aṣṭottara-śata- 
śrī-śrīmad-bhakti-vedānta 
nārāyaṇa gosvāmī mahārāja kī jaya, 

jaya nitya-līlā-praviṣṭa oṁ 
viṣṇu-pāda aṣṭottara-śata- 
śrī-śrīmad-bhakti-vedānta 
vāmana gosvāmī mahārāja kī jaya, 

jaya nitya-līlā-praviṣṭa oṁ 
viṣṇu-pāda aṣṭottara-śata- 
śrī-śrīmad-bhakti-prajñāna 
keśava gosvāmī mahārāja kī jaya, 

jaya nitya-līlā-praviṣṭa oṁ 
viṣṇu-pāda aṣṭottara-śata- 
śrī-śrīla bhakti-siddhānta 
sarasvatī gosvāmī prabhupāda kī jaya,

śrī-śrīla gaura-kiśora-dāsa gosvāmī mahārāja kī jaya, 

jaya nitya-līlā-praviṣṭa śrī-śrīla saccidānanda

śrīla jagannātha-dāsa bābājī mahārāja kī jaya, 

jaya samasta-rūpānugā-gauḍīya-guru-varga kī jaya, 
jaya nitya-līlā-praviṣṭa oṁ 
viṣṇu-pāda aṣṭottara-śata- 
śrī-śrīmad-bhakti-vedānta svāmī mahārāja kī jaya, 

jaya nitya-līlā-praviṣṭa oṁ 
viṣṇu-pāda aṣṭottara-śata- 
śrī-śrīmad-bhakti-vedānta 
trivikrama gosvāmī mahārāja kī jaya, 

jaya gauḍīya vedāntācārya śrīla 
baladeva vidyā-bhūṣaṇa prabhu kī jaya, 
jaya śrīla viśvanātha cakravartī ṭhākura kī jaya, 

jaya śrīla narottama-śrīnivāsa- 
śyāmānanda-prabhu-traya kī jaya, 
jaya śrīla kṛṣṇa-dāsa kavi-rāja gosvāmī prabhu kī jaya, 
jaya śrīla vṛndāvana-dāsa ṭhākura kī jaya, 

jaya śrī-rūpa, sanātana, bhaṭṭa-raghunātha, 
śrī-jīva, gopāla-bhaṭṭa, dāsa-raghunātha 
ṣaḍ-gosvāmī prabhu kī jaya, 

jaya śrī-svarūpa-dāmodara- 
rāya-rāmānandādi gaura-pārṣada-vṛnda kī jaya, 
jaya nāmācārya śrīla hari-dāsa ṭhākura kī jaya, 

premase kaho śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya- 
prabhu-nityānanda-śrī-advaita-gadādhara- 
śrīvāsādi-śrī-gaura-bhakta-vṛnda kī jaya, 

śrī-antardvīpa māyāpura, sīmantadvīpa, 
godrumadvīpa, madhyadvīpa, koladvīpa, ṛtudvīpa, 
jahnudvīpa, modadrumadvīpa, rudradvīpātmaka 
śrī-navadvīpa-dhāma kī jaya, 

śrī-śrī-rādhā-kṛṣṇa-gopa-gopī-go- 
govardhana dvādaśa-vanātmaka 
śrī-vraja-maṇḍala-dhāma kī jaya, 

śrī-rādhā-kuṇḍa-śyāma-kuṇḍa-gaṅgā- 
yamunā-tulasī-bhakti-devī kī jaya, 
śrī-jagannātha-baladeva-subhadrā-sudarśanaju kī jaya, 

śrī-gopīśvara-mahādeva kī jaya, 
śrī yoga-māyā paurṇamāsī devī kī jaya, 

śrīmatī vṛndā-devī kī jaya 
śrī-nṛsiṁha-varāha-deva kī jaya, 
bhakta-pravara śrī-prahlāda mahārāja kī jaya, 

cāri-dhāma, sampradāya, ācārya-vṛnda kī jaya, 
vraja-patana-śrī-caitanya-maṭha kī jaya, 

śrī-keśavajī gauḍīya maṭha o tat-śākhā-maṭha-samūha kī jaya, 
śrī-harināma-saṅkīrtana kī jaya, 

ananta-koṭī vaiṣṇava-vṛnda kī jaya, 
śrī-gaura-premānande hari hari bola
IDX.en_translation:
All glories to Śrī Śrī Guru, Gaurāṅga, Gāndharvikā, Giridhārī, and Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Vinoda-bihārī-jīu! 

Now your dīkṣā-guru’s name should be glorified. 

All glories to nitya-līlā-praviṣṭa Oṁ Viṣṇupāda Aṣṭottara-śata Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja! 

All glories to nitya-līlā-praviṣṭa Oṁ Viṣṇupāda Aṣṭottara-śata Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktivedānta Vāmana Gosvāmī Mahārāja! 

All glories to nitya-līlā-praviṣṭa Oṁ Viṣṇupāda Aṣṭottara-śata Śrī Śrīmad Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja! 

All glories to nitya-līlā-praviṣṭa Oṁ Viṣṇupāda Aṣṭottara-śata Śrī Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Prabhupāda! 

All glories to nitya-līlā-praviṣṭa Paramahaṁsa Bābājī Śrī Śrīla Gaura Kiśora Dāsa Gosvāmī Mahārāja! 

All glories to nitya-līlā-praviṣṭa Śrī Śrīla Saccidānanda Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura! 

All glories to nitya-līlā-praviṣṭa Vaiṣṇava-sārvabhauma Śrīla Jagannātha Dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja! 

All glories to the entire Rūpānuga Gauḍīya Guru-varga! All glories to nitya-līlā-praviṣṭa Oṁ Viṣṇupāda Aṣṭottara-śata Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktivedānta Svāmī Mahārāja! 

All glories to nitya-līlā-praviṣṭa Oṁ Viṣṇupāda Aṣṭottara-śata Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktivedānta Trivikrama Gosvāmī Mahārāja! 

All glories to Gauḍīya Vedāntācārya Śrīla Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa Prabhu! All glories to Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura! 

All glories to the three Lords: Śrīla Narottama, Śrīnivāsa, and Śyāmānanda! All glories to Śrīla Kṛṣṇa-dāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī Prabhu! All glories to Śrīla Vṛndāvana Dāsa Ṭhākura! 

All glories to the Six Gosvāmīs: Śrī Rūpa, Sanātana, Bhaṭṭa Raghunātha, Śrī Jīva, Gopāla Bhaṭṭa, and Dāsa Raghunātha! 

All glories to the associates of Gaura, including Śrī Svarūpa Dāmodara and Rāya Rāmānanda! All glories to Nāmācārya Śrīla Haridāsa Ṭhākura! 

Say with love: All glories to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, Prabhu Nityānanda, Śrī Advaita, Gadādhara, Śrīvāsa, and all the devotees of Gaura! 

All glories to Śrī Navadvīpa-dhāma, which consists of Antardvīpa (Māyāpura), Sīmantadvīpa, Godrumadvīpa, Madhyadvīpa, Koladvīpa, Ṛtudvīpa, Jahnudvīpa, Modadrumadvīpa, and Rudradvīpa! 

All glories to Śrī Vraja-maṇḍala-dhāma, consisting of the twelve forests, Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, the cowherd boys and girls, the cows, and Govardhana Hill! 

All glories to Śrī Rādhā-kuṇḍa, Śyāma-kuṇḍa, Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Tulasī, and Bhakti-devī! All glories to Śrī Jagannātha, Baladeva, Subhadrā, and Sudarśana-jīu! 

All glories to Śrī Gopīśvara Mahādeva! All glories to Śrī Yogamāyā Paurṇamāsī Devī! 

All glories to Śrīmatī Vṛndā Devī! All glories to Śrī Nṛsiṁha and Varāhadeva! All glories to the best of devotees, Śrī Prahlāda Mahārāja! 

All glories to the four Dhāmas, the four Sampradāyas, and the Ācāryas! All glories to Vrajapaṭṭana Śrī Caitanya Maṭha! 

All glories to Śrī Keśavajī Gauḍīya Maṭha and all its branch Maṭhas! All glories to Śrī Harināma-saṅkīrtana! 

All glories to the unlimited millions of Vaiṣṇavas! Chant “Hari! Hari!” in the bliss of Gaura-prema!

IDX.search: sri ujjvala rasasara svabhavatah dviprakara vipralambha sambhoga akhyana vina vipralambhasraya sambhogera pusti naya tai vipralambhera vidhana purva raga tatha mana pravasa vaicittyajnana vipralambha cari ta prakara sangamera purvariti labhe purva raga khyati darsane sravane janma tara

IDX.verses:
śrī-ujjvala rasasāra, svabhāvataḥ dviprakāra, 
‘vipralambha’ ‘sambhoga’ ākhyāna 
vinā vipralambhāśraya, sambhogera puṣṭi naya, 
tāi vipralambhera vidhāna 

‘pūrva-rāga’ tathā ‘māna’, ‘pravāsa’, ‘vaicittya’jñāna, 
vipralambha cāri ta’ prakāra 
saṅgamera pūrvarīti, labhe ‘pūrva-rāga’-khyāti, 
darśane śravaṇe janma tā’ra 

anurakta dampatira, abhīṣṭa āśleṣa, sthira-, 
darśana-virodhī bhāva ‘māna’ 
‘sa-hetu’ ‘nirhetu’ māna, praṇayera pariṇāma, 
praṇayera vilāsa pramāṇa 

sāma, bhedakriyā, dāne, natyupekṣā-suvidhāne, 
sahetu-mānera upaśama 
deśa, kāla, veṇu-rave, nirhetuka mānotsave, 
kare atiśīghra uparama 

viccheda-āśaṅkā haite, premera ‘vaicittya’ citte, 
premera svabhāve upajaya 
deśa, grāma, vanāntare, priya je pravāsa kare, 
‘pravāsa’ ākhya vipralambha haya
IDX.en_translation:
The essence of the brilliant transcendental mellow is naturally of two types: separation and union. Without the foundation of separation, union cannot be fully nourished; therefore, separation is a necessary arrangement. 

Prior attraction, transcendental pique, separation due to dwelling elsewhere, and the feeling of novelty despite constant union—these are the four types of separation. The preliminary stage before union attains the renown of “prior attraction”; it is born from seeing and hearing. 

For loving couples, the desired embrace, though steady, is opposed by the sentiment of pique. Pique with a cause and pique without a cause are both outcomes of pure affection; they are evidence of love’s delightful pastimes. 

By means of conciliation, creating a division of interest, giving gifts, and feigned neglect—through these well-arranged methods, pique with a cause is pacified. By considering the place, the time, and the sound of the flute, the festival of causeless pique very quickly comes to an end. 

From the apprehension of separation, a feeling of novelty naturally arises from the very nature of love. When the beloved departs for another country, village, or forest, that is the separation known as “absence.”

nara-mātraṁ tārayet kṛṣṇa-nāma śrī-hari-bhakti-vilāsa śrī-śrī-jagannātha-deva-vandanā mahāmbhodhes tīre kanaka-rucire nīla-śikhare vasan prasādāntaḥ sahaja-bala-bhadreṇa balinā subhadrā-madhyasthaḥ sakala-sura-sevā-vasarado- jagannāthaḥ svāmī nayana-pathagāmī bhavatu me śrī-śrī-jagannāthāṣṭakama nīlācala-nivāsāya nityāya paramātmane balabhadra-subhadrābhyāṁ jagannāthāya te namaḥ śrī-śrī-nṛsiṁha-deva-vandanā namaste narasiṁhāya prahlādāhlāda-dāyine hiraṇyakaśipor-vakṣaḥ śilā-ṭaṅka-nakhālaye śrī-nṛsiṁha-purāṇa ito nṛsiṁhaḥ parato nṛsiṁho jato jato jāmi tato nṛsiṁhaḥ bahir-nṛsiṁho hṛdaye nṛsiṁho nṛsiṁham-ādiṁ śaraṇaṁ prapadye śrī-nṛsiṁha-purāṇa śrī-nṛsiṁha, jaya nṛsiṁha, jaya jaya nṛsiṁha prahlādeśa jaya padmā-mukha-padma-bhṛṅga vāgīśā jasya vadane lakṣmīr-yasya ca vakṣasi jasyāste hṛdaye saṁvit taṁ nṛsiṁham-ahaṁ bhaje prahlāda-hṛdayā-hlādaṁ bhaktāvidyā-vidāraṇam śarad-indu-ruciṁ vande pārīndra-vadanaṁ harim śrī-bhāvārtha-dīpikā śrī-śrī-rāmacandra-vandanā nīlāmbuja-śyāmala-komalāṅgaṁ sītā-samāropita-vāma-bhāgam pāṇau mahāsāyaka-cārucāpaṁ namāmi rāmaṁ raghu-vaṁśa-nātham śrī-rāma-carita-mānasa dakṣiṇe lakṣmaṇo dhanvī vāmato jānakī śubhā purato mārutīr jasya taṁ namāmi raghūtamam śrī-śrī-daśāvatāra-vandanā vedān uddharate jaganti vahate bhū-golam udvibrate daityān dārayate baliṁ chalayate kṣatra-kṣayaṁ kurvate paulastyaṁ jayate halaṁ kalayate kāruṇyam-ātanvate mlecchān-mūrchayate daśākṛti-kṛte kṛṣṇāya tubhyaṁ namaḥ śrī-gīta-govindama
IDX.en_translation: śrī-yamunā-snāna-vandanā O Kalinda-tanayā! O Devī! O increaser of supreme bliss! I bathe in your waters; please liberate me from all offenses. śrī-rādhā-kuṇḍa-snāna-vandanā Possessing good fortune equal to Rādhikā, worshipped by all tīrthas. Be pleased, O Rādhikā-kuṇḍa! I bathe in your auspicious waters. śrī-śyāma-kuṇḍa-snāna-vandanā Manifested from the lotus foot of Kṛṣṇa on the pretext of killing Ariṣṭa. Protect me, a fallen soul; I bathe in your waters, O Śyāma-kuṇḍa! śrī-paurṇamāsī-vandanā Expert in arranging the various playful pastimes of the master of Rādhā, whose lotus feet are worshipped by Vraja. Worshipped by the entire universe for her mercy and other qualities. I bow my head to Śrī Paurṇamāsī. śrī-vṛndā-devī-vandanā O protectress of the moving and non-moving living entities of Vṛndāvana! O Vṛndā! By the good fortune of those two Rasikas, you are wealthy. Please grant mercy so that I may be counted among the attendants of Śrī Rādhikā. Devoid of devotion, tossed by hundreds of thousands of offenses into the waves of lust and other vices. O merciful one! I have taken shelter of you. O Vṛndā, I bow to your lotus feet. śrī-vraja-vāsi-vṛnda-vandanā Where Brahmā joyfully desires birth among the grass and bushes, always daily offering various activities. Those dear people who reside there in the land of Vraja are worshipable by me with supreme humility; they are inlaid with piety. śrī-gopīśvara-śiva-vandanā O master of the land of Vṛndāvana, glories to you, O Soma, O Soma-maule! Worshipped by Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanātana, and Nārada. O Gopīśvara, O enjoyer of Vraja, please bestow unconditional prema at your two lotus feet. Obeisances, obeisances unto you. śrī-tulasī-vandanā Mother of Mahā-prasāda, increaser of all good fortune. Remover of mental and physical diseases eternally, O Tulasī! Obeisances unto you. śrī-gaṅgā-vandanā The vessel of the Lord’s pastimes, whose body is nectarean rasa, whose greatness is loudly proclaimed by the assembly of sages, Śiva, Brahmā, and Indra. Filled with great mercy, I worship Gaṅgā, whose drops of water destroy the multitude of sins. śrī-vedavyāsa-deva-vandanā Whose father is Parāśara and who is the father of Śukadeva. I worship that Vyāsa, who resides in Badarī, Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana. śrī-śukadeva-vandanā Whom, leaving home without undergoing ceremonies, having no duties, Dvaipāyana called out “O Son!”, agitated by separation, and absorbed in him, the trees responded. I bow to that Muni who is the heart of all beings. Who spoke this essence of all scriptures, the unique lamp of knowledge for those desiring to cross the blinding darkness. Who spoke the confidential Purāṇa out of compassion for materialistic people. I surrender to that son of Vyāsa, the guru of munis. śrīmad-bhāgavata-vandanā That primeval Lord, the abode of mercy, the color of a Tamāla tree, the most beneficial incarnation. The bridge over the boundless ocean of material existence. We worship the Śrīmad Bhāgavatam. śrī-śrī-nāma-vandanā Glories, glories to the blissful form of the name of Murāri, which causes one to give up efforts in prescribed duties, meditation, and pūjā. Which, if taken even once somehow or other, bestows liberation to living entities. My supreme nectar, my only life and ornament. Sweeter than sweet, the most auspicious of auspicious things, the excellent fruit of the creeper of all Vedas, conscious by nature. Chanted even once, with faith or with negligence, O best of the Bhṛgus! The name of Kṛṣṇa delivers any human being. śrī-śrī-jagannātha-deva-vandanā On the shore of the great ocean, on the blue summit shining like gold. Residing inside the palace with his brother Balabhadra. Between them is Subhadrā; giving opportunity for service to all suras. May that Jagannātha Svāmī be visible to my eyes. To the resident of Nīlācala, the eternal Paramātmā. To Balabhadra and Subhadrā, and to you Jagannātha, obeisances. śrī-śrī-nṛsiṁha-deva-vandanā Obeisances to Narasiṁha, who gives joy to Prahlāda. Whose nails are like chisels on the stone-like chest of Hiraṇyakaśipu. Narasiṁha is here, Narasiṁha is there. Wherever I go, there is Narasiṁha. Narasiṁha is outside, Narasiṁha is in the heart. I take shelter of Narasiṁha, the origin. Śrī Narasiṁha, glories to Narasiṁha, glories glories to Narasiṁha. Lord of Prahlāda, glory to the bee of the lotus face of Padmā. On whose face is Vāgīśā, on whose chest is Lakṣmī. In whose heart is knowledge, I worship that Narasiṁha. The joy of Prahlāda’s heart, the destroyer of the devotees’ ignorance. Resplendent like the autumn moon, I bow to the lion-faced Hari. śrī-śrī-rāmacandra-vandanā Whose limbs are soft and dark like a blue lotus, with Sītā seated on his left side. Holding a great arrow and beautiful bow in his hands, I bow to Rāma, the lord of the Raghu dynasty. On the right is Lakṣmaṇa holding a bow, on the left is the auspicious Jānakī. In front is Mārutī, I bow to that best of the Raghus. śrī-śrī-daśāvatāra-vandanā You deliver the Vedas, support the worlds, lift the earth, tear apart the demon, deceive Bali, destroy the warrior class, conquer Paulastya, hold the plow, extend mercy, and bewilder the mlecchas. I offer obeisances to You, Kṛṣṇa, who assume these ten forms.

IDX.first_line: śrīdāma bale ogo rāṇī vidāya de tora nīlamaṇi
IDX.search: sridama bale ogo rani vidaya de tora nilamani laye jaba gostha vihare godhana carana kari ami diba tomara hari nivedana kari joda kare rani bale ki balili na pathava vanamali tomara sabao jao vane bada hale lalane laye jeo kanane pathaiba toma saba sane
IDX.author: jñānadāsa
IDX.verses: śrīdāma bale ogo rāṇī, vidāya de tora nīlamaṇi laye jāba goṣṭha vihāre godhana cāraṇa kari, āmi diba tomāra hari nivedana kari joḍa kare rāṇī bale ki balili, nā pāṭhāva vanamālī tomārā sabāo jāo vane baḍa ha’le lālane, la’ye jeo kānane pāṭhāiba tomā sabā sane śunare śrīdāma bhāi, āmāra jāoyā ha’la nāi mā vidāya nāhi dila more jñāna-dāsa kahe śuna, yaśodāra jīvana jāni ki nā jāni vidāya kare
IDX.en_translation:
Śrīdāma says: “O Queen! Bid farewell to your Blue Jewel. I will take Him for pastimes in the pasture. Grazing the cows, I will give (back) your Hari. I make this request with folded hands.” 

The Queen says: “What did you say? I will not send Vanamālī. You all go to the forest too. When He grows up, take Him to the forest with affection. I will send Him with all of you.” 

“Listen, O brother Śrīdāma! My going has not happened. Mother did not give me farewell.” Jñāna Dāsa says: “Listen, I know Yaśodā’s life; I do not know if she will bid farewell or not.”

IDX.search: srimati radhika krsnakanta siromani krsnapriya madhye tanra sama nahi dhani munigana sastre radha kundera varnane gandharvika tulya kunda karaye ganane
IDX.author: bhaktisiddhānta sarasvatī ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
śrīmatī rādhikā-kṛṣṇakāntā-śiromaṇi 
kṛṣṇapriya-madhye tāṅ’ra sama nāhi dhanī 

munigaṇa śāstre rādhā-kuṇḍera varṇane 
gāndharvikā-tulya kuṇḍa karaye gaṇane 

nāradādi-priyavarge je prema durlabha 
anya sādhakete tāhā kabhu nā sulabha 

kintu, rādhā-kuṇḍe snāna jei jana kare 
madhura rasete tāṅ’ra snāne siddhi dhare 

aprākṛta-bhāve sadā yugala-sevana 
rādhā-pāda-padma labhe sei harijana 

śrī-vārṣabhānavī kabe dayitadāsere 
kuṇḍa-tīre sthāna dibe nija-jana ka’re 

‘upadeśāmṛta’ dhari’ rūpānuga-bhāve 
jīvana jāpile kṛṣṇa-kṛpā sei pā’be 

satya, tretā, dvāparera je-sakala bhakta 
kṛṣṇakṛpā labhiyāche gṛhastha-virakta 

bhāvī-kāle, vartamāne bhaktera samāja 
sakalera padarajaḥ jāce dīna āja 

bhakativinoda-prabhu anuga je-jana 
dayita-dāsera tā’ra pade nivedana 

dayā kari’, doṣa hari’, bala ‘hari! hari!’ 
‘upadeśāmṛta’-vāri śiropari dhari’
IDX.en_translation:
Śrīmatī Rādhikā is the crest-jewel of Kṛṣṇa’s beloveds. Among Kṛṣṇa’s beloveds, there is no one as rich in love as Her. 

In the scriptures describing Rādhā-kuṇḍa, the sages count the Kuṇḍa as equal to Gāndharvikā (Rādhā). 

The love that is rare even for the dear devotees like Nārada is never easily attainable by other practitioners. 

But one who bathes in Rādhā-kuṇḍa attains perfection in that sweet mellow through his bath. 

Serving the Divine Couple eternally in a transcendental mood, that devotee of Hari attains the lotus feet of Rādhā. 

When will Śrī Vārṣabhānavī, accepting him as Her own, give Dayita-dāsa a place on the bank of the Kuṇḍa? 

If one passes his life holding the “Upadeśāmṛta” in the mood of a follower of Rūpa Gosvāmī, he will obtain Kṛṣṇa’s mercy. 

All the devotees of Satya, Tretā, and Dvāpara yugas who were detached householders attained Kṛṣṇa’s mercy. 

Today, this lowly person begs for the dust of the feet of all the devotees in the society of devotees, both in the future and the present. 

Whoever is a follower of Bhaktivinoda Prabhu—Dayita-dāsa makes this submission at his feet. 

Be merciful, remove my faults, and say “Hari! Hari!”, holding the water of “Upadeśāmṛta” upon my head.

IDX.search: srivasa vacana sravana kariya sadhvi pativratagana soka parihari mrta sisu rakhi hari rase dila mana srivasa takhana anande matiya angane aila punah nace gora sane sakala pasari gaya nandasuta guna
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
śrīvāsa-vacana, śravaṇa kariyā, 
sādhvī pativratāgaṇa 
śoka parihari’, mṛta śiśu rākhi’, 
hari-rase dila mana 

śrīvāsa takhana, ānande mātiyā, 
aṅgane āila punaḥ 
nāce gorā-sane, sakala pāsari, 
gāya nandasuta-guṇa 

cāri daṇḍa rātre, marila kumāra, 
aṅgane keha nā jāne 
śrī-nāma-maṅgale, tṛtīya prahara, 
rajanī atīta gāne 

kīrtana bhāṅgile, kahe gaura-hari, 
āji kena pāi duḥkha? 
bujhi, ei gṛhe, kichu amaṅgala, 
ghaṭiyā harila sukha 

tabe bhakta-jana, nivedana kare, 
śrīvāsa-śiśura kathā 
śuni’ gorārāya, bale, hāya hāya, 
marame pāinu vyathā 

keha nā kahile, āmāre takhana, 
vipada-saṁvāda sabe 
bhakativinoda, bhakata-vatsala, 
snehete majila tabe
IDX.en_translation:
Hearing Śrīvāsa’s words, the chaste and devoted wives gave up their grief; leaving the dead child, they gave their minds to the nectar of the Lord’s service. 

Śrīvāsa then, intoxicated with bliss, came back to the courtyard. He danced with Lord Caitanya, forgetting everything, and sang the glories of the son of Nanda. 

Four units of time into the night, the boy died, but no one in the courtyard knew. The late night passed in the auspicious chanting of the Holy Name. 

When the congregational chanting ended, Lord Caitanya said, “Why do I feel sorrow today? I understand that some inauspiciousness has occurred in this house, taking away the happiness.” 

Then the devotees related the story of Śrīvāsa’s child. Hearing this, the Lord said, “Alas, alas! I feel pain in My heart! 

“Why did no one tell Me the news of this calamity then?” Bhaktivinoda says: the Lord, who is affectionate to His devotees, was then immersed in love.

IDX.search: srivase kahena prabhu tuhu mora dasa tuya prite bandha ami jagate prakasa bhaktagana senapati srivasa pandita jagate ghusuka aji tomara carita
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses: śrīvāse kahena prabhu,- “tuhū mora dāsa tuyā prīte bāṅdhā āmi jagate prakāśa bhaktagaṇa-senāpati-śrīvāsa-paṇḍita jagate ghuṣuka āji tomāra carita prapañca-kārā-rakṣiṇī māyāra bandhana tomāra nāhika kabhu, dekhuka jagajjana dhana, jana, deha, geha āmāre arpiyā āmāra sevāra sukhe ācha sukhī hañā mama līlāpuṣṭi lāgi’ tomāra saṁsāra śikhuka gṛhastha-jana tomāra ācāra tava preme baddha āchi āmi, nityānanda āmā-dūhe suta jāni’ bhuñjaha ānanda nityasattva suta jā’ra, anitya tanaye āsakti nā kare sei sṛjane pralaye bhaktite tomāra ṛṇī āmi ciradina tava sādhu-bhāve tumi kṣama mora ṛṇa” śrīvāsera pā-ya bhaktivinoda kujana kākuti kariyā māge gaurāṅga-caraṇa
IDX.en_translation:
The Lord said to Śrīvāsa, “You are My servant. I am revealed in the world, bound by your love. 

O Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita, general of the devotees! Let your character be proclaimed throughout the world today. 

The bondage of illusion, which keeps the soul in the prison of the material world, never affects you; let all the world see this. 

Offering wealth, followers, body, and home to Me, you remain happy in the joy of My service. 

For the nourishment of My pastimes, let all householders learn from your life and conduct. 

I am bound by your love, and so is Nityānanda. Knowing us both as your sons, enjoy bliss. 

One whose son is the eternal truth does not become attached to transient sons in creation or dissolution. 

In devotion, I am indebted to you forever. Through your saintly nature, please forgive My debt.” 

Bhaktivinoda, the lowly one, at the feet of Śrīvāsa, earnestly begs for the lotus feet of Lord Caitanya.

IDX.search: srivasera prati caitanya prasada dekhiya sakala jana jaya sri caitanya jaya nityananda bali nace ghana ghana srivasa mandire ki bhava uthila taha ki varnana haya bhavayuddha sane ananda krandana uthe krsna premamaya
IDX.author: saccidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
śrīvāsera prati, caitanya-prasāda, 
dekhiyā sakala jana 
jaya śrī-caitanya, jaya nityānanda, 
bali’ nāce ghana ghana 

śrīvāsa-mandire, ki bhāva uṭhila, 
tāhā ki varṇana haya 
bhāvayuddha-sane, ānanda-krandana, 
uṭhe kṛṣṇa-premamaya 

cāri bhāi paḍi’, prabhura caraṇe, 
prema-gadagada-svare 
kāṅdiyā kāṅdiyā, kākuti kariyā, 
gaḍi’ jāya prema-bhare 

“ohe prāṇeśvara, e hena vipada, 
pratidina jena haya 
jāhāte tomāra, caraṇa-yugale, 
āsakti bāḍite raya 

vipada-sampade, sei dina bhāla, 
je-dina tomāre smari 
tomāra smaraṇa-, rahita je-dina, 
se-dina vipada, hari” 

śrīvāsa-goṣṭhīra, caraṇe paḍiyā, 
bhaktivinoda bhaṇe 
tomādera gorā, kṛpā vitariyā, 
dekhāo durgata jane
IDX.en_translation:
Seeing the mercy shown to Śrīvāsa by Lord Caitanya, all the people repeatedly danced, chanting: “All glories to Śrī Caitanya! All glories to Nityānanda!” 

What emotions arose in the temple of Śrīvāsa? How can they ever be described? Amidst a war of ecstasies, the crying of joy, full of love for Kṛṣṇa, arose. 

The four brothers fell at the Lord’s feet with voices choked with love. Weeping and pleading, they rolled on the ground in great love. 

“O Lord of my life! May such distress happen every day, so that my attachment to Your lotus feet may continuously increase. 

In distress or prosperity, that day is good when I remember You. The day devoid of Your remembrance—that day is true distress, O Lord!” 

Falling at the feet of Śrīvāsa’s associates, Bhaktivinoda says: “May your Lord Caitanya, distributing His mercy, reveal Himself to all distressed souls.”

Listen, O twice-born! Whatever sins you have committed—if you do not commit them again, I will take all of them away from you. 

Give up violence toward others, robbery, and all other unrighteous acts. Do not perform them again. 

Follow the path of righteousness and chant the Holy Name of Lord Hari. Then you will also be able to deliver others. 

Gather all the robbers and thieves by calling them to you, and lead everyone onto the path of righteousness.

They experience all the symptoms of ecstatic love, and these emotional transformations become Their ornaments along with Their contrary moods and intense longing. Initiated into the sacrifice of love with Lalitā and other friends, They become lost in the happiness They achieve. 

Many forest pastimes occur—swinging, water sports, the stealing of the flute, the drinking of nectar, and again the worship of the Sun-god. How many pastimes they perform! Thereafter, with Their friends, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa are absorbed in amorous play. 

In Rādhā-kuṇḍa, such unparalleled eternal pastimes occur every day. For those whose eyes of pure love are open, these become visible; otherwise, they cannot be seen.

I worship Gadādhara, the greatly learned guru and master, who is expert in arranging the emotions of the newly brilliant and others, who delights in the varied rasas of the ocean of Gaura-bhakti, who guides us on the path of intense devotional attachment, and bestows residence in Vraja and other holy places. 

I worship Gadādhara, the greatly learned guru and master, who is honored by the multitude of devotees whose essence is the lotus feet of Śacī’s Son, who is most beloved by Kṛṣṇa, who resides in the lotus of Gaura’s heart, who embodies Mukunda in Gaura’s form, and who bestows one’s inherent spiritual nature. 

I worship Gadādhara, the greatly learned guru and master, who is the sole cause for revealing the service of the groves and other such things, who always gives the ecstatic love of the sakhīs, who is the embodiment of great rasa, who is the most excellent true guru, who bestows the lotus feet of those always surrendered to him. 

I worship Gadādhara, the greatly learned guru and master, who is the beloved sprout revealing Mahāprabhu’s great rasa, who always has the desire to reveal the sprout of great rasa, who brings joy in the mood of the gopīs of Vraja and others to Mahāprabhu. 

I worship Gadādhara, the greatly learned guru and master, who enhances devotion to the lotus feet honored by the multitude of best brāhmaṇas, who insists on revealing his own body as the soul of Rādhikā, who bestows the bright nectar through teaching all the scriptures of devotion. 

I worship Gadādhara, the greatly learned guru and master, by whose sweet nectar from the lotus feet of his beloved ones, he bestows Gaura-bhakti, the great rasa-ocean nectar, who is always accompanied by the eight bodily transformations of ecstatic love, who bestows devotion to his chosen Deity. 

I worship Gadādhara, the greatly learned guru and master, whose mind is steeped in the waves and colors of his unique sweet love; even a man whose mind is thus infused quickly attains the qualification for the mood of a woman; let my mind, like a maddened bee, approach him, whose heart is imbued with ujjvala-rasa. 

Whoever reads these eight verses on Gadādhara, which always bestow the nectar of great rasa, with great devotion, which describe the festival of the gopīs of Vraja, will attain the eligibility for the jewel of devotion to the lotus feet of Śacī’s Son, through the service of the lotus feet of Rādhikā and Gadādhara.

Tapanamiśra’s son, Śrīla Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī, set out to see the Lord, leaving all other duties behind. 

From Kāśī he journeyed by the path through Bengal, accompanied by a servant. 

In this way, Raghunātha arrived at Jagannātha Purī and eagerly met Mahāprabhu at His feet. 

Performing full obeisances, he fell at the Lord’s feet, and the Lord, knowing Raghunātha, embraced him. 

“It is good that you have come; behold the lotus-eyed Lord Jagannātha. Today you will partake of sanctified food with Me.” 

The Lord told Govinda to arrange a dwelling for him and introduced him to Svarūpa Dāmodara and other devotees. 

In this manner, he remained with the Lord for eight months, and day by day his joy increased by the Lord’s mercy. 

From time to time, he would invite Mahāprabhu to his home and cook various delicious preparations. 

Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa was very skilled in cooking; whatever he prepared was like nectar. 

With supreme satisfaction the Lord would eat, and Raghunātha would then partake of the Lord’s remnants. 

After eight months, the Lord bade him farewell and instructed him: “Do not marry. 

Go and serve your elderly parents, and study the Śrīmad Bhāgavatam with a devotee scholar. 

Come again to Purī once more.” Saying this, the Lord placed a garland around his neck. 

Embracing him, the Lord bade him farewell, and Raghunātha, overwhelmed with love, began to weep. 

Taking leave from Svarūpa Dāmodara and the other devotees, he returned to Varanasi. 

For four years he served his parents at home and studied the Bhāgavatam with a devotee scholar. 

When his parents passed away, he became detached and again went to the Lord, melting in divine emotion. 

As before, he stayed with the Lord for eight months, after which the Lord again gave him an order: 

“By My command, Raghunātha, go to Vṛndāvana and reside there with Rūpa and Sanātana. 

Always read the Bhāgavatam and chant the Holy Names of Lord Kṛṣṇa; soon the Lord will bestow His mercy upon you.” 

Saying this, the Lord embraced him, and by the Lord’s mercy, he became intoxicated with divine love. 

He had received a fourteen-cubit Tulasī garland from Lord Jagannātha, along with leftover betel leaves and rice from a festival. 

The Lord gave him those items, and he kept the garland, considering it his worshipable Deity. 

Receiving the Lord’s command, he came to Vṛndāvana and took shelter of Rūpa and Sanātana Gosvāmīs. 

In Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī’s assembly he would read the Bhāgavatam, and while reading, his mind would become overwhelmed with love. 

With tears, trembling, and a choked voice, he could sometimes not even continue reading. 

His voice was sweet like a cuckoo’s, and he was expert in the melodic modes; while reading one verse, he would express four different melodies. 

When Lord Kṛṣṇa’s sweet qualities came to his mind, he would be so overwhelmed with love that he knew nothing else. 

He surrendered at the feet of Lord Govinda, who was his life’s treasure. 

He instructed his disciples to build a temple for Lord Govinda and had ornaments made for the Deity. 

He would not listen to worldly gossip, nor would he speak it; his twenty-four hours were spent in worship and topics about Lord Kṛṣṇa. 

He would not hear any criticism of the devotees; he only knew that everyone was engaged in the worship of the Lord. 

During meditation, he would wear the garland given by Mahāprabhu and keep a token of the Lord’s remnants around his neck. 

By Mahāprabhu’s mercy, divine love flowed from him unimpeded. The Lord’s mercy upon Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa was indeed a great fruit.

On the heated sand, like a drop of water—in the society of sons, friends, and wife, forgetting You, my mind, I dedicated myself to them. Now, of what use will I be? 

O Lord Mādhava! I am hopeless about the final outcome. You are the deliverer of the world and merciful to the poor; therefore, I place my faith in You. 

Half of my life I spent in sleep; how many days have passed in old age and childhood? In secluded groves, with women, I was intoxicated by amorous sports; when will I ever worship You? 

How many four-headed Brahmās die again and again, but You have no beginning or end. They are born from You and again they merge into You, just like the waves of the ocean. 

Vidyāpati says: “At the end, fearing the God of Death, I see no other refuge besides You. You are called the Beginningless Lord without origin; now the burden of delivering me is Yours.”

O venerable devotees, I make this petition: I am a very fallen and wicked person. Fate has drowned me in the terrible ocean of material existence; please grab me by the hair and carry me across. 

Fate is very powerful and does not listen to religious knowledge; it always binds me with the ropes of my own actions. I see no trace of deliverance—all I see is distress. I am helpless, and therefore I cry out in anguish. 

Lust, anger, greed, illusion, pride, and false ego—each pulls me toward its own place. Such is my mind that it wanders like a blind person, knowing neither the right path nor the wrong one. 

I did not accept good counsel, and my mind was absorbed in evil; I placed no hope in Your feet. Narottama dāsa says: seeing and hearing of this condition, I feel fear. Please deliver me and take me into Your company.

IDX.en_translation:
The feet of the Vaiṣṇava ṭhākura are the great treasure of the earth. Listen, oh brother, with a single mind. One who takes their shelter and worships, Kṛṣṇa never abandons them; all others simply die in vain. 

The water from the Vaiṣṇava’s feet has the power to bestow prema-bhakti; no one else is so powerful. The dust from the Vaiṣṇava’s feet is an ornament for the head; there is no end to such ornaments. 

It is written in the Purāṇas that holy water from pilgrimage sites is pure by nature, but all that is merely a deception of devotion. All these cannot compare to the water from the Vaiṣṇava’s feet, by which all desires are fulfilled. 

In the association of Vaiṣṇavas, the mind is joyful at every moment, and one always experiences the direct association of Kṛṣṇa. Humble Narottama Dāsa Ṭhākura weeps, his heart finds no patience: “Why has my condition become so broken?”

IDX.verses: ṭhumaka calata rāmacandra bājata paiñjaniyā kilaka kilaka oṭhata dhāe, girata bhūmi laṭapaṭāe dhāya māta goda leta daśaratha ki raniyā vidurama se aruṇa adhara, bolata mukha madhura-madhura subhaga nāsikā me cāru laṭakata laṭakaniyā tulasī dāsa ati ānanda, dekhi kai mukhāravinda raghuvara chabi ke samāna raghuvara chabi baniyā
IDX.en_translation:
Lord Rāmacandra walks with toddling steps, and His anklets are jingling. 

Giggling, He gets up and runs, then falls upon the ground, stumbling. Queen Kaushalyā runs and takes Him into her lap. 

His lips are reddish like rubies, and He speaks very sweetly. On His beautiful nose, a charming ornament dangles. 

Tulasīdāsa feels great joy upon seeing His lotus-like face. The beauty of the Lord is His only comparison.

No love for the holy name has developed in me. Bhakativinoda’s heart is overwhelmed with sorrow.

You have remained in Mathurā. The residents of Vraja are distressed, crying out and lamenting, “Kānu! Kānu!” 

Yaśodā and Nanda sit as if blind, unable to find the courage to rise. The cowherd friends and the cows are desolate; the sound of the flute is not heard, and the city marketplace is empty. 

The bees, abandoning the flowers, roll on the ground, and the trees look sad. The peahens do not dance, the doves do not coo, and the cuckoos do not sing. 

Rādhā is wasting away with the fever of separation; the fire of separation is everywhere. Even the waters of the Yamunā have become like fire—so says Govinda dāsa.

You are indeed an ocean of mercy and a friend of the fallen. O Lord, please be mindful of me. I have fallen into bad association and have been swallowed by the great whale of lust. O Master, please deliver me! 

All my life I have been absorbed in offenses and have not sincerely worshiped You. Yet You are my only refuge. Do not abandon me, O Lord of my life, for there is no one more fallen than me. 

The name “Purifier of the Fallen” is Your declaration, O dark-complexioned Lord! If You neglect me, I have no other shelter. Even if I am an offender, still You are my only refuge; this is as true as a chaste wife’s husband being her only refuge. 

You are indeed the Supreme Deity; You will not neglect me. Please hear, O Lord of my life! Even if I commit offenses, still You are my Master. Please make me Your servant by giving me service. 

My heart is ruined by lust; it does not hear what is good for itself. The evil desires of my mind do not cease. O Master, please accept me; You are the wish-fulfilling tree of desire. Let everyone witness Your mercy. 

There is no one as fallen as me in all the three worlds. Take the name “Purifier of Narottama!” Let this name resound throughout the world: “The Lord delivers the fallen!” Make me Your own servant, O lifter of the hill. 

Narottama is very distressed. O Lord, make me happy through worship and congregational chanting. The obstacles do not go away, and this is my greatest fear. I submit this prayer to You constantly.

Your lotus feet are worshiped by devoted ones like Śiva and others. Having attained the supreme abode of the Supreme Lord, You shine greatly. For all assemblies of surrendered devotees, You are the shining wish-fulfilling tree that fulfills their desires. O son of Śacī, O my Lord, O giver of liberation, please show mercy to me, the dull-witted. 

Indeed, even those with vast intelligence like Sārvabhauma are unable to fully describe You, who are considered a great incarnation. Who else, then, can be skillful enough? Therefore, I offer my supreme obeisances to You. O son of Śacī, O my Lord, O giver of liberation, please show mercy to me, the dull-witted. 

That which was not revealed in any way by the scriptures or even the Upanisads, and that which was not even revealed by incarnations in other ages—O ocean of mellows, You are now scattering that jewel of devotion on this earth. O son of Śacī, O my Lord, O giver of liberation, please show mercy to me, the dull-witted. 

You astonish the stage of dancing with Your own expanding love. You manifest the nectar of love for the assemblies of surrendered devotees, just like the three-eyed Lord Śiva. O You who are difficult to understand for those arrogant people tainted by false ego, O son of Śacī, O my Lord, O giver of liberation, please show mercy to me, the dull-witted. 

Those people born on earth who have taken birth in low families—You deliver even them with Your abundant and beautiful mercy. Thus, with a joyful heart, I take refuge in You. O son of Śacī, O my Lord, O giver of liberation, please show mercy to me, the dull-witted. 

From Your lotus-like mouth flows the sweet honey of gentle words. This creates a multitude of devotees who, like bees, are eager for that nectar. O ocean of jewel-like Holy Names which bring auspiciousness to all people! O son of Śacī, O my Lord, O giver of liberation, please show mercy to me, the dull-witted. 

Your face is sweet like the moon, and Your eyes are like shining, ever-awake lotus flowers. Your lips are beautiful like a cluster of smiles, and Your chest is broad. Your arms are powerful like raised snakes, and Your splendor is like millions of Cupids. O son of Śacī, O my Lord, O giver of liberation, please show mercy to me, the dull-witted. 

I am a wicked person on this earth, yet You are golden-colored like the ketakī flower. Even though I am full of various faults, You do not show even a trace of finding fault in me. Therefore, with a humble mind, I worship You, O Lord who are compassionate to the fallen. O son of Śacī, O my Lord, O giver of liberation, please show mercy to me, the dull-witted. 

O festival for the entire world! For those people who, with their minds fixed on Your lotus footprints, recite these eight verses—O delight of Śacī’s heart, O Lord whose fame shines like the moon—O Lord, please bestow upon them abundant good fortune born of Your own love.

Vṛndāvana is beyond the power of speech to describe—a spiritual abode dense with the bliss of divine love. In that place of manifest happiness there is no suffering from old age or death, and the mellows of Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes are always present. 

The love of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa defeats many-times refined gold; in their joyful waves, they are an ocean of mellows. Their eyes, like chakora birds, drink in that love; both are friends of the happiness of love. 

Rādhā, the best of beloveds, is enchanting on the left side and bears the effulgence of golden Kṛṣṇa. Her sari is red with affection, and she wears charming blue silk; ornaments adorn her every limb. 

Their eyes drink in the pastimes of beauty; both are the very life of the companions, who are immersed in joy. Beyond the perception of the Vedas, upon a jeweled altar, they serve the youthful Divine Couple daily. 

Why do you not worship the Lord, having obtained such a rare human birth? Why do you die entangled in the bonds of material existence? Give up other ritualistic activities and do not look toward mundane religion; instead, perform devotional service to the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. 

Material objects lead toward danger; you do not worship the Lord of Vraja, the essence of happiness, the son of Nanda. Heaven, impersonal liberation, and the enjoyment of hellish material existence—all are the destruction and perversion of human birth. 

Do not place faith in the material body; the lord of death is a strict disciplinarian. The results of actions are an ocean of sorrow. Seeing and hearing this, worship according to the saintly scriptures and fix your attachment upon the lotus feet of the Divine Couple. 

Fruitive activities and speculative knowledge are merely pots of poison; those who eat them thinking them to be nectar always wander through various species, eating abominable things, and their birth leads only to degradation. 

One who has no attachment for Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa and yet calls another their lord knows nothing of loving devotional service. Such people have no trace of devotion; they meditate in illusion, and their worthless conceptions are in vain. 

People perform knowledge and work but do not know the yoga of devotion, thus remaining ignorant in many ways. Do not listen to them; knowing the ultimate reality, loving devotion is the life of the devotees. 

The Lord pervades the universe, and Brahmā and Śiva are His order-carriers; His pastimes are sweet. Whoever knows this truth is the most excellent, and I will always associate with such persons. 

Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Lord; become extremely thirsty for Him and worship Him with the mood of Vraja. In the company of devotees who relish divine mellows, always enjoy with great joy while residing in Vṛndāvana. 

Day and night, filled with spiritual emotion and meditating in the mind, I will always reside in the Vraja of Nanda. Know this statement to be true and never bring anything else into it; this is the authoritative word of Śrī Jīva Gosvāmī. 

Fix your mind upon the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa’s devotees and, according to their words, always become like the companions; joining their group, I will always wander in Vraja. 

Singing the narrations of the mellows of His pastimes and meditating on the youthful Divine Couple, I will pray with longing. In life and in death I desire nothing else—so says humble Narottama dāsa.

vācya, vācaka-ei dui svarūpa tomāra 
vācya-tava śrī-vigraha cidānandākāra 

vācaka-svarūpa-tava śrī-kṛṣṇādi nāma 
varṇarūpī sarvajīva-ānanda-viśrāma 

ei dui svarūpe tava ananta prakāśa 
dayā kari’ deya jīve tomāra vilāsa 

kintu jāniyāchi nātha, vācaka-svarūpa 
vācyāpekṣā dayāmaya-ei aparūpa 

nāma-nāmī bheda nāi-vedera vacana 
tabu nāma-nāmī ha’te adhika karuṇa 

kṛṣṇa-aparādhe jadi nāme śraddhā kari’ 
prāṇa bhari’ ḍāke nāma-rāma, kṛṣṇa, hari 

aparādha dūre jāya, ānanda-sāgare 
bhāse sei anāyāse rasera pāthāre 

vigrahasvarūpa vācye aparādha kari’ 
śuddhanāmāśraye sei aparādhe tari 

bhakativinoda māge śrī-rūpa-caraṇe 
vācaka-svarūpa nāme rati anukṣaṇe
IDX.en_translation:
Vācya and Vācaka—these two are Your forms. Vācya is Your divine form, the embodiment of eternal knowledge and bliss. 

Vācaka is Your holy name, which in the form of syllables is the resting place of all souls’ bliss. 

In these two forms, Your manifestation is endless; out of mercy, You grant Your divine pastimes to the living entities. 

But I have known, O Lord, that Your name is even more merciful than Your form—this is wonderful. 

The Vedas declare that there is no difference between the Name and the Named. Still, the Name is more compassionate. 

If, even after committing offenses against Kṛṣṇa, one has faith in the Name and calls out names like Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, or Hari with a full heart, 

then the offenses vanish, and that person floats effortlessly in the ocean of bliss, in the vast expanse of divine mellows. 

Though one may offend the Deity form, one can cross over those offenses by taking shelter of the pure Name. 

Bhaktivinoda begs at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa for constant attachment to the Holy Name.

vada vada hari, chadma nā kariha, 
vipade beḍhala deśa

śravaṇa daśana keśa 

tāra pāche pāche, locana vacana, 
tārā dohe dila bhaṅga 
mora mora kari, rātra-dine mari, 
jamadūte dekhe raṅga 

sundara nagare, prati ghare ghare, 
viṣama jamera thānā 
daṇḍa je divasa, vatsara gaṇiche, 
kona dine dibe hānā 

dārā-putra-vadhū, jatana kariche, 
sakali nimera titā 
maraṇa samaye, hāte gale bāndhi, 
mukhe jvāli dibe citā 

vadana bhariyā, hari nā baliyā, 
śamana taribe kise 
dāsa locana, kahiyā phāraka, 
maricha āpana doṣe
IDX.en_translation:
Speak, speak the Name of Lord Hari! Do not pretend. The country is surrounded by calamity. Knowing this truth, they have already fled—your ears, your teeth, and your hair. 

Behind them, your eyes and your speech have both broken their promise. Saying “mine, mine,” you die day and night while the messengers of the God of Death see this as a show. 

In this beautiful city, in every house, there is a terrible outpost of the God of Death. Counting the days and years of your punishment, on which day will he finally strike? 

Your wife, sons, and daughters-in-law all take care of themselves; everything is as bitter as neem. At the time of your death, they will bind your hands and neck and light the funeral pyre at your mouth. 

If you do not wholeheartedly chant the Name of Lord Hari, how will you ever cross over the messenger of death? Locana Dāsa says clearly: “You are dying only due to your own fault.”

Superior even to Mathurā is the abode of Vṛndāvana, where the Lord fulfilled His desire for the Rāsa dance festival. 

Superior even to Vṛndāvana is Govardhana Hill, where Lord Kṛṣṇa and Śrīmati Rādhā-rāṇī performed Their pastimes. 

Superior even to Govardhana Hill is the bank of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, where the Lord of Gokula was immersed in the nectar of divine love. 

Leaving Govardhana Hill and Rādhā-kuṇḍa, anyone who makes their place of worship elsewhere—there is no one as foolish as them. 

The bank of Rādhā-kuṇḍa is the supreme place and the very abode of divine love.

I first offer my obeisances to the feet of my initiating spiritual master and all my instructing spiritual masters. 

Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī, Śrīla Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī, Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī, Śrīla Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī, and Śrīla Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī—these six are my instructing spiritual masters. 

To the lotus feet of all of them, I offer millions of obeisances. 

To all the devotees of the Supreme Lord, headed by Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita—I offer a thousand obeisances to their lotus feet. 

Advaita Ācārya is the Lord’s plenary portion incarnation; to His lotus feet, I offer millions of obeisances. 

Lord Nityānanda Rāya is the Lord’s own manifested form; I offer obeisances to His lotus feet, of which I am a servant. 

Gadādhara Paṇḍita and the other associates are the Lord’s personal potencies; at the feet of all of them, I offer a thousand obeisances. 

Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya is the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself; at His lotus feet, I offer unlimited obeisances.

Its three pure branches exist for the delight of the learned: “Upadeśa” (Instruction), “Upalabdhi” (Realization), and “Ucchvāsa” (Outpouring of Emotion). 

Taking shelter of this tree, a learned person obtains the fruit of auspiciousness: servitude in the pastimes of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa in the forest of Vṛndāvana. 

Having honored the Vaiṣṇavas, the brāhmaṇas, and all living entities eternally, I, being humble, sing this song based on the rasa of Vraja.

IDX.en_translation:
The night ends and light enters; rise up, O soul, and leave your sleep. Chant the names of Hari, Mukunda, Murāri, Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and Hayagrīva. 

Chant the names of Nṛsiṁha, Vāmana, Śrī Madhusūdana, and Śyāma. All glories to the killer of Pūtanā, the destroyer of Kaiṭabha, and to Rāma, the son of Daśaratha. 

He is Yaśodā’s darling, Govinda, Gopāla, and the Lord of Vṛndāvana. He is the beloved of the gopīs, the lover of Rādhā, and the most beautiful in all the world. 

He is the destroyer of Rāvaṇa, the butter-thief, and the one who stole the clothes of the gopīs. He is the cowherd of Vraja, the protector of the cowherds, the captivator of the mind, and the player of the flute. 

He is worshiped by the great yogis—the son of Nanda who removes the fears of the residents of Vraja. Like a fresh cloud with a charming form, He is the enchanting flute-player. 

He is the son of Yaśodā, the killer of Kaṁsa, and the one who enjoys the rāsa dance in the groves. In the kadamba forest, He is absorbed in the rāsa dance as a resident of the forests of Vṛndāvana. 

He is the enhancer of bliss, the abode of love, and more enchanting than Cupid. He is the enchanter of the minds of the cowherd girls and the abode of all good qualities. 

He is the life of the Yamunā, absorbed in pastimes—the moon for the chakora bird of the mind. O my mind, sing the glories of Kṛṣṇa, the nectar of the Holy Name, and follow these words of mine.

IDX.en_translation:
When awakened love becomes active, then external manifestations of emotion arise. Revealing the inner emotions, it creates excellent external transformations, whatever is appropriate at that time. 

Dancing, singing, rolling on the ground, crying loudly, twisting the body, roaring, yawning, heavy breathing, disregard for public opinion, salivation, excessive reeling, hiccups and so on, and loud laughter. 

All born from the body and mind, these “ornaments” are excellent manifestations, declared to be twenty types. One is named “udbhāsvāra”; and disheveling of hair, a radiant scent, and disarray of clothing are other transformations. 

Lamentation, conversation, incoherent talk, repetition, denial, excessive messages, pretense, advice, commands, and indirect references—these are specific types of verbal manifestations.

O friend of the distressed! Whether You punish me or show me mercy, I have no other refuge but You. Even if a hundred million thunderbolts or pure fresh rain should fall, the chataka bird still praises the cloud. 

As I hear of the incomparable and difficult worship of the ancient devotees, my heart—devoid of even a trace of devotion—burns with despair. But upon hearing of Your all-pervading wave of compassion, O remover of sins, this heart, sprinkled with a drop of hope, attains coolness within.

IDX.en_translation:
On the other side of Virajā river, is the pure transcendental abode. Above that is Śrī Gokula, named the forest of Vṛndāvana. 

Vṛndāvana is a Cintāmaṇi, a mine of transcendental bliss jewels. It is a spiritual, unparalleled vision. Within it is a wonder: Kṛṣṇa is the essence of all trees, like a sapphire-like Tamāla tree. 

Upon Him is a golden creeper, conquering all abodes, risen, supremely purifying. She is the essence of the bliss-giving potency, whose name is Mahābhāva (the highest state of ecstatic love). She is enchanting even the enchanter of the three worlds. 

Known by the name Rādhā, pleasing the heart of Govinda, she shines in supreme bliss. That creeper’s leaves and flowers, the group of confidantes like Lalitā, all together, firmly bind the tree. 

By the touch of the creeper, the Kṛṣṇa tree is joyful. Without the creeper, it cannot exist at any time. 

Without the Tamāla, the creeper cannot survive. That creeper always yearns for union. 

Bhaktivinoda sees their union, and desires nothing else at any time.

IDX.en_translation:
The distortions of the mind in the form of material desires In my heart, they enjoy uncontrollably. 

Alas, how much effort I made! The distorted intelligence did not leave, and finally my life departs. 

These terrible distortions made me restless. Peace found no place, my inner self is agitated. 

When will Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī bestow mercy upon me, and deliver me by offering appropriate renunciation? 

When will Sanātana Gosvāmī free me from material objects, and, becoming merciful, surrender me to Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu? 

When will Śrī Jīva Gosvāmī, with the waters of established philosophical conclusions, extinguish the fire of arguments, in which my mind burns? 

Hearing the name of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, when will ecstasy arise, and by drinking the nectar of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, when will I become free from sorrow? 

This person is a wicked soul, poorer than the poorest, a humble soul who begs for the shelter of the feet of the devotees of Viṣṇu.

Everyone is intoxicated by material sense objects and knows nothing of the truth of the Holy Name of Kṛṣṇa. The entire world has become devoid of devotion. Bitten by the poisonous snake of Kali-yuga, living entities are scorched by the false tastes of illusion, and they do not even know who they really are. 

Everyone is busy celebrating the festivals of their own sons and daughters, and there is not even a trace of any other auspicious activity. They worship demons with meat and wine and commit violence against various living beings. This is the condition throughout the land. 

Seeing this and feeling great compassion, Lord Kṛṣṇa, assuming the name “Kamalākṣa” (the Lotus-eyed One), descended in the land of Gauḍa. His only desire was to cause the Prince of Vraja to incarnate along with all His associates. 

Taking the lead before everyone else to deliver the living entities, He manifested Himself in Śāntipura. Vaiṣṇava Dāsa says: “All sins will now be destroyed, and everyone will receive the Holy Name of Kṛṣṇa.”

A pure renunciant performs the congregational chanting of the Holy Names. He maintains his life only by eating what he receives through begging. 

If a renunciant depends on others for his needs, his purpose is not achieved, and Lord Kṛṣṇa neglects him. 

If a renunciant indulges the desires of his tongue, his spiritual goal is lost, and he becomes a slave to material tastes. 

A renunciant should always perform the congregational chanting. He should fill his belly only with vegetables, leaves, fruits, and roots. 

One who wanders through society just to satisfy the desires of the tongue, being dedicated only to his stomach and genitals, will never attain Lord Kṛṣṇa. 

O renunciant brother! Do not let mundane talk enter your ears. Do not speak of worldly news when you meet others. 

O brother! Do not even converse with women in your dreams. Remember, you have left your wife at home to come to the forest of renunciation. 

If you wish to maintain your love for Lord Gaurāṅga, then always keep the story of Choṭa Haridāsa in your mind. 

Do not eat palatable foods, and do not wear fine clothes. Always serve Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa within your heart. 

Like the senior Haridāsa Ṭhākura, always chant the Holy Names of Kṛṣṇa. During all eight periods of the day, serve Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in the groves of Vṛndāvana.

Risen in the world, the sun of the Holy Name destroys ignorance. Giving up all the opulence of illusion, the saintly soul becomes devoted to it. 

O Holy Name of Hari! You are the sun, the dispeller of the darkness of ignorance. Who indeed knows Your glory? What learned person can recount Your many glories and proclaim them all in a loud voice? 

Your glimmer first appears, and the darkness of this material existence is almost swallowed. 

Quickly destroying the darkness, supreme knowledge bestows sight upon the eyes that were blind to reality. 

That supreme knowledge is indeed pure devotion, which awakens an awakens an inclination focused on the Lord. 

This wonderful pastime is always Yours; Bhaktivinoda has understood its essence.

Vraja-dhāma is the eternal wealth, the two persons Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, Who have become one body absorbed in divine pastimes. Along with their abode, they have appeared in Gauḍa-deśa, Bringing their own eternal associates with them. 

O mind, know this as the absolute truth: In Navadvīpa, Gaura-hari, performing nāma-saṅkīrtana, Distributed the nectar of prema throughout Gauḍa. 

Under the pretext of sannyāsa, that same Hari in Nīlācala, Is Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, the master of ascetics. Taking Dāmodara and Rāmānanda, feeling supreme bliss, He revealed deep confidential truths in great detail. 

Teaching those truths and the ultimate goal to Raghunātha, He sent him to the presence of Śrī Rūpa. Śrī Dāsa Gosvāmī in Vraja, worshipping Kṛṣṇa with Rūpa, Has written the verses of “Manaḥ-śikṣā.” 

To be the servant of the servant of those whose hope is great, This Bhaktivinoda is most humble and possesses nothing. He sings this “Manaḥ-śikṣā Bhāṣā” wherever pure devotees are found, May they mercifully grant him a hearing.

Rādhā-Śyām, Śyāmā-Śyām! You give happiness to the minds of the people of Vraja. 

Peacock-feather crown, shark-shaped earrings, Vaijayantī garland around the neck. Sweet ankle-bells on the feet. Rādhā-Śyām, Śyāmā-Śyām! 

Beautiful face, eyes like lotus petals, Your crooked glance is captivating. Enchanting player of the flute. Rādhā-Śyām, Śyāmā-Śyām! 

Grazing cows in Vṛndāvana, stealing the minds of the gopīs. Holder of Śrī Govardhana. Rādhā-Śyām, Śyāmā-Śyām! 

Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, both have now met, incarnating as the Golden Form (Gaura). Preaching the religion of kīrtana. Rādhā-Śyām, Śyāmā-Śyām! 

Without You, I have no one else; the Name and Form are the Avatāra. I surrender at Your feet; Nārāyaṇa (Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī) surrenders. Rādhā-Śyām, Śyāmā-Śyām!

Thereafter, the sinner will find no release in the material world. For them, there is never any progress or destination; they are uselessly wandering in their activities. 

Śrī Locana dāsa, hoping for devotion, speaks and writes the glories of Hari. I do not even wish to see the face of one who does not have the intelligence to appreciate such essential nectar.

O Devi! Be pleased! Bestow mercy upon me! Show me the pair of lotus faces of You two sporting here in the play-groves of Vṛndāvana with the playful movements of the best of intoxicated elephants. 

Alas, O Devi! With a voice choked with the weight of piteous words, falling on the ground like a stick, I beg with intense distress: making this ignorant person an object of Your mercy, O Gāndharvikā, count me among Your own people. 

O Śyāmā! When will I worship You, whose body is bound by the left arm of Śyāma, who has enchanted all the people of the universe with a beauty superior to the beauty of the Husband of Ramā (Viṣṇu), and who possesses a wealth of form rare even for Indirā? 

O Devi! Covering You with a cloth of the color of a cloud and removing the anklets from Your feet, when will I joyfully make You go on a tryst at night in the bower where the Son of the King of Vraja is shining? 

When will this person massage the lotus feet of You two, the ornaments of the three worlds, who are seated on a play-bed made of multitudes of flowers in the bower and enjoying sweet, joking pastimes? 

O Queen of Vṛndāvana! When will I fan You two with a yak-tail whisk, seated at the root of a tree on the bank of Your Kuṇḍa, Your lotus faces kissing the drops of sweat from the fatigue of pastimes? 

O beautiful-eyed one! You are hiding in the hollow of a bower with Mukunda. “Citra herself indicated it; not I!”—when will I lead You, who are thus feigning anger with knitted eyebrows, before the Son of the King of Vraja? 

When will I see You, having conquered the Son of the King of Vraja in the curiosity of a war of words, intoxicated with pride, with speech expanding with great arrogance, being praised profusely by the blooming friends? 

Whoever surrenders and recites this prayer of eight verses to the Daughter of Vṛṣabhānu nicely, She, meeting with Her Beloved and holding joy, accepts a wave of mercy towards him.

All the holy places in the three worlds that destroy darkness were brought together by the Prince of Vraja. He personally immersed Himself in this pond, whose glories are now manifest. That very pure water of Śyāma-kuṇḍa is my refuge. 

Lord Kṛṣṇa, with humble words, requested Rādhā: “O slender-limbed one! O Rādhā! Please take a bath here in this pure water, which is praised as a holy place.” That very pure water of Śyāma-kuṇḍa is my refuge. 

Any sin arising from the slaying of the bull demon was considered finished by Lord Kṛṣṇa after He bathed here. But Rādhā, having victoriously rejected this holy place, manifested Her own pond along with all Her friends. That very pure water of Śyāma-kuṇḍa is my refuge. 

When all other holy places, terrified and speechless, humbly approached the moon-like Kṛṣṇa and submitted: “If Rādhā, the refuge of the helpless, avoids us, then what refuge do we have?”, the Lord showed His mercy. That very pure water of Śyāma-kuṇḍa is my refuge.

On its nearby bank, charming groves are arranged. These groves were given to Subala and the Lord’s other friends by Śrīmati Rādhikā and Her companions. It is a royal place, abounding with various flowers, creepers, and desire trees. That very pure water of Śyāma-kuṇḍa is my refuge. 

Whoever, being intelligent, recites these eight verses in praise of Śyāma-kuṇḍa with love for Him who is like a fresh cloud and for Her with golden effulgence, quickly attains the Son of the King of Vraja. He will become worshipable by Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa and Their gopī companions.

In the sacred land of Vraja, for the dearest beloveds of Lord Kṛṣṇa, this pond quickly generates the desire-tree of divine love in the heart of anyone who bathes here. To that soul it is exceedingly dear. That extremely fragrant Rādhā-kuṇḍa alone is my refuge.

This is intensely the land of love for the moon of Vraja, Lord Kṛṣṇa, and it is as dear to Him as the crown-jewel of the gopīs herself. Even though known by Her Name, it is intimately connected to Her. That extremely fragrant Rādhā-kuṇḍa alone is my refuge.

IDX.en_translation:
The son of Yaśomatī, the chief lover of Vraja, Kṛṣṇa, who delights Gokula. The wealth of the gopīs’ lives, the enchanter of Cupid, and the subduer of the serpent Kāliya. 

Pure Harināma is a nectarine pastime. He is the Lord of the forests, the ever-fresh supreme lover, the flute-player adorned with beautiful garments. 

The protector of the people of Vraja, the destroyer of the demon dynasty, and the protector of Nanda’s cows. He is Govinda, Mādhava, the butter thief, and the beautiful cowherd boy of Nanda. 

He roams on the banks of the Yamunā, stole the garments of the gopīs, and enjoys the rāsa dance, full of mercy. He is the beloved of Śrī Rādhā, the supreme dancer of Vṛndāvana, and the shelter of Bhaktivinoda.

IDX.first_line: yat kiṅkarīṣu bahuśaḥ khalu kāku vāṇī
